releases.title: Side Acquires Boutique Art Studio Roboto Entertainment in Creative Services Push
releases.body:
Founder Andrea Cordella appointed Global Head of Art as Side establishes new Chengdu studio

CHENGDU, China, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Leading games services provider, Side, today acquired the boutique games art studio, Roboto Entertainment, strengthening its global art capabilities and presence in mainland China. Roboto Entertainment founder and industry veteran, Andrea Cordella, will lead Side's global art division and act as studio head for the new Chengdu site. His team will work closely with Side Shanghai as well as Side's wider network of art and co-development teams spread across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia.

"When half the titles at gamescom's Opening Night Live this year were made in China, the world notices. China has long been one of the most important markets for our industry, and I'm fiercely proud of the fact that our team there is hungry for more work, so we're going to grow." said Deborah Kirkham, CEO at Side.

While the games industry has reported a slowdown globally in recent years, the Chinese market is expected to grow by 4% in 2026 and hit $59.8B by 2030. It boasts some of the highest player engagement rates, esports engagement, player hours, and player spend, making the region an attractive space for developers.

"This acquisition is a double-down on a winning regional strategy. With Andrea as our Global Head of Art and a new studio in Chengdu, we now have some of the industry's best environment and world-building artistic talent," continued Kirkham.

Cordella founded Roboto Entertainment in 2014, specialising in environment and world building art for games. The Chengdu-based team has worked on AAA and AA releases across console and mobile games.

Andrea Cordella said, "I knew from the moment I met Deborah and the team at Side that the company aligned with the values my team and I hold dear. We strive for excellence and hold creativity close to our hearts – games are the only art medium where the consumer plays an equal role to the creator, and we will continue to deliver that creativity to every brief, now collaborating with teams across the world and supporting developers on a range of projects. It goes without saying, but I can't wait to get started."

Side's QA offering recently expanded through a partnership with leading AI QA platform, Modl.ai, announced at Gamescom earlier this year. Side, which provides Player Support, QA, Localisation, LQA, Datasets, Codev, Art and Audio, already offers its full suite of services to China-based developers.

The new studio, combined with new expertise in environment art through Andrea and his team, will allow the company to offer developers in China and beyond more than ever before.  

About Side: 

Side is a global video game development and services provider, offering technical and creative solutions to many of the largest developers and studios around the world. Founded in 2009, Side has grown from their Japanese roots to become a global force in the technology industry, with 15+ studios in over a dozen countries across the Americas, Europe, and Asia. Their industry-leading services include art production, game development, audio production, quality assurance, localisation, localisation QA, player support, community management, and datasets. For more information, visit www.side.inc

releases.title: University of Phoenix highlights ways students can reduce college costs during National Transfer Student Week
releases.body:
Scholarships, transfer credits and prior-learning pathways help eligible students identify cost savings and affordability of degree completion

PHOENIX, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- University of Phoenix is recognizing National Transfer Student Week by highlighting the range of pathways that can help eligible students reduce education costs and make informed decisions about their educational journeys. Scholarships, transfer credits, prior learning assessments and alternative credit pathways offer students opportunities to gain insights about affordability and saving time and money on earning a degree while building on previous academic and professional achievements. 

"Many students assume affordability depends on a single scholarship or financial aid source," said Director of Financial Education Initiatives and Repayment Management, Chris Conway. "In reality, transfer credit, scholarship opportunities, prior learning and alternative credit pathways can work together to help reduce costs and create a more efficient path to degree completion. Understanding those options early can make a meaningful difference for students."

As University of Phoenix celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026, the institution is reflecting five decades of helping working adults build on previous academic achievement and professional experience rather than start over. Today, transfer-credit pathways and scholarship opportunities remain an important part of that mission, helping eligible students reduce costs while pursuing degrees aligned with career goals.

Impact of Transfer-friendly programs

Affordable education pathways can help students continue pursuing their goals through life's most challenging seasons. For University of Phoenix transfer student Melonie Olipant, transfer credits helped her return to school after having children and continue making progress toward degree completion.

"Everyone expects a mother to say, 'I'm doing it for my children,' and they have always been a huge part of my why," Olipant said. "But there were moments when I was so tired, overwhelmed and lost that I didn't even know who I was doing it for anymore. I was so busy trying to hold everything together that I lost sight of myself.

"Still, I kept going not because I always felt strong, but because I refused to let the hardest season of my life become the ending of my story. Now, only a few credits away from my degree, I realize I wasn't just fighting for a better future for my children. I was fighting for myself, too. I didn't just earn a degree. I gave myself a future I once wasn't sure I'd see."

Scholarships help students reduce education costs

University of Phoenix offers multiple scholarship opportunities for eligible students like Olipant, ensuring that every new, qualifying student receives financial assistance. The Phoenix® Scholarship is available to students with at least three years of work experience, while the Transfer Scholarship is for those with 12 to 60 transfer credits.

  • Phoenix® Scholarship Savings Breakdown:

Bachelor's, Master's and Doctoral: Maximum value of $1K, provided the student maintains eligibility, applied over a set number of courses.

  • Transfer Scholarship Savings Breakdown:

Bachelor's: Maximum value of $3K, provided the student maintains eligibility, applied over 20 courses

In addition to University scholarships, alternate credit providers like Straighterline, Sophia and Study.com offer students an opportunity to earn general education credits via self-paced courses. Eligible students may complete general education courses with an alternative credit provider and then transfer eligible credits to University of Phoenix, helping them save time and money.

In addition to scholarships, transfer credit opportunities and alternate credit providers, University of Phoenix offers a comprehensive Savings Explorer® tool that presents information about scholarship opportunities, as well as transferring college credit and earning credit for prior learning through Prior Learning Assessment, national testing programs, alternative credit providers, and military service. By answering a few simple questions via the Savings Explorer tool, prospective students can find out what other students with relevant experience have saved.

University of Phoenix students and alumni have access to the Career Services for Life® commitment, helping to ensure the tools, resources, and support needed to thrive in their career of choice.

About University of Phoenix

University of Phoenix is Built for Real Life. 50 Years Strong. The University innovates to help working adults enhance their careers and develop skills in a rapidly changing world through flexible online learning, relevant courses, academic AI pillars, and skills-mapped curriculum for associate, bachelor's and master's degree programs. Active students and alumni have access to Career Services for Life® resources including career guidance and tools. For more information, visit phoenix.edu.

releases.title: The Vilcek Foundation Announces the 2026 New American Perspectives Program at the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival (HIFF)
releases.body:
Presented in partnership with HIFF, the program spotlights five immigrant filmmakers through screenings and special events, including a master class with Academy Award® winner Ke Huy Quan

HONOLULU, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Vilcek Foundation, in partnership with the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival (HIFF), presents the New American Perspectives (NAP) program at the 46th edition of the festival, running on O'ahu from October 21–November 5, 2026.

NAP spotlights immigrant filmmakers, celebrating the powerful impact of diversity in contemporary cinema in the United States through public film screenings, Q&A sessions with filmmakers and actors, and a panel discussion. This year's NAP program will also feature a book talk and master class by Academy Award®-winning actor Ke Huy Quan.

A mainstay festival program for the past two decades, NAP welcomes a cohort of five foreign-born artists this year. The distinguished 2026 group includes featured filmmaker Quan (b. Vietnam) and four guest filmmakers: Henry Ian Cusick (b. Peru), Liz Sargent (b. South Korea), Alex Tarrant (b. New Zealand), and Michelle Zhou (b. China). This program represents the U.S. premiere of new films from Cusick and Tarrant. The program will also mark the debut of feature-length films by Sargent and Zhou.

"From stories of wartime bravery to period pieces set during cinema's Golden Age, this year's New American Perspectives program celebrates the humanity at the heart of filmmaking and showcases the importance of diverse voices in the craft," Vilcek Foundation President Rick Kinsel says. "The Vilcek Foundation is proud to continue our longstanding partnership with the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival and spotlight the ingenuity of storytellers from around the globe."

The 2026 NAP program is buoyed by two featured events. First, NAP's quartet of guest filmmakers take the stage for a panel discussion exploring both their creative journeys and how immigrant and Indigenous perspectives can challenge conventional narratives and democratize the film industry.

Second, Academy Award®-winning actor Quan hosts a book talk for his debut work, Never Say Die: A Memoir. Reflecting on his journey from childhood stardom to behind the camera and back again, Quan discusses his life, career, and the lessons from over four decades in film. A HIFF career achievement honoree, Quan will also lead a master class discussion following a screening of his classic film Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.

NAP guest filmmakers will participate in Q&A sessions following select screenings. Filmmakers Henry Ian Cusick and Alex Tarrant will also participate in HIFF's Guest Filmmaker Program, which brings artists from around the globe into Hawaiʻi's K-12 classrooms.

"These five films show the power and depth of American storytelling today — and are informed by the remarkable journeys of the filmmakers themselves," Jean H. Lee, executive director of the Hawaiʻi International Film Festival, says. "We are grateful to the Vilcek Foundation for bringing us work that will inspire the next generation of filmmakers here in Hawaiʻi to tell their own rich and varied stories as well."

More information on the NAP program and participating filmmakers can be found below. Tickets to the NAP and HIFF46 can be purchased at hiff.org.

FEATURED EVENTS

New American Perspectives: In Conversation

Oct 26 | 6:00 p.m. HST | Honolulu Civil Beat, 3650 Waialae Ave, Suite 200, Honolulu, HI 96816

NAP guest filmmakers Henry Ian Cusick, Liz Sargent, Alex Tarrant, and Michelle Zhou unite for a discussion about their careers and the importance of diversity across the filmmaking landscape. This panel discussion is supported in part by Honolulu Civil Beat and will be held in its offices.

Never Say Die: Book Talk with Ke Huy Quan

Nov 1 | 11:30 a.m. HST | da Shop: books + curiosities, 3565 Harding Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Join Academy Award®-winning actor, HIFF career achievement honoree, and NAP featured filmmaker Ke Huy Quan for an intimate conversation celebrating his new book Never Say Die: A Memoir. Book signing to follow.

Born in Vietnam, Quan spent a year in a refugee camp before arriving as a refugee in the United States in 1979. Shortly after, he earned breakout roles in Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom and The Goonies before stepping away from acting to work behind the scenes in film production and stunt choreography. His acclaimed return performance in Everything Everywhere All at Once earned him an Academy Award, Golden Globe, Critics Choice Award, and Screen Actors Guild Award for Best Supporting Actor. Quan remains the only Vietnamese actor to win an Oscar.

Special Presentation and Master Class: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom

Nov 1 | 2:00 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Ke Huy Quan made his cinematic debut as the precocious Short Round in Steven Spielberg's 1984 classic Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom. Notorious for its gruesome imagery and outdated Orientalism, the prequel to Raiders of the Lost Ark remains a rollicking blockbuster. Join Quan for a film screening and master class on filmmaking following.

FILM SCREENINGS AND FILMMAKER Q&As

Los Vampires

Oct 26 | 7:45 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 27 | 4:30 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Henry Ian Cusick stars in this meta-horror set in 1930s Hollywood. Carlos Villarías (Cusick) is hired to play Dracula in the Spanish-language production, filming overnight on the same soundstages as the English-language movie featuring Bela Lugosi. Tensions mount as a string of murders on the darkened soundstage begins to blur the line between performance and possession. Los Vampires is in Spanish and English with English subtitles. The October 26 presentation marks the film's U.S. premiere and will be followed by a Q&A with Cusick.

Cusick (b. Peru) is an actor, director, and filmmaker known for his work across screen and stage. Born in Peru, raised in Trinidad and Scotland, and now based in Hawaiʻi, Cusick trained at the Royal Scottish Academy of Music and Drama and began his career as a classical theatre actor. He earned a Primetime Emmy nomination for his turn as Desmond Hume on the serial mystery Lost. His extensive television work includes starring roles in The 100, Scandal, The Passage, and MacGyver. Cusick's short film, Dress, won Best Short Film at the Peace on Earth Film Festival and at HIFF33.

Take Me Home

Oct 24 | 6:00 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 25 | 2:15 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Rooted in the real-life experiences of writer and director Liz Sargent and star Anna Sargent, Take Me Home follows Anna, a Korean American adoptee caring for her aging parents in a Florida suburb. When a devastating heat wave disrupts their fragile routine, Anna, her sister Emily, and their father Bob must confront an uncertain future. This intimate drama explores disability, family, and resilience with compassion and hope. The October 25 screening of Sargent's first feature-length film will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmaker.

Sargent (b. South Korea) is a Korean American adoptee whose award-winning filmmaking examines themes including adoption and family relationships. A writer and director with a background in choreography, she brings a unique visual and emotional sensibility to her storytelling, shaped by her experiences as the middle child of 11 siblings and her intersectional identity. Take Me Home premiered in the U.S. competition section of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where Sargent received the Waldo Salt Screenwriting Award. The film debuted globally at the Berlin International Film Festival, where it was presented as part of the Perspectives Competition.

Sgt. Haane

Oct 23 | 6:30 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 30 | 3:15 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

On April 19, 1943, 28th Māori Battalion soldier Haane Manahi led a daring assault on the fortress of Takrouna in Tunisia, helping change the course of the North African campaign during World War II. Though recommended for the Victoria Cross, the honor was never awarded. Starring Alex Tarrant as Manahi, this powerful film directed by Tearepa Kahi explores courage, sacrifice, and the enduring legacy of a Māori hero whose amazing story continues to inspire generations. Sgt. Haane is in Te Reo Māori with English subtitles. A Q&A with Tarrant will follow the premiere screening.

Tarrant is an Auckland-born actor of Māori, Samoan, and Niuean descent. A graduate of New Zealandʻs national drama school, Te Kura Toi Whakaari O Aotearoa, Tarrant made his international feature debut in Night Raiders. One of the Pacific's most recognizable actors, Tarrant is best known for his lead role as Kai Holman in NCIS: Hawaiʻi, as Valandil in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, and for television roles across New Zealand and Australia.

Big Little Things

Oct 25 | 8:00 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Oct 28 | 3:30 p.m. HST | Consolidated Kahala Theatres, 4211 Waialae Ave, Honolulu, HI 96816

Seeking to appease her seemingly perfect middle-class Chinese family, Lei brings a man home on New Year's Eve to pretend to be her boyfriend. The unexpected appearance of her real girlfriend shatters this carefully constructed facade, and Lei finds herself caught between familial obligation, cultural expectations, and the desire to live authentically. Big Little Things is in Mandarin and Cantonese with English subtitles. HIFF represents Big Little Things' U.S. premiere, as well as Michelle Zhou's first feature-length film. A Q&A with the filmmaker will follow the first screening.

Zhou (b. China) is a Los Angeles-based writer and director whose work explores intimate relationships and shifting power dynamics. Zhou's short film, Fish Eye, won Best Short Film at the 46th USA Film Festival and her screenplay Under the Snow was a Sundance Screenwriters Lab semi-finalist. Her debut feature, Big Little Things, premiered in the Orizzonti section of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. It won the WIP (Work-in-Progress) Activator Market Potential Award at the 62nd Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival and was presented at the 2025 Far East Film Festival as part of Udine's Focus Asia section.

The Vilcek Foundation

The Vilcek Foundation raises awareness of immigrant contributions in the United States and fosters appreciation for the arts and sciences. Established in 2000, the foundation has provided over $17.5 million to individuals and nonprofit organizations in support of this mission.

The Vilcek Foundation is a private operating foundation, a federally tax-exempt nonprofit organization under IRC Section 501(c)(3). To learn more, please visit vilcek.org.

Hawaiʻi International Film Festival

The Hawai'i International Film Festival (HIFF), an Academy Awards®-qualifying festival, celebrates dynamic cinema from Asia and the Pacific while championing Native Hawaiian and Indigenous filmmakers through powerful storytelling and groundbreaking programming.

BROOKLYN, N.Y., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In a powerful celebration of creativity, determination, and the limitless possibilities of the human spirit, 36-year-old Brooklyn native Amanda Ortiz born with Down Syndrome is making her musical debut with the release of Dear Amanda, an original album featuring songs written by Ortiz, with contributions from legendary American singer and songwriter Stephanie Mills.
releases.title: BROOKLYN SONGWRITER AMANDA ORTIZ BORN WITH DOWN SYNDROME RELEASES DEBUT ALBUM DEAR AMANDA
releases.body:
36-year-old songwriter brings her musical dreams to life with contributions from Grammy Award Winning Singer Stephanie Mills

BROOKLYN, N.Y., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In a powerful celebration of creativity, determination, and the limitless possibilities of the human spirit, 36-year-old Brooklyn native Amanda Ortiz born with Down Syndrome is making her musical debut with the release of Dear Amanda, an original album featuring songs written by Ortiz, with contributions from legendary American singer and songwriter Stephanie Mills. 

"Amanda is just a wonderful spirit and it's just amazing that she wrote these beautiful songs. I was on board with this project immediately. I'm raising a child with special needs. My son is 25 now, but I never bought into his disabilities. I think these children are very special," said Grammy Award Winning Singer Stephanie Mills.

In celebration of Down Syndrome Awareness Month, Dear Amanda is a testament to the power of perseverance and the audacity to follow your dreams. "Have faith in yourself, be brave and have the confidence to achieve your life long dreams," says Amanda Ortiz who wrote the songs after completing online courses at the College of Adaptive Arts in California.

Born with down syndrome, Amanda has always been interested in performing largely in part to her grandmother's love of jazz music. Her music is deeply personal and rooted in family influence. Writing and performing is something her grandmother instilled in her early on as a way to help Amanda reconnect with her Hispanic-Italian heritage. 

"She loves learning new things. Ever since she took this song writing class, she exploded," said Amanda's mom Linda Mandracchia. "This is beyond anything I would have expected. I didn't know anything like this would happen. Amanda just said she wants to be in the music business so this is all a surprise to me."

Amanda writes across a wide range of styles and themes, including jazz, Latin, pop, soul, blues, and country, with songs centered on love, grief, nature, joy, seasons , color, music, and dance—all expressed in her own voice.

The album was executive produced by musical composer Ira Antelis, best known for producing music for commercials, records, theater, movies, etc. Antelis has worked with such artists as Marc Anthony, Patti La Belle Christina Aguilera and B.B. King. 

"I think Amanda is an inspiration. The whole idea of people pursuing their dreams is why I was inspired to help bring this project to life," said Ira Antelis.

At a time when conversations surrounding inclusion and representation are more important than ever, Ortiz is helping redefine what is possible for artists with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

releases.title: THE OPTIX NETWORK ANNOUNCES NOVEMBER 1 LAUNCH, INTRODUCING A NEW DESTINATION FOR ORIGINAL ENTERTAINMENT AND INDEPENDENT STORYTELLING
releases.body:
Creator-First Streaming Platform Opens Founding Memberships Ahead of November 16 Premiere of Its First Original Series, House of Ink.

NEW YORK, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Optix Network, a new premium streaming platform dedicated to original entertainment, independent storytelling and creator-focused opportunities, will officially launch November 1, 2026, introducing a fresh entertainment destination for audiences and content creators.

Designed to bring compelling stories and diverse programming to viewers, the platform will feature a growing catalog of original series, feature films and documentaries, with content from independent producers and established studios. Accessible across web, mobile and major connected TV platforms, Optix aims to deliver an entertainment experience that connects audiences with the stories and personalities they love.

"Our vision for The Optix Network extends far beyond launching another streaming service," said an Optix Network spokesperson. "We want to connect audiences with compelling entertainment while creating meaningful opportunities for independent storytellers to share their work, earn from their creativity and build lasting careers."

The network will introduce its first original series, House of Ink, premiering November 16, 2026, marking the beginning of an expanding slate of original programming. The unscripted series brings together familiar personalities Ceaser Emanuel, Sky Days, Spyder, Krystal Morales and Bux, navigating evolving businesses, relationships, personal challenges and new beginnings. Offering audiences an intimate look at ambition, reinvention and life beyond the spotlight, the series marks a new chapter for its cast.

House of Ink is the first of several planned original productions, complementing a broader entertainment library spanning scripted and unscripted series, independent films, feature films and documentary programming.

A NEW MODEL FOR INDEPENDENT CREATORS

Beyond its entertainment offerings, The Optix Network is developing a creator-focused distribution model designed to provide independent filmmakers, producers and production companies with additional opportunities to monetize their work.

Through a combination of licensing arrangements, performance-based royalties and potential profit-sharing opportunities, the platform aims to create new revenue streams for content partners while supporting the long-term growth of independent productions.

Additional founding-member benefits include a digital VIP badge and recognition on the network's Founders Wall. Limited to 5,000 Memberships.

releases.title: ELEC825 TELEVISION PROGRAM 'OUR INFRASTRUCTURE MATTERS' CELEBRATES FIRST-EVER NEW YORK EMMY AWARD NOMINATION
releases.body:
"NJ Roads Are Not Boring" Recognized in Public Affairs – Single Program Category

SPRINGFIELD, N.J., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Our Infrastructure Matters, an internet and television program dedicated to showcasing the people, projects and industries that build and maintain our critical infrastructure, celebrated a major milestone with its first-ever New York Emmy Award nomination.

The program's featured segment, "Method to the Madness: NJ Roads Are Not Boring," was nominated in the Public Affairs – Single Program category, recognizing the television series' commitment to telling compelling stories about infrastructure and the skilled union workforce behind it.

The nomination was celebrated at the New York Emmy Awards ceremony held on October 10, 2026. While the program did not take home the award, earning a nomination alongside some of the region's leading television productions represents a significant achievement for the series and its production team.

"Receiving our first New York Emmy nomination is an incredible honor and a testament to the hard work and creativity of everyone involved in producing Our Infrastructure Matters," said Executive Producer Michael Makarski. "Our mission has always been to shine a spotlight on the skilled men and women who build, maintain and modernize the infrastructure we depend on every day. This recognition reinforces the importance of telling their stories."

The nominated segment, "NJ Roads Are Not Boring," takes viewers behind the scenes of New Jersey's transportation infrastructure, highlighting the engineering, innovation and skilled labor required to build and maintain the state's complex roadway network.

Through engaging storytelling and firsthand perspectives, the segment demonstrates that the roads millions of residents travel each day are anything but ordinary — representing the expertise, dedication and craftsmanship of the professionals responsible for keeping New Jersey moving.

"This nomination is particularly meaningful because infrastructure is something most people take for granted," added ELEC825 Director Mark Longo. "The goal of the program is to bring these projects to life, showcase the extraordinary work happening across New Jersey and give viewers a greater appreciation for the union workforce that quietly makes it all possible."

Presented by the New York Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences (NATAS), the New York Emmy Awards recognize excellence in television and digital media production throughout the region.

The historic nomination marks an exciting new chapter for Our Infrastructure Matters, reinforcing the program's commitment to educating the public about infrastructure investment, workforce development and the vital contributions of organized labor.

About Our Infrastructure Matters

Our Infrastructure Matters is a television and web program dedicated to highlighting the people, projects and investments that strengthen New Jersey's infrastructure. Through original feature stories, the program showcases the skilled Operating Engineer union workforce, innovative technologies and critical infrastructure projects that support the region's economy and quality of life.

Our Infrastructure Matters airs Saturdays & Sundays on News12 NJ+ and can be found online at https://www.youtube.com/@OurInfrastructureMatters or on https://tristateinfrastructurenews.com.

releases.body:
"LIVE FROM YEONNAM : HYUKOH" Brings Together Artists, Grassroots Venues and Local Communities in Seoul

  • Held on October 11 in Seoul's Yeonnam-dong neighborhood, featuring live performances, a block party and a music flea market
  • Brought together grassroots music venues, artists and local creatives as part of Marshall's global KEEP LIVE MUSIC ALIVE campaign
  • Drew an estimated peak attendance of approximately 1,350 visitors, bringing Marshall's MADE OF LOUD brand philosophy to the local live music scene

SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Marshall successfully concluded "LIVE FROM YEONNAM : HYUKOH," held on October 11 at Channel 1969 and the nearby Dongjin Market parking area in Seoul's Yeonnam-dong neighborhood. The event featured live performances by HYUKOH and other artists, alongside a music flea market and block party, highlighting the local venues and communities that contribute to live music culture.

"LIVE FROM YEONNAM : HYUKOH" was held as part of Marshall's global KEEP LIVE MUSIC ALIVE (KLMA) campaign. The initiative supports grassroots music venues and local music communities where emerging artists and new music cultures take shape, helping create an environment in which live music can continue to thrive. Through the event, Marshall brought together artists, venue operators, local creatives and audiences to share in the experience of live music.

Channel 1969, one of the event's main venues, is a grassroots live music venue that has worked with Marshall since the early stages of its local music initiatives in Korea. The venue hosted live performances by OYSTERS, SAILORHONEYMOON, Tiger Disco and HYUKOH. Meanwhile, the nearby Dongjin Market parking area hosted a music flea market and block party, with performances from Channel 1969 livestreamed to the outdoor space so visitors could enjoy the music both inside and outside the venue.

According to on-site attendance estimates, the event attracted up to approximately 1,350 visitors. Around 150 audience members attended the live performances at Channel 1969, while attendance at the Dongjin Market area increased after 6 p.m., reaching its highest level between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. The event demonstrated how live music experiences can extend beyond a single venue to engage a wider range of local spaces and communities.

The event also marked the first local activation in Korea to bring Marshall's MADE OF LOUD brand philosophy to life following its introduction earlier this year. MADE OF LOUD reflects Marshall's longstanding connection to live music, artists, venues and music communities. Through this platform, Marshall is reinforcing its commitment to music culture and the people behind it, extending its role beyond consumer audio products.

"Marshall has stood alongside artists, music venues and music lovers for more than 60 years," said Issei Iimura, Head of Marketing, Korea, at Marshall. "Guided by the philosophy of MADE OF LOUD, we will continue to spotlight and support the people and places where live music begins and grows."

Following the Yeonnam-dong event, Marshall plans to expand its LIVE FROM series to other locations, music genres and online and offline communities. The series will form part of Marshall's continued KEEP LIVE MUSIC ALIVE activities, through which the brand aims to strengthen its collaboration with grassroots venues, artists and local music communities across Korea.

ABOUT MARSHALL GROUP

Marshall Group is the audio, tech and design powerhouse uniting musicians and music lovers through genre-breaking innovation. Marshall is uniquely positioned with over 60 years of rock 'n' roll attitude on stage, at home and on the go. Our iconic products are brought to life by a dedicated team of 800 passionate employees and sold in over 90 markets worldwide.

ABOUT MARSHALL AMPLIFY 

Marshall Amplify is Marshall's initiative to support grassroots music. Through the initiative, Marshall commits an amount equal to 1% of member purchases on marshall.com, starting with grassroots music venues. Learn more at marshall.com/amplify.

BILLERICA, Mass., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- E Ink, a pioneer and leading global developer of ePaper technology, today announced a partnership with FUJIFILM Imaging Systems Co., Ltd. to establish a large-format color ePaper signage business, initially targeting the railway sector. Upon successful completion of prototype assessments, the companies will begin introducing select sizes in 2027.

ePaper is increasingly turned to as an alternative display medium in the railway industry, especially due to labor shortages and the rising costs associated with printing, transporting, installing, and disposing of traditional paper posters.

E Ink and Fujifilm Imaging Systems will combine E Ink's ePaper technology with Fujifilm Imaging Systems' established railway-sector business foundation, implementation capabilities, and operational expertise. Together, the companies plan to provide end-to-end support for large-format color ePaper signage, spanning customer proposals, installation, and ongoing operation.

The details regarding the full-color ePaper sizes and release dates are as follows:

  • 55-inch E Ink Marquee
    • Prototype Release: December 2026
    • Mass-Production Release: March 2027
  • B1-size E Ink Marquee
    • Prototype Release: October 2027
    • Mass-Production Release: January 2028

"We see significant opportunity for E Ink's ePaper to replace traditional print posters in Japan's transportation industry, particularly as our large-format and color capabilities continue to advance," said JM Hung, President of E Ink Holdings. "With the visibility of print and the flexibility of digital updates, ePaper helps organizations streamline content changes, reduce printing and material waste, and deliver timely information using very little power."

"Fujifilm Imaging Systems' expertise in imaging, printing, color management, and quality control strongly complements E Ink's pioneering leadership in ePaper technology," said Takashi Toyofuku, Director at FUJIFILM Imaging Systems. "By bringing together these capabilities and our established customer relationships, we are well positioned to accelerate the adoption of large-format ePaper—beginning with railway advertising and signage and expanding over time into other industries throughout Japan."

Its low-power displays enable customers to reach their sustainability goals, and E Ink has pledged using 100% renewable energy in 2030 and reaching net zero carbon emissions by 2040. E Ink has been recognized for its efforts by receiving validation from Science-Based Targets (SBTi) and is listed in both the DJSI World and DJSI Emerging Indexes and is listed in Taiwan's Taipei Exchange (TPEx) and the Luxembourg market. releases.title: Space Nuclear Power Corporation Awarded DARPA Agreement for Ground Test of Autonomous Nuclear Reactor Controller
releases.body:
Other Transaction Agreement to advance active reactor control through a follow-on ground test of Kilopower reactor technology

LOS ALAMOS, N.M., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Space Nuclear Power Corporation (SpaceNukes) announced today that the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has awarded the company an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under the Fast Capacitance (Fat Cat) program. Managed by Dr. Tabitha Dodson in DARPA's Defense Sciences Office, the Fat Cat program seeks to advance autonomous reactor operation for national security missions. The contract supports development and ground testing of advanced reactor control technologies that extend the demonstrated capability of American nuclear power.

The award extends a continuous line of nuclear power development and builds directly on SpaceNukes' successful nuclear power demonstration heritage. In 2018, key members of the SpaceNukes team, while employed by Los Alamos National Laboratory and NASA, performed the foundational Kilopower Reactor Using Stirling Technology (KRUSTY) work — conducting the only full-power ground test of a new American space reactor in five decades. Under the current agreement, SpaceNukes and Los Alamos National Laboratory will design, build, and conduct a follow-on nuclear ground test of a Kilopower reactor incorporating active control rod operation—an advancement beyond the passively controlled architecture demonstrated in the 2018 KRUSTY test.

"This award recognizes the maturity and continuity of the team that designed, built, and tested KRUSTY in 2018," said Patrick McClure, COO of SpaceNukes. "We are proud to work alongside Dr. Dodson and Los Alamos National Laboratory to deliver the next demonstrated step in American nuclear power."

The phased program structure includes design, procurement, and integration gates leading to the ground demonstration, producing both nuclear-tested hardware and the engineering basis for autonomous, actively-controlled reactor operation. Integration work will be conducted at SpaceNukes' workshop in Medina, Ohio, led by Chief Engineer Marc Gibson. The work positions American industry to provide reliable nuclear power across a broader range of mission profiles, including those requiring dynamic power management and rapid response under varying operational conditions.

"There is no substitute for demonstrated technology when American national security objectives are at stake," said Andy Phelps, CEO of SpaceNukes. "This award lets us advance the work begun in the KRUSTY program and bring another tested capability forward for the nation."

About Space Nuclear Power Corporation (SpaceNukes)

Space Nuclear Power Corporation was founded on the belief that nuclear power is essential to our future, both on Earth and in space. The company's goal is to enable the successful deployment of fission reactors in space. SpaceNukes brings together the core engineering and program management team behind the foundational KRUSTY demonstration in 2018. David Poston (CTO) and Patrick McClure (COO) performed this work at Los Alamos National Laboratory; Marc Gibson (Chief Engineer) led the program at NASA Glenn Research Center. The team is joined by Omar Mireles (formerly NASA Marshall Space Flight Center) and Andy Phelps (CEO). SpaceNukes holds a license from Los Alamos National Laboratory for the Kilopower technology and operates from headquarters in Los Alamos, New Mexico, and workshops in Los Alamos with additive 3D printing and in Medina, Ohio, with thermal and vacuum capabilities.

releases.title: Parks Associates: 39% of US Internet Households Watch Live Events or Sports Through On-Demand Streaming Services
releases.body:
45% of pay-TV subscribers use pay TV to access live video, while 25% of US internet households use FAST services

PLANO, Texas, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Parks Associates' research The New Live TV Model: Skinny Bundles, Sports, News finds 39% of US internet households watch live events or sports through an on-demand streaming service, showing the growing role of streaming services in delivering live programming. The expanding mix of options to watch video is changing how consumers find and watch sports, news, and events, as live video viewing is no longer synonymous with pay TV.

Parks Associates research also finds:

  • 25% watch live video through free ad-supported television (FAST) services.
  • 21% report they don't watch live video at all.

"Consumers value live content but struggle to find and access it," said Michael Goodman, Director, Entertainment Research, Parks Associates. "The challenge for providers is making live content accessible. Sports is a good example, with programming now distributed across multiple services and platforms."

Consumer interest in live sports is growing alongside broad-appeal entertainment. According to Parks Associates consumer research, comedy (60%), drama (56%), and news (50%) are the most popular content categories, while 48% report watching live sports. Subscription VOD (SVOD) services continue to add sports, news, and live events while FAST services build engagement through curated linear channels.

"Competition for viewers is increasingly about more than the content itself," Goodman said. "Providers need to deliver an experience that makes it easy for consumers to find, access, and move between live and on-demand programming."

Parks Associates will host Future of Video: Business of Streaming on November 17-18 at Marina del Rey, California, sponsored by Adeia, InterDigital, OTT.X, and TheDesk.net. Future of Video provides insight into successful OTT strategy deployments, challenges for pay-TV providers, and the role of connected CE in the growth of video viewing, new content formats, and the overall impact to the video market.

releases.title: WayUp Launches New Mobile App, Giving Students and Recent Grads a Faster Way to Catch Entry-Level Roles Before They Fill Up
releases.body:
CHICAGO, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- WayUp, the job search and recruiting marketplace built exclusively for college students and early-career job seekers, today announced the launch of its redesigned mobile app for iOS and Android. The app sends real-time alerts the moment a followed company posts a new internship or entry-level role, and lets candidates apply using the resume, education, and experience already saved to their WayUp profile, removing the need to rebuild an application from scratch for every role.

The launch comes as the market for early-career hires has tightened measurably: recent-college-graduate unemployment reached roughly 5.6% in the second quarter of 2026, among the highest readings in a decade outside the pandemic, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. With fewer no-experience entry-level openings available and employers moving quickly once applications start arriving, how fast a candidate sees and acts on a posting has become a meaningful factor in getting noticed.

"Right now, nearly half of entry-level jobs that used to require zero experience have disappeared, and recent grad unemployment just hit its highest point in a decade outside the pandemic," said Amy Farr-Jones, VP Growth at WayUp. "Students aren't losing out because they're not qualified—they're losing out because they see the role three days too late. We built the new WayUp app so the moment a great entry-level role opens, the right person sees it first and can move on it immediately."

releases.title: New Survey Data Shows AI Reshaping College and Career Plans
releases.body:
HelloCollege data shows widespread AI use in coursework, rising career anxiety and shifting views on majors and degrees

OAK BROOK, Ill., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HelloCollege today released findings from its 2026 College Student AI Survey, showing that AI is already shaping how college students learn, plan and think about their futures. The survey found that 66% of current college students are more concerned about their future career because of AI, 50% say AI has changed how they understand the use of a college degree and 82% use AI in their coursework.

The findings suggest students are not just experimenting with AI. They are incorporating it into everyday academic life while also weighing what it could mean for the long-term value of higher education. As AI becomes more common in the classroom, students are asking bigger questions about whether a degree will still deliver the career security and return on investment they expected.

That uncertainty is already influencing decision-making. More than 1 in 3 (37%) students say they are shifting their career plans around AI, showing AI is changing not only how students complete their work but also how they choose their path forward.

"AI is not some far-off thing for students," said Kevin Krebs, founder and CEO of HelloCollege. "It is already part of how they study, how they search for colleges and how they think about what comes after graduation. What this survey shows is that students see the value in AI, but they are also getting nervous about where they fit in. They are asking real questions about which majors still make sense, which careers feel safer and whether a college degree is going to give them the kind of return they expected in a job market that is changing fast."

Student sentiment in the survey reflects that uncertainty. Over half (58%) of college students believe AI is not a net good for society, with the biggest concerns being mass layoffs, difficulty telling truth from fiction, data privacy, learning loss and mass surveillance.

At the same time, students see potential upside, with 25% saying their biggest hope for AI is better work conditions through automation, followed by more free time and new fields of employment.

HelloCollege's full 2026 College Student AI Survey findings and methodology are available at www.sayhellocollege.com/blog/college-students-using-ai-statistics/. To learn more about HelloCollege or speak with a college counselor, visit sayhellocollege.com.

About HelloCollege

Founded in 2012 by Northwestern University alum and first-generation college graduate Kevin Krebs, HelloCollege is a national college counseling firm helping families navigate the admissions process with confidence. Through private counseling, workshops, and free resources, the company offers a team-based approach to college counseling, tutoring, essay coaching, and financial aid strategy. HelloCollege has guided more than 5,700 students to top universities and educated over 50,000 families nationwide, and it has been recognized by Forbes Advisor as one of the Best College Admissions Consultants of 2026 and rated Excellent on Trustpilot.

releases.title: The most powerful superconducting magnet ever flown to space, made with Faraday Factory HTS tape, launches aboard Starburst-1
releases.body:
Zenno Astronautics' breakthrough magnetic technology incorporates special high temperature superconducting tape developed by Faraday Factory Japan

TOKYO, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Faraday Factory Japan celebrates the successful launch of Zenno Astronautics' largest Supertorquer to date aboard Portal Space Systems' Starburst-1. The Almighty Magnet is the world's most powerful magnetic actuator ever built and flown to space. The launch took place aboard SpaceX's Falcon 9 Bandwagon-5 mission on October 20, 2026.

Developed and engineered by Zenno, Supertorquer uses advanced superconducting magnet technology to generate powerful magnetic interactions with Earth's magnetic field. Faraday Factory has supplied specially customized high temperature superconducting (HTS) tape to meet Zenno's demanding performance requirements for this pioneering space application.

The development of superconducting space technologies represents a major opportunity to transform how spacecraft operate and interact in orbit. High temperature superconductor magnets enable exceptionally strong magnetic fields while minimizing energy consumption, paving the way for compact, powerful, and energy-efficient space systems. Since partnering in 2024, Faraday Factory and Zenno have steadily accelerated this work.

"Almighty Magnet is opening the door to a whole new set of capabilities in space, from mass drivers and magnetic radiation shields to advanced satellite mobility. We're building and flying the superconducting technology that makes this possible, and Faraday Factory Japan is our partner in that effort," said Max Arshavsky, Founder and CEO of Zenno.

"The launch of Starburst-1 marks an important milestone for Faraday Factory, demonstrating the HTS potential to enable some of the most demanding and innovative applications of superconductivity. We strongly support game-changing Zenno's effort to electrify space technologies," said Sergey Lee, Founder and CEO of Faraday Factory Japan.

About Faraday Factory

Faraday Factory Japan runs the largest manufacturing facility of high temperature superconductor (HTS) tape worldwide. Over recent years, the company has delivered more than 10,000 km of HTS tape to hundreds of customers. The company serves a rapidly growing market of HTS tape, which is led by ever increasing demand from fusion energy, power grid, aerospace, railway, healthcare, and other high-tech markets.

www.faradaygroup.com

About Zenno

Zenno develops the most powerful magnetic technologies for space. This is a new class of superconducting systems designed to power the next era of human expansion. Our belief is simple — stable and scalable infrastructure in space will rely on resources already present there.

Zenno is building that future by harnessing one of the fundamental forces of the universe, electromagnetism. Our superconducting technologies enable fuel-free spacecraft positioning, radiation shielding, and electromagnetic acceleration systems for defense, transportation, and industrial activity in space.

releases.body:
Hydrogen power units supplied critical energy to everything from concerts and festivals to major golf tournaments

VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This year, GeoPura, a UK-based hydrogen power provider, recently acquired by Ballard Power Systems (NASDAQ: BLDP) (TSX: BLDP), made hydrogen integral to live entertainment. 

Powered by Ballard fuel cells, Hydrogen Power Units (HPU) deliver reliable electricity while cutting harmful air pollution near stages, production areas and crowds, protecting the health of artists, crews and attendees and improving air quality for surrounding communities. 

The Energy-as-a-Service offering combines equipment, hydrogen supply, transport, on-site storage and operational support, thereby giving organisers a fully managed power solution that meets production standards, while supporting a cleaner, healthier event environment. 

Having powered the HYDRO stage at Boomtown in 2025, GeoPura's HPU2 systems supplied the 20,000-capacity stage throughout the build and live festival in 2026, supporting the sound, lighting and visual production behind performances from Skrillex, Four Tet and Groove Armada. At Edinburgh Summer Sessions, HPUs were used to supply main-stage power and site infrastructure, embedding hydrogen into the delivery of a major concert series. These projects built on previous deployments at American Express presents BST Hyde Park, LIDO Festival and the Isle of Wight Festival. 

In sport, the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands (GeoPura's first continental European golf deployment) received critical power – without CO₂, nitrogen oxides or particulate emissions at the point of use – from hydrogen, which also powered infrastructure at the Genesis Scottish Open.  

This was the summer that saw even more repeat deployments, larger festival commitments and further integration into event power planning. Alongside GeoPura's established work in film, television and live broadcasting, GeoPura provided the combined business with an operating model for expansion into the US, Canada, Europe and wider international markets. 

Andrew Cunningham, President of Ballard, said: "This summer, hydrogen powered the performances, production and infrastructure that major events depended on. Organisers are incorporating it into their plans, returning for subsequent seasons and increasing the scale of their deployments. 

"Boomtown's move from HYDRO to HYDRO XL captures that progress. We're seeing the same shift in film and television, where customers need reliable power on location and want to reduce diesel use, noise and air pollution - clean power has become a requirement across these industries.

"Our ambition is for clean power to become the default across these industries. With Ballard's fuel cell expertise and international reach alongside our hydrogen supply and operational capabilities, we can expand this approach to more customers and markets." 

Marty Neese, Chief Executive Officer of Ballard, said: "GeoPura is already delivering power to customers, supplying the hydrogen and managing the service. Combining these capabilities with Ballard's technology and global reach broadens our offering and creates opportunities to capture value across equipment, fuel and operations. 

"The US and Canada offer exciting potential, from festivals and major sporting events, to film and television production. We can build on our UK experience to develop a complete service for these markets, while selectively expanding across Europe and North America. The same capabilities also serve construction, infrastructure and other customers facing grid constraints, alongside our established business in heavy-duty mobility." 

The combined business aims to make managed hydrogen power a mainstream choice across more sectors and markets. Its growing operations in events and screen production provide a base for international expansion, alongside longer-duration applications in construction, grid support and critical power, where customers need dependable electricity beyond the capacity of existing connections. 

About Ballard

Ballard Power Systems (NASDAQ: BLDP; TSX: BLDP) is a global leader in zero-emission hydrogen energy solutions and an integrated Energy-as-a-Service (EaaS) provider. Together, with its wholly owned subsidiary, GeoPura Ltd., Ballard delivers turnkey, vertically integrated hydrogen ecosystem solutions spanning hydrogen production, logistics, refuelling, zero-emission fuel cell engines, and stationary Hydrogen Power Units.

Ballard powers critical off-grid, stationary applications - including construction, events, film sets, healthcare, defense, temporary power infrastructure, and supplies fuel cell engines for heavy-duty mobility applications such as bus, rail, and marine. With an EaaS model, combined with cutting-edge technology across the hydrogen value chain, Ballard decarbonizes mission-critical operations worldwide. MISSISSAUGA, ON, Oct. 21, 2026 /CNW/ -- The Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) is reinforcing its commitment to holding licence holders accountable following the conviction of Aya Electric Inc. and its owner and Designated Master Electrician, Razi Khan, for their involvement in a permits-for-sale scheme that enabled unlicensed electrical work at homes across Southern Ontario.
releases.title: Licensed Electrical Contractor and Owner Fined $122,000 in Permits-for-Sale Scheme
releases.body:
ESA conviction reinforces serious consequences for licence holders who circumvent electrical safety requirements and put Ontarians at risk.

MISSISSAUGA, ON, Oct. 21, 2026 /CNW/ -- The Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) is reinforcing its commitment to holding licence holders accountable following the conviction of Aya Electric Inc. and its owner and Designated Master Electrician, Razi Khan, for their involvement in a permits-for-sale scheme that enabled unlicensed electrical work at homes across Southern Ontario.

Aya Electric and Khan were fined a combined $122,000 under the Electricity Act, 1998 after an ESA investigation uncovered a paid arrangement in which the company obtained electrical permits for work performed by an unlicensed contractor.

ESA's investigation found that Aya Electric obtained permits for electrical work at six residential properties located in Clarington, Brantford, Milton and Markham. Khan collected payments for the permits while an unlicensed contractor carried out the work. The individual was not employed by Aya Electric, had no electrical qualifications, was not properly insured and worked without supervision from the company or Khan.

In September 2026, Aya Electric and Khan pleaded guilty to offences under the Electricity Act, 1998. The company was fined $92,000 and Khan was fined $30,000 and placed on probation. ESA is currently reviewing the matter and considering whether further administrative action is warranted.

In its sentencing reasons, the Ontario Court of Justice characterized Khan's conduct as deceptive and bordering on fraud, noting that he charged more than twice the cost of an ESA permit. The court considered Khan's licensing status an aggravating factor, recognizing that he understood ESA's permitting process and used that knowledge for financial gain. The court also emphasized the potentially catastrophic consequences of the offences, including fire and loss of life, and the importance of imposing penalties that deter others from circumventing electrical safety requirements.

"Using a licensed business to obtain permits for an unlicensed contractor undermines the protections Ontario's electrical safety requirements provide," said Emily Larose, Vice President of Regulatory and General Counsel, Electrical Safety Authority. "We help licence holders meet their responsibilities, but when those responsibilities are deliberately ignored, we will act. These fines send a strong message that profiting from arrangements that put public safety at risk carries serious consequences."

ESA investigators also observed Khan performing electrical work at a seventh home in Brantford alongside two unlicensed contractors. No electrical permit had been obtained from ESA for that job. As Aya Electric's Designated Master Electrician, Khan was responsible for planning and supervising electrical work carried out on the company's behalf.

"A Licensed Electrical Contractor's licence cannot be rented, loaned or used to legitimize unlicensed electrical work," said Sarah Kempel, Director of Licensing, Electrical Safety Authority. "Obtaining permits for work that is being performed by an unlicensed contractor represents a deliberate disregard for Ontario's licensing framework and the accountability that comes with holding a licence."

Help protect your community: report electrical safety concerns

By law, only Licensed Electrical Contractors (LECs) can be hired to perform electrical work in Ontario homes and businesses. If you suspect unlicensed electrical work or a Licensed Electrical Contractor failing to meet their responsibilities, report your concerns to ESA. Reports can be submitted anonymously, but the more details you provide, the better equipped ESA is to investigate and take action.

Report suspicious electrical activity: Visit ESAsafe.com/ReportAContractor.

Verify a Licensed Electrical Contractor: Before hiring someone to do electrical work in your home, ask for their seven-digit ECRA/ESA electrical contractor licence number and check it at FindaContractor.ESAsafe.com.

If hiring a general contractor, confirm they use an LEC for electrical work. An electrician's qualifications or a Master Electrician's licence alone are not sufficient.

About the Electrical Safety Authority

The Electrical Safety Authority's (ESA's) role is to improve public electrical safety in Ontario. ESA is an administrative authority responsible for administering specific regulations under the Electricity Act, 1998 (Part VIII) related to the Ontario Electrical Safety Code, the licensing of Electrical Contractors and Master Electricians, electricity distribution system safety, and electrical product safety. ESA works extensively with stakeholders throughout the province on education, training and promotion to foster electrical safety across the province.

More information on the Electrical Safety Authority can be found at ESAsafe.com, through Facebook, X and on LinkedIn.

releases.title: Rockwell Automation Introduces FactoryTalk Conductor, an AI-Native Orchestration Platform for Industrial Automation
releases.body:
New software connects AI agents, skills and workflows across the automation lifecycle

MILWAUKEE, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rockwell Automation, Inc. (NYSE: ROK), the world's largest company dedicated to industrial automation and digital transformation, today announced the introduction of FactoryTalk® Conductor™, a new AI-native orchestration platform designed to coordinate AI-powered work across the industrial automation lifecycle, creating a foundation for AI-enabled workflows from system design through operation and maintenance. The software will make its public debut at Automation Fair® 2026 in Boston, where attendees will receive an exclusive first look ahead of its planned commercial availability in the first quarter of 2027.

According to Rockwell Automation's 2026 State of Smart Manufacturing Report, one-third of manufacturing operations are already AI-augmented, with adoption expected to accelerate in the years ahead. As manufacturers move from AI experimentation to broader deployment, they need practical ways to connect technology, workflows and expertise. FactoryTalk Conductor is designed to meet that need through a single platform that brings AI together across engineering environments.

"The next phase of industrial AI will be defined by orchestration rather than individual copilots," said Craig Resnick, Vice President, ARC Advisory Group. "Manufacturers need AI technologies that can coordinate tasks across software systems, engineering tools and operational data. FactoryTalk Conductor reflects the industry's evolution toward agentic automation by bringing AI agents, workflows and industrial expertise together in a unified environment."

FactoryTalk Conductor enables users to initiate engineering tasks using natural language and intelligently connects the software, AI capabilities and workflows needed to complete them. At launch, the platform will integrate with Studio 5000 Logix Designer®, Logix Echo™, Emulate3D® and FactoryTalk® Optix™, providing coverage across key design, development, simulation and testing workflows. Additional integrations across Rockwell Automation's software portfolio, including FactoryTalk® Design Studio™, FactoryTalk® Historian, Plex® and Fiix®, are planned to follow, expanding AI-powered workflows across the industrial automation lifecycle.

"What makes FactoryTalk Conductor unique is the combination of AI orchestration and trusted industrial expertise," said Matheus Bulho, senior vice president, software & control, Rockwell Automation. "Customers can leverage Rockwell Automation-verified agents and skills, create capabilities tailored to their business, and connect AI across software, data and services. This creates a scalable foundation for accelerating engineering work while maintaining the standards required in industrial environments."

Key benefits include:

  • Supporting enterprise AI and governance requirements, giving organizations the flexibility to leverage FactoryTalk Hub-hosted AI services or connect their preferred large or small language models, including locally hosted open-weight models that can help reduce ongoing token consumption costs.
  • Accelerating engineering workflows across the automation lifecycle by coordinating activities across design, development, testing and verification environments.
  • Reducing complexity across software applications by enabling AI-powered workflows that span Studio 5000 Logix Designer, Logix Echo, Emulate3D, FactoryTalk Optix and other Rockwell Automation solutions.
  • Applying AI with greater confidence and reliability through Rockwell Automation-developed integrations that connect software, data and services across industrial operations.
  • Extending trusted automation expertise through Rockwell Automation-verified agents and skills, helping teams accelerate work with capabilities purpose-built for industrial applications.

Manufacturers attending Automation Fair 2026 will be able to experience FactoryTalk Conductor demonstrations across multiple show floor experiences, including Technology & Services Showcase, Industry Pavillion, Innovations, as well as dedicated technical sessions.

Additional information about FactoryTalk Conductor and Automation Fair can be found at www.rockwellautomation.com.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is FactoryTalk Conductor?

FactoryTalk Conductor is an AI-native orchestration platform that connects AI agents, skills, workflows and automation software to help engineers accelerate system design, development and testing activities through natural language interactions and trusted industrial expertise.

How is FactoryTalk Conductor different from an AI copilot?

While traditional AI copilots assist with individual tasks, FactoryTalk Conductor enables multiple AI agents, workflows and software tools to work together across engineering processes. This enables broader automation of complex, multi-step activities that span applications, data sources and teams.

When will FactoryTalk Conductor be available?

FactoryTalk Conductor will be previewed at Automation Fair 2026 in Boston and is expected to be commercially available in the first quarter of 2027.

What Rockwell Automation products can FactoryTalk Conductor work with?

FactoryTalk Conductor is designed to work across a growing portfolio of Rockwell Automation software. At launch, it will support Studio 5000 Logix Designer®, Logix Echo™, Emulate3D® and FactoryTalk® Optix™, with additional integrations planned for FactoryTalk® Design Studio™, FactoryTalk® Historian, Plex®, Fiix® and other solutions over time.

Can customers create and deploy their own AI agents and skills?

Yes. In addition to Rockwell Automation-verified agents and skills, customers can create and deploy their own agents and skills to support company standards, industry requirements and unique engineering workflows

About Rockwell Automation

Rockwell Automation, Inc. (NYSE: ROK), is a global leader in industrial automation and digital transformation. We connect the imaginations of people with the potential of technology to expand what is humanly possible, making the world more productive and more sustainable. Headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Rockwell Automation employs approximately 26,000 problem solvers dedicated to our customers in more than 100 countries. To learn more about how we are bringing the Connected Enterprise® to life across industrial enterprises, visit www.rockwellautomation.com.

releases.body:
ST. LOUIS, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Parents as Teachers National Center announced today that it has been named as a Finalist in two categories: Podcast Show in Content & Media, Education, Art & Culture and Podcast Episode in Content & Media, Health, in The 6th Annual Anthem Awards.

Anthem Winners are selected by the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences. Judges for the 6th Annual Anthem Awards include an esteemed panel of leaders from leading organizations and companies dedicated to social impact, including Nancy Brown, CEO, American Heart Association, Heather Malenshek, CMO, Land O'Lakes, Inc., Jesse Tyler Ferguson, Award-Winning Actor & LGBTQ+ Advocate, Patrice Duckworth, Chief Inclusion Officer, Johnson & Johnson, Fatima Graves, President & CEO, National Women's Law Center, Justina Nixon-Saintil, Vice President & Global Chief Impact Officer, IBM, and many others.

"We're thrilled to see the impact sector bounce back, share their stories, and expand their impact after a challenging year last year," said Anthem Awards General Manager, Patricia McLoughlin. "This year's Finalists are truly setting the standard for how to advocate for a cause, inspire action, create impact, and overall make this world a better place."

The Parents as Teachers Podcast highlights experts and practitioners in the field of early childhood home visiting to share insight about supporting families during a child's earliest years. The show offers perspectives from diverse backgrounds to inform and enhance awareness across topics including early relational health, maternal and infant health, social support, and more.

Featured guests include leaders and professionals from Columbia University, Washington University in St. Louis, the Institute for the Advancement of Family Support Professionals, and more. The episode, recognized as a finalist, highlights the voices of a Parents as Teachers parent educator and mother, Christy Roberts, alongside her son, Will, an artist and speaker who is autistic.

"Every family has a story, and every voice has the power to inspire change," said Constance Gully, President and CEO of Parents as Teachers National Center. "Our podcast amplifies the voices and experiences of those working alongside families every day, sparking important conversations about early childhood development, maternal health, and family well-being. We believe these conversations have the power to inspire change and help every child get the strong start they deserve, and it's an honor to receive this recognition from the Anthem Awards."

Alongside the Finalist Announcement comes the launch of Anthem Community Voice in Partnership with NationBuilder, an annual voting campaign and celebration to uplift the work of Anthem Finalists. Supporters can celebrate the work of the Parents as Teachers Podcast online from October 13th to October 29th at celebrate.anthemawards.com. All Finalists are also in the running to win a Gold, Silver, or Bronze Anthem Award selected by Anthem judges. All Winners for the 6th Annual Anthem Awards will be announced on November 5, 2026.

About Parents as Teachers:

Parents as Teachers creates strong communities, thriving families, and children who are healthy, safe, and learning by matching parents and caregivers with trained professionals for regular personal home visits during a child's earliest years, from pregnancy through kindergarten. With over 188,000 families served in all 50 U.S. states, 127 Tribal organizations, and six other countries, the Parents as Teachers evidence-based home visiting model is backed by over 40 years of research-proven outcomes for children and families. Annually, Parents as Teachers National Center supports over 10,000 professionals and partners with more than 2,000 organizations, including school systems, social service nonprofits, health departments, tribal organizations, and military installations.

About The Anthem Awards:

Launched in 2021 by The Webby Awards, The Anthem Awards recognizes impactful brands, nonprofits, and individuals that are setting the standard for good worldwide. The Anthem Awards honors work across seven core causes: Belonging & Inclusion; Education, Art & Culture; Health; Human & Civil Rights; Humanitarian Action & Services; Sustainability, Environment & Climate; and Technology. This season's partners and sponsors include NationBuilder, Sustainable Brands, NationSwell, The Bloom, the Social Innovation Summit and The Nonprofit Alliance. The Awards were founded in partnership with the Ad Council, Born This Way Foundation, Feeding America, GLAAD, Mozilla, NAACP, NRDC, WWF, and XQ.

About The Webby Awards:

Hailed as the "Internet's highest honor" by The New York Times, The Webby Awards is the leading international awards organization honoring excellence on the Internet, including Websites and Mobile Sites; Video & Film; Advertising, Media & PR; Apps, Software & Immersive; Social; Podcasts; Games; Creators and AI. Established in 1996, The Webby Awards received over 13,000 entries from all 50 states and over 70 countries worldwide this year. The Webby Awards are presented by the International Academy of Digital Arts and Sciences (IADAS). Sponsors and Partners of The Webby Awards include Adobe, WP Engine, Patreon, ElevenLabs, Framer, Meta, NAACP, KPMG, The Wall Street Journal, Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter, SXSW, The Podcast Show, and Authentic.

In the news release, IAB Opens Public Comment on New Guide to Inform Cross-Channel Measurement Decisions, issued 20-Oct-2026 by Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that the link at the end of the release has been updated. The complete, corrected release follows:

IAB Opens Public Comment on New Guide to Inform Cross-Channel Measurement Decisions

New "Project Eidos" Output Gives Marketers a Decision-First Approach to Interpreting and Applying MMM, Incrementality, and Attribution Results

Public Comment Open Through November 4, 2026

NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade organization for the digital advertising ecosystem, today announced the release of its Cross-Channel Measurement Decision Guide for public comment. Developed as part of Project Eidos, the guide advances IAB's work to help marketers use cross-channel measurement evidence to make better-informed investment and optimization decisions. Public comment is open through November 4, 2026.

The guide gives marketers, agency teams, and measurement partners a decision-first approach to selecting, interpreting, and applying evidence from methods like Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), incrementality testing, and attribution, including when their findings appear to tell conflicting stories. Rather than starting with whatever metrics happen to be available, it starts with the business decision at hand and works backward to the evidence best suited to inform it.

"Measurement only works if the industry has confidence in the answers it produces, and right now, MMM, incrementality, and attribution can each tell a different story about the same campaign," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "This guide doesn't ask marketers to pick a winner among those methods. It gives them a disciplined way to work through the options and make an informed decision they can trust. That's exactly the kind of foundational work Project Eidos was built to do."

The guide has three connected parts:

  • The Decision Guide: Lays out a decision-first sequence, from business outcome to decision, measurement question, measurement approach, evidence, interpretation, and action
  • The Decision Navigator: Applies that sequence to common decisions, such as allocating budget across channels or assessing whether an investment is creating incremental value, and helps readers determine which methods fit the question and how to weigh the evidence
  • The Measurement Reference Library: Brings together existing metric definitions and supporting context to help readers interpret the evidence used in the Decision Guide and Decision Navigator

"We built this to be used, not just read," said Matt Shapo, Senior Director, Measurement, IAB. "The real test is whether it holds up in an actual planning conversation, like when a channel reports a strong attributed ROAS that an incrementality test doesn't back up. That's exactly the kind of scenario we want the industry weighing in on before we finalize it."

IAB is especially seeking feedback on whether the guide reflects real-world measurement decisions, whether its method-fit and interpretation guidance holds up when results conflict, and whether its scenarios are realistic enough for day-to-day planning. The release directly supports IAB's mission to drive growth, trust, and innovation across the digital advertising ecosystem.

"Marketers rely on measurement to make consequential investment decisions, but they don't always feel confident that their approaches deliver the evidence they need," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "60–75% of marketers say advanced measurement falls short across key dimensions such as rigor, timeliness, trust, and efficiency, and this guide helps them connect evidence from different measurement approaches to the decision at hand. It also helps them understand what the findings can support, and identify where additional testing or calibration is needed. That gives brands and their partners a stronger foundation for putting measurement into action."

The public comment period is open from October 20, 2026 through November 4, 2026. To review the Cross-Channel Measurement Decision Guide and submit feedback, click https://www.iab.com/guidelines/cross-channel-measurement-guide-open-for-15-day-public-comment/

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. The trade group fields critical research on interactive advertising, while also educating brands, agencies, and the wider business community on the importance of digital marketing. In affiliation with the IAB Tech Lab, IAB develops technical standards and solutions. IAB is committed to professional development and elevating the knowledge, skills, expertise, and collaboration of the workforce across the industry. Through the work of its public policy office in Washington, D.C., the trade association advocates for its members and promotes the value of the interactive advertising industry to legislators and policymakers. Founded in 1996, IAB is headquartered in New York City.
