NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- XGIMI, a global leader in premium smart projection and home entertainment, today announces the official launch of its AURA 3 Series, a new generation of ultra-short-throw (UST) laser TVs first showcased at IFA 2026. Built around XGIMI's vision of Living Room Cinema, the series combines advanced projection technology, cinematic picture quality, and high-performance gaming for modern living spaces.

Building on the iris technology first introduced in the TITAN Noir Series, the AURA 3 Series features XGIMI's Dual Dynamic Iris system, delivering native contrast of up to 8,000:1 for deeper blacks and more nuanced shadow detail. With up to 5,700 ISO lumens of brightness, an RGB triple-laser light source, premium cinematic format support, and 4K 120Hz high-refresh-rate support, the series brings together vivid picture quality and smooth performance for movies, live sports, and gaming.

With a 0.163:1 ultra-short-throw ratio, the AURA 3 Series projects a 120-inch image from approximately 8 inches away, with screen sizes reaching up to 200 inches. This space-saving design delivers a cinema-scale viewing experience without requiring a ceiling-mounted projector or a dedicated home theater room.

Engineered for Cinematic Picture Quality and Gaming

The AURA 3 Series combines advanced light control and RGB triple-laser technology to deliver premium large-screen entertainment. Key features of the flagship AURA 3 Max include:

  • Up to 5,700 ISO Lumens for bright, vivid images
  • Up to 8,000:1 Native Contrast with Dual Dynamic Iris
  • X-VISION AI Image Processor
  • Built-in Google TV
  • Dolby Vision®, HDR10+, HLG, IMAX Enhanced & Filmmaker Mode
  • Anti-RBE technology for reduced rainbow effect in both 2D and 3D
  • Cinematic 3D with two pairs of 3D glasses included
  • 80W Harman Kardon speakers with Dolby Atmos
  • 4K at 120Hz, with VRR, ALLM, and AMD FreeSync Premium for smoother, more responsive gameplay. The high refresh rate also helps reduce the perceived rainbow effect (RBE), contributing to a more comfortable viewing experience.

From cinematic movies and live sports to fast-paced gaming, the AURA 3 Series brings versatile, big-screen entertainment into everyday living spaces.

Exclusive Kickstarter Pricing and Bundle Options

The AURA 3 Series launches on Kickstarter with two models at exclusive introductory prices:

Shipping is expected to begin in December 2026 for the AURA 3 Series projectors, followed by fixed ALR screens in January 2027 and XGIMI Ascend floor-rising screens in February 2027.

releases.title: Podcast Host and Former Navy SEAL Shawn Ryan Teams Up with SIG SAUER to Donate Firearms and Emergency Kits to Local Sheriff's Department
releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shawn Ryan, former Navy SEAL and host of "The Shawn Ryan Show," has partnered with the SIG SAUER Charitable Foundation to donate essential firearms and equipment to the Hickman County Sheriff's Department. Ryan and the SIG Team presented the donation in person yesterday alongside local county sheriff's deputies, the mayor, and city council members.

Driven by a mission to support law enforcement, Ryan acted after learning the department was facing severe budget constraints and utilizing equipment over 25 years old.

"How are these men and women supposed to protect our community if they're not properly equipped?" said Ryan. "As a Tennessee resident, I knew I needed to step in and help support our local community."

"When Shawn brought the Hickman County Sheriff's Department to our attention, we knew we had to help," said Jason Wright, VP of Marketing at SIG SAUER. "This initiative aligns perfectly with the SIG SAUER Charitable Foundation's mission, and we are proud to partner with Shawn to make it happen."

The donation equips the department with 30 SIG SAUER M400 rifles, ROMEO5 electro-optics, SLX suppressors, and FOXTROT-MSR compact mounted lights. Additionally, the department will receive top-of-the-line emergency kits to ensure officers are prepared for critical situations. At the event, SIG SAUER announced they will provide advanced rifle training for the department as well.

To learn more about Shawn Ryan, visit his podcast at shawnryanshow.com and follow him on social media. Additional information on the SIG SAUER Charitable Foundation is available at sigsauer.com.

For media inquiries or to schedule an interview, please contact Cathy Cardenas at cathy@cathycardenas.com.

releases.title: Ukrainian Cultural Festival Brings Three Weeks of Film, Theater and Poetry to New York, Closing Nov. 6 at Carnegie Hall
releases.body:
NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The  fourth annual Ukrainian Cultural Festival (UCF), presented by Razom for Ukraine, runs through Nov. 6  at venues across New York City, with 18 extraordinary events. The festival began Oct. 18 at Carnegie Hall with the U.S. premiere of Oleh Bezborodko's Steel, Violet, Rage—the first four-hands piano concerto by a Ukrainian composer. 

From Oct. 22–26, UCF presents a dedicated Cinema weekend at DCTV's Firehouse Cinema and QUAD Cinema:

  • Narrative & Documentary Screenings: Gar O'Rourke's Sanatorium (Ireland's 98th Academy Awards entry), Nice Ladies, Scream of My Blood: A Gogol Bordello Story, Silent Flood, Honeymoon, To the Victory!, and Cuba & Alaska.
  • Short Film Programs & Workshops: Docudays UA short films, Linoleum Fest animation, an XR immersive technology discussion, and an animation masterclass with Sashko Danylenko. Most screenings feature live filmmaker Q&As.

On Oct. 26, Teatro LATEA hosts scenes and discussion from The Reckoning, a London-born documentary-theater piece by DASH Arts based on war witness testimonies gathered by The Reckoning Project, ahead of its 2027 North American tour. A screening of Richard Nelson's More Beauty Than Sorrow, the final installment in his Lesia Ukrainka series, shows at The Public Theater, Nov. 4. 

UCF's literary programming (Oct. 28 – Nov. 1) highlights Ukrainian writers and translators:

  • Oct. 28: "Poet as Witness" featuring soldier-poets Yaryna Chornohuz and Lesyk Panasiuk, and translator Amelia Glaser, at Poets House.
  • Oct. 30: A panel on modernist playwright Lesia Ukrainka at the NYPL. Stage Directors Virlana Tkacz and Rory Pelsue lead the conversation.
  • Nov. 1: "Ukrainian Poetry Outburst" at Ukrainian National Home, featuring Gogol Bordello frontman Eugene Hütz and master bandurist Julian Kytasty.

UCF concludes Nov. 6 at Zankel Hall with a performance uniting the Chamber Girls' Choir of the M.V. Lysenko Kyiv State Lyceum and the Westchester Children's Chorus.

Razom for Ukraine is a leading U.S.-based nonprofit organization working to build a secure, democratic, and prosperous Ukraine. Founded in 2014, Razom ("together" in Ukrainian) supports urgent needs in Ukraine while investing in long-term solutions across health, civil society, advocacy, and culture. As Ukraine's future has global implications, Razom strengthens trauma care systems, supports local leaders and communities, and connects Ukraine to the world.

releases.title: California's ADU Boom Hits Record Numbers as Acton ADU Brings the Backyard Housing Movement to Public Television Audiences Nationwide
releases.body:
ADU design-build specialist Acton ADU to appear on All Access with Andy Garcia as an industry expert on how accessory dwelling units are reshaping housing for families across California and the United States

CAMPBELL, Calif., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Accessory dwelling units are now one of the fastest-growing forms of housing in America, and Acton ADU is helping a national audience understand why. The California design-build company, which specializes exclusively in ADUs, was selected as an industry specialist for All Access with Andy Garcia, an educational series airing on Public Television stations nationwide. The segment explores the ADU movement and its growing impact on families and homeowners across California and the country.

The feature arrives as ADU growth hits record levels. California issued 41,831 ADU permits in 2025, an all-time high and a more than thirtyfold increase from the 1,336 permitted in 2016, with ADUs accounting for roughly a quarter of all new homes permitted statewide (California Department of Housing and Community Development Annual Progress Report data, as of the September 2026 release). In Los Angeles and San Francisco, more permits were issued for ADUs in 2025 than for all other forms of housing combined (Cotality, as of 2025). In Los Angeles County alone, a record 10,200+ ADUs were completed in 2025, accounting for 37 percent of the county's new housing (USC Lusk Center for Real Estate).

"The most important thing happening in California housing isn't downtown, it's in backyards," said Stan Acton, founder of Acton ADU. "Families are using ADUs to keep aging parents close, give adult children an affordable place to land, and build lasting value on property they already own. That's a generational shift in how Americans think about home, and it's why we were honored to help tell this story on Public Television."

In the segment, Acton ADU explains what ADUs are, why demand for backyard homes has accelerated, and how thoughtful small-home design determines whether an ADU performs for decades. The company also shares the thinking behind Family Integrity Planning, its framework for helping homeowners use ADUs to keep generations close, care for the people they love, and grow long-term value at home.

Founded on more than 35 years of residential construction experience, Acton ADU has completed hundreds of projects across California and serves homeowners throughout the San Francisco Bay Area, East Bay, San Gabriel Valley, and greater Los Angeles county.

The segment featuring Acton ADU will begin distribution on October 26, 2026 on more than 170 participating Public Television stations nationwide, and will air through October 2027.

Interview Availability

Acton ADU founder Stan Acton is available for media interviews on:

  • The ADU movement and California housing policy, including the rise of pre-approved ADU plans
  • Multigenerational living and Family Integrity Planning
  • Why designing a small home well is harder than designing a big one
  • What homeowners should know before building an ADU

To schedule an interview, contact James Parks at info@actonadu.com.

About Acton ADU

Acton ADU is a California design-build company specializing in accessory dwelling units. Serving homeowners throughout the San Francisco Bay Area, East Bay, and San Gabriel Valley, Acton ADU provides an all-in-one partnership covering feasibility, design, permitting, construction, and warranty. Every project is built to perform for decades, backed by a proven process built on No Surprises, Thoughtful Procedures, and Pride and Quality. Learn more at ActonADU.com.

releases.title: AS AI SLOP FLOODS SOCIAL FEEDS, ONVIBE'S SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING PLATFORM, ENHANCED WITH AGENTIC AI, DELIVERS CONTENT WORTH POSTING
releases.body:
LG NOVA-backed company OnVibe helps boost social media engagement with relevant content, in-depth insights and tailored strategies with a conversational, AI-driven platform built for business owners

News Summary

  • OnVibe has launched a new agentic AI system that streamlines content creation and helps businesses get greater value and build social media presence more effectively.
  • New features include in-depth performance evaluations for Instagram and LinkedIn that identify what's working,  where content falls short and opportunities for improvement, at no cost.
  • The conversational AI interface makes the platform accessible to businesses without in-house marketing expertise, closing a critical gap in their ability to compete on social media.
  • For businesses seeking hands-on support, OnVibe offers a Concierge service with marketing experts that execute strategic plans and content on the client's behalf, while leveraging OnVibe's AI engine

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OnVibe, an AI-powered social marketing company backed by LG NOVA, LG Electronics' North America Innovation Center, today unveiled a new agentic AI system that powers its social marketing platform, carrying business context from content recommendations through creation and Instagram publishing.

AI has made it easy to generate a post in seconds. As feeds fill with content that looks and sounds alike, the harder work is knowing which ideas reflect a business, connect with its audience and deserve a place in the feed. For founders and small teams, that work competes with building products, serving customers and running day-to-day operations.

The system brings together ideas, writing, visual creation, scheduling and Instagram publishing in one conversation, helping businesses turn ideas into finished posts with fewer steps. It delivers daily content ideas shaped by each business's context and helps users develop their chosen ideas into finished posts. Users can also ask it to develop a content plan and schedule posts across multiple days.

"Small teams have enough to do without figuring out what to ask an AI each morning," said OnVibe CEO Sahar Arshad. "OnVibe looks at what has worked for your business, what your audience responds to and what is happening in your niche. It brings you ideas with a reason behind each one. You choose the direction, and the same conversation can take it all the way to publication."

Acting as a personal AI agent for the business's Instagram, OnVibe has an informed memory and adapts to the client's work style to provide professional, customized guidance aligned with the business's needs and goals, so businesses can confidently decide what to post.

OnVibe's VibeCheck helps businesses and creators understand what's working in their social content, where the gaps are and what to post next. It evaluates positioning, content pillars and engagement patterns, then provides suggested posts and practical recommendations to strengthen their social presence. For accounts with existing content, OnVibe can analyze up to 50 recent posts to understand content patterns and audience response. The feature helps users assess posting consistency, engagement and content formats.

Free evaluations are available at audit.onvibe.co, with no platform signup required, for Instagram business and creator accounts, as well as LinkedIn profiles of founders and executives and LinkedIn company pages.

How the New System Works

OnVibe's agentic system is designed to carry context and work across the steps involved in social marketing:

  • Ideas that arrive ready to develop: Daily Drop offers content ideas tailored to the business, with creative direction, suggested copy or scripts, captions, hashtags and visuals. Each idea includes an explanation of why it was recommended.
  • Memory users can shape: OnVibe builds on what it learns about a business's voice, visual style, goals, location, market and preferences across conversations. Users can review and update that memory, upload their own images and add PDF brand guidelines. They can also ask why a particular idea fits.
  • A conversation that adapts to the task: Users can request a precise edit or provide a broader brief. They can refine a static post, build a carousel or generate a multi-day content plan, then schedule or publish finished posts directly to Instagram within the same conversation.
  • Writing guided by practitioners: Captions follow guidance developed by OnVibe's social media experts to help the writing sound specific to the business.

The free Starter Plan supports one connected Instagram account and requires no credit card. Higher creation limits are currently available at no cost for a limited time.

Expert Support Through OnVibe Concierge

OnVibe's Concierge program provides businesses with a team to manage their social presence using OnVibe's Agentic AI Engine. Its strategists and creatives handle social strategy, content creation, publishing and performance across Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok and Facebook, using OnVibe's AI engine as the backend to refine the work over time. In two months, OnVibe Concierge helped an early-stage technology client triple its follower count while increasing posting frequency from one to five posts per week across four social channels. To build awareness and make the product's value more relatable, OnVibe developed a consistent brand voice, content built around real-world experiences, user-generated content and a paid distribution strategy.

Concierge supports ongoing social marketing as well as company launches, product introductions and entry into new markets, including international businesses launching in the U.S. The team helps sharpen the message and carry the story across the channels where the business needs to build an audience.

Why It Matters Now

Social media is an important way for businesses to be discovered, yet maintaining a presence often falls to people wearing many hats. According to Constant Contact's Q2 2026 Small Business Now report, 49 percent of consumers surveyed globally use social media to find new small businesses, compared with 40 percent who use search engines. The report also found that 47 percent of small business owners surveyed manage their social media entirely on their own.

To get started with OnVibe, visit onvibe.co. To request a free Instagram or LinkedIn performance evaluation, visit audit.onvibe.co.

About OnVibe

OnVibe is an AI-powered social marketing platform that helps small businesses and startups decide what to say, create content that reflects their brand, publish it and learn from the results. Developed within LG NOVA, OnVibe offers a free self-serve platform and OnVibe Concierge, an expert-led service for teams seeking hands-on strategy and execution. Learn more at onvibe.co.

About LG NOVA

LG NOVA, the North America Innovation Center for global innovation leader LG Electronics, is a team focused on bringing innovation from the outside to LG. LG NOVA is based in Santa Clara, Calif. The center's mission is to fuel innovation for LG and its partners by creating and launching new ventures to become the next growth engine for LG. Learn more at lgnova.com.

About LG Electronics USA

LG Electronics USA Inc., based in Englewood Cliffs, N.J., is the North American subsidiary of LG Electronics Inc., a smart life solutions company with annual global revenues of more than $60 billion. In the United States, LG sells a wide range of innovative home appliances, home entertainment products, commercial displays, air conditioning systems and vehicle components. LG is an 11-time ENERGY STAR® Partner of the Year. For the latest news from LG Electronics USA, visit lg.com/us/newsroom. For more information on LG Electronics, visit LG.com.

releases.title: Canadians can't control the commute, but they can control how it feels: new SiriusXM study reveals the changing experience on the road
releases.body:
Commuting experiences vary across six Canadian markets, while 73% say time on the road would be worse without audio

TORONTO, Oct. 20, 2026 /CNW/ -- For the second year in a row, SiriusXM surveyed drivers across the country to understand how their experiences are changing on the road, the regional realities shaping their journeys and the role audio plays along the way.

More than one third (37%) of Canadians say their time on the road has worsened over the past year. At the same time, as work schedules and daily routines continue to shift, changing when, why and how often Canadians are on the road, people are finding ways to make more of that time. Nearly half (47%) say their drive feels like time entirely their own, while 73% say their drive would be worse without audio.

"Canadians can't always control the traffic, distance or delays that come with being on the road, but they are able to manage how they spend that time," said Susan Simpson, Senior Director, Brand, Marketing and Communications, SiriusXM Canada. "This year's study shows the important role audio can play in that experience, and how it can help make time behind the wheel feel more enjoyable, meaningful and their own -- something SiriusXM is proud to deliver to drivers every day."

Where You Live Shapes How You Commute

The study reveals distinct commuting realities across Canadian cities:

  • Toronto drivers face some of the longest and most stressful journeys, with 27% driving for an hour or more and 48% describing the experience as stressful.
  • Vancouver drivers show that shorter drives don't always mean easier ones, with only 11% driving for an hour or more, yet 46% describing their commute as stressful.
  • Montreal drivers have a strong connection to audio, with 85% saying their time in the car would be worse without it and 31% saying audio is the part of their drive they value most.
  • Calgary commuters are most frustrated by other drivers, with 42% citing them as their top stressor, while more than half (54%) say their drive feels entirely their own.
  • Winnipeg commuters are feeling the impact of construction, with 23% citing road construction or closures as their top stressor.
  • Regina commuters report some of the most manageable journeys, with 57% travelling less than 30 minutes and 26% describing their drive as stressful.

SiriusXM has teamed up with Canadian recruiter and career expert Emily Durham (@emily.the.recruiter), whose work gives her a firsthand view into how workplace trends, hybrid schedules and changing routines are reshaping when, why and how Canadians commute.

"The way we work has changed, and so has the way we commute," said Emily Durham. "Being in the car isn't just about getting to and from the office anymore. Whether you're heading into work, dropping off the kids, going to an appointment or running errands, it can be a chance to reset and make that time feel like your own. Having something you genuinely enjoy listening to can completely change how that journey feels."

Audio Makes the Journey Better

The SiriusXM Canadian Commute study shows that audio continues to play an important role, particularly among younger Canadians. Among audio listeners aged 18–34, half (50%) say audio improves their mood, while nearly a third (32%) have looked forward to their drive because of something they planned to listen to.

SiriusXM gives Canadians the freedom to choose what they want from their drive, whether that's music to energize, news to stay informed, comedy to lighten the mood or something to help them unwind. With 425+ channels across talk, comedy, news, sports and more, plus ad free music, SiriusXM offers something for every drive, mood and moment.

Eligible customers can get SiriusXM in their car + app for $6/month for 12 months. Click here to sign up and experience what SiriusXM has to offer. See Offer Details.

Survey Methodology: These are the findings of a survey conducted by Angus Reid Group on behalf of SiriusXM from September 1-9, 2026 among a sample of n=1,256 working adults living in Canada who commute by car and are members of the Angus Reid Forum. The survey was conducted in English and French. For comparison purposes only, a probability sample of this size would carry a margin of error of ±2.8 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.

About SiriusXM Canada

Sirius XM Canada Inc., operating as SiriusXM Canada, is the country's leading audio entertainment company. SiriusXM creates and offers ad-free music; premier sports talk and live events; comedy; news; podcasts; and exclusive talk and entertainment. SiriusXM is available in vehicles from every major car company, as well as on smartphones and all connected devices on the SiriusXM app. For more information, visit siriusxm.ca.  

Join SiriusXM Canada on Facebook, on X, on Instagram and on YouTube.

SiriusXM radios and accessories are available from retailers nationwide and online at SiriusXM. In addition, SiriusXM Music for Business provides ad-free music to a variety of businesses. SiriusXM is also a leading provider of connected vehicles services, giving customers access to a suite of safety, security, and convenience services including automatic crash notification, stolen vehicle recovery assistance, enhanced roadside assistance and turn-by-turn navigation.

SiriusXM Canada has been designated one of Canada's Best Managed Companies 17 years in a row and is currently a Platinum Club Member.

releases.title: LMBPN® Publishing Expands Library Access Through New Partnership with Hoopla Digital
releases.body:
More than 3,000 titles, including multilingual editions, to reach participating U.S. public libraries

LAS VEGAS, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LMBPN® Publishing today announced a distribution agreement with Hoopla Digital, expanding access to its catalog of more than 3,000 titles through participating U.S. public libraries.

For the first time, LMBPN's full catalog, including multilingual titles, is set to become broadly available through Hoopla, helping library patrons discover its authors and series while expanding libraries' selection of genre fiction.

LMBPN's catalog has generated nearly 17.5 million combined book sales and Kindle Unlimited reading equivalents worldwide, with more than 5.9 billion Kindle Edition Normalized Pages (KENP) read. Its science fiction, fantasy, urban fantasy, paranormal, romantasy, LitRPG, and action-adventure titles include long-running series with established global readerships.

"This is an important expansion for LMBPN because it gives more readers a way to discover our authors, explore our worlds, and enjoy our long-running series," said Robin Cutler, President of LMBPN® Publishing. "Libraries remain one of the most trusted avenues for book discovery. Through our partnership with Hoopla, we are opening our catalog to a new audience of library readers and making our stories accessible on a scale that was not previously possible."

"Libraries have always been a place for discovery, and requests for new genres and diverse, multilingual content continue to grow," said Brad Rose, VP of Content Strategy at Hoopla. "Our partnership with LMBPN helps us meet that demand, giving libraries an even wider range of titles to offer their patrons."

The agreement gives library patrons a new way to discover LMBPN's books and participating libraries access to high-interest independent fiction, including multilingual editions. For LMBPN, Hoopla extends its reach beyond retail and subscription channels.

About LMBPN® Publishing

Founded in 2015 by bestselling author Michael Anderle, LMBPN® Publishing is an independent publisher of more than 3,000 titles across science fiction, fantasy, urban fantasy, paranormal, romantasy, LitRPG, action-adventure, and related genres. Its fast-paced, long-running series reach international readers through digital publishing and multilingual editions.

Michael Anderle is an Amazon Top 30 bestselling author and Dragon Award nominee. In 2024, Amazon recognized him as the fifth most-read Kindle Unlimited author in the UK over the program's first decade.

About Hoopla Digital

With a mission to serve public libraries and their patrons, Hoopla is the only all-in-one app that provides online and mobile access to millions of eBooks, audiobooks, comics and manga, music, movies, TV, and more with BingePass. Available in 115+ world languages, content on Hoopla is available for free with a valid library card. Hoopla is the pioneer of the pay per use model that allows library patrons to borrow content immediately, no waits or holds required. Headquartered in Holland, Ohio, Hoopla is a service of Midwest Tape, a trusted partner to public libraries for over 35 years. For more information, or to download the Hoopla app, visit hoopladigital.com.

Gathering at Los Angeles Trade-Technical College will focus on connecting Promise programs to high-demand careers and stronger regional economies

releases.title: College Promise and Los Angeles Community College District to Convene National Leaders at 2026 Careers Institute, Celebrate 10 Years of LA College Promise
releases.body:
Gathering at Los Angeles Trade-Technical College will focus on connecting Promise programs to high-demand careers and stronger regional economies

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- College Promise, in partnership with the Los Angeles Community College District (LACCD), will host the 2026 College Promise Careers Institute on Oct. 21–22, 2026, at Los Angeles Trade-Technical College, convening leaders from higher education, workforce, philanthropy, government, and industry around a central question: how Promise programs can move more learners into high-demand careers and strengthen regional economies. The Institute will also mark the 10th anniversary of LA College Promise, one of the nation's leading Promise programs and a 2025 College Promise National Impact Award honoree.

Under the theme Igniting Prosperity: The Path to Fueling Talent, Innovation, and Opportunity, sessions will cover:

  • Aligning Promise programs with regional workforce needs and employer demand
  • Artificial intelligence and the changing skills economy
  • Expanding opportunity for men and parenting students, building on College Promise's national student-father initiative
  • Communicating educational and economic outcomes, and return on investment, to policymakers, funders, and the public
  • Sustainable funding models that keep Promise programs strong for the long term

Launched in 2016 through a partnership among LACCD, the Los Angeles Unified School District, the City of Los Angeles, the Los Angeles Area Chamber of Commerce, and philanthropic and community partners, LA College Promise is a model that has expanded educational opportunity for thousands of students demonstrating how coordinated community investment can help learners reach their potential and contribute to the region's economic future.

"Ten years ago, Los Angeles made a promise to its students, and LA Promise has spent the decade keeping it, showing firsthand the power of the Promise program idea," said Rosye Cloud, interim CEO of College Promise. "Across the country, that's hundreds of Promise programs giving students and families a real path to college and a career. It's helping community partners rethink how we connect education, workforce opportunity, and economic mobility. That's the life-changing work we're in Los Angeles to celebrate and build on at the Careers Institute."  

"Our LA Promise graduates feel like family to me. I have celebrated with them at commencement, listened to their stories, and watched them become the nurses, technicians, teachers, and entrepreneurs who power our city", said Dr. Alberto J. Román, LACCD Chancellor. "Ten years ago, Los Angeles made a promise to its young people that college would be within reach. Thousands of students have kept their end of that promise with courage and determination. Welcoming the Careers Institute to Los Angeles Trade-Technical College gives us the opportunity to share their success with the nation and recommit ourselves to the next generation of Promise scholars."

Today, the national College Promise movement includes more than 470 Promise programs serving communities in all 50 states. Together, these programs help learners earn credentials, connect to careers, and contribute to stronger local and regional economies and communities.

College Promise extends its gratitude to its National Advisory Board, National Leadership Council, national partners, philanthropies, and donors. Special thanks to the Andrew Carnegie Foundation, ECMC Foundation, The Kresge Foundation, The College Board, and CollegeAPP for their invaluable support.

About College Promise

College Promise is a national, nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing educational and economic opportunity by supporting Promise programs that increase college access, completion, and workforce success. Through research, policy leadership, technical assistance, and cross-sector partnerships, College Promise works to ensure that all learners have clear pathways to prosperity.

About the Los Angeles Community College District

The Los Angeles Community College District is the nation's largest community college district, serving hundreds of thousands of students annually through nine colleges. Through LA Promise, LACCD and its partners have expanded access to higher education by providing financial support, student success services, and pathways to degrees, certificates, transfer, and careers.

releases.body:
CARLSBAD, Calif., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The NAMM Foundation opens applications for the 2027 Best Communities for Music Education (BCME) Award, marking the program's 28th consecutive year of recognizing school districts and individual schools across the nation that prioritize music education as an essential part of a well-rounded education.

BCME shines a national spotlight on the educators, school leaders, families and community partners working to ensure students have meaningful opportunities to participate in music. By celebrating communities that make music education a priority, the program demonstrates the value of sustained investment in music learning and inspires other schools and districts to strengthen their own programs.

New for 2027, eligible BCME applicants will also have the opportunity to apply for the Dinah Gretsch Impact Award, which will provide awards of up to $5,000 each to as many as 10 schools and districts demonstrating financial need and a commitment to strengthening and sustaining music education.

Applications for the 2027 BCME program are open October 20, 2026, through January 5, 2027, at nammfoundation.org/bcme.

Recognizing Communities That Put Music First

Across the country, BCME honorees demonstrate how sustained investment in music education creates meaningful opportunities for students. Their work reflects a shared commitment among educators, administrators, families and community leaders to make music an integral part of the school experience.

From established programs with decades of recognition to first-time honorees expanding access and participation, these communities illustrate the many ways music education enriches students' lives.

Dinah Gretsch Impact Award: Extending the Impact of Music Education

While BCME recognizes communities for prioritizing music education, the Dinah Gretsch Impact Award offers an additional opportunity to support eligible schools and districts that demonstrate financial need and are committed to strengthening their programs.

In 2027, up to 10 recipients will receive awards of up to $5,000 each to help sustain and expand music education opportunities. Title I schools, districts with Title I schools, and non-public schools demonstrating financial need are eligible to apply through the BCME application process.

The award honors Dinah Gretsch and her enduring commitment to music education, access and the belief that music can create opportunity and connection for every student.

28 Years of Raising the Bar for Music Education

For nearly three decades, the Best Communities for Music Education program has provided national recognition for schools and districts that make music education a priority.

BCME honorees demonstrate their commitment through investment in music programs, access and participation, quality instruction, community engagement and sustained support. Their achievements show how schools and communities can work together to make music an enduring part of students' educational experiences.

By recognizing these communities, The NAMM Foundation celebrates what is working, elevates the importance of music education nationwide and encourages more school districts to invest in opportunities that help students learn, grow and thrive through music.

2027 BCME Key Dates

  • October 20, 2026: Applications open



  • January 5, 2027: Application deadline



  • Spring 2027: BCME honorees and Dinah Gretsch Impact Award recipients announced

School districts and individual schools nationwide are encouraged to apply and share how they are creating meaningful opportunities for students to learn, perform, create and connect through music.

Apply and learn more: Best Communities for Music Education

About The NAMM Foundation

The NAMM Foundation is a 501(c)3 public charity established in 2006, born from the National Association of Music Merchant's (NAMM) decades-long commitment to giving back. Since its founding, the Foundation has invested over $20 million to expand access to music making and music education for people of all ages.

releases.title: Campus Launches Online Associate Degree in Cybersecurity Built for AI-Driven Threats
releases.body:
The two-year college's new degree includes preparation for CompTIA Security+, CEH, and AWS certifications, with live classes taught by experienced practitioners and university faculty that also teach at some of the nation's top colleges.

NEW YORK, October 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Campus, a two-year accredited college built for a generation of learners frustrated by the cost and pace of higher education, today announced the launch of its Associate of Science in Cybersecurity degree program. The program is designed to give students an affordable path into a four-year degree or a career in cybersecurity, equipping them with the skills they'll need to defend against increasingly sophisticated, artificial intelligence-driven threats.

AI is reshaping both how cyberattacks are carried out and the skills security teams need to respond. According to ISC2's 2025 Cybersecurity Workforce Study, 95% of cybersecurity professionals surveyed reported at least one skills gap on their team, and 73% said AI will create more specialized cybersecurity skills. In the new program, students learn the foundations of network security, threat detection, and ethical hacking, along with how to use AI in that work and defend against it when attackers do the same.

"Today's threats are becoming increasingly sophisticated. Attackers are already using AI to write phishing emails or make phone calls that sound exactly like a manager or family member," said Kaari Casey, Vice President of Academic Operations at Campus. "Entry-level IT professionals today must be able to catch that kind of deception quickly, and recognize when an AI tool's recommendation is wrong. Our students will develop the knowledge, skills, and judgment it takes to navigate this new world."

Building on the cybersecurity concentration Campus introduced within its Associate of Science in Information Technology in July, the program offers live, synchronous instruction taught by veteran cybersecurity practitioners and professors at top universities such as UC Davis, St. John's University, and University of Notre Dame. Over eight quarters, students move from introductory coursework in IT, cybersecurity, and AI to networking, cloud foundations, and IT ethics, then to network security, security operations and threat detection, and ethical hacking. AI runs through the curriculum: students learn to spot AI-generated deception in early security scenarios, validate AI-assisted recommendations in network-defense labs, and study how AI is used on both sides of an attack.

"Students in this program will build and test network defenses, work step by step through simulated incidents, and have to justify every decision they make. That rigor is what prepares students for the day-to-day work of an entry-level security role" said Casey.

Students also leave prepared for the high-value, industry-recognized certifications employers often look for in entry-level hires. Preparation for certification exams is built directly into students' coursework, which includes the content needed for students to sit for CompTIA's A+, Network+, Security+, and CySA+ exams, as well as the EC-Council Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH) and AWS Cloud Practitioner and Solutions Architect certifications. Students who earn a B or higher in both their final course grade and final exam for a qualifying course are eligible for a Campus-funded certification exam voucher.

Students can apply starting now at campus.edu/online-cybersecurity-associate-degree. Classes will start in January 2027, with tuition set at $2,440 per quarter or $7,320 per academic year, including books and supplies.

As the first college built in the AI era, Campus is backed by entrepreneurs and investors including Sam Altman, Shaquille O'Neal, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, and 8VC, and is led by a board of respected former college presidents including John Wilson of Morehouse College and Gail Mellow of LaGuardia Community College. Campus delivers live, online classes taught by faculty who also teach at top colleges like Stanford and Howard. Campus' unique approach is grounded in a pioneering tech platform and a heavily-researched student success model proven to double two-year college graduation rates. Campus provides students with dedicated advisors, on-demand tutoring, and personalized coaching. Upon completion, students take skills learned in the program into the workforce or transfer to a growing number of four-year institution transfer partners.

About Campus

Campus is a new way to go to college, built for students looking for a lower-cost, faster launchpad into a career – or a four-year degree. Campus delivers live, online classes taught by professors who also teach at leading universities like Stanford and Howard University. The college's unique approach is grounded in a pioneering technology platform and a heavily-researched student success model that offers students dedicated advisors and on-demand tutoring and coaching to ensure their academic access. Campus was named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies. To learn more, visit campus.edu.

releases.body:
From the Yankees clubhouse to baseball's looming labor showdown, Sturtze and host Shana Orczyk Sissel examine the money, power and financial risks reshaping professional sports.

LIVE TODAY: Tuesday, October 20, 2026 | 12:00 PM ET

WASHINGTON, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CrossCheck Media Inc. today announced that former Major League Baseball pitcher Tanyon Sturtze, who spent 12 seasons in the major leagues, including three with the New York Yankees, will appear live on Franchise Value today at 12:00 PM Eastern Time on Biz Talk Today TV (BTT).

The episode will stream live on the CrossCheck Media YouTube channel and across Biz Talk Today TV's distribution network.

Hosted by Shana Orczyk Sissel, CEO and Founder of Banríon Capital Management and author of Tough Minded, Franchise Value examines the increasingly sophisticated business of professional sports, where franchise valuations, labor negotiations, media rights and financial markets collide.

Today's episode brings an unusually revealing perspective to that conversation.

Sturtze experienced professional baseball from both ends of the financial spectrum. He was an Opening Day starter for the Tampa Bay Devil Rays, one of baseball's lowest-payroll organizations, before joining the New York Yankees and becoming a key member of manager Joe Torre's pitching staff.

His career offers firsthand insight into the financial realities facing professional athletes, from negotiating contracts and competing for roster spots to managing injuries that can abruptly change a player's earning potential.

Now working in the insurance industry, Sturtze brings a second perspective to the business of sports: how athletes, teams and financial institutions evaluate and manage risk.

Baseball's Billion-Dollar Labor Battle

The conversation arrives at a pivotal moment for Major League Baseball.

With the league's collective bargaining agreement scheduled to expire December 1, 2026, owners and players are confronting potentially consequential negotiations over salary caps, minimum payroll requirements, revenue sharing and the possibility of another work stoppage.

At the center of the debate is competitive balance.

The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers are preparing to meet in the World Series despite operating with substantially smaller payrolls than many of baseball's biggest-market franchises.

Their success raises an important question: Does Major League Baseball need a salary cap to create competitive balance, or would a cap primarily give owners greater control over labor costs?

Sissel and Sturtze will explore that question through the experiences of a former player who competed for both a small-market organization and the New York Yankees.

Inside the Yankees Clubhouse

Beyond baseball's labor negotiations, viewers can expect a firsthand look at life inside one of professional sports' most recognizable franchises.

Sturtze will discuss his experiences in the major leagues, the differences between small-market and big-market organizations, and the financial pressures facing players whose careers depend on performance, health and contract negotiations.

The discussion will also examine how injuries can affect an athlete's financial future and why insurance and risk management have become increasingly important components of professional sports.

When Athletes Become Financial Assets

Today's episode will also explore a developing intersection between Wall Street and professional athletics.

From sports-related futures contracts and proposed investment funds to platforms offering investors exposure to athletes' future earnings, financial innovation is creating new ways to participate in the economics of professional sports.

But those developments raise significant questions about regulation, insider information, athlete compensation and financial risk.

Sissel and Sturtze will examine who benefits from these emerging financial products, who bears the risk and whether the athletes themselves are adequately protected.

The conversation will also touch on rising franchise valuations, media-rights economics and the expanding role of institutional capital in professional sports.

releases.body:
Defense Unicorns CMMC addresses NIST SP 800-171 requirements, providing hands-on guidance, assessor-ready evidence, and year-round continuous compliance for the Defense Industrial Base

SAN ANTONIO, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Defense Unicorns, a leader in open-source and secure defense software delivery, today announced the launch of its end-to-end Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) solution, Defense Unicorns CMMC. Defense Unicorns CMMC is designed specifically for companies across the Defense Industrial Base (DIB), including small businesses, independent software vendors (ISVs), and enterprise defense contractors. The new offering fast-tracks NIST SP 800-171 readiness while ensuring continuous, year-round compliance.

"A stronger defense industrial base gives our nation greater capacity to deliver what the mission demands," said Dr. Rob Slaughter, CEO and Co-Founder of Defense Unicorns. "We need more companies bringing their talent, technology, and innovation to defense. Our job is to help them enter that market, grow, and deliver securely. By reducing the burden of CMMC readiness, we help contractors focus their people and resources on building the capabilities our warfighters need."

With Department of War contract eligibility tied directly to cybersecurity readiness, defense contractors face mounting pressure to navigate complex technical controls, gap remediation, and extensive documentation requirements. Defense Unicorns CMMC eliminates compliance bottlenecks by combining expert implementation, tailored assessment documentation, and ongoing maintenance without forcing contractors to overhaul existing IT infrastructure.

Key Offerings & Capabilities

Defense Unicorns CMMC provides a comprehensive path to accreditation built around four core pillars:

  • End-to-End Implementation & Maintenance: Hands-on configuration of security controls, gap remediation, assessment support, and ongoing guidance to keep documentation and evidence current as systems, scope, and flow-down requirements change.
  • Vendor-Agnostic System Compatibility: Seamless integration within existing IT environments, including Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and complex hybrid operating systems—working alongside existing Managed Service Providers (MSPs and internal IT).
  • Assessor-Ready Evidence Packets: Generation of complete, audit-ready compliance packages containing tailored System Security Plans (SSPs), policies, procedures, architecture diagrams, databases, and supporting evidence.
  • Partnering with Certified Assessment Bodies (C3PAOs): Close collaboration with Certified Third-Party Assessment Organizations (C3PAOs) to remediate failed CMMC assessments and ensure streamlined evaluation workflows.

Despite recent regulatory pauses surrounding Phase II assessment rollouts, contractual requirements under DFARS 252.204-7012 and Phase I NIST SP 800-171 self-assessments remain fully active. Defense Unicorns' expert team equips DIB organizations with the technical safeguards and continuous evidence generation required to satisfy government audits and protect Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) at all times.

To learn more about Defense Unicorns CMMC or to schedule a consultation with a Defense Unicorns CMMC Certified Professional, visit defenseunicorns.com/solutions/industry/cmmc/.

About Defense Unicorns

Defense Unicorns is a veteran-owned defense technology company founded in 2021 by Rob Slaughter, Jeff McCoy, and Andrew Greene to make software a strategic deterrent for the U.S. Department of War. The company builds open-source, airgap-native technologies that enable the secure development, delivery, and sustainment of mission software across cloud, on-premises, airgapped, and tactical edge environments. Defense Unicorns' technology is trusted by operators of critical systems across the U.S. Navy, Army, Air Force, and Space Force. Learn more at https://defenseunicorns.com.

NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Great American Media announced today that Kellie Barnes has joined the company as Vice President of Marketing , bringing more than three decades of entertainment marketing experience spanning film, music, live events and faith-based entertainment.

Kellie Barnes joins Great American Media as VP of Marketing, bringing experience in entertainment and audience growth.

In her new role, Barnes will bring her expertise in integrated marketing, audience development, strategic partnerships and brand strategy to Great American Media's growing portfolio.

"Kellie understands how to connect great content with the audience it was created to serve," said Kaitlyn Haubrich, Chief Brand Officer and Chief of Staff, Great American Media. "She brings a strong combination of entertainment marketing experience, strategic thinking and a real understanding of the faith and family audience. As Great American Media continues to grow, Kellie will be an important part of how we strengthen our brands and reach new viewers."

Barnes most recently served as Head of Marketing for Smallbone Management/for KING + COUNTRY, where she oversaw marketing, promotions, public relations and partnerships across film and streaming projects. Her work included marketing and PR strategy for music and film releases, documentary campaigns, sponsorships, licensing and audience-growth initiatives.

Prior to that, she spent more than eight years as Director of Marketing at Fathom Entertainment, leading integrated marketing, strategic partnerships and event marketing for theatrical releases and cinema events distributed nationwide. Barnes directed campaigns for theatrical events, live broadcasts, concerts, documentaries and specialty programming and led a team responsible for more than 25 – 30 theatrical events annually.

Earlier in her career, she spent 20+ years with Allied Integrated Marketing, ultimately serving as Vice President of Marketing. There, she launched the company's specialty Faith Marketing Division and led national and regional campaigns for major motion picture studios including Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, Lionsgate and Fox Searchlight Pictures.

Barnes' career has centered on building integrated campaigns that increase brand awareness, strengthen audience engagement and support business growth while working across creative, publicity, digital, production and executive teams.

A long-time Formula 1 enthusiast, JJ fulfilled his dream by performing at the race in his home country of Singapore, bringing his passions for music and motorsport together in one night.

The three artists enriched the event's entertainment lineup with a rich tapestry of Chinese‑language musical styles and live performances. Their appearances drew a positive response from both the artists and their fans. The participating artists expressed their excitement at taking the stage and how honored they felt to perform, with JJ describing it as a dream stage. releases.title: College Student Mental Health: New AllOne Health Research Reveals Who Seeks Counseling and How They Access Care
releases.body:
Peer-reviewed research examines 2,800 counseling cases across 36 higher education institutions, revealing how students access support for mental health, relationship concerns, and everyday stress.

WILKES-BARRE, Pa., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Anxiety, depression, and grief were the leading reasons college students sought counseling through AllOne Health's Student Assistance Program (SAP), with mental health concerns accounting for 61% of cases, according to a pair of peer-reviewed studies published in the Journal of Education and Human Development. Students also reached out for help with personal relationships (19%) and everyday life stress (17%).

The research, announced today by AllOne Health, a leading provider of Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs), Student Assistance Programs (SAPs), and integrated whole health solutions, gives university presidents, student affairs professionals, healthcare service providers, and other campus leaders a data-driven view of what brings students to counseling, how quickly they connect with care, and how a Student Assistance Program can complement campus services.

"Today's college students bring a wide range of life experiences, schedules, and needs. Student Assistance Programs give institutions an innovative way to meet them," said Keith Wasley, President & CEO of AllOne Health. "When a student reaches out, fast access to high-quality clinical care and in-the-moment support makes the biggest impact. Our SAP is designed to complement campus student services by giving students a trusted place to turn, 24/7, by phone, app, or video."

What Brings Students to Counseling

The counseling study analyzed 2,800 cases from 36 colleges and universities across the United States between 2020 and 2024, examining why students sought support, how counseling was delivered, and how they used services. Students who used counseling represented a broad range of ages and life stages. Key findings include:

  • Mental health was the leading concern. Mental health issues accounted for 61% of cases, including anxiety (23%), depression and mood disorders (11%), grief and loss (5%), and other emotional issues (22%).
  • Relationships and everyday stress were also common. Personal relationship concerns accounted for 19% of cases, and personal life stress accounted for 17%.
  • Counseling was delivered almost entirely by video or phone. Based on the 1,986 cases with recorded modality, online video accounted for 89% of cases, telephone counseling for 10%, and in-person counseling for 1%.
  • Nearly 1 in 4 cases were resolved in a single session. Students used an average of 3.5 sessions over 47 days, and 24% of cases used just one session of counseling to resolve the student's concern.
  • The length of care varied with student needs. The largest share of cases used 2 or 3 sessions (42%), and about a third (34%) used 4 to 9 sessions, with sessions spaced about 18 days apart on average.
  • Students represented a broad range of ages. 27% of clients were of traditional undergraduate age (18 to 24), while 33% were 25 to 29 years old, 26% were in their 30s, and 14% were 40 to 75 years old.

Why It Matters for Higher Education

Among students who used the program, mental health concerns were the most common reason for seeking support, followed by relationship difficulties and everyday stress. With counseling available by video or phone, students can connect with care around their classes, work, and family responsibilities, when and where they need it.

"Through our partnerships with colleges and universities, AllOne Health's Student Assistance Program has been extending the reach of campus counseling centers, providing additional licensed clinical support aligned with each institution's student mental health initiatives, goals, and services," said Jason C. McDaniel, Regional Vice President of Operations at AllOne Health and co-author of the studies. "With nearly a quarter of cases in our study resolved in a single session, focused counseling helps our partner institutions support more students with the resources they already have."

Fast, Flexible Access When Students Reach Out

During intake, 11% of cases included a brief "In-the-Moment" telephone support call, and across the five-year study period, the first call was answered in about 16 seconds on average. Students most often began their requests for counseling by phone (70%) or through the mobile app (30%), both available 24/7.

"Students use counseling for many reasons, ranging from anxiety and depression to relationship difficulties and personal stress, and this mix differs slightly by age as well," said Mark Attridge, Ph.D., co-author of the study. "Understanding why and how students use counseling can help institutions consider the support resources needed by students in different age groups."

Practical Support for Daily Life

A companion study examined 5,604 work/life service cases among students at 29 colleges and universities. Personal life and convenience support accounted for 44% of those cases, followed by financial referrals (36%), legal referrals (12%), and childcare assistance (4%). Students used personal life concierge support at three times the rate of employees using AllOne Health's EAP work/life services over the same period (44% vs. 14%). Together, the two studies show how Student Assistance Programs can complement campus services by giving students access to both counseling and practical resources for real-life problems.

"The purpose of this research was to develop a clearer profile of students who use Student Assistance Program services, including the concerns that bring them to counseling and how they access support," said Dr. Attridge. "By documenting these service-use patterns and comparing them with existing research on campus counseling center users, we can better understand the role of external SAP services."

About the Research

The studies describe service utilization among AllOne Health program users. The samples were not designed to represent all college students in the United States, measure changes in student well-being or academic outcomes, or establish the effectiveness of a particular service model. The work-life study sample was especially concentrated among students attending large, private, for-profit institutions and fully online or hybrid schools.

Both studies were authored by Mark Attridge, Ph.D., M.A., of Attridge Consulting, Inc., and Jason C. McDaniel, LCSW, CEAP, MBA, of AllOne Health, and published in the Journal of Education and Human Development in March 2026. Dr. Attridge, an independent research consultant, was engaged by AllOne Health to conduct the studies. McDaniel is an AllOne Health executive.

About AllOne Health

AllOne Health is a leading provider of Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) and whole health solutions that support employees, students, and their families while helping organizations strengthen workforce well-being and performance. The company combines clinical expertise, compassionate human support, and accessible technology across Employee Assistance, Organizational Consulting, Wellness, Crisis Support, and Corporate Concierge. Trusted by over 11,000 clients, with 14+ million lives covered, AllOne Health helps people live well and organizations grow stronger, driving positive change for organizations, powered by people who care. Learn more at AllOneHealth.com.

releases.body:
Hosted by CEO Robert Dalton, the podcast brings professional insight, personal stories, and meaningful conversations to families navigating aging and homecare.

PEEKSKILL, N.Y., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What does it truly mean to age well? How can families prepare for changing care needs without sacrificing independence, dignity, or quality of life?

These questions drive the return of Embracing Angels, an educational podcast hosted by Robert Dalton, CEO of Angels on Call Homecare, an award-winning New York homecare organization specializing in Dementia, Parkinson's disease, and personalized aging-in-place services.

Originally introduced in 2024 with a focus on end-of-life experiences, Embracing Angels returns with an expanded mission: making conversations about aging, caregiving, and long-term care more accessible, informed, and meaningful.

"Over the years, I've seen how overwhelming it can be for families to navigate care decisions, especially when they don't know what questions to ask or where to turn," said Robert Dalton, CEO and podcast host. "I want this podcast to be a place where we talk openly about aging, share what we've learned, and help people feel better prepared for whatever comes next. These are conversations every family deserves to have."

Real Conversations. Diverse Voices. Meaningful Perspectives.

Embracing Angels explores subjects extending beyond traditional healthcare discussions, including aging in place, family caregiving, private-pay homecare, Dementia, Parkinson's disease, independence, and the emotional realities of supporting loved ones through life's transitions.

Through professional perspectives, personal narratives, and thoughtful discussions, the podcast seeks to connect healthcare expertise with lived experiences, offering listeners practical knowledge alongside stories that reflect the humanity behind care.

The relaunch episode, "Why We're Still Embracing Angels, and Private Pay Home Care Explained," addresses misconceptions surrounding homecare coverage and helps families understand important considerations when exploring care options.

Its return during Long-Term Care Planning Month reinforces the importance of education and proactive decision-making.

Extending a Legacy Beyond the Home

Founded in 2005 by Registered Nurse Pamela Fitzpatrick, Angels on Call Homecare has spent more than two decades advancing personalized homecare. Its distinction as the nation's first dual-accredited homecare provider in Dementia and Parkinson's care reflects its commitment to specialized education, clinical excellence, and meaningful quality of life.

"Redefining the aging experience requires more than advancing how care is delivered. It requires transforming how society understands aging itself," said Eric J. Dalton, Vice President of Angels on Call Homecare. "Knowledge creates confidence, and confidence empowers families to make decisions that reflect what matters most. Embracing Angels extends our belief that aging should never mean losing your identity, purpose, or voice. The conversations we start today can meaningfully shape the care people experience tomorrow."

Join the Conversation

Designed for older adults, families, Care Professionals, and healthcare professionals, Embracing Angels invites listeners to discover meaningful perspectives on aging, care, and human connection.

releases.summary: NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet and the Stanley Brothers were officially inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame on Sunday, October 18, during the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum's 2026 Medallion Ceremony. But the multiplatinum singer, the ace songwriter, and the bluegrass music pioneers were connected long before they became the 159th, 160th and 161st Hall of Fame members together.
releases.title: Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet, and the Stanley Brothers Join Country Music Hall of Fame in Emotional Medallion Ceremony
releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet and the Stanley Brothers were officially inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame on Sunday, October 18, during the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum's 2026 Medallion Ceremony. But the multiplatinum singer, the ace songwriter, and the bluegrass music pioneers were connected long before they became the 159th, 160th and 161st Hall of Fame members together.

Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum CEO Kyle Young, who led the Medallion Ceremony, recounted in his remarks that McGraw arrived in Nashville at 1 a.m. on May 9, 1989, with a pawn shop guitar and an ambitious dream to make country music. Later that morning, the world learned that the young New Traditionalist singer Keith Whitley had died.

"Now, some people might call that a bad omen," McGraw said during his induction speech. "I've come to believe it was something else. I think Nashville was telling me the truth on my very first day: that this music costs something. The people who make it give everything that they've got. And if you're lucky enough to make it down the road, you owe it to the ones that didn't and the ones who paved it."

Whitley, a 2022 Country Music Hall of Fame inductee, was a student of bluegrass music. Early in his career, he started a band with 2018 inductee Ricky Skaggs that specialized in the repertoire of the Stanley Brothers. Whitley and Skaggs later became members of Ralph Stanley & the Clinch Mountain Boys. Only a few months before he died at age 34, Whitley earned his second #1 single with the song "When You Say Nothing at All," written by Overstreet and 2017 Hall of Fame inductee Don Schlitz.

"I don't believe that's coincidence — I believe that's country music," McGraw said. "It's a chain, and every link holds up the next one."

TIM MCGRAW

With an ear for memorable songs and a musical style that could be both tough and tender, Tim McGraw became one of the most versatile and recognizable country music stars in the 1990s and 2000s. After establishing his music career, he explored acting and landed leading roles in the Hollywood films "The Blind Side," "Country Strong" and "Friday Night Lights," and in the TV series "1883."

"Someday I hope some kid pulls into town with everything they own in a suitcase and a dream too big to fit in it. Maybe they'll hear one of my songs on the radio. And I hope it tells them what I learned from Keith: getting here comes with a cost," a visibly emotional McGraw said as he concluded his speech. "But standing here tonight, in front of all of you, in front of all of my heroes . . . in this moment, tonight, man, it's worth it."

McGraw's list of thank yous began with seven women who helped him reach this career pinnacle: his mother, Betty Ann D'Agostino Trimble; his wife, fellow country singer Faith Hill; his daughters, Audrey, Gracie and Maggie; and his sisters, Sandy and Tracey. Alabama member Randy Owen also focused on McGraw's roots while leading his induction.

"Home has never left his heart. Family has never left his heart. Country music has never left his heart," Owen said. "We're all so lucky that we can call him one of us."

Musical tributes to McGraw included Parker McCollum's heartfelt and faithful version of McGraw's first #1 single, 1994's "Don't Take the Girl"; a sweet rendition of McGraw's 1997 chart-topper, "Just to See You Smile," by Lainey Wilson, who grew up down the road from where McGraw was raised; and Lady A's take on "Live Like You Were Dying," arguably the night's most emotional performance. The trio's Charles Kelley, who was recently diagnosed with a rare blood cancer, sang lead with deep feeling and skill, and bandmates Dave Haywood and Hillary Scott elevated the award-winning crossover hit with their powerful harmony vocals.

"Hearing my songs sung back in your voices is such a strange and beautiful thing," McGraw told them all. "It's like . . . finding a letter you wrote a long time ago and learning it got to where it was going."

PAUL OVERSTREET

A master of catchy melodies and clever, concise wordplay, Paul Overstreet wrote some of the most popular and enduring songs of the 1980s and'90s, including 27 Top Ten country hits between 1981 and 1991 and 13 #1 hits overall. BMI named him Country Songwriter of the Year for an unprecedented five consecutive years (1987 to 1991), and the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame inducted him in 2003.

"Paul took his own ups and downs and turned them into three-minute messages of hope for millions of listeners — title by title, song by song, hit by hit," said Museum CEO Kyle Young. Overstreet's songs brought a modern perspective to time-tested themes: relationships, faith, family, the power of love to unify and heal — and, in the case of a Blake Shelton chart-topper, bad days. Before performing his 2004 single "Some Beach," Shelton told the crowd about how, as a teenager, he idolized Overstreet and, as an aspiring artist, hoped to one day record one of his songs.

"I never dreamed that my Paul Overstreet song would be a song called 'Some Beach,'" he said to laughter, "but damn it, I'm proud of it."

In addition to Shelton's performance, Country Music Hall of Fame member Dean Dillon delivered a song he wrote with Overstreet, "If I Could Bottle This Up," which George Jones recorded in 1988 with Shelby Lynne, while Jamey Johnson's deep and powerful voice proved a perfect match for Randy Travis's 1987 award-winning hit "Forever and Ever, Amen." Overstreet was inducted by Tanya Tucker — whose 1973 concert in Waco, Texas, persuaded Overstreet to move to Nashville to begin his career as a songwriter and singer. Tucker, who recorded Overstreet's composition "I Won't Take Less Than Your Love" with Overstreet and Paul Davis and scored a #1 country hit — praised the songwriter's talent and his heart.

"The brilliant songwriting of Paul Overstreet speaks for itself, but it's Paul Overstreet the friend and the brother that will always be dear to me," she said. In 1988, several months in a rehabilitation program left Tucker uncertain about her life and career, but when she heard "I Won't Take Less Than Your Love" on the radio after leaving the facility, she recalled, "It gave me something to live for and reminded me of the love of a friend that could and would last a lifetime."

THE STANLEY BROTHERS

Before Hall of Fame members Vince Gill and Ricky Skaggs performed the bluegrass standard "Rank Stranger" with guitarist Jeff White, Skaggs said there was nobody happier to see the Stanley Brothers join the Country Music Hall of Fame. Judging by the standing ovations and loud cheers from the crowd throughout the three-hour ceremony, however, that's debatable. Clearly, the induction of brothers Ralph and Carter Stanley, officially performed by Gill, was long awaited by many in attendance.

"This moment has been a lifetime in the making, and it is difficult to put into words what it means to see my father, alongside my Uncle Carter, honored in this way — just the way my daddy wanted it to be — both of them side by side," said Lisa Stanley Marshall, daughter of Ralph Stanley, who represented the Stanley family alongside her brother, Ralph Stanley II, and her cousin, Jeanie Stanley, Carter Stanley's daughter.

"They were the cream of the crop," Jeanie added, "and it has been a long time coming."

Two additional performances in the Stanleys' honor showed just how driving and high-spirited bluegrass can be. Billy Strings and his band earned a standing ovation for their high-octane take on "How Mountain Girls Can Love," full of fast-fingered solos. Similarly, the First Ladies of Bluegrass — Alison Brown, Becky Buller, Sierra Hull, Missy Raines and Molly Tuttle — dazzled with fiery solos on a brisk version of "Bound to Ride." They perform the song with Dolly Parton on a new Stanley Brothers tribute album and added the recordings of Parton's spirited interjections into their live performance.

"Ralph Stanley often rejected the word 'bluegrass' as means of describing the Stanley Brothers' music. It was 'old-time mountain music,' he said, and no one should dare challenge the good doctor on defining his own craft," Museum CEO Kyle Young said. "However, the acoustic instrumentation, the stark lyrics, [and] the blood-resonant harmonies all point to a definitive musical style that is as popular today, eighty years since its commercial inception, [as] ever before."

ABOUT THE MEDALLION CEREMONY

The annual Country Music Hall of Fame Medallion Ceremony is when the year's members-elect officially join their heroes, influences and peers as Hall of Fame members. The celebratory ceremony highlights each new member's talent, achievements and legacy through emotional speeches, surprise musical tributes and video biographies, and a current Hall of Fame member inducts each member-elect.

At the 2026 Medallion Ceremony, the museum's 31st, the Medallion All-Star Band backed many of the night's tribute performances. Led by musical director and acoustic guitarist Biff Watson, the group also included drummer Mark Beckett, keyboard player Jen Gunderman, harmony singer Tania Hancheroff, bassist Alison Prestwood, fiddler and mandolin player Deanie Richardson, pedal steel player Scotty Sanders, acoustic guitarist and harmony singer Jeff White and electric guitarist Charlie Worsham.

At the start of the night, attendees observed a moment of silence in honor of Dolly Parton and Don Schlitz, the two Country Music Hall of Fame members who died within the last year. Patty Loveless, who joined the Hall of Fame in 2023, closed the event with an upbeat performance of "Will the Circle Be Unbroken," altering the lyrics just slightly in tribute to Parton and Schlitz.

The Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum produces the Medallion Ceremony, and the Country Music Association — which elects new Country Music Hall of Fame members —underwrites the event with City National Bank. This is the museum's 31st Medallion Ceremony

About the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum:
