releases.title: SUBARU, THE ASPCA®, AND IHEARTMEDIA EXPAND PARTNERSHIP TO SUPPORT SHELTER ANIMALS THROUGH ADDITIONAL $25,000 DONATION AND NATIONAL MEDIA CAMPAIGN
releases.body:
New Collaboration builds upon Subaru's 19-year partnership with the ASPCA® and shines a spotlight on National Make A Dog's Day and October's Subaru Loves Pets® campaign

CAMDEN, N.J., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Subaru of America, through its Subaru Loves Pets® initiative, together with iHeartImpact, a community impact division of iHeartMedia designed to help corporate brands partner with nonprofits through their advertising spends with iHeartMedia, today announced an expanded collaboration with the ASPCA® (The American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals®) to help improve the lives of shelter animals across the country. As part of the partnership, Subaru donated an additional $25,000 to support their ongoing commitment to helping shelter animals find loving homes.

This collaboration builds upon Subaru's 19-year partnership with the ASPCA, which began in 2008 through the Subaru Share the Love® Event. Through the Subaru Loves Pets initiative, Subaru and its retailers are committed to improving the lives of as many shelter animals as possible and are proud to be the largest corporate donor to the ASPCA. With more than $75 million donated to national and local pet-focused organizations, they have supported the adoption, rescue, transport and health of more than 900,000 animals.

Alan Bethke, Senior Vice President of Marketing, Subaru of America, Inc.: "Subaru and our national network of retailers are fortunate enough to partner with the ASPCA and to see the profound impact that a pet's unconditional love can have on peoples' lives. With this additional donation and recognition from iHeartMedia, the work we are doing together as part of Subaru Loves Pets will go even further to support the most vulnerable animals in need, and to help shelter animals find loving homes."

Every October, Subaru retailers partner with local animal welfare organizations to help prepare shelter pets for adoption through ASPCA-administered grants and a series of pet-focused events held in communities across the country. As part of this year's campaign, Subaru will celebrate its eighth annual National Make A Dog's Day on October 22 – a day created by Subaru to encourage dog lovers nationwide to do something special for their dogs while inspiring more people to consider adopting, fostering or supporting an Underdog as a life-changing way to Make A Dog's Day. Subaru is especially passionate about supporting older and disabled dogs – affectionally called the "Underdogs" – who are often overlooked and spend more time waiting in shelters to find loving homes.

Meredith Galli, Director of Corporate Partnerships, ASPCA: "The ASPCA is proud to be the recipient of this generous donation from iHeartImpact, made possible through our longstanding partnership with Subaru of America. We are thankful to Subaru for selecting the ASPCA as the beneficiary of this gift, which will help strengthen our efforts to create better outcomes for vulnerable animals nationwide."

The need remains significant. According to the ASPCA, 5.8 million dogs and cats entered shelters and rescues in 2025, with many waiting day after day for the chance to find a loving home.

Together, Subaru, the ASPCA and iHeartImpact aim to inspire more people to support shelter animals while expanding awareness of Subaru's long-standing commitment to pet adoption and welfare. Through the partnership, iHeartMedia and iHeartImpact will help expand the reach of Subaru's October campaign with a national broadcast initiative designed to encourage audiences across the country to learn more about shelter pet adoption and fostering.

Jenna Craig, President, National Media Team, iHeartMedia: "National Make A Dog's Day is a powerful reminder of the impact each of us can have on the lives of shelter animals. As a media partner that reaches 9 out of 10 Americans every month, we're proud to collaborate with Subaru and the ASPCA to help bring this message to our audiences nationwide and inspire more people to adopt, foster, and support pets waiting for a second chance."

Learn more about how Subaru is supporting shelter animals across the country at Subaru.com/pets.

About Subaru of America, Inc.

Subaru of America, Inc. (SOA) is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Subaru Corporation of Japan. Headquartered in Camden, N.J., the company markets and distributes Subaru vehicles, parts, and accessories through a network of about 640 retailers across the United States. All Subaru products are manufactured in zero-landfill plants, including Subaru of Indiana Automotive, Inc., the only U.S. automobile manufacturing plant designated a backyard wildlife habitat by the National Wildlife Federation. SOA is guided by the Subaru Love Promise®, which is the company's vision to show love and respect to everyone and to support its communities and customers nationwide. Over the past 20 years, SOA and the SOA Foundation have donated more than $357 million to causes that Subaru and its customers care about, and Subaru employees have logged more than 130,000 volunteer hours. Through these actions and more, Subaru is dedicated to being More Than a Car Company® and to making the world a better place.

For additional information, visit media.subaru.com.

Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and YouTube.

About the ASPCA

The ASPCA® (The American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals®) believes every animal deserves to live free from suffering. For 160 years, we've been on the frontlines to save, transform and protect millions of lives in the fight against animal cruelty. As the nation's first and leading animal welfare organization, we assist animals in need through on-the-ground disaster and cruelty interventions, behavioral rehabilitation, animal relocation and placement, legal and legislative advocacy, and the advancement of the sheltering and veterinary communities through research, training and resources. As a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit corporation with more than 2 million supporters nationwide, our commitment to eliminating animal cruelty is unwavering. For more information, visit aspca.org, and follow the ASPCA on Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok.

[Nasdaq: IHRT] is the leading audio media company in America, with nine out of ten Americans listening to iHeart broadcast radio in every month. iHeart's broadcast radio assets alone have a larger audience in the U.S. than any other media outlet and over four times the ad-enabled audience of the largest digital only audio service. iHeart is the largest podcast publisher according to both Podtrac and Triton, with more downloads than the next two podcast publishers combined, has the most recognizable live events across all genres of music, has the number one social footprint among audio players, has the highest-reach and most engaged influencers, and is the only fully integrated audio ad tech solution across broadcast, streaming and podcasts. The company continues to leverage its strong audience connection and unparalleled consumer reach to build new platforms, products and services. Visit iHeartMedia.com for more company information.

releases.title: Under The Motto "Distribution Is The New Moat," Nomada Fund Launches As The World's First New Media Fund
releases.body:
Backed by leading media outlets and communities in the U.S. and Latin America, the fund invests distribution instead of capital as AI makes software cheaper to build and community and trust become key advantages.

MIAMI, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nomada Fund today launched as the world's first New Media fund. Instead of capital, it invests Media Credits in sustained distribution across more than 10 New Media platforms, including newsletters, podcasts, communities, events, SEO, and GEO.

The firm is backed by ILB Media Group, a New Media conglomerate of more than 20 finance and investment outlets in the U.S. and Latin America, giving portfolio startups early distribution to investors, founders, and customers.

A proven model

Nomada Fund uses the same financial structure as Media for Equity (M4E) funds, where media groups trade advertising space for equity, with two differences: it operates on New Media platforms instead of TV, radio, or print, and it invests at Pre-seed and Seed rather than at maturity. This makes it the world's first Distribution for Equity (D4E) fund.

With AI agents and no-code tools, a small team can recreate a working product in days. What competitors cannot copy is the trust of people who follow a company, open its emails, and recommend it. Hence the firm's motto: "Distribution is the new moat." A startup's moat, what protects it from competitors, used to be technology. Today, it is the ability to reach the right people and turn visibility into trust.

"A startup's most valuable asset is no longer just its product, but its brand and relationships," said Jose Kont.

The team

Co-founder and Managing Partner Jose Kont is a New Media expert with 20+ years of experience and partner at Impacta VC, CAFI, and Cuantico VP. Co-founder and Venture Partner Israel García Ballesteros is CEO and founder of Startuplinks, the leading Spanish-speaking community of VC funds and accelerators, with 270+ institutional members. They are joined by Venture Partners Rodrigo Giacaman (Startups Latam), Ileana Figueroa (Pulso Capital), and Jose Manuel Aguirre (TECHLA), and by legal partner Eugenia di Marco, trained at UC Berkeley School of Law and MIT.

Rival IQ's 2026 Social Media Industry Benchmark Report puts brands' median Instagram engagement at 0.30% of followers, down from 0.36%. Nomada Fund helps startups move that "rented attention" into owned channels like newsletters, communities, and events.

"When anyone can build software over a weekend, the edge goes to whoever reaches the right people first," the firm said.

releases.body:
Other highlights: 1906 Indian Camelback motorized bicycle, $61,500; Gilbarco gas pump with porcelain Mohawk Indian face, $31,980; circa-1930s Zeroline single-sided porcelain sign, $28,800

DENVER, Pa., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The two top-selling lots at Morphy's October 4 Automobilia, Petroliana & Advertising auction were full-size vintage automobiles. An impressive 1932 Cadillac 355-B seven-passenger Imperial limousine registered to notorious gangster Al Capone sped off for $78,000, while a well-documented silver-blue metallic1964 Chevrolet Impala hardtop crossed the finish line at $74,400.

The rest of the auction consisted of more than 650 lots of motoring-related signage, service station items and vehicles designed to please collectors at every price point. The event was held live at Morphy's Pennsylvania gallery, with all forms of remote bidding available. Morphy's has long-been renowned as the auction house collectors depend on for rare automobilia and petroliana.

The 1932 Cadillac 355-B seven-passenger Imperial limousine with body by Fisher was finished in cream with burgundy fenders and accents. A binder documented nearly $95,000 worth of mechanical restoration, refurbishment and detailing had been performed by Classic & Exotic Service in 2011 and 2012. A New York Certificate of Sale identified notorious Prohibition-era gangster Alphonse "Al" Capone as its original purchaser/owner. Rochelle Cadillac Co., of New Rochelle, New York, was shown as the seller.

The well-documented 1964 Chevrolet Impala finished in silver blue metallic over a coordinated blue bucket-seat interior had a VIN # of 41447S178226, identifying it as a genuine St Louis-built V-8 Super Sport hardtop. Power was supplied by Chevy's dual-quad 409-c.i. engine, producing 425 horsepower thru 11.0:1 compression. The odometer displayed 52,659 miles. The car started with ease and the drive was very smooth.

Following the two automobiles, the auction's number three top achiever was a1906 Indian Camelback motorized bicycle built by The Hendree Manufacturing Company (later The Indian Motocycle Company, with no "R" in motorcycle). The bike was a true survivor in barn-fresh condition, retaining its factory paint job in Springfield Blue, while the 311 cubic inch, 2.25-hp air-cooled single-cylinder motor with a production number of 2877 was untouched, with all major components intact. The motor turned over with good compression, the wheels spun freely, and the brakes worked just fine. One lucky bidder "rode" it home for $61,500.

A Gilbarco gas pump originally found in Northern California, one of very few known examples with a porcelain Mohawk Indian computing face, changed hands for $31,980, topping the $30,000 high estimate. The pump's condition was described as being like NOS (new/old stock). The color and gloss were perfect, with no notable wear to the Indian graphic, and it lit up nicely.

There were two bona fide "sleepers" in the sale. One was a circa-1930s single-sided porcelain flange sign graded 9.0 for the Pickwick Stages Ticket Office, an excellent example of a seldom-seen sign. Each side displayed excellent color and gloss, with no noticeable field wear. The 28¾-inch by 25½-inch sign more than doubled the $8,000 high estimate, reaching $19,680.

The second of the two sleepers was just as impressive. It was a circa-1930s Zeroline ("The Standard Oil For Motor Cars") single-sided porcelain sign, 23¾ inches in diameter and graded 9.0 out of 10 for condition. The sign showed very good color throughout and a great graphic, which no doubt helped it to more than double its $12,000 high estimate and realize a robust $28,800.

To discuss consigning to a future Automobilia, Petroliana & Advertising auction, or other auction hosted by Morphy's, call Dan Morphy at 877-968-8880 or email 425004@email4pr.com. All enquiries are kept strictly confidential, and there is never an obligation to consign. Online: www.morphyauctions.com.

releases.title: TECNO and BBC StoryWorks Unveil New Film Exploring the Human Stories Behind "100 Portraits of Becoming"
releases.body:
As part of TECNO and artist Angélica Dass's global "100 Portraits of Becoming" project, the new BBC StoryWorks film reveals the personal journeys behind the portraits, bringing to life a shared vision of seeing beyond the image to understand the people behind it.

HONG KONG, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Global innovative technology brand TECNO has jointly produced and released a new film with  BBC StoryWorks to unveil the project of "100 Portraits of Becoming," a two-year global portrait project co-created by TECNO and internationally acclaimed visual artist Angélica Dass which started from Kenya as the first chapter. Building on TECNO's philosophy of inclusive imaging technology and Angélica Dass's distinctive approach to portraiture, the project plans to bring together 100 portraits and personal stories across five countries, moving beyond visual representation to explore the individuality and humanity behind each portrait. Through the personal journeys featured in the film, audiences gain a glimpse into the energy and aspirations of people navigating today's changing world — how they are finding their own paths, shaping new possibilities and imagining who they want to become.

The film also explores the shared vision behind TECNO's collaboration with Dass. While TECNO's Universal Tone technology seeks to fairly represent the beauty of different skin tones and human diversity, Dass's work has long challenged the labels and assumptions through which we see others. Together, they bring a shared belief to "100 Portraits of Becoming": that being seen is about more than appearance — it is also about being understood for who we are.

Through the film, this idea comes to life in Kenya, where the first chapter of "100 Portraits of Becoming" began. It introduces some of the people behind the portraits, each with a different story of finding their own way forward. For agripreneur Alex Mutua Muli, opportunity wasn't something to seek elsewhere, but something to create at home. By connecting local farmers to wider markets, he is helping build a future in the community where he grew up. Alexander Odhiambo took a different path, turning an uncertain start to his career into a new beginning. From a small apartment in Nairobi, he co-founded a software company that has since grown to serve markets across Africa, opening doors for others along the way. And for Jelimo Cheboi, what began as a small WhatsApp group became something much bigger. As co-founder of GirlSkate Nairobi, she has helped turn a shared passion for skateboarding into a growing community where girls and women can challenge expectations, find belonging, and express themselves on their own terms.

Their stories are different, but each challenges an assumption about what is possible — whether it is where opportunity can be found, what a career can become, or who gets to belong. Together, they offer a glimpse of the people behind the portraits, whose lives cannot be summed up by a single image or label.

"The beauty of this project was the chance to look beyond an image and let people tell their own stories. Through their passions and experiences, every person we met brought a vibrancy and depth to the film that a single portrait may not fully capture. We hope the film will encourage audiences to see people with a little more curiosity and a little more understanding," said Tom Deakin, Director, Content Strategy at BBC StoryWorks APAC.

"100 Portraits of Becoming" is a two-year global project bringing together 100 portraits and personal stories across Kenya, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Brazil. Together, these portraits and stories will form a growing collection that celebrates the many different ways of being human — 100 people, 100 stories and 100 ways to see humanity. Following its first chapter in Kenya, the project will continue its journey to more countries around the world, uncovering new stories, experiences and perspectives on what it means to become. Stay tuned for more inspiring stories and the latest updates from "100 Portraits of Becoming" on the BBC StoryWorks project page and "100 Portraits of Becoming" by TECNO and Angelica Dass official website.

About TECNO

As a global innovative technology brand with operations in over 70 markets, TECNO has been committed to revolutionizing the digital experience in global emerging markets, relentlessly pushing for the perfect integration of contemporary, aesthetic design with the latest technologies and AI. TECNO offers a wide range of smartphones, smart wearables, laptops and tablets, smart gaming, HiOS operating systems and smart home products. Guided by its brand essence of "Stop At Nothing," TECNO is committed to unlocking the newest technologies and AI-powered new experiences for forward-looking individuals, inspiring them to never stop pursuing their best selves and their best futures. For more information, please visit TECNO's official site: www.tecno-mobile.com.

About "100 Portraits of Becoming" by TECNO and Angélica Dass

"100 Portraits of Becoming" is a global portrait project created by TECNO together with internationally recognized artist Angélica Dass. Over two years, it will produce one hundred portraits across five countries — Kenya, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Brazil — pairing Dass's portrait methodology with TECNO's Universal Tone inclusive imaging technology. Each portrait moves beyond a face to the person behind it: to lives unfolding across different cultures, generations and moments of social change. One hundred portraits become one hundred ways of seeing humanity — and one growing archive of who we are, told by the people living it. To learn more, please visit: https://www.tecno-mobile.com/100portraitsofbecoming/.

The show will spotlight the beloved '60s soul classics covered on By Any Means: The Album — featuring music from and inspired by the feature film BY ANY MEANS, starring Mark Wahlberg and Yahya Abdul-Matteen II — plus the original title track written by 17-time Oscar® nominee Diane Warren, performed by Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees The Isley Brothers and Nashville singer-songwriter David Kushner. "By Any Means" is widely predicted to be a 2027 Academy Award® nominee for Best Original Song, including by outlets like Variety, TheWrap, and all 4 critics in Awards Watch's 2027 Oscars predictions: https://awardswatch.com/2027-oscar-predictions-all-below-the-line-and-feature-categories/

Ole Smoky Distillery is the marketing partner for By Any Means: The Album and the Moonshine & Music Tour. CEO Mike Novy says, "At Ole Smoky, we believe great music is meant to be shared. That's why we're proud to support emerging artists through this 7-city tour, giving fans the chance to discover new stars while celebrating some of the songs that have shaped American music. Whether it's gathering around a stage or sharing a jar of Ole Smoky, we're all about creating moments that bring people together."

The Moonshine & Music Tour will play 7 cities with substantial Black music history: St. Louis, Nashville, New Orleans, Atlanta, Jacksonville, Myrtle Beach, and Los Angeles. Opening the tour in St. Louis is significant, as the Gateway City is home to "By Any Means" title track performers The Isley Brothers, whose breakout hit "Shout" was released in 1959. Jacksonville is where Ray Charles — whose "Hit the Road Jack" and "Georgia On My Mind" are covered on the album by Brandy & Pynk Beard and 2'Live Bre & The BoykinZ, respectively — began his performing career at age 15, including at the Ritz Theatre.

Apple Music's Color Me Country Radio host Rissi Palmer selected a local opening act at every show. Palmer — who received the Academy of Country Music's 2024 ACM Lift Every Voice Award — remarks "Color Me Country Radio and The Color Me Country Foundation are so proud to have handpicked each of the openers for this tour. I believe in lifting up my peers through grants and opportunities, and this partnership with Anzie Blue Records and Ole Smoky Distillery has made that mission possible with this historic and culturally significant tour. Y'all are in for a soulful and joyful experience!"

By Any Means: The Album was released on September 25, and its Special Edition vinyl is available for pre-order now here: https://theorchard.indiemerch.com/collections/anzie-blue/products/by-any-means-the-album?variant=67649569292470 The album is executive produced by Surf Club co-founder Hit-Boy, whose extensive production credits include Beyoncé, Jay-Z, Travis Scott and Drake, and Dr. Blum, whose credits include Twenty One Pilots, Big Sean and Nas. Parasol Music, co-founded by Martin Wave, served as a creative and production partner on the album.

Musically directed by Anzie Blue Records country artist and GRAMMY® nominated songwriter Pynk Beard, By Any Means: The Album brings together artists across generations and genres to reinterpret songs connected to the sound and spirit of the 1960s. Brandy, Kashus Culpepper, Keb' Mo', Tone Stith, and others put their own stamp on songs from iconic artists — including a dozen Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees, with three in the Rock Hall's premiere induction class: Ray Charles, Sam Cooke, and James Brown. The "By Any Means" original title track makes The Isley Brothers the latest of more than 40 Rock Hall inductees to release a Diane Warren composition.

Much of the album was recorded at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama in less than a week — bringing the project to a place with deep roots in American soul music and to Pynk Beard's home state.

The official "By Any Means" music video, featuring The Isley Brothers and Kushner, was released September 4. Watch here: https://youtu.be/pZaWebkmJDY Directed by Fran Strine of F26 Productions — who directed Dolly Parton's Live at London O2 Arena film — the video was followed on September 25 by Pynk Beard's "We Shall Overcome," also directed by Strine: https://youtu.be/iRaA3oz8U44 Strine is directing an upcoming music video for "Bring It on Home to Me" with Keb' Mo and Pynk Beard.

Net proceeds from By Any Means: The Album benefit the Black Music Action Coalition (BMAC), supporting the organization's work to advance equity, expand opportunity, and create pathways for the next generation of artists, creatives, and music industry professionals. Anzie Blue Records and Ole Smoky were among the sponsors of BMAC's 2026 gala, which took place during the album's release week and honored Black music icons Patti LaBelle, Public Enemy, and Common. https://variety.com/2026/music/news/patti-labelle-common-public-enemy-bmac-gala-2026-1236875682/

The Moonshine & Music Tour follows By Any Means: The Album artists Pynk Beard, Steve Ray Ladson, and The BoykinZ playing an acclaimed arena show at the State Fair of Texas — the nation's largest attended state fair — upon the album's release. Ladson appeared on WFAA ABC program "Good Morning Texas" to discuss By Any Means: The Album, the impact of its BMAC benefit, and Oscar buzz surrounding the title track. Watch here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zG2KG5lfCM0 The tour was then announced by Pynk Beard on WSMV NBC program "Today In Nashville." Watch here: https://youtu.be/iO0Jf5-I9BI

releases.title: Vail Turns Up the Volume, Unveils First Wave of Artists for Its Biggest Music Season Yet
releases.body:
ILLENIUM and Ian Asher kick off Vail's biggest music season yet, alongside seven on-mountain performances and two brand-new venues

VAIL, Colo., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- With the first snowfall on Vail Mountain's peaks this week and snowmaking kicked off last night, anticipation for winter is building fast. This season, Vail is raising the bar with its most ambitious music lineup yet, bringing more live music, more venues and more unforgettable performances to the mountain and village than ever before.

Headliners and New Venues

Kicking off the season on December 11, GRAMMY®-nominated, multi-platinum artist ILLENIUM will headline a marquee performance at the new Dobson Arena, ushering in a winter packed with music experiences designed for the mountains. With the potential for surprise performances throughout the weekend, fans will want to keep a close eye on social media at @VailMtn for artist announcements and unexpected moments.

On January 16, Southern California DJ, producer and remix sensation Ian Asher takes over Dobson Arena. Best known for his viral electronic and house remixes, including the billion-stream "Makeba" remix that earned Remix of the Year honors, Asher represents the next generation of dance music talent and expands Vail's growing lineup of nationally recognized artists.

Freshly transformed into a premier entertainment venue, Dobson Arena combines more than 56,000 square feet of state-of-the-art production capabilities with unmistakable alpine character, creating a concert experience unlike any other in the Rockies.

"There's nothing quite like live music in the mountains, and we're excited to bring even more of it to Vail this winter," said Shaydar Edelmann, vice president and chief operating officer of Vail Mountain. "Working alongside the Town of Vail and our community partners, we're creating more opportunities for guests to come together and enjoy incredible music in a legendary setting."

This winter builds on a breakout 2025/26 season, when Vail hosted on-mountain performances from globally recognized artists including SOFI TUKKER, Dillon Francis, Chris Lorenzo and John Summit. Always dreaming bigger, Vail is expanding its music footprint even further with seven on-mountain performances, three more than last season, plus two brand-new music venues.

Following the success of last season's first-ever sunrise concert beneath the Legendary Back Bowls sign, Vail is once again pushing the boundaries of what an alpine music experience can be. Additional artists, venues and mountain activations will be unveiled throughout the season, giving fans new reasons to visit and new ways to experience music at elevation. Announcements will be released throughout the winter on @VailMtn.

Vail Après Scene

As Vail's live music lineup grows, so does the experience surrounding it. This winter, the destination will pair headline performances and on-mountain sets with a robust lineup of après events, culinary offerings and nightlife experiences throughout the village.

  • NEW! The Vail Ice Bar: A beloved Vail tradition returns. Located next to the Legendary Back Bowls Gate, the reimagined Vail Ice Bar blends alpine nostalgia with a lively outdoor gathering space for drinks, music and après in the heart of Vail Mountain. See images of the historic Vail Ice Bar HERE.
  • Après All Day at Express Lift (base of Gondola One, starting opening day): More than 50 performing artists, nearly double last season with live DJs every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 2:30–5:30 p.m., in collaboration with Vail Mountain partner Outer Range Brewing. See full schedule HERE. 
  • Chasing Rabbits: When the lifts stop spinning, the night is just getting started. The Rabbit Hole returns with high-energy DJ sets and unforgettable winter nights, following performances by Loud Luxury, Dombresky and Chris Lorenzo. This winter's lineup, coming soon, already includes a Coachella headliner, a Billboard Music Awards nominee and internationally recognized DJs.
  • Stoke Sessions: Live Music every Friday for the first month of the ski season in Vail. Bundle up, sip something warm, and celebrate the season with the Vail community. Lineup Announcement coming soon! Follow @discovervailcolorado to be the first to know.

Epic Passes on Sale for the 2026/27 Winter Season

Epic Passes are on sale now and with new savings for young adults, skiers and riders ages 13-30 can save 20% on an Epic Pass or Epic Local Pass. Plus, guests who purchase an Epic Pass or Epic Local Pass now will receive five Epic Friend Tickets offering 50% off adult lift tickets, making it easier to bring the crew along and save. Epic Friend Tickets can also be used for 25% off child lift ticket prices.

About Vail Mountain

Vail Mountain spans more than 5,300 acres of terrain, including the Legendary Back Bowls and Blue Sky Basin. Founded in 1962, Vail is one of the world's premier mountain destinations and a part of the Vail Resorts network connected by the Epic Pass. For more information, visit Vail.com.

releases.title: Doussan Music Group Expands with New Nashville Office and Leadership Appointments
releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. and COVINGTON, La., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Doussan Music Group (DMG Presents), an independent live entertainment and concert promotion company, is expanding its national presence with the opening of a second office in Nashville, Tennessee, and key leadership appointments.

The new office in Nashville's Wedgewood-Houston neighborhood complements the company's headquarters in Covington, Louisiana, strengthening its connections with artists, agents, venues, and industry partners nationwide.

DMG's expansion follows an extremely successful period of touring and concert promotion. In 2025 and 2026, the company promoted and produced seven college stadium dates featuring The Boys From Oklahoma package, featuring Turnpike Troubadours and Cross Canadian Ragweed, with all shows selling out or nearly selling out. DMG also co promoted Alan Jackson's final touring performance at Nashville's Nissan Stadium, capping Alan's previous two-year, 10-city arena tour. Upcoming engagements include a 16-date fall tour with platinum-selling country artist Jon Pardi and 10 November dates for Aaron Lewis's Acoustic Origins tour. Additional tours planned for 2027 are expected to be announced this fall.

To support its continued growth, DMG has strengthened its leadership team with three personnel updates:

  • Anna Margaret Kilgore joined the company as Talent Buyer in April 2026. With experience in marketing, project management, and touring promotion, she will focus on expanding DMG's event portfolio and building relationships with artists, agencies, and venues.



  • Hale Neitzschman has been named Director of Finance. He will oversee financial operations, event settlements, strategic planning, and financial processes supporting the company's growing touring schedule.



  • Rebecca Saladis has been promoted to Director of Booking, Touring, & Artist Relations. She will lead booking strategy, tour execution, and artist relations.

"Opening our Nashville office, in Wedgewood Houston, the new music hub, is a natural next step in our evolution," said Russell Doussan, President and CEO. He emphasized the company's accomplishments over the past three years and its commitment to working with talented artists to create memorable live music experiences. Founded on artist-first partnerships and exceptional live entertainment, Doussan Music Group continues to expand its concert promotion, tour production, artist relations, and venue partnerships across the country.

releases.title: Lumara Film Festival Announces Finalists for Inaugural AI Film Festival
releases.body:
Presented by MoonPay and Venice, the inaugural Lumara Film Festival festival received more than 700 submissions from filmmakers worldwide and today reveals six finalists competing for the Grand Prize and Jury Selection, with winners announced live at the World Premiere at the Roxy Hotel Cinema in New York on October 26. The evening will also feature an exclusive extended prologue of jury member and AI filmmaker Gossip Goblin's new film "Gods Don't Give Gifts.", the first-ever AI film slated for a wide theatrical release at the end of this year.

NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lumara Film Festival, an independent film festival for the artists defining a new era of filmmaking, presented by MoonPay and Venice, has announced the six finalists competing for its Grand Prize and Jury Selection awards and the 16 nominees for its five category awards.

Lumara was created to find and celebrate the films coming out of a transformative moment for cinema. AI has given filmmakers a new set of tools and a new creative language that opens the door to opportunities otherwise unavailable to many. Submissions were open from July 24 to September 15 and drew more than 700 films. Entry was free and open worldwide, and filmmakers could use any AI filmmaking platform available.

Films were evaluated by a jury of the world's leading AI filmmakers and internet-culture figures including Voidstomper, Gossip Goblin, Chris White (executive producer, A24's "Backrooms"), JBoogxCreative, Heavy Pulp, SÜNDERMANN, BLVCKL!GHT, Ansem and FaZe Banks. Films were judged on the strength of the idea, the quality of the storytelling, and how well the filmmaker used AI.

The six finalists will now move into competition for the Grand Prize of $32,000 and 3.2 million Venice AI credits and the Jury Selection award of $20,000 and 2 million Venice AI credits.

The finalists are:

  • "Black Thunder" (Ryan Lightbourn)
  • "Candy" (Jiaze Li)
  • "Gabriel" (T Zhang)
  • "Killabears – The Broadcast" (Mikael Tyrsen)
  • "Living with a Merman" (Chris Capel)
  • "Mianmian" (Yingjie Chen)

This year's categories and their nominees include:

  • Terminal Award (best experimental film), $12,000 and 1.2 million Venice AI credits
    • "REVIVER" (Aleksey Dor)
    • "Stories My Great Great Great Grandmother Told Me" (Philippe Noguchi)
    • "THE LAST TRIBE" (Stephane Benini)
  • Serenissima Award (best film made with Venice), $12,000 and 1.2 million Venice AI credits
    • "Black Thunder" (Ryan Lightbourn)
    • "Er Loop" (Marco Magario)
    • "Never Forget" (Allan Ecax)
  • Get Shorty Award (best film under two minutes), $8,000 and 800,000 Venice AI credits
    • "Ato de [Later]" (Luke Mazey)
    • "COMPULSION" (Gyuseon Lee)
    • "Do Not Disturb" (Adrian Daniel Botnariu)
    • "Summer Afternoon, July 1994" (Charlie Park)
  • Mouse Award (best film for children or young adults), $8,000 and 800,000 Venice AI credits
    • "Far away home" (Siping Song)
    • "FIX" (Eunha Lee, Sora Lee and Hakhoon Lee)
    • "Roraima" (Ishan Devare Modi)
  • Rekt Award (best satire, comedy or musical about finance, markets or crypto), $8,000 and 800,000 Venice AI credits
    • "Great Pepe Wars" (Aiden Guo)
    • "JUST SAY SOLANA" (Yassine Le Gall)
    • "ROLL EVERYTHING" (Ashanth Phillips)

The winner of each category award will be announced on the Venice and MoonPay channels.

The finalists will be screened in full at the inaugural Lumara screening and awards night taking place on October 26 at the Roxy Hotel Cinema in New York City, with winners announced at the event.

The evening will also include screenings of the category-winning films, and new work previews from members of the jury, including an exclusive an exclusive extended prologue of Gossip Goblin's new film God's Don't Give Gifts, the first AI film slated for a wide theatrical release at the end of this year.

The winning films will premiere online on X and YouTube on October 27.

About MoonPay

MoonPay is a global financial technology company that provides infrastructure for moving value across traditional and digital financial systems. Founded in 2019, MoonPay serves more than 35 million customers in 180 countries and more than 1500 enterprise clients across crypto and fintech. Its products support payments, trading, commerce, stablecoin infrastructure and other services that connect conventional payment networks with blockchain-based financial rails. MoonPay maintains regulatory licenses and authorizations in multiple jurisdictions, including the United States and European Union. For more information, visit www.moonpay.com.

About Venice

Venice is a privacy-first AI platform built for unlimited creative freedom. It gives filmmakers unrestricted access to the world's leading video, image and audio models in one private workspace, alongside frontier text and code models, without censorship and without surveillance. Trusted by 5 million users, Venice runs leading video models including Seedance 2.5, image models from OpenAI, Google and xAI, and voice and music generation, so a filmmaker can make the story exactly as they envision it, rather than the one a platform allows. Venice is accessible through its app and API. Learn more at venice.ai.

releases.title: New Industry Report: Franchise Demand Is Normalizing, but Advertising Engagement Is Surging
releases.body:
Reshift Media's flagship quarterly franchise development report reveals a 40.7% decline in ownership search demand from early-2026 highs, while advertising engagement rises 26.8%, inquiry conversion increases 166.6%, and lead generation costs fall 68%.

NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Franchise ownership interest in the United States is returning to historic levels following an exceptional surge earlier this year, and new research suggests prospective franchisees are becoming significantly more responsive to recruitment advertising. According to The Franchise Development Outlook: Q3 2026, the flagship quarterly franchise development intelligence report from Reshift Media and Franify, active franchise ownership search demand has declined considerably from its February peak while advertising engagement and inquiry conversion rates have strengthened dramatically.

The full Q3 2026 Franchise Development Outlook report, available as a free download, includes proprietary franchise development indices, historical trends, advertising performance data, economic analysis, and forecasts through March 2027.

The report's proprietary Franchise Development Demand Index (FDDI), which tracks U.S. Google search interest related to franchise ownership, reached 107.6 in September 2026, down 40.7% from its February peak of 181.4. Despite the decline, search demand remains 7.6% above its 2022–2024 historical baseline. Reshift Media forecasts a continued return toward normal levels through the remainder of 2026, followed by a modest seasonal recovery in early 2027.

However, the report reveals a contrasting trend in franchise recruitment advertising. Engagement with outbound social media franchise advertisements increased 26.8% compared with Q3 2025, while the rate at which advertising clicks generated franchise inquiries increased 166.6%. At the same time, the indexed cost per inquiry declined 68.0% year-over-year.

"The most interesting finding is the growing disconnect between active franchise ownership searches and advertising engagement," said Steve Buors, CEO and Co-Founder of Reshift Media. "We're seeing fewer people actively searching for franchise opportunities than we did earlier this year, but the people responding to franchise advertising are engaging at much higher rates. For franchisors, that suggests there is still considerable opportunity to generate interest and inquiries with the right advertising strategy, even as overall search demand returns to more typical levels."

Franchise Ownership Demand Expected to Normalize Through Early 2027

The FDDI measures relative search interest across a basket of franchise ownership-related terms, indexed to a 2022–2024 baseline of 100. During Q3 2026, the index averaged 111.9, representing a 15.2% decline compared with the same quarter in 2025.

Although active search demand remains above historical norms, the report forecasts continued moderation through Q4 2026, with the FDDI projected to average 102.8. A modest seasonal rebound is expected in Q1 2027, when the index is forecast to average 111.0, considerably below the exceptional levels recorded in early 2026.

The research also identifies elevated financing costs, persistent inflation, weak consumer confidence, and broader economic uncertainty as factors that may continue to influence prospective franchisees' investment decisions.

Advertising Performance Points to a More Responsive Audience

While the volume of active franchise ownership searches has declined, Reshift Media's proprietary advertising indices suggest that people encountering franchise opportunities through outbound advertising are increasingly willing to engage.

The Franchise Advertising Engagement Index reached 117.4 in Q3 2026, its strongest third-quarter reading in the available dataset. The Franchise Advertising Inquiry Conversion Index climbed to 229.5, indicating that a substantially higher proportion of advertising clicks are generating recorded franchise inquiries compared with a year earlier.

These improvements have contributed to a sharp reduction in inquiry generation costs. The Franchise Advertising Cost Per Inquiry Index reached 40.2 in September 2026, down from 125.8 in Q3 2025.

The findings suggest that although fewer individuals may be proactively researching franchise ownership, there remains strong interest among prospective candidates who encounter relevant opportunities through advertising.

"For franchise development teams, this reinforces the importance of reaching beyond people who are already searching for a franchise," added Buors. "Search marketing remains essential, but effective outbound advertising can introduce franchise opportunities to people who may be interested in business ownership without actively looking for it. The data suggests those audiences are responding particularly well right now."

The report cautions that higher advertising engagement and inquiry conversion do not necessarily translate directly into qualified franchise candidates or completed franchise sales.

AI Is Emerging as Another Franchise Discovery Channel

Beyond advertising performance, the report examines the growing influence of artificial intelligence on franchise candidate research.

Research cited in the report indicates that ChatGPT usage among U.S. adults has increased substantially, reaching 44% in 2026. Additionally, a September 2026 study found that 27% of surveyed franchise prospects identified ChatGPT as one of their most useful tools when researching franchise opportunities.

These findings highlight the growing importance of ensuring franchise information is accessible, accurate, and discoverable across AI-powered research platforms, alongside traditional search engines, franchise directories, and digital advertising channels.

About The Franchise Development Outlook

The Franchise Development Outlook is Reshift Media and Franify's flagship quarterly franchise development intelligence report, providing original research into U.S. franchise ownership demand, recruitment advertising performance, economic conditions, and emerging candidate research behaviors.

The Q3 2026 edition includes four proprietary franchise development indices, historical trend analysis, advertising engagement and inquiry conversion data, economic indicators, and forecasts through March 2027.

The complete Franchise Development Outlook: Q3 2026 report is available to download free of charge.

About Reshift Media and Franify

Reshift Media is an award-winning digital marketing agency specializing in franchise and multi-location organizations. Serving more than 200 clients across 22 countries, Reshift Media provides digital marketing strategy, paid media, search engine optimization, social media marketing, website development, and proprietary marketing technology designed for the unique needs of franchise organizations.

Franify is Reshift Media's proprietary franchise digital marketing platform, designed to help franchisors and franchisees coordinate, execute, and optimize digital marketing campaigns across multiple locations.

For more information, visit www.reshiftmedia.com.

releases.body:
LOS ANGELES, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Recorded in 2001. Held back for the good of rock 'n' roll. TRAILER PARK PAM has arrived.

As Universal Music Entertainment debuts the self-titled original album today, the band is finally ready to reveal its bold strategy: wait 25 years for rock 'n' roll to be declared dead, then unveil an album recorded when it was still breathing.

The band — Keith Megna on vocals, his brother David Megna on bass, Hans Hettich on lead guitar, and Chuck Sparks on drums — spent the last quarter century allowing the world to catch up.

"We could see where things were headed in 2001," said lead singer Keith Megna. "We figured we'd let the entire music industry change, collapse, rebuild itself, and then see if Friday was a good day to release it."

"The time is now," said David Megna. "Some bands are ahead of their time. We wanted documentation."

Former manager John Asher confirmed that the delay was absolutely intentional.

"A lot of people would call this an unreleased album," said Asher. "We prefer an extremely exclusive listening period."

This time capsule recording, produced by Jerry Harrison of Talking Heads, will make you want to call your Mom after listening to the heartfelt "Photo Memories." Break out an old Hendrix vinyl after exorcising the ghosts of "Falling Stars."  Or smash your TV by the time "Talk Circus" reaches its final chord. 

Now, after surviving the death of the CD, the rise of streaming, and several generations of people explaining that rock is dead, TRAILER PARK PAM is ready to be unearthed.

The wait is over.

Out October 16, 2026 on all streaming platforms.

releases.body:
The upcoming Toronto conference will bring together clinical research leaders to discuss Canada's competitiveness, innovations in clinical trial design and opportunities to improve patient access to research.

TORONTO, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Xtalks is pleased to announce its role as an official Media Partner for the 2026 CTO Clinical Trials Conference, taking place November 4–5, 2026, at the Hilton Toronto. Hosted by Clinical Trials Ontario (CTO), the two-day event will bring together leaders from the pharmaceutical and medical device industries, healthcare, academia, research institutions and patient organizations to exchange ideas on the future of clinical trials in Canada.

The 2026 conference will explore how Canada can strengthen its position in global clinical research, with discussions on improving trial efficiency, integrating research into patient care and expanding access to clinical trials.

"CTO's Clinical Trials Conference has become one of Canada's most important forums for bringing together diverse voices from across the clinical trials community to share knowledge, challenge thinking and drive innovation," said Susan Marlin, President & CEO, CTO. "We look forward to welcoming delegates and presenters from across Canada and around the world to help shape better, smarter and faster clinical trials that ultimately deliver greater value for patients and participants."

The program will feature keynote presentations from Christine Elliott, former Ontario Minister of Health and Deputy Premier, and Dr. Tor Biering-Sørensen, Professor and Founding Head of the Center for Translational Cardiology and Pragmatic Randomized Trials. Elliott will examine why Canada needs to become more competitive in clinical research and better connect research with patient care, while Dr. Biering-Sørensen will discuss clinical trial innovations from Denmark and the European Union (EU).

Other sessions will address the modernization of clinical trial regulations, the use of AI and health data in research, and efforts to accelerate study start-up. This includes a discussion of early lessons from CTO's QuickSTART initiative, which has demonstrated a 45-day study start-up timeline in its first studies.

Attendees will also gain insights into psilocybin research, including clinical trials underway in Canada and the opportunities and challenges surrounding psychedelic-assisted care.

The agenda will also explore equitable access to clinical trials, Indigenous research sovereignty and approaches to making research more patient-centred. Sessions will examine advance consent in acute stroke trials and how a breast cancer study challenged conventional treatment approaches.

"Having attended last year's CTO Clinical Trials Conference, I was struck by the energy in the room and the thoughtful questions and exchanges among attendees," said Soumya Shashikumar, Senior Life Sciences Journalist at Xtalks. "As a Media Partner, Xtalks looks forward to support this year's discussions on clinical trial innovation, efficiency and patient access."

releases.title: From Raider to Bronco: GRCC, WMU to Guarantee Admission for Transfer Students
releases.body:
New Bronco Bound partnership offers a direct path to a bachelor's degree, guaranteed scholarships and more

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A GRCC Raider today. A WMU Bronco tomorrow. For Grand Rapids Community College students dreaming of earning a bachelor's degree, that next step is about to become a lot more certain.

Through a new partnership called the Bronco Bound Guarantee, students who earn an associate degree at GRCC will be guaranteed admission to Western Michigan University, along with an annual scholarship ranging from $1,000 to $4,500 for eligible students.

Leaders from both institutions will make the partnership official during a signing ceremony at 3 p.m. Friday, Oct. 16, at GRCC's Applied Technology Center, Secchia Piazza, on the college's main campus in Grand Rapids. Media are invited to attend.

"Strong partnerships create strong pathways for students. This agreement reflects a shared commitment to making higher education more accessible, affordable and connected," said GRCC President Dr. Kathryn A. Rogalski. "We are proud to partner with Western Michigan University, an institution that recognizes the quality of a GRCC education and the strong foundation our students bring to their next chapter. Together, we are creating more opportunities for students to achieve their educational goals and build a brighter future for themselves and our communities."

The Bronco Bound Guarantee is designed to take some uncertainty out of transferring from community college to a four-year university.

"Having led a community college, I know the important role these institutions play in helping students discover their potential and pursue their goals," said WMU President Russ Kavalhuna.

"Our partnership with Grand Rapids Community College builds on that foundation. We want students to arrive at Western knowing they belong here, find opportunities to put their learning into practice and have the support to thrive, graduate, and build meaningful careers."

In addition to guaranteed admission, qualifying GRCC students will have their WMU application fee waived and receive scholarship consideration automatically, with eligible students guaranteed an annual award of $1,000 to $4,500.

Students will also have access to dedicated transfer advising and recommended academic plans to help them make the most of their credits. Those who can complete an associate degree through an approved transfer guide or program agreement will have their defined credits apply toward the corresponding WMU degree requirements, avoiding the frustration of losing credits along the way.

And students won't have to wait until their first day at WMU to begin feeling like Broncos.

Prior to admission, eligible students will enjoy early access to university resources and campus experiences, including free admission to WMU sporting events, excluding hockey.

The partnership is about more than providing a route to admission. It is also about helping students make a successful transition into university life, connect with the Bronco community and take advantage of distinctive academic programs and experiential learning opportunities.

The partnership also recognizes the importance of completing a GRCC credential. Through a no-cost reverse transfer process, students who continue their education at WMU can have eligible university credits transferred back to GRCC to help them earn an associate degree.

GRCC and WMU will continue working together beyond the signing ceremony, with WMU participating in at least one transfer-focused event each semester and both institutions reviewing student enrollment and achievement data to strengthen the partnership.

For GRCC students, Bronco Bound means the journey toward a bachelor's degree can begin with greater confidence, knowing their next opportunity is already within reach.

About Grand Rapids Community College

GRCC was established in 1914 — Michigan's first community college — and is focused on making college education accessible and affordable. Classes are scheduled weekdays, evenings and Saturdays in Grand Rapids, Holland and online. We offer traditional liberal arts and occupational career pathways, adult education courses and skilled training courses and apprenticeships.

About Western Michigan University

WMU students are individuals who are truly unique. At Western, we celebrate the passions that drive students and the possibilities that inspire them. For us, a degree is a pursuit of purpose where students are empowered to learn and where an experience-driven education leads to a meaningful career. Broncos prosper. Nine out of 10 graduates are employed quickly, working in their field in jobs they like. WMU students make their mark on the world—Grammy recipients, Super Bowl champions, doctors, teachers, pilots and countless others have flourished here. Western is the place where students become the best version of themselves. WMU is a public research university, offering a range of undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs to more than 17,000 students. Learn more at https://wmich.edu/

releases.title: California Opens New Workforce Pell Grant Application Portal for Institutions to Determine Career Training Program Eligibility
releases.body:
SACRAMENTO, Calif., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The California Student Aid Commission (CSAC) today announced the launching of the state application portal for the new federal Workforce Pell (WFP) Grant Program. The WFP state application portal will open on October 21 for higher education institutions and career technical education providers to apply for state authorization to participate in the program.

Articulated in California Senate Bill 135, on behalf of the Governor, CSAC is the designated California state agency to determine whether an institution's short-term program meets the state and federal program requirements, in consultation with the California Workforce Development Board and the Labor and Workforce Development Agency. After a short-term program has been deemed eligible, institutions submit the information directly to the U.S. Department of Education (ED) for review and final approval. The ED will notify institutions of their eligibility to participate in the WFP and allow eligible students to begin accessing these new federal Workforce Pell Grants disbursed through the campus financial aid office.

The WFP grant represents one of the most significant expansions of federal financial aid in decades. WFP is designed to expand financial aid opportunities for students pursuing short-term, high-quality workforce training programs that lead directly to high-skill, high-wage, or in-demand occupations. Completed 100 days since the passage of the state budget, the state portal marks a significant milestone in California's implementation efforts and begins the process of identifying programs across the state.

Institutions and programs seeking eligibility are strongly encouraged to participate in CSAC's Webinar on October 20., California Get Ready: A Pathway to a Successful Workforce Pell Grant Application will cover the portal requirements in detail including a technical guide to address federally required formular and state eligibility requirements. 

Expanding Access to In-Demand Career Technical Education

The portal launch by the California Student Aid Commission allows for institutions to apply to be eligible starting in the 2026-27 academic year. For students, this means that eligible students enrolled in approved short-term career technical education (CTE) programs can soon begin receiving federal WFP Grants. Designed for programs running between 150 and 599 clock hours (8 to 15 weeks), WFP helps learners quickly gain specialized skills for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers.

Unlike traditional Pell Grants, WFP can also be used by students who already hold a bachelor's degree (provided they do not hold a graduate degree). Coupled with the recent changes to Cal Grant C, which now includes programs as short as 8 weeks; students will be able to stack both Cal Grant C and Workforce Pell Grant, creating powerful new reskilling and upskilling pathways for California's adult workforce.

Leaders Across California on Workforce Pell Grant Program:

"California is building more pathways to good-paying careers — and making sure opportunity isn't limited by where you come from or whether you have a four-year degree," said Governor Gavin Newsom . "Through Workforce Pell, we're expanding financial aid opportunities and helping Californians move faster into in-demand jobs, build new skills, and get ahead in our growing economy."

"Ensuring our workforce development programs are directly tied to regional labor market needs is essential for California's economic future," said Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin. "With the signing of AB 1534, the state authorization process safeguards student investments by prioritizing high-quality programs that deliver true economic value, higher wages, and strong career outcomes for our workforce."

"By establishing Workforce Pell as an option for California students, we are chipping away at the college affordability barriers adult learners face in every region of our state," said Dr. Daisy Gonzales, Executive Director of the California Student Aid Commission . "The California Student Aid Commission supports colleges and universities, who provide high- quality, short-term career technical education and skills training, and with Workforce Pell as an option, state and federal aid will open new doors for adult learners and working learners. The portal opening is California's spirit of innovation to strengthen workforce pipelines by centering financial aid as a catalyst for economic mobility in our state." "Short-term credentials are vital vehicles for rapid social and economic mobility," said Dr. Sonya Christian, Chancellor of the California Community Colleges . "The launch of Phase One allows our community colleges to align state and federal support around targeted workforce programs, empowering more students to gain immediate industry-recognized skills and transition into sustainable, living-wage careers." "At Compton College, we see firsthand how targeted, short-term training can transform lives and lift entire communities," said Dr. Keith Curry, President/CEO of Compton College . "Workforce Pell removes significant financial barriers for working adults and many of our students who need flexible, accelerated options to gain career-ready credentials without taking on debt, or for many of our students, additional debt." "Home care and child care providers across California rely on continuous skill-building to adapt, advance, and better serve our communities," said Doug Moore, Executive Director of United Domestic Workers (UDW/AFSCME Local 3930) . "Expanding federal Pell support to short-term workforce training provides working people and adult learners a vital, realistic bridge to higher wages and career advancement."

Student Requirements

To be eligible for a Workforce Pell Grant, students must:

  • Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and meet federal Pell Grant eligibility requirements.
  • Hold a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
  • Be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen.
  • Not be currently enrolled in a bachelor's or higher-level degree program.
  • Enroll in an approved short-term workforce program at a participating institution.

Institutional Application & Letters of Intent

To disburse or advertise Workforce Pell funds, institutions must secure state authorization from CSAC, the California State Governor, and the U.S. Department of Education.

  • Portal Submission: Eligible institutions seeking program authorization can submit program data through the new CSAC program portal launching October 21.
  • Letters of Interest (By December 15, 2026): Institutions seeking eligibility that do not have existing data-sharing agreements with the Employment Development Department (EDD) pursuant to Unemployment Insurance Code Section 1095 must submit a letter of interest to CSAC and the Office of Cradle-to-Career Data on or before December 15, 2026 (and annually thereafter).
    • Letter Requirements: Must indicate the name and number of programs, the targeted high-demand sectors aligned with state EDC 69871 lists, and average class sizes. Applications for these institutions will be processed following statutory updates governing equivalent data sharing.

The California Student Aid Commission currently serves over 2.2 million students and administers over $3.9 billion of student financial aid programs and services, including the Cal Grant, the Middle Class Scholarship, and the California Dream Act Application. The Commission serves as a resource for policymakers and the public on college affordability and financing issues, and advocates for policy changes to eliminate cost as a barrier to any qualified California student pursuing a higher education. Visit our website at www.csac.ca.gov or follow us on social media by clicking on our Link Tree.

releases.body:
The weekly show has published 13 episodes with the leaders of some of the largest organizations in higher education and travel, including Marriott Vacations Worldwide, Azamara Cruises, Southern New Hampshire University, Western Governors University, Miami Dade College and Dallas College, plus the U.S. Department of Labor. MIAMI, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The New Normal, the show about how enterprises are deploying AI agents and generating real ROI, today released its 13th episode and confirmed a weekly cadence through 2027. Presented by OutRival, the Miami-based company building AI digital workers for voice, SMS and email, the show has recorded 30 episodes with the leaders of some of the largest organizations in higher education, travel and government, and plans to have 100 recorded by 2027. New episodes publish every Thursday at thenewnormal.fm.

The New Normal is hosted by OutRival Co-Founder and CEO Ruben Harris and Co-Founder and President Timur Meyster. Vice President, Head of Travel Jeff Herzfeld, a 20-year cruise and hospitality sales operations veteran, co-hosts the travel episodes. The show's next chapter is insurance: recordings with carrier, agency and brokerage leaders begin Q4 2026, co-hosted by OutRival's Vice President, Head of Insurance, Eric Weinstein.

The Premise

Most AI coverage is about what might happen. The New Normal is about what already did. Every episode puts a senior operator in the chair to walk through the use cases they actually deployed, the numbers they actually saw, and the decisions they got wrong along the way. No vendor pitch, no futurism, just leaders who run large organizations explaining how the work is changing inside them.

How the Show Is Made

Every episode is recorded in person. The OutRival team gives each guest two options: fly to OutRival's headquarters in Miami, or the hosts fly to the guest's headquarters. The second option is the one the team prefers, because being on site is how you learn how a leader is actually thinking about these decisions, and it puts a light on the people behind the C-suite: the enrollment counselors, advisors, sales associates, contact center teams and technologists responsible for creating an amazing experience for every student, traveler and policyholder. The episodes are produced by Mike Landsberg and Thomas Risavy of Grove Station Studios.

The show was built for industries that live on the phone: higher education, insurance and travel, where the relationship between a brand and the people it serves runs through millions of calls, texts and emails. Nobody proves the point like Bob Becker, the cruise industry sales legend responsible for more than $50 billion in sales at Carnival, Norwegian and Celebrity, who filled ships primarily through the phone.

His episode, released today, is live here. Those are the industries where getting AI right matters most, because a human will always be in the loop at some point to create a delightful experience for the student, the traveler or the policyholder. The leaders on the show have already made the hard calls about where that point is, and they are thinking past the first call: how AI agents can help their people provide care through the entire journey, from the first inquiry to the trip after this one. Together, the institutions represented in the first 13 episodes serve more than one million students a year and millions of travelers.

Why the Show Exists

Every new normal begins as the risk most people avoid today and the standard everyone copies tomorrow. After conversations with more than 300 enterprise leaders, the OutRival team found that most companies are still not running AI in production at scale, and the few that are have a lead the rest of the market cannot see coming. The New Normal exists to put those leaders on the record. The guests are the ones putting digital workers on the org chart, writing job descriptions for them, and reorganizing teams so humans and AI work side by side.

Most companies still treat AI as reactive support, a smarter way to answer the phone once a customer finally calls. The leaders on the show flipped it. They use it to reach out first: the inquiry that never got a callback, the application someone almost finished, the policy up for renewal, the guest ready to book the next trip. The show covers inbound and back-office use cases too, but the questions it keeps coming back to are about where leaders stopped waiting and started the conversation themselves.

13 Episodes, Three Industries, One Format

The show launched in June 2026 with higher education, added the U.S. Department of Labor as its first government guest, and opened its travel chapter in October. Published episodes, in order:

  1. Kermit Cook, CEO, Penn Foster: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/penn-foster-kermit-cook
  2. Madeline Pumariega, President, Miami Dade College: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/miami-dade-college-president-madeline-pumariega-on-deploying-ai-at-scale-in-higher-education
  3. Scott Pulsipher, President, Western Governors University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/wgu-scott-pulsipher
  4. David Andrews, Chancellor, UMass Global: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/umass-global-david-andrews
  5. Mark Milliron, President, National University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/national-university-mark-milliron
  6. Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President, Southern New Hampshire University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/snhu-lisa-marsh-ryerson
  7. Gregory Fowler, President, University of Maryland Global Campus: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/umgc-gregory-fowler
  8. Taylor Stockton, Chief Innovation Officer, U.S. Department of Labor: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/dol-taylor-stockton
  9. Raghu Krishnaiah, Chief Operating Officer, University of Phoenix: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/university-of-phoenix-raghu-krishnaiah
  10. Justin Lonon, Chancellor, Dallas College: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/dallas-college-justin-lonon
  11. Mike Flaskey, President and COO, Marriott Vacations Worldwide: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/marriott-vacations-worldwide-mike-flaskey
  12. Dondra Ritzenthaler, CEO, Azamara Cruises: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/azamara-cruises-dondra-ritzenthaler
  13. Bob Becker, the King of Outbound, former sales executive at Carnival, Norwegian and Celebrity, released today: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/bob-becker-king-of-outbound

Insurance episodes, co-hosted by Eric Weinstein, will cover how carriers, agencies and brokers are putting AI agents to work. Additional higher education, travel and insurance executives are already recorded and scheduled.

What the Guests Are Saying

"I want more of our people to be able to do the heart work, and I want to offload the hand work," said Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President of Southern New Hampshire University, on where AI belongs at a university serving 300,000 learners.

"A pilot is an initiative. Scale is a transformation," said Madeline Pumariega, President of Miami Dade College, on why the college went all in rather than piloting.

"You don't have the reach that these digital workers do," said Mike Flaskey, President and COO of Marriott Vacations Worldwide, on what AI adds to a 1,400-person sales organization.

"So if AI's coming and it can help us, let's go," said Dondra Ritzenthaler, CEO of Azamara Cruises.

"Hope is a pretty poor strategy in business," said Bob Becker, the sales leader who built the outbound model used across the cruise industry, on why he started AI with one use case.

What the Hosts Are Saying

"The most useful conversations about AI were happening in private, between operators, and nobody was recording them," said Ruben Harris, Co-Founder and CEO of OutRival. "Thirteen episodes in, the pattern is clear. The leaders winning with AI did not wait for a perfect pilot. They put it to work on the conversations they were already having with students, travelers and policyholders, and they measured it. We have 30 of those stories recorded, and we will have 100 by 2027."

"Every enterprise is being told to deploy AI. Almost nobody is being shown what it looks like when it works," said Timur Meyster, Co-Founder and President of OutRival. "We built OutRival to put digital workers into production at scale, so we know the difference between a demo and a deployment. The New Normal exists to make that difference public. The leaders on this show are not forecasting. They are reporting results, and they are putting their names on them."

"I started on the phones at Carnival and spent twenty years running sales floors, so I know how this industry reacts to a pitch about the future. We've heard it. We've bought it. Most of it didn't work," said Jeff Herzfeld, Head of Travel at OutRival. "This show skips the pitch entirely. It's leaders in cruise, vacation ownership and hospitality telling you what they actually did with this technology and what happened next. Honest, specific, and on the record. That conversation used to happen behind closed doors. Now you're in the room."

Who Should Watch

The show is built for presidents, chancellors, provosts and enrollment leaders in higher education; CEOs, contact center and revenue leaders in cruise, vacation ownership and hospitality; carrier, agency and brokerage executives in insurance; and anyone responsible for deciding how AI shows up in front of a student, a traveler or a policyholder.

The show is also tailored towards established vendors and startups who are obsessed with learning how their customers and potential customers think. New episodes publish every Thursday, with short clips released across YouTube Shorts, Instagram and LinkedIn.

releases.body:
New benefit gives eligible family members one tuition-free course for every five completed, a clear way to plan for and reduce the cost of a degree

PHOENIX, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- University of Phoenix today announces a new family tuition benefit that gives eligible family members of employees at organizations with University of Phoenix education alliances a clear, predictable way to save on a degree: one tuition-free course for every five courses completed.

The benefit comes as students and families are asking for more clarity about what college will cost. In Strada Education Foundation's 2026 report The Price Transparency Imperative, roughly two-thirds of students, parents and prospective adult learners rank cost transparency as a top priority for college affordability, and 71% of parents of college students say the same of multi-year price guarantees.

"Education benefits are most meaningful when people have a clear, practical way to use them," said Raghu Krishnaiah, chief operating officer at University of Phoenix. "Our employer alliances already connect working adults with education designed around real-world needs. Extending tuition-free course opportunities to eligible family members puts those existing relationships to work for more people, creating additional pathways to learning while helping families manage the cost of a degree."

How the family tuition benefit works

The new benefit provides eligible family members with opportunities to reduce tuition costs while pursuing their education goals.

  • Who is eligible: Eligible family members of employees whose organizations have qualifying education alliances with University of Phoenix.



  • How it works: Eligible family members can receive one tuition-free course for every five courses completed.



  • Timing requirements: To receive a tuition-free course, students must complete five courses and begin the sixth course within 365 days of posting attendance in their first course.

For many adults, cost is what stands between considering a degree and starting one. In a national survey of adults who had considered but never enrolled in postsecondary education, the Council for Adult and Experiential Learning (CAEL) found that half of those who didn't apply said they could not afford the program, and 73% said lower costs would make them more likely to enroll in the future.

The family benefit offers eligible families a predictable way to reduce that cost, along with access to the University's flexible five- and six-week online course model, designed to help adults balance education with work, family and other responsibilities.

Building on a commitment to affordable higher education

The family tuition benefit builds on University of Phoenix's broader approach to making higher education more affordable through predictable pricing, flexible learning and opportunities to save time and money on a degree.

In October, the University announced its new Locked-In Pricing Guarantee, effective Nov. 2, 2026, which will give new students one fixed per-course price covering tuition and resource fees through completion of their enrolled program.

The University also offers opportunities for eligible students to lower education costs through scholarships, transfer credits, credit for prior learning and employer tuition benefits. Together, these options reflect the University's focus on helping working adults pursue career-relevant education while managing the financial demands of everyday life.

Through its employer alliances, University of Phoenix continues to expand access to education savings and learning opportunities that support the needs of today's workforce and their families.

To learn more about the new family tuition benefit, including eligibility requirements, visit phoenix.edu/familybenefits.

About University of Phoenix

University of Phoenix is Built for Real Life. 50 Years Strong. The University innovates to help working adults enhance their careers and develop skills in a rapidly changing world through flexible online learning, relevant courses, academic AI pillars, and skills-mapped curriculum for associate, bachelor's and master's degree programs. Active students and alumni have access to Career Services for Life® resources including career guidance and tools. For more information, visit phoenix.edu. 

About University of Phoenix Workforce Solutions 

University of Phoenix Workforce Solutions helps companies align employee development to business strategy through skills-based solutions designed to address evolving workforce needs. Its Adaptable Skills Solutions brings together professional development, education savings and AI skills intelligence provided through Skillmore, a University of Phoenix affiliate, to support workforce planning, retention and talent mobility. By combining data, tools and education resources, Workforce Solutions offers practical ways to identify skills gaps, inform workforce decisions and prepare employees for long-term adaptability in a rapidly changing workplace. Learn more at https://www.phoenix.edu/workforce-solutions.html.
