releases.body:
The Definitive Pinball Documentary That Deserves an Extra Ball

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vision Films announces the North American and UK Transactional VOD release of the feature length documentary film Pinball: Beyond the Bumpers on October 20, 2026 from New Video Images. Directed and produced by Mark Helms and produced by Helms with Alejandro Torné, this definitive history follows the "silver ball" from its humble beginnings in 1600's Europe to the major resurgence today including past and present gaming legends and the technological advances that now draw collaborations with rock stars, celebrities, and major brands. The filmmakers will be representing the film at this year's Pinball Expo in Chicago on October 14-18.

Watch the trailer HERE.

Pinball is a phenomenon loved all over the world, still growing in popularity in the 21st century. The International Flipper Pinball Association tracks over 137,000 active ranked players globally, up from just 500 players in 2006 and leading pinball manufacturers are seeing new machine sales increase 15-20% annually.

Helms is known for the 1995 film The History of Pinball, the first thorough dive into the long and global history of the popular arcade game. This current iteration not only updates past interviews but utilizes his trove of video footage, historical data, and addresses the complexities of the game and industry not often seen. The film examines every angle, from the game's history of objectifying women to the women now competing at the highest levels worldwide, as well as pinball's enduring engineering marvels and the ongoing advances in licensing and technology.

Lise Romanoff, CEO and Managing Director of Vision Films, says, "After watching this immersive documentary, you will never look at a pinball machine the same way again. Jam packed full of fun, the film shows how pinball has evolved over centuries."

Filmmaker Mark Helms shares, "I always believed that pinball — the game — was never clearly understood by the vast majority of the public, so I made this documentary to pull back the curtain on pinball, exposing the highs, the lows, the controversies, and ultimately, its bright future. We trace the game from crude beginnings to today's cutting-edge wonder machines, played and enjoyed around the world. After watching this documentary, you'll understand exactly why pinball is in the middle of its modern-day resurgence."

When Helms was asked what he tells his friends the first time, they play one of the newer machines, he laughed and said, "I always say the same thing: 'This ain't your granddaddy's pinball machine.'"

The cast includes Roger Sharpe, Gary Stern, Steve Ritchie, Mark Helms, Reby Hardy, Crystaltina, and more.

For more information, please visit and follow: www.beyondthebumpers.com

DENVER, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrackVia today announced that TrackVia Government, the field operations intelligence platform built for federal, state, and local agencies, has achieved FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) Certification through the 2F Game Warden® Platform, expanding TrackVia's ability to support U.S. government organizations and contractors operating in secure, mission-critical environments.
releases.title: TrackVia Government Achieves FedRAMP® Class C Certification, Expanding Secure Mission Operations for Federal Agencies and Contractors
releases.body:
Certification through Second Front Systems brings TrackVia's Field Operations Intelligence platform into secure government environments where workforce readiness, program execution and mission delivery depend on speed and trust

DENVER, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TrackVia today announced that TrackVia Government, the field operations intelligence platform built for federal, state, and local agencies, has achieved FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) Certification through the 2F Game Warden® Platform, expanding TrackVia's ability to support U.S. government organizations and contractors operating in secure, mission-critical environments. 

Government missions depend on thousands of operational processes that have to work every day, managing personnel and readiness, coordinating projects and programs, tracking resources, supporting field teams, exchanging information with contractors and partners, and ensuring work moves securely across organizations. Those processes are often fragmented across legacy systems, spreadsheets, email and disconnected applications.

Agencies cannot simply replace the systems they already depend on. The federal government spends more than $100 billion annually on IT and cyber-related investments, with agencies historically reporting that roughly 80% goes to operations and maintenance of existing IT, including legacy systems, according to the U.S. Government Accountability Office.

Now, TrackVia Government gives agencies and contractors a different path, modernizing the operational layer around the systems they already rely on, without requiring replacement of core infrastructure. TrackVia helps organizations connect the people doing the work, the workflows that execute the mission and the operational data leaders need to make decisions, now within a FedRAMP-certified environment designed for secure government use.

"Government organizations shouldn't have to choose between speed and security," said Aylin Basom, Chief Executive Officer of TrackVia. "The work our customers run on TrackVia can be directly connected to workforce readiness, program execution, field operations and mission delivery. That work has to move quickly, but it also has to meet the security and governance standards the government requires. FedRAMP Certification allows us to bring the flexibility and speed TrackVia is known for into environments where trust and security are non-negotiable. Agencies and contractors can modernize critical operational workflows, connect existing systems and give teams better visibility into the work, without having to rebuild everything from scratch."

TrackVia Government runs on Second Front Systems' Game Warden, a pre-accredited DevSecOps platform designed to accelerate the deployment of commercial software into government environments while providing inherited security controls and continuous monitoring TrackVia has been listed in the FedRAMP Marketplace under the TrackVia Government listing.

"Agencies aren't going to decommission core infrastructure, and the best commercial software doesn't ask them to," said Nick Woodruff, General Manager, North America at Second Front Systems. "TrackVia now has its own FedRAMP listing, and our teams worked side by side to bring it into an accredited environment that preserved its flexibility and kept it working with the systems agencies already run. Our partnership goes well beyond the platform, from the accredited environment to how we take it to agencies together."

Built for the Work Behind the Mission

Government operations rarely fit neatly into a single off the shelf application. TrackVia Government can support operational use cases such as:

  • Workforce readiness, personnel coordination and resource management
  • Program and project execution
  • Field operations and inspections
  • Contractor and subcontractor coordination
  • Secure collection and exchange of operational information
  • Compliance and audit workflows
  • Asset, site and logistics management
  • Mission support processes spanning multiple teams and systems

Because TrackVia is configurable, organizations can adapt workflows as mission requirements, teams and operating conditions change, without relying on lengthy custom software development cycles.

"The opportunity for us is much bigger than digitizing forms or replacing spreadsheets," Basom said. "We want TrackVia Government to become the operational layer that helps agencies and contractors coordinate mission-critical work, understand what is happening across their operations and act faster when conditions change."

About TrackVia

TrackVia is a Field Operations Intelligence platform that helps organizations connect, control, and continuously improve mission-critical operations. TrackVia brings together field teams, operational workflows and enterprise data to create real time visibility, automate work and turn operational data into actionable intelligence. TrackVia Government, the company's FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) Certified environment, extends that platform to federal, state, and local government customers. To learn more, visit trackvia.com.

About Second Front Systems

Second Front Systems (2F) is a public-benefit software company powering software for the free world. We eliminate the friction that slows innovation, enabling faster, more secure development and deployment of software across government and regulated networks. Built by national security veterans and backed by top-tier venture capital, our platform is trusted by the world's leading organizations to cut deployment timelines from years to weeks. We move fast, solve hard problems, and deliver trusted capabilities where they're needed most. Our work strengthens global security and gives the United States and its allies a lasting competitive advantage. Learn more at secondfront.com.

releases.title: pubX Raises $5M Series A Led by Chicago Ventures and Acquires Compliant to Build Agent-to-Agent Advertising Infrastructure from the Ground Up
releases.body:
Buyer and seller agents transact directly on infrastructure built for agents, governed on both sides of every buy, with Compliant's media quality and governance signals in every decision

NEW YORK and LONDON , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- pubX, which builds agent-to-agent infrastructure for advertising, today announced a $5 million Series A led by Chicago Ventures and the acquisition of Compliant, the media quality and governance company. Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. Compliant will retain its name and operate as a pubX company, led by CEO Jamie Barnard. Within pubX, Jamie will take the role of President, Global Demand Growth, leading the company's global growth strategy across agencies, advertisers and the wider buy-side.

pubX builds the agents that plan, buy, sell and optimize advertising — and the infrastructure they transact on. Its buyer agents and seller agents work directly with one another, from brief to reporting, across every channel, so that more of every dollar reaches the media and the publisher behind it. pubX began on the publisher side, spending years helping publishers price and sell their inventory. Compliant, founded by former Unilever and P&G executives, has focused principally on the demand side, delivering measurable value to global brands and their agencies. The acquisition unites brand and publisher in one company, and that experience, on both sides of the market is what shaped the company's vision for something new: infrastructure designed from the ground up for agents to buy and sell directly. Built on the open Ad Context Protocol (AdCP), it works for buyer and seller alike.

Trust as the founding product principle

pubX was built on the premise that no one hands their media budget to a system they don't trust, so trust, transparency, and accountability are built into the infrastructure itself, on both sides of every transaction. Its agents are educated by pubX: governance checks on every buy, decisions that are reasoned, traced and auditable, with Compliant's quality signals shaping what they consider. The agents are guided by the client, on the brand's own brief, plan, publishers and commercial rules. People stay in control: the client sets the level of autonomy and approves the plan at key stages, and the agents execute inside those rules. As trust is earned, autonomy grows.

"Programmatic took this industry from fax machines and spreadsheets into more automated and real-time platforms in two short decades, and everything we've done since builds on that premise," said Andrew Mole, CEO and co-founder of pubX. "Agents let us finish what was started. You tell them how you buy, you sign off where it matters, and every page of the brief gets read every single time. For the first time, the infrastructure has caught up with what brands want to achieve with their advertising and how publishers want to sell."

"For years, brands have searched for high-quality, high-performing inventory with real, relevant and engaged audiences. Compliant built the Data Integrity and CTV Quality Indexes so that they could do that with certainty rather than speculation," said Jamie Barnard, CEO of Compliant. "Inside pubX, those media quality and governance signals sit in the decision itself, so an agent weighs them before it buys. This is what gives each CMO the confidence to trust pubX's agents."

"Every part of the advertising industry is asking how agents will improve buying and selling, and most answers so far are an agentic layer built on existing infrastructure. Co-founders Andrew Mole and Alex Rosen, pubX's CTO, have built advertising infrastructure before, and this time they built it for agents from the start, on both sides of the transaction, with a publisher base that already trusts them and a design that keeps the client in control. That is a rare starting position, and the Compliant acquisition makes it stronger," said Stuart Larkins, Co-founder & General Partner at Chicago Ventures.

The funding will support pubX's expansion in the United States, the build-out of its demand-side business serving brands and agencies, continued development of its buyer and seller agents on AdCP, and the integration of Compliant's signals across the platform.

"For a publisher, agentic buying is about discoverability. Buyer agents see the audiences and environments we actually have, backed by our first-party data, and that puts us in front of spend that never reached us before, in an environment we can win. It amplifies what our sales team already does well," said Stephanie Mazzamaro, Head of Revenue and Data, Paradium.AI, formerly The Arena Group.

"As advertising increasingly moves toward agentic buying, discoverability becomes critical," said Jason Taylor, Chief Revenue Officer, USA TODAY Co. "Publishers that invest in trusted content, engaged audiences, and brand-safe environments should be more visible to AI-powered buying platforms. The opportunity is to create a more transparent marketplace where quality is recognized and rewarded."

pubX at Advertising Week New York

On Wednesday, October 7, pubX will run a live agent-to-agent media buy at a private executive lunch during Advertising Week New York. A campaign for Reckitt's Mucinex brand will go from brief to live placement, with Reckitt's trading team approving the plan at key stages and publishers including Paradium.AI and USA TODAY Co. reviewing and accepting the campaign as it happens. Attendance is by invitation.

About pubX

pubX builds agent-to-agent infrastructure for advertising. Its buyer and seller agents, educated by pubX, trained by the client, and governed on both sides of every transaction, let brands, agencies and publishers plan, buy, sell and optimize media directly, with trust earned one campaign at a time. Learn more at www.pubx.ai

About Compliant

Compliant, a pubX company, is the media quality and governance company behind the Data Integrity and CTV Quality Indexes, used by leading global advertisers and industry bodies to measure data integrity and media quality across the supply chain. Learn more at www.compliant.global

About Chicago Ventures

Chicago Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital fund founded to fill a market gap in early-stage capital for tech companies outside traditional hubs like Silicon Valley, focusing on undercapitalized tech ecosystems in the Central U.S. and beyond. They lead seed rounds "before it's obvious" and operate a formal platform function that serves as a direct extension of portfolio companies' teams, with their network explicitly architected to provide customer introductions, expert help, and talent access at scale rather than just for sourcing deals. Learn more at www.chicagoventures.com

COLUMBUS, Ohio, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Palace Theatre will celebrate its 100th anniversary by bringing Ray Charles' music back to a stage where he performed throughout his career. CAPA today announced that country artist Jackson Dean and jazz trumpeter Etienne Charles will join host Paul Shaffer and an all-star cast for Palace 100: The Genius of Ray Charles at 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at the Palace Theatre in downtown Columbus.
releases.title: Palace Theatre brings Ray Charles' music back to its stage for one-night-only centennial concert
releases.body:
Country artist Jackson Dean and jazz trumpeter Etienne Charles join all-star lineup for Palace 100 concert

COLUMBUS, Ohio, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Palace Theatre will celebrate its 100th anniversary by bringing Ray Charles' music back to a stage where he performed throughout his career. CAPA today announced that country artist Jackson Dean and jazz trumpeter Etienne Charles will join host Paul Shaffer and an all-star cast for Palace 100: The Genius of Ray Charles at 7:30 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at the Palace Theatre in downtown Columbus.

An all-star lineup spans musical genres

Dean and Charles join a lineup that includes Grammy Award-winning R&B and jazz vocalist Patti Austin; multiplatinum singer-songwriter Aloe Blacc; Grammy-nominated gospel singer-songwriter Blessing Offor; Grammy and Academy Award-winning singer Lisa Fischer; Grammy-nominated singer Monica Mancini; and Columbus native, singer and songwriter Billy Valentine. A Guggenheim Fellow, Etienne Charles is known for blending jazz with Afro-Caribbean musical traditions.

Spanning R&B, jazz, gospel, country and contemporary music, the lineup reflects the range of styles Charles explored throughout his career.

Paul Shaffer and Gregg Field bring personal Ray Charles connections

Paul Shaffer, David Letterman's longtime musical director and bandleader, will host the evening. Shaffer performed with Charles on programs including Saturday Night Live and Late Night with David Letterman. The concert will be produced by Grammy and Emmy recipient, music producer, and former drummer for Ray Charles, Gregg Field.

"Ray Charles represents the kind of musical excellence that transcends genres, generations and boundaries," CAPA Vice President of Marketing and Sales Peter Keiser said. "Bringing his music back to the Palace honors his extraordinary legacy and the theatre's history as a place where great artists and unforgettable moments continue to come alive."

Palace 100 at a glance

  • Event: Palace 100: The Genius of Ray Charles
  • Occasion: The Palace Theatre's 100th anniversary
  • Date: Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026
  • Time: 7:30 p.m.
  • Location: Palace Theatre, 34 W. Broad St., Columbus, Ohio
  • Host: Paul Shaffer
  • Producer: Gregg Field
  • Featured artists: Aloe Blacc, Billy Valentine, Blessing Offor, Jackson Dean, Patti Austin, Lisa Fischer, Etienne Charles and Monica Mancini 
  • Tickets: Starting at $62.50 at the CAPA Ticket Center at the Ohio Theatre, 39 E. State St.; online at www.capa.com; or by phone at 614-469-0939
  • Significance: A one-night-only concert created for the Palace Theatre's centennial

An exclusive concert for the Palace Theatre's 100th anniversary

Created specifically for the Palace Theatre's centennial, the concert will be performed only once, in Columbus, and will not tour to other cities. Charles performed at the Palace Theatre throughout his career, most recently on June 6, 1992. Bringing his music back to the Palace links the theatre's history with a new generation of performers and audiences.

"A theatre doesn't reach its 100th anniversary by simply surviving—it gets there by becoming part of the lives of generations of people," Field said. "The Palace Theatre has that kind of history. For its centennial, we're bringing the music of Ray Charles, who performed on that very stage, back to the Palace with an extraordinary collection of artists. Having worked with Ray for many years, I can't imagine a more powerful way to honor his legacy and celebrate 100 years of this extraordinary theatre."

National talent and Columbus musicians share the Palace stage

The program will include a special rendition of "America the Beautiful," one of Charles' best-known interpretations. The concert will bring nationally recognized artists together with musicians from the Columbus Symphony Orchestra, Columbus Jazz and The Ohio State University School of Music. Led by Grammy-nominated conductor Chris Walden, the orchestra will feature Grammy-nominated guitarist Dean Parks, bassist Nathan East (Eric Clapton), Columbus Hammond organist and former Ray Charles band member Bobby Floyd, saxophonist Tom Scott (Blues Brothers) and Grammy-winning keyboardist Matt Rollings. The concert also marks a homecoming for Columbus native Billy Valentine, a performer and songwriter who co-wrote "My World," the title track of Charles' 1993 album.

The Palace Theatre celebrates 100 years

Billed as "A Theatre of a Thousand Wonders," the Palace Theatre opened Nov. 8, 1926, as a vaudeville house. Over the next century, its stage welcomed generations of artists and audiences across nearly every performing arts genre. Six days after the Palace's 100th birthday, Palace 100: The Genius of Ray Charles will celebrate that history by returning Charles' music to its stage.

The concert is one of several programs CAPA has planned in celebration of the Palace Theatre's centennial. Visit www.capa.com/100-celebration-palace for additional information.

FORT MYERS, Fla., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Great Place To Work® and Fortune have selected Eightpoint Interactive, Inc., part of Eightpoint, a global technology group that builds and scales consumer digital products across mobile, desktop, and digital media platforms, for the 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing™ List. This is Eightpoint Interactive's second time being named to this prestigious list, this year coming in at 32nd place. Earning a spot means that Eightpoint Interactive is one of the best companies to work for in the country.

The Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing list is based on analysis of survey responses from over 10,000 employees at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies in the advertising and marketing industry.

"Being recognized again by Fortune and Great Place To Work is especially meaningful because it reflects the experience of our employees," said Deniz Gezgin, CEO of Eightpoint. "We have worked hard to build a culture where talented people can do ambitious work, continue growing, and have a real impact. This recognition belongs to our team and the environment they help create every day."

The Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing list is highly competitive. Great Place To Work, the global authority on workplace culture, determines its lists using its proprietary Trust Index™ Survey to evaluate and certify thousands of organizations in America's largest ongoing annual workforce study, based on over 1.3 million survey responses and data from companies representing more than 7.3 million employees.

Survey responses reflect a comprehensive picture of the workplace experience. Honorees were selected based on their ability to offer positive outcomes for employees regardless of job role, work status, or other demographic factors.

"Congratulations to the Fortune Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing," says Michael C. Bush, CEO of Great Place To Work. "People are at the heart of work in every industry, and advertising is no exception. These companies show how delivering for your people drives financial performance and turns fear of the future into the confidence to win."

Eightpoint Interactive has earned Great Place To Work Certification™ for three consecutive years, in 2024, 2025, and 2026. The company was previously ranked on the 2024 Fortune Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing™ List and the 2024 Fortune Best Small Workplaces™ List.

About Eightpoint

Eightpoint is a global technology group that builds and scales consumer digital products across mobile, desktop, and digital media platforms.

Eightpoint's growing ecosystem includes products such as NOAA Live Weather Radar, a high-clarity weather app powered by official government data; Easy Homescreen, an Android launcher designed to make smartphones simpler and more accessible; and Wave Browser, an eco-friendly web browser backed by a long-term partnership funding ocean cleanup.

Focused on quality, speed, and long-term value, Eightpoint builds digital products that integrate seamlessly into everyday life. To learn more, visit https://eightpoint.io

About the Fortune Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing List

Great Place To Work selected the 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Advertising & Marketing by gathering and analyzing confidential survey responses from over 1.3 million employees, representing the experiences of over 7.3 million employees in the U.S in 2025 and 2026. Of those responses, over 10,000 were collected from employees at Great Place To Work Certified companies in the advertising and marketing industry, and this list is based on that feedback. To be eligible for the list, companies must have 10 or more employees. Read the full methodology.

To get on this list next year, start here.

 About Great Place To Work

As the global authority on workplace culture, Great Place To Work, a UKG company, brings 30 years of groundbreaking research and data to help every place become a great place to work for all. Its proprietary platform and Great Place To Work Model help companies evaluate the experience of every employee, with exemplary workplaces becoming Great Place To Work Certified and receiving recognition on a coveted Best Workplaces list.

Follow Great Place To Work on LinkedIn, X, and Instagram, and sign up for the Great Place To Work LinkedIn newsletter, Culture Edge, to get the latest research on what drives business success.

About Fortune Media

Fortune is a global multi-platform media company built on a legacy of trusted, award-winning reporting and information for those who want to make business better. Independently owned, Fortune tells the stories of the world's biggest companies and their leaders as well as a new generation of innovators who are moving business forward. Digitally and in print, Fortune measures corporate performance through rigorous benchmarks, and holds companies accountable, in regions around the world. Its iconic rankings include Fortune 500, Fortune Global 500, Most Powerful Women, and World's Most Admired Companies. Fortune builds world-class communities by convening industry thought leaders for exclusive summits and conferences, including the Fortune Global Forum, Fortune Brainstorm Tech, and Fortune Most Powerful Women. For more information, visit fortune.com.

TORONTO, Oct. 5, 2026 /CNW/ -- It's the gift that keeps giving as Hallmark Channel's Countdown to Christmas returns to W Network and STACKTV beginning Friday, October 16. Over 10 consecutive weeks, W Network is Canada's official holiday cheer headquarters, wrapping up and delivering heartwarming stories centered around the magic of the season. Following last year's Hallmark Channel's Countdown to Christmas, where W Network reached over 8 million Canadians and was ranked as the #1 specialty entertainment station for A25-54, F25-54 and total viewers*, this year's lineup features 34 all-new movie premieres, one special and two returning series reuniting viewers with household favourites, notable stars and feel-good holiday tales. With Hallmark Channel's Countdown to Christmas full lineup available to stream exclusively on STACKTV, the festivities continue as W Network will also be available on National Free Preview from November 1 to November 30. Please check local listings for additional information.

"The spirit of the holidays comes alive with the annual return of Hallmark Channel's Countdown to Christmas on W Network and STACKTV," said Jennifer Abrams, SVP Content and Marketing. "Our long-standing partnership with Hallmark continues to bring Canadian audiences the heartwarming stories, familiar faces and holiday magic they look forward to year after year.  

MOVIES

From time-travel twists to holiday meet cutes, this year's movie lineup is loaded with festive fun, heartfelt romance, and the magic of connection.

Debuting Saturday, November 28 at 8 p.m. ET/PT, Lacey Chabert and Travis Van Winkle star in Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True where a holiday wish in Cinderella Fountain may turn their rivalry into romance.  Disney alumni Christy Carlson Romano and Richard Kind also star in this holiday tale set at The Most Magical Place on Earth.

In the time-travel tale with a holiday twist, The Nights Before Christmas, premiering Saturday, November 14 at 8 p.m. ET/ PT is an all-new Canadian movie starring Tyler Hynes and Laci J Maily. Marty is happily caught in a time loop on Christmas Eve until he encounters a down on her luck Chloe and for the first time since the loop started, he wants to see Christmas Day.

Continuing the time travels adventures, A Grand Biltmore Christmas follows Elizabeth as she travels from 1915 to 2026 Biltmore, where she reconnects with Michael and falls in love with the wonders of the 21st century. Airing Saturday, December 5 at 8 p.m. ET/PT, A Grand Biltmore Christmas stars Holland Roden, Niall Matter, Andie MacDowell, James Trevena, Jonathan Frakes, Rachel Boston and Wes Brown.

The Holiday Touchdown franchise returns with Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story joining the lineup on Saturday, October 17 at 8 p.m. ET/PT. Avery writes an article profiling a woman attending her 500th Bears game, who only agrees to the story if her grandson serves as Avery's ambassador to Chicago for the holidays. This match made on the field stars, Lyndsy Fonseca, Robert Buckley, Marsha Mason, Barbara Alyn Woods, and Khary Payton with tons of special cameos, including Marilu Henner and Tamera Mowry-Housley.

TV SERIES

Festive fan favourite, Canadian original, Mistletoe Murders is back with Season 3 on Thursday, November 5 at 8 p.m. ET/PT. Emily and Sam tackle new mysteries that come to town and in the process further ignite their flame all while Emily's past threatens her time in Fletcher's Grove. Based on the Audible global hit podcast of the same name and created by Ken Cuperus, Mistletoe Murders from Lionsgate Canada and Headspinner Productions stars Sarah Drew as Emily Lane and Peter Mooney as Sam Wilner with special guest appearances from Holly Robinson Peete and Catherine Bell.

All aboard for the return of Christmas at Sea as Season 2 premieres on Monday, December 21 at 8 p.m. ET/PT, with back-to-back episodes. In this unscripted series, Hallmark superfans are rockin' around the high seas celebrating the holidays aboard a Christmas cruise. Across four-episodes superfans experience life changing moments and share in the joy of the season with a few surprises from their favourite Hallmark stars. Christmas at Sea features appearances from Benjamin Ayres, Jonathan Bennett, Rachel Boston, B.J. Britt, Wes Brown, Erin Cahill, Paul Campbell, Taylor Cole, Nikki DeLoach, Heather Hemmens, Tyler Hynes, Ginna Claire Mason, Brendan Penny, Kimberley Sustad, Andrew Walker and Ashley Williams.

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As both storied institutions observe milestone anniversaries in 2026, Roddenberry Entertainment, torchbearers of the Star Trek franchise and Gene Roddenberry's legacy, and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, managed by Caltech have planned an exciting activation, bringing two stargazing stewards of science fiction and science together in an exciting extension of their enduring collaboration.
releases.title: RODDENBERRY ENTERTAINMENT AND NASA's JET PROPULSION LABORATORY JOIN TO CELEBRATE LANDMARK ANNIVERSARIES
releases.body:
Historic collaboration will feature w programming to mark 60 years of Star Trek and 90 years of JPL

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As both storied institutions observe milestone anniversaries in 2026, Roddenberry Entertainment, torchbearers of the Star Trek franchise and Gene Roddenberry's legacy, and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, managed by Caltech have planned an exciting activation, bringing two stargazing stewards of science fiction and science together in an exciting extension of their enduring collaboration.

For Roddenberry Entertainment, September 8 marks the 60th anniversary of the day Gene Roddenberry's groundbreaking sci-fi drama premiered on NBC. In over half a century since, The Original Series has grown into a sprawling universe of 12 spin-off television series, 13 feature films, and countless books, comics, and video games.

Meanwhile, October 31 marks nine decades since a group of Caltech graduate students and fellow enthusiasts began experimenting with rocketry in a dry riverbed near La Cañada Flintridge, Calif. The years that followed would see JPL grow from a test site in the Arroyo Seco to the crown jewel of Earth's extra-planetary robotic research ambitions. Voyager, the Mars rovers, and the Deep Space Network all trace their beginnings to JPL.

Caltech JPL and Roddenberry Entertainment have shared a special relationship over their histories. Throughout the development and production of Star Trek, Gene Roddenberry consulted often with JPL scientists and engineers to ensure that his vision of a spacefaring future was as feasible and believable as possible. In the 1970s, Roddenberry contacted John Casani, then JPL's Voyager project manager, who loaned Roddenberry a physical model of the Voyager probe, inspiring the sentient spacecraft V'Ger from "Star Trek: The Motion Picture."

Roddenberry's desire to ground his science fiction in real-world science meant a continued need to work closely with the real-world scientists at JPL. His stories and those that followed have honored those scientific advancements that have enabled us to travel to the stars in our time. In turn, many at JPL and Caltech proudly attribute their career paths to Star Trek and its vision of an interstellar future guided by reason, inclusion, and mutual aspiration.

The hub of this united celebration comes in the form of a uniquely exciting interview series titled "Those Who Look Up."

VIEW "THOSE WHO LOOK UP" TEASER HERE

Those Who Look Up

Going all the way back to The Original Series, Gene Roddenberry sought inspiration from scientists of the day, whose work could catapult the mind into the 23rd century. Honoring the inspiration Gene found in science, and looking at the subsequent reverberative effect Star Trek has had on the scientific community, Roddenberry Entertainment will be releasing its "Those Who Look Up" series – A collection of interviews featuring JPL and Caltech subject matter experts and Star Trek actors. The series will showcase the synergy between the two entities, and give human faces to the enduring intersection between science and science fiction. JPLers and Star Trek stars will explore how the work they do every day has influenced another person, another industry, and the world at large.

The series will be structured in a way that reflects the cyclical nature of the rapport between Star Trek and Caltech JPLers. Including four people from JPL and four members of Star Trek talent, the series begins with a JPLer interviewing a Star Trek actor, who, in turn, interviews another JPLer. That JPLer then interviews another Star Trek actor, who interviews another JPLer. At the series conclusion, the last person in the sequence will close the loop by interviewing the person who conducted the first interview.

"Having been lucky enough to visit JPL on a number of occasions, I've often considered the wonderful gift JPL gave to my father and Star Trek so long ago," said Roddenberry Entertainment CEO Eugene "Rod" Roddenberry, Jr. "Now, to recognize that his creation has reciprocated in such a significant way, and to see that in the faces of individuals who participated in our series, is tremendously rewarding."

ABOUT RODDENBERRY ENTERTAINMENT

Roddenberry Entertainment is a science fiction leader, passionately providing thought-provoking, quality genre entertainment that sustains the legacy of our founder, Gene Roddenberry. We are devoted to producing viewer-centric entertainment that actively recognizes the integral role audiences play in the creation of any franchise, as well as the role substantive entertainment can play in bettering society. Our productions promote experience over observation; encouraging audiences to think, question and challenge the status quo of the world in which we live.

ABOUT NASA JET PROPULSION LABORATORY

A division of Caltech in Pasadena, California, JPL is NASA's center of excellence for robotics and deep space exploration. The federally funded research and development center helped launch America's first satellite, Explorer 1, in 1958, and became a part of the agency later that year. Since then, JPL has managed such historic missions as Voyager, Galileo, Cassini, the Mars Exploration Rover program, the Perseverance Mars rover, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, Europa Clipper, and many more.

releases.title: WZC Networking Marks 20 Years of Engineering Emergency Responder Radio Coverage
releases.body:
NOVI, Mich., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- WZC Networking marks its 20th anniversary this year, reflecting two decades of designing, installing, and testing the in-building radio systems that keep firefighters and EMS crews connected when they move inside a structure. When a radio goes silent inside a building, a crew loses contact with command at the moment communication matters most. That's the gap WZC was built to close.

In 2006, RF engineer John Wierzgac founded WZC around an uncomplicated truth: concrete and steel might block a fire, but they shouldn't choke out a distress call. Twenty years later, WZC has become Michigan's benchmark for Emergency Responder Communication Enhancement Systems (ERCES) and Public Safety DAS. We don't sit back and wait for signal drops to expose a blind spot. Instead, we pull up a chair with developers, fire chiefs, and inspectors long before the first antenna hits the roof, wiring absolute reliability directly into the blueprint.

Buildings have radically evolved since 2006. Thick concrete and low-E glass save energy, but they block radio signals, creating dead zones in stairwells, basements, and interior corridors where portable radios lose contact with the outside. Where a building cannot meet the coverage thresholds required under NFPA 1225 and IFC Section 510, as adopted locally, an ERCES is required. WZC treats that coverage as a life-safety system rather than a permit item, and looks for blind spots in design rather than at the certificate-of-occupancy inspection.

A Building Days from Opening, and a Signal That Wasn't There

Days before the Corewell Health Endoscopy Center was set to open, acceptance testing identified insufficient in-building radio coverage, putting the fire marshal's sign-off and the facility's certificate of occupancy at risk with a fixed opening date approaching.

The Christman Group brought in WZC Networking. The team designed a compliant solution, expedited equipment procurement, and produced documented test results that satisfied the fire marshal and supported the issuance of a temporary certificate of occupancy, allowing the facility to open on schedule while the permanent system was completed.

It's the kind of save that never makes headlines because it isn't supposed to happen at all. A healthcare facility opened on time. A general contractor learned who to call before groundbreaking on the next project, not after a failed test threatens the finish line. That's why Christman looks to WZC first now: not because of a sales pitch, but because the work held up when the schedule had no room left.

Fifty-One Percent, Not Even Close to Enough

At Clawson Manor Co-op, a 15-story senior living complex, energy-efficient glazing and heavy exterior cladding were severely attenuating public safety radio frequencies. A WZC Networking survey found that only 51 percent of the property met required signal thresholds. In the egress corridors, where reliable communication is critical during an emergency, that figure dropped to just 34 percent. For hundreds of elderly residents who cannot evacuate rapidly during a crisis, those gaps could have left arriving crews without reliable communications.

WZC engineered and installed a signal booster and distributed antenna system sized for the building's envelope. On re-test, the property passed in 100 percent of tested grid areas, exceeding the thresholds required under NFPA 1225 and IFC Section 510 as adopted locally. Clawson Fire Department Battalion Chief and Fire Marshal John Ruthenbeck noted, "The City of Clawson was more than satisfied with the design and installation of the system by WZC Networking and the professional service provided to both the residents of the Clawson Manor and the Clawson Fire/Police and EMS Agencies."

Nobody on the Other End of That Radio Is Replaceable

Behind each of these projects are people who aren't statistics. At Clawson Manor, there are several hundred residents who cannot evacuate quickly on their own. At Corewell Health, there are patients under sedation and the staff responsible for getting them out.

When fire marshals deny an occupancy permit, the code is not the end goal. Protecting the people inside the building is. WZC operates on one inviolable principle: no contractor's deadline and no construction budget is worth a human life. A wall should only ever shelter people, never cut them off from the communication that could save them.

Passing Once Is Not Compliance

WZC makes one point clear to owners and facility managers: an ERCES is not finished at commissioning. NFPA 1225 requires ongoing inspection and testing of these systems, covering donor signal, amplifier gain, alarm reporting, and battery backup performance, along with periodic verification of in-building coverage. Buildings and the RF environment around them change over time, and a system that passed when it was commissioned may not perform the same way years later. Responsibility for maintaining that compliance sits with the building owner.

In practice, a system that passed at turnover and has not been touched in four years is a system nobody can vouch for. WZC provides ongoing ERCES inspection, testing, and documentation programs so owners maintain current, AHJ-ready records rather than discovering a lapse during an inspection or, worse, during an incident.

Twenty Years, One Principle

Earlier this year, WZC hosted fire chiefs and fire marshals for an open workshop on ERCES field conditions, focused on education rather than a product pitch. "Twenty years in, it still comes down to the same thing," says founder John Wierzgac. "A radio has to work on every floor and in every stairwell, not just in the lobby. If it doesn't, the system isn't finished, whether or not anyone is inspecting it that day."

That principle drives every project WZC takes on, from healthcare clinics to senior living centers. First responders don't view emergency communication as code compliance; they see equipment they have to be able to depend on. That focus has not changed as WZC has expanded. "Most of the buildings we walk into were never designed with radio coverage in mind," says Nate Wierzgac, Chief Operating Officer. "Nobody asks the question early, so it surfaces at the end, when it is expensive to fix. We would rather be in that conversation during design, and we would rather owners know the testing obligation doesn't stop at turnover."

From a Novi startup to a multi-state partner, WZC Networking has built its practice one building, one grid test, and one clear channel at a time, so that when the call comes, it carries.

WZC Networking is an RF engineering and technology integration firm founded in 2006 in Novi, Michigan. WZC designs, installs, tests, and maintains Emergency Responder Communication Enhancement Systems (ERCES), public safety and cellular DAS, structured cabling, Wi-Fi, security and CCTV, and audiovisual systems. The company also delivers ongoing managed and compliance services for multi-site clients across the United States.

Learn more at https://www.wzcnetworking.com

releases.title: Tanya Zuckerbrot, Founder of F-Factor, Resolves Lawsuit Against Emily Gellis After Six Years of Litigation
releases.body:
Settlement Includes $240,000 Payment and Public Video Apology to Remain Pinned on Gellis' Social Media Profile for Three and a Half Years

NEW YORK, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tanya Zuckerbrot, MS, RD, founder of F-Factor, has resolved her defamation and cyberstalking lawsuit against fashion influencer Emily Gellis after six years of litigation. As part of the settlement, Gellis is publishing a public video apology on her Instagram account, acknowledging that the allegations she promoted were not supported by verified evidence.

"I spent 25 years building my career and F-Factor, only to watch a smear campaign built on lies destroy my company within months," said Zuckerbrot. "While I was fighting to save everything I had worked for, I was also enduring relentless cyberstalking and harassment that reached into my home and my family's life. An apology cannot undo that damage or give us back those years, but this settlement represents accountability. Now, I'm focused on rebuilding F-Factor, returning to the work I love and reclaiming the future I worked so hard to create."

Under the settlement, Gellis agreed to pay Zuckerbrot $240,000 in monthly installments of $500 over 40 years. The payment represents reimbursement for the costs of trauma treatment Zuckerbrot underwent as a result of the campaign. The settlement also requires Gellis to publish a video apology on her social media and keep it pinned to the top of her profile for three and a half years, ensuring it remains prominently visible to visitors.

The lawsuit arose from Gellis's social media campaign against Zuckerbrot and F-Factor. The lawsuit alleged Gellis used her platforms to amplify anonymous allegations to a large online audience, including claims of arsenic contamination, serious health harms and personal misconduct. In her public apology, Gellis acknowledged that the allegations she shared were based on anonymous submissions rather than verified medical, scientific or expert analysis.

According to court records, Gellis posted more than 4,500 Instagram stories about F-Factor in just 75 days. The total number of videos and posts about her over the following years exceeded 50,000. As the posts escalated, Gellis shifted from product allegations to deeply personal attacks involving false accusations of drug use, tax evasion and criminal activity.

As the case stated, F-Factor products were co-manufactured in a pharmaceutical–grade facility and tested for microbiological safety, heavy metals and label accuracy. Certificates of analysis and a toxicology report supported their safety. Despite receiving this documentation, Gellis continued to promote allegations of contamination and claimed "tens of thousands" of victims, figures she now publicly acknowledges were inaccurate and false. releases.body:
33-year marketing firm founded by Mark J. Murray enters a new chapter focused on strategy, growth, technology and expanded capabilities while honoring the contributions of Marilyn J. Bina and the entire PRIME team

MAPLE GROVE, Minn., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- After 33 years of helping businesses grow and supporting its communities, Prime Advertising + Design Inc. is entering a new chapter under the leadership of Steve Jung and a new name: Prime Marketing + Design LLC. The evolution reflects PRIME's growing focus on strategy, technology and expanded marketing capabilities.

PRIME was founded by Mark J. Murray, who built the company around a commitment to creativity, strong relationships, exceptional service, community involvement, and helping businesses grow. His mother, Marilyn J. Bina, joined a few years later and became his longtime business partner, playing an integral role in PRIME's growth, relationships and commitment to giving back.

"When I founded PRIME 33 years ago, I never could have imagined the people, businesses and communities we'd have the opportunity to work with," Murray said. "I was fortunate to have my mom, Marilyn, join me and eventually become my business partner. Her impact on PRIME has been tremendous. I'm incredibly proud of what we've built together and excited for what comes next."

Murray will remain actively involved in Prime Marketing + Design, working alongside Jung and the existing team. He will focus on client growth, strategy, relationships and business development.

Jung is already well known to PRIME through M&G Trailer, one of the agency's longtime and valued clients. Jung also owns Silver Spur Ranch, a high-end wedding and event venue, and a more recent client of PRIME's. These relationships have allowed PRIME to experience firsthand Jung's leadership philosophy and his ability to build and grow companies.

"PRIME has an incredible history, talented people, strong client relationships and a reputation built over 33 years," Jung said. "My goal isn't to change what makes PRIME special. It's to invest in it, build upon it and create even more opportunities for our employees and clients."

Strategy First: An Extension of the Client's Team

Prime Marketing + Design will expand its role as a strategic marketing and technology partner, serving as a complete outsourced marketing department or an extension of a client's internal team.

"Businesses don't need more vendors," Murray said. "They need the right experts at the table who understand their business, goals and challenges, and work together to help them grow."

Investing in Website Development and AI Search

PRIME will place an increased emphasis on website strategy, design and development, as well as emerging AI search technologies and AI-powered discovery.

As consumers increasingly use AI-powered platforms to research businesses, compare solutions, and make purchasing decisions, the company plans to help clients strengthen their websites, content, digital authority, and visibility across both traditional search engines and emerging AI platforms.

"Marketing and technology are evolving quickly," Murray said. "We want to help our clients understand what's changing and take advantage of new opportunities."

Marilyn J. Bina: An Integral Part of the PRIME Legacy

Marilyn J. Bina joined PRIME a few years after its founding and became Murray's longtime business partner. Her focus on relationships, community involvement and giving back helped shape PRIME's culture and growth for more than three decades.

"My mom, Marilyn, has been my business partner, my best friend, and an incredible part of PRIME's story," Murray said. "Her ability to build relationships, care about people and connect with our communities has always been at the heart of who we are."

Throughout its history, PRIME has worked with businesses, municipalities, nonprofits, youth organizations, and community groups to grow brands, communicate with residents, strengthen communities, and support meaningful causes.

"We're proud of our first 33 years," Murray said. "Now we are excited to see where we can take PRIME next. The sky is the limit!"

Prime Marketing + Design LLC, formerly Prime Advertising + Design Inc., is a full-service marketing, creative and technology company with 33+ years of experience helping businesses and organizations grow.

Services include strategy, branding, digital marketing, social media, websites, AI and SEO search, content, photo and video, print, publications, community engagement and integrated campaigns.

PRIME serves as a complete outsourced marketing department or an extension of an internal team, bringing together expertise across marketing, creative, digital and technology.

releases.title: Mentor Collective Launches Flash Mentoring to Close the Career Readiness Gap in Higher Education
releases.body:
New flexible mentoring model gives every student access to alumni expertise, complementing Mentor Collective's Structured Mentoring programs

BOSTON, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mentor Collective, higher education's preferred edtech platform for student mentorship, announced the launch of Flash Mentoring, a new, purposeful model built around focused, single-session conversations between students and alumni. Flash Mentoring joins Mentor Collective's existing Structured Mentoring model to support the full arc of the student journey, from belonging to employability, on one platform.

Higher education institutions are under unprecedented pressure to demonstrate career readiness, workforce outcomes, and degree ROI. Many students, including first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented students, still lack access to the professional networks that open doors, and not every student is looking for, or has time for, a long-term match. Mentor Collective meets students right where they are. With Flash Mentoring, every student has a low-barrier way to build real-world social capital on their own terms: whenever they need it, and as often as they need it, with no long-term commitment required.

"Every student's path looks different, and their support should too," said Patrick Garayta, Chief Executive Officer of Mentor Collective. "Some students want an ongoing relationship with a peer mentor. Others need the right person with the right experience for one purposeful conversation. Flash Mentoring and Structured Mentoring are built for exactly that reason, and together, they mean no students' needs will fall through the cracks."

Flash Mentoring is also designed with alumni in mind. Traditional engagement strategies, from reunions to newsletters to committee service, reach only a small fraction of a given alumni base. Flash offers a flexible, time-boxed way for alumni to give back in a single conversation, activating graduates who would never respond to a longer commitment. At the same time, advancement and alumni relations teams gain a new, trackable form of engagement to bring to leadership.

"Career offices and advancement teams keep telling us the same thing: their networks are bigger than their engagement numbers show," said Jennifer Kious, Director of Marketing at Mentor Collective. "Flash Mentoring is specifically built to reach the alumni who are typically disengaged. Every conversation becomes data our partners can use to tell a clearer story about alumni engagement and student outcomes."

Flash Mentoring gives every student a low-barrier way to build that access: a focused conversation with an alum around a specific question or goal, without the long-term commitment of a traditional mentoring program. For alumni, it offers a meaningful, flexible way to give back on their own schedule. For institutions, every conversation becomes a logged, reportable data point that strengthens the case for continued investment in student success.

Many students, including first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented students, still lack access to the professional networks that open doors, and not every student is looking for, or has time for, a long-term match. Flash Mentoring gives every student a low-barrier way to build real-world social capital on their own terms: a single, focused conversation with an alum around a specific question or goal, whenever they need it, and as often as they need it, with no long-term commitment required.

Flash Mentoring is available now to all higher education institutions, on its own or alongside Structured Mentoring, through the same co-branded experience and reporting dashboard partners already use to track student outcomes.

Mentor Collective expects Flash Mentoring to help partner institutions nationwide expand access to career readiness support, close equity gaps in social capital, and give alumni a meaningful, low-lift way to stay connected to their alma mater.

To learn more about Flash Mentoring, visit mentorcollective.org.

Mentor Collective is an education technology provider that drives student enrollment, retention, and career readiness through research-backed, scalable mentorship solutions. The company's mission is to ensure every learner realizes their full potential through connections, confidence, and support—not by chance, but by design. Mentor Collective enables institutions to embed personalized mentorship into the fabric of the learner experience, strengthening belonging, closing social capital gaps, and accelerating career readiness. Backed by over a decade of results, Mentor Collective supports more than one million participants across 200+ partnerships.

releases.body:
Show launched on a $5,000 grant after the 2025 L.A. Fires Invites Listeners to vote for Signal's Listener's Choice Award by Oct. 15

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- #L.A. Rising -- Stories of Healing, Help & Hope, a nonprofit podcast created by a Los Angeles fire survivor, has been named a Finalist in the 5th Annual Signal Awards, one of the podcast industry's leading international honors, in the Mental Health category. The news follows the show's national 2026 Best of the Year Award in Tech & Media, from a program created by former Hearst Magazines senior editors.

The Signal Awards are "mission-focused on uplifting the podcast medium by recognizing the most potent, meaningful and unprecedented audio projects being made today." Its judges – ranging from author Jay Shetty to content executives at Ted Talks, NPR and YouTube -- are described as "the architects, instigators and trailblazers of the medium."

The finalist episode, "Writing to Surprise Ourselves: Fire Survivor Kathleen Katims' Saved by a Story," is also in the running for the Signal Listener's Choice Award, a global public vote that drew more than 385,000 votes in 2025. Fans can vote through Oct. 15 at vote.signalaward.com. Gold, Silver and Bronze winners will be announced Oct. 20.

The recognition is remarkable given how the show began. Two weeks after the January 2025 "fire hurricane" devastated two Los Angeles communities, veteran podcast host Kim Marshall -- who escaped the Palisades Fire on foot with a small suitcase and two dogs -- launched #L.A. Rising with no network behind it, just a $5,000 small business grant from L.A. County Supervisor Lindsay Horvath's office and a pro bono production partner. Her goal: a trusted place for survivors' stories of resilience, and for expert resources and wellness tools, long after national media moved on.

"What stood out most to me was the raw authenticity: a survivor host sharing survivor stories, without the distance much disaster coverage carries," said one Best of the Year judge.

With Emmy-winning broadcaster Giselle Fernandez as Advising Producer, #L.A. Rising has expanded to disasters worldwide, from flooding in Brazil and Texas Hill Country to Category 5 Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica. Its premise: lessons learned from one disaster can be a catalyst of hope and inspiration for the next. Wellness Lift segments pair each story with coping strategies like deep breathing, contrast bathing, meditation and understanding grief.

International podcast agency NOVA helps produce the show. "This wasn't just a local story — it was a global moment," said NOVA CEO Hayden Lyon. "When Kim came to us with #L.A. Rising, launching it pro bono was an easy decision."

Since early 2026, Marshall and NOVA also help produce After the Fire USA's "How to Disaster" podcast on megafire recovery. 

About #L.A. Rising

A nonprofit podcast about resilience in a warming world, hosted by Kim Marshall, in fiscal partnership with the Creative Visions Foundation, featuring survivors, community leaders and experts on disaster recovery. Learn more at larisingstories.org or on Instagram @larisingpodcast.

for Its Denver Wellness Sanctuary to Listeners Anywhere, at Any Time

NEW YORK, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sacred Society, the Colorado-based wellness sanctuary, is expanding beyond its physical space with the launch of three 24/7 YouTube livestreams featuring the functional music created for Rest, Focus and Enjoy at www.sacredsocietymusic.com.

Each stream serves a distinct purpose. Rest provides a soundtrack for winding down and quiet moments; Focus accompanies work, study and concentration; and Enjoy brings more uplifting sounds to social settings and everyday activities. Corresponding playlists are available across major streaming services.

At the center of this new chapter is Toci, the character who connects Sacred Society's music to a larger visual and narrative world shaped in part by Beltran and Guerrero's Mexican heritage. Her story begins with a simple idea: healing is not something you chase, but something you allow. Like many people, Toci loses touch with that understanding amid the noise and movement of modern life. Her journey is one of return, using sound as a way back to herself. Through Toci, Sacred Society Music gives a face and story to the philosophy behind its music, inviting listeners to make that same return in their own lives.

The launch builds on an idea that began inside Sacred Society's wellness sanctuary based in Denver. Founders Barbie Beltran and Jose Guerrero initially developed the music because they wanted a specific sonic environment for guests and couldn't find existing options that fit their vision. To bring this vision to life, they teamed up with music executives Adelio Lombardi (Side 3 Studios) and Bradley Roulier (Beatport co-founder), along with music producer and songwriter Jon Bonus to create Sacred Society Music. That starting point continues to shape the project: rather than adapting an existing artist catalog for wellness use, Sacred Society Music creates its catalog specifically around how and when people intend to listen.

The approach arrives as functional listening becomes an increasingly visible part of the broader music business, with listeners using music alongside sleep, work, meditation and other daily activities. Sacred Society Music's model keeps those uses within one simple framework while combining ambient composition, meditative elements and immersive production, including music mixed exclusively in Dolby Atmos.

Visitors can experience the full world of Sacred Society Music at www.sacredsocietymusic.com, including 24/7 streaming music, interactive digital oracle card pulls, and more.

Today, the Rest, Focus and Enjoy livestreams will also be available on Sacred Society Music's official YouTube channel HERE and across streaming platforms everywhere.

But this is only the beginning for Sacred Society Music. As the project continues to reach audiences globally, Sacred Society is building a world that extends beyond listening, bringing together music, storytelling, mindfulness and culture in new ways. Additional releases, experiences, and elements of the Sacred Society universe will continue to unfold in the months ahead.

ABOUT SACRED SOCIETY MUSIC

Sacred Society Music creates functional music that helps people tune their inner life. We started from necessity. Guests in our Denver sanctuary needed more than background noise. They needed sound designed to support rest, sharpen focus, and lift the mood. Off-the-shelf tracks fell short, so we built our own. We compose original, frequency-informed music mixed in Dolby Atmos. It began as an in-house solution. Now it serves studios, spas, and storytellers who design spaces where people can actually feel something.

releases.title: MediaRadar Expands Sports Intelligence to Reveal Total Event Investment™ Across Advertising and Sponsorship
releases.body:
Sports Intelligence in Insights Studio connects TV broadcast, exclusive live streaming sports advertising and sponsorship insights to provide a more complete view of how brands invest across sports.

NEW YORK, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MediaRadar today announced Total Event Investment™, a proprietary framework that reveals the broader picture of brand investment around major events and cultural moments. Purposefully built for the sports economy, Total Event Investment brings previously fragmented advertising and sponsorship insights together in Insights Studio, the company's newly introduced intelligence platform.

Sports investment extends far beyond the traditional media buy. Brands advertise across TV broadcast and exclusive live streaming sports while simultaneously investing in teams, leagues, athletes and major sporting events through broadcast integrations, virtual placements, in-venue signage, equipment sponsorships and creative campaigns.

"What's especially exciting in sports right now is the innovation happening around how brands can participate," said Jay Nielsen, VP of Product at MediaRadar. "New formats, integrations and sponsorship opportunities are creating more ways for advertisers to show up. Total Event Investment brings those signals together to reveal the broader strategy behind how brands are investing across sports."

Beyond the Media Buy

Total Event Investment grew from MediaRadar's research surrounding the 2026 Men's World Cup, where 6,737 brands invested $1.42 billion across advertising, official sponsorships, athlete and national team partnerships and creative campaigns.

That work helped shape MediaRadar's expansion into sponsorship analytics, complementing its existing TV broadcast and exclusive live streaming sports advertising coverage.

MediaRadar customers can now explore sponsorship signals alongside MediaRadar's Creative, Competitive, Commercial and Market Intelligence to understand how advertising, sponsorship and creative work together as part of a broader brand strategy.

Computer Vision Expands Sponsorship Intelligence

MediaRadar's proprietary Logo Recognition technology uses computer vision to identify brand logos and on-screen placements, transforming visual brand exposure into structured sponsorship intelligence.

Logo Recognition builds on MediaRadar's proprietary Classification Engine, which uses machine learning to organize and enrich advertising data at scale. Together, these capabilities expand the signals MediaRadar can identify, structure and connect through Total Event Investment.

From Media Occurrence to Brand Commitment

While developed through a sports lens, Total Event Investment can extend to other cultural moments, from a championship game or awards show to a month-long tournament or season.

The framework examines how brands show up before, during and after that moment across media investment, sponsorship, creative strategy, activation timing and cross-channel presence, moving beyond individual media occurrences to understand the broader brand commitment surrounding an event.

Understanding the Full Partnership

"When MediaRadar first released Live Streaming Sports in 2025, adding the coverage to our intelligence stack was a no-brainer," said Brett Joss, Head of Sponsorship Sales at Jomboy Media. "While baseball is core to our business, we need visibility into brands investing across other marquee sports. Total Event Investment gives us a more complete picture in one place, helping us move from understanding the market to acting on it."

For brands and agencies, Sports Intelligence provides a way to benchmark competitors, understand multi-sport investment strategies and see how sponsorship connects to paid advertising and creative. For media companies, leagues, teams and rights holders, it provides visibility into brands investing across sports to help identify whitespace and commercial opportunities.

See Total Event Investment in Action

NEW YORK, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Diray Media, the woman-owned, WBENC-certified performance media company pairing four decades of media expertise with its own proprietary optimization technology, has selected Media Consulting Group (MCG) as its upstream optimization partner for streaming TV. Recognizing that the supply side was the next frontier in its performance discipline, Diray identified MCG's buy-side-focused optimization as the missing layer — one that structures and continuously improves the streaming supply behind Diray's campaigns before it ever reaches the bid.

Diray has built its reputation on turning media into measurable business impact— by scoring every placement against client outcomes and adjusting until performance improves. Diray identified the supply side as the next lever in that discipline and chose MCG to shape supply procurement upstream, before a placement is ever won. MCG's distinct approach to securing streaming inventory starts with Diray's sophisticated buying practices, using those insights to shape higher-quality, more relevant supply before it reaches the bid. The two functions were built to work together: Diray's technology proves out what happens after the buy; MCG's optimization shapes what is available to buy in the first place.

What the partnership delivers for Diray Media's clients. Diray now pairs its optimization technology with an upstream supply layer of its own choosing: MCG continuously analyzes and shapes the supply behind Diray's campaigns — reducing exposure to low-value or over-concentrated inventory before it reaches the DSP and expanding reach on the sources that perform. As a single, neutral, buy-side-only layer across the major supply platforms Diray runs on.. The result, as Diray designed it, is a cleaner operational layer: ready-to-activate deal IDs for the DSPs Diray already uses, ongoing visibility and control at the supply level, and more room for Diray's strategists and buyers to stay focused on client outcomes.

From the partners

"Diray built a media services solution that delivers tremendous value — and a culture that demands client performance, backed by technology that scores every placement against real business outcomes. Diray recognized that the supply side was the next place to create advantage for their clients, and that's what makes this partnership possible. Our job is to make sure the inventory feeding their process is the best it can possibly be, before a single bid is placed. Media in, business impact out only holds up if what goes in is good — that is the part we own."

— Daniel Elad, Co-Founder & CRO, Media Consulting Group

SUGGESTED PARTNER QUOTE — PENDING DIRAY MEDIA ATTRIBUTION AND APPROVAL

With our performance-driven clients as an example, we had already identified the gaps on the supply side — low priority supply flooding our bid requests and unbalanced distribution to a small number of platforms – what we needed was a partner who could close it. MCG did exactly that, helping improve our supply-side operations — sharpening the inventory available to the campaign — while customizing the solution around our performance-driven clients' goals and the way their customers actually respond. That combination of operational improvement and client-specific customization gives our team more control before the bid, without changing what makes our buying approach work."

— Dean Chandler, SVP, Media & Video Innovation, Diray Media

Media Consulting Group (MCG) is a buy-side-focused media consulting and activation partner. Working upstream on the supply side through optimization, insights, and analysis, MCG improves how supply is structured and activated before it reaches the bidder, helping agencies, brands, and traders get more out of their media spend. MCG only generates revenue when it creates measurable value. Learn more at wermcg.com.

Diray's strategists, buyers, and analysts work directly on every account, turning what a campaign produces into the outcomes that matter most to each client: sales, orders, leads, and market share. releases.title: Keyfactor Appoints Former CyberArk CEO Matt Cohen to Board of Directors and Strategic Advisor
releases.body:
Appointment comes as Keyfactor closes $1B+ growth investment led by Summit Partners and accelerates its next phase of scale beyond $200 million in ARR

ATLANTA and STOCKHOLM, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Keyfactor, the leader in trust infrastructure for AI and machines, today announced the appointment of former CyberArk CEO Matt Cohen to its Board of Directors. Cohen will also serve as a strategic advisor to Keyfactor CEO Jordan Rackie, providing an additional source of perspective and operating experience as the company enters its next phase of growth and scale.

The appointment coincides with the closing of Keyfactor's previously announced $1 billion-plus growth investment led by Summit Partners and follows the company's recent milestone of surpassing $200 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). Together, the developments reflect Keyfactor's continued growth and accelerate investment behind its Trust Control Plane and expand its leadership across machine identity, cryptography, AI security and post-quantum readiness.

Cohen most recently served as CEO of CyberArk, where he helped lead one of cybersecurity's defining growth stories and ultimately the company's approximately $25 billion acquisition by Palo Alto Networks. Over more than two decades in technology, Cohen has built and scaled global businesses, led major strategic and operational transformations, and created significant enterprise value. Before becoming CyberArk's CEO in 2023, he served as its Chief Revenue Officer and Chief Operating Officer. Earlier in his career, he held senior leadership roles at PTC, including Executive Vice President of Worldwide Field Operations, helping scale the company beyond $1 billion in ARR.

"As we began thinking about Keyfactor's next chapter with Summit and the rest of our Board, we were very intentional about the experience and perspective we wanted around the table," said Jordan Rackie, CEO of Keyfactor. "As our market opportunity continues to expand, we're entering a phase where scaling with ambition, discipline and operational rigor will be critical."

"Matt was someone we pursued very deliberately. He has operated at the scale we aspire to reach, helped build a category leader in cybersecurity and navigated many of the opportunities and inflection points that lie ahead for Keyfactor. We share similar values around leadership, transparency and how to approach both opportunities and challenges. He brings tremendous experience and judgment to our Board, and I'm equally excited to have him as a strategic and trusted advisor as we navigate Keyfactor's next phase of growth."

Keyfactor has emerged as a global leader at the intersection of machine identity and cryptography as enterprises confront an unprecedented expansion in the number of machines, workloads, applications and AI agents that must be authenticated and trusted. The company's Trust Control Plane represents the next evolution of how enterprises manage trust across these environments. It creates a unified control layer that brings together visibility, intelligence, policy and action across machine identity and cryptography.

"The most exciting companies are often positioned at the intersection of major technology shifts, and that's exactly where I believe Keyfactor sits today," said Cohen. "AI, machine identity, cryptographic modernization and the transition to post-quantum security are converging to create one of the most significant security challenges enterprises will face over the next decade."

"Keyfactor has meaningful scale, a strong culture and a clear vision for where the market is headed. From my early conversations with Jordan, we found a lot of common ground, and I saw a leader who's clear-eyed about what the next level of growth truly demands. I'm excited to join the Board, serve as a strategic advisor to Jordan and help the team capitalize on the tremendous opportunity ahead."

Summit Partners' investment provides additional resources to help accelerate Keyfactor's growth strategy, which focuses on continued product innovation, international expansion, strategic acquisitions and investment across the company's global organization. Cohen's appointment reflects a broader philosophy around preparing Keyfactor for its next phase: continuing to strengthen the leadership team while surrounding the company with Board members, advisors and partners who bring relevant experience from the scale Keyfactor intends to reach.

For more information, visit https://www.keyfactor.com/.

About Keyfactor

Keyfactor is the leader in trust infrastructure for AI and machines. The platform equips enterprises to take control of the machine identities and cryptography that safeguard every digital interaction. By bringing fragmented tools and assets into a single control plane, security teams can see their cryptographic landscape, find and remediate risk exposure, roll out compliant and quantum-safe cryptography, and issue a cryptographic identity to every machine, workload and AI. Trusted by the largest enterprises and government agencies, Keyfactor delivers the resilient foundation organizations need to keep running uninterrupted in the AI and quantum era. Learn more at www.keyfactor.com or follow Keyfactor on LinkedIn.
