TORONTO and CHICAGO, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Polymath Research Inc., a provider of enterprise-grade infrastructure for regulated digital securities and tokenized financial instruments, today announced its collaboration with CineCity Studios, a Chicago film and television production facility, to explore the development of a technology-enabled investment platform targeted towards film and entertainment investors.
releases.title: Polymath and CineCity Studios to Explore a Tokenized Film Investment Platform
releases.body:
The collaboration will marry Polymath's digital securities infrastructure with CineCity's film production ecosystem to explore a tokenized film investment vehicle

TORONTO and CHICAGO, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Polymath Research Inc., a provider of enterprise-grade infrastructure for regulated digital securities and tokenized financial instruments, today announced its collaboration with CineCity Studios, a Chicago film and television production facility, to explore the development of a technology-enabled investment platform targeted towards film and entertainment investors.

Under the proposed structure, Polymath would serve as a technology partner to develop a tokenized film investment vehicle, providing infrastructure and expertise to support digital securities issuance, investor onboarding, compliance workflows, investor management, and the ongoing administration of tokenized interests. Polymath is a technology provider. It is not a broker-dealer, funding portal, investment adviser, or placement agent, and is not offering, recommending, or providing advice with respect to any security.

The initiative addresses a longstanding challenge in independent film finance: connecting quality productions with capital efficiently while giving investors a structured way to participate in a diversified portfolio of entertainment-related opportunities. According to Natalie Hirsch, Interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of Polymath:

"The film industry is just one of many exciting examples of where tokenization can solve real-world capital formation problems. CineCity has the facilities, industry relationships, and production ecosystem, while Polymath brings the technology and capital markets infrastructure. Together, we have an opportunity to build a modern investment model around an asset class that historically has been inaccessible to many private investors."

The proposed investment strategy is expected to evaluate opportunities across the film-finance lifecycle and a range of financing structures. Final investment parameters, structure, and offering terms remain subject to legal, regulatory, and commercial review.

CineCity Studios operates a 140,000-square-foot film and television production facility in Chicago that has hosted major productions from Disney, Fox, Netflix, Comcast, NBCUniversal, and Tyler Perry Studios, as well as commercial productions for global brands including BMW, Rolls-Royce, Lamborghini, Xfinity, and Foot Locker/Nike, among others. The studio has also invested in expanding its technology and production capabilities as it continues to support Chicago's growing independent film and television community. According to Stanley Wozniak, Managing Partner of CineCity Studios:

"There's a tremendous amount of capital looking for differentiated investment opportunities, while filmmakers are constantly looking for more efficient ways to finance and produce quality productions. The film and television industry has a constant, growing need for new content. The exciting addition of VP LED Studios on campus brings cutting-edge virtual production, motion capture, multi-cam tracking, Unreal Engine, and AI integration to Chicago. We're bringing next-generation filmmaking to the studio with LED virtual production, combining immersive digital environments and real-time technology to expand creative possibilities and give filmmakers greater control. With VP LED, you can be anywhere. Working with Polymath gives us an opportunity to bring frontier technology into that equation and explore an investment model that can connect these two worlds in a way that has never before been possible."

Future productions at CineCity Studios qualify for Illinois' expanded Film Production Tax Credit, a 35% credit on eligible in-state spending. For investors, the credit creates an opportunity to reduce the effective cost of qualifying production expenditures by 35%, allowing a greater portion of invested capital to be directed toward the production and its revenue-generating assets. With the program extended through 2038, CineCity Studios offers productions a long-term opportunity to take advantage of one of the nation's most competitive film incentives. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, introduced in 2026, would add a federal credit of 20% on U.S. labor. If passed as described, a Chicago production could combine Illinois' 35% credit with the federal 20% credit for a total of 55%, which would make Illinois one of the strongest places in the world to film.

For Polymath, the proposed collaboration would represent another application of tokenization beyond traditional financial assets and real estate, demonstrating how digital securities infrastructure can be applied to intellectual property, entertainment, and alternative investments.

About Polymath

Polymath develops enterprise-grade infrastructure for the issuance, compliance, and lifecycle management of regulated digital securities and tokenized financial instruments. Through its purpose-built technology and capital markets ecosystem, Polymath enables issuers and market participants to create and manage tokenized representations of real-world assets within compliant frameworks, supporting investor onboarding, regulatory controls, and post-issuance administration.

On August 18, 2026, Polymath announced an agreement to be acquired by TruGolf Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRUG), a transaction expected to bring Polymath's purpose-built blockchain and tokenization infrastructure to the U.S. public markets, subject to customary closing conditions.

Learn more at polymath.network

About CineCity Studios

CineCity Studios is a 140,000-square-foot Chicago-based production campus providing comprehensive studio, virtual production, and office facilities for film and television. The facility supports independent movies, major motion picture productions, commercial campaigns, and entertainment industry events such as Filmscape, Half-Rez, Chicago International Film Industry Days, the SAG-AFTRA Baron Awards, the Actors Empowerment Summit, the Pop-Up Asian Film Festival, the Latino Film Festival, IATSE Marketplace, the Best of the Midwest Film Festival Awards, and Chicago Innovation. CineCity Studios advances education, professional training, and industry collaboration, helping strengthen and connect Chicago's growing film and television production community.

Learn more at cinecitystudios.com

Important Notice

The investment vehicle described in this release remains under development. No securities are currently being offered pursuant to this announcement. Any future offering will be made only pursuant to applicable offering documents and in accordance with applicable securities laws and regulations. This release is not an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any security, and is not a recommendation with respect to any investment.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable U.S. and Canadian securities laws. Forward-looking statements include, without limitation, statements regarding the anticipated collaboration between Polymath and CineCity Studios, the expected benefits of the collaboration, the development and structure of a potential tokenized film investment vehicle, potential investment strategies and opportunities, the availability of film production tax credits and the status of proposed legislation, future adoption of tokenized assets, and the proposed acquisition of Polymath by TruGolf Holdings, Inc.

These forward-looking statements are based on current expectations, estimates and assumptions and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause actual results or developments to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements. Such risks include, without limitation, the parties' ability to develop and implement anticipated initiatives, changes in market, economic and regulatory conditions, the tax credits referred to herein being unavailable, evolving legal and compliance requirements relating to digital assets and tokenized securities, technological challenges, the pace of adoption of tokenized securities and digital assets, and the satisfaction of conditions required to complete the proposed acquisition of Polymath by TruGolf. releases.title: Kargo Launches Karlo, Opening Agentic Media Buying to Smaller Teams and Businesses
releases.body:
Karlo brings connected video and cross-platform campaign capabilities that previously required enterprise-scale budgets and teams to a wider set of advertisers

NEW YORK, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kargo today announced the general availability of Karlo, a self-serve agentic media buying platform built for smaller teams and businesses. Karlo gives smaller teams and businesses direct access to the same creative and media technology Kargo has built over two decades, in a simplified, self-serve format designed for their size and speed.

Karlo is powered by two core technologies: Creative Science®, grounded in decades of Kargo's proprietary cross-platform performance data, and Media Intelligence, which combines premium audience data with Kargo's contextual signals. Smaller teams can use the platform to plan, create, and activate campaigns across the open web, CTV, and social from one system, bringing Karlo's "One Platform. Every Screen." approach to a wider set of advertisers.

Karlo gives smaller businesses a way to run connected video campaigns that previously required enterprise-scale budgets and staff. Setup takes minutes, campaigns can be launched and adjusted, and reporting lives in one place, all from a single self-serve platform.

"Most of the agentic tools launching right now are built around bidding and targeting, functions that were already pretty well-automated," said Harry Kargman, founder and CEO of Kargo. "Creative usually sits outside that loop, untouched, even though it's the biggest lever on performance. Karlo takes the creative a business already has and incorporates it into decision-making, scoring, and adjustments, alongside targeting and bidding, in real time. Smaller teams get the same advantage our biggest clients have had for years, without needing the budget or staff they'd normally need to get there."

In a campaign with the Ad Council for its "Love, Your Mind" mental health initiative, Karlo was used to reach adults who tend to disengage from traditional mental health messaging. The campaign drove a 21% lift in ad recall and a 10% lift in aided awareness.

Karlo takes a different approach: instead of setting up separate buys, often with multiple buyers, for CTV, social, and the open web, the platform brings all three into one flow built around a single audience target. It evaluates creative performance alongside media decisions and uses the results to improve campaigns while they're running, so advertisers don't need a dedicated analyst to monitor the account.

Smaller teams can start with existing marketing or briefing documents, or use natural-language prompts to set campaign goals, build audiences, and manage campaigns without learning the workflows of multiple buying platforms. Karlo's contextual technology helps determine where and when ads should appear based on what people are engaging with, adding another layer beyond traditional audience segments and giving smaller advertisers a level of targeting precision usually reserved for bigger budgets.

"Karlo gave us an innovative way to meaningfully engage an audience that can truly benefit from mental health messaging and resources," said DJ Perera, chief media officer at the Ad Council. "This partnership is a powerful example of how the Ad Council's Mental Health Initiative leverages the best of marketing, media, and AI technology to improve mental health outcomes for those who are struggling."

Karlo is available today. To learn more, visit karlo.com.

About Kargo

Kargo is an advertising platform that brings creative and premium media together to improve performance across screens. We combine high-impact creative with precision targeting and 100% premium inventory across CTV, social, the open web, and retail media. Our proprietary AI and Creative Science® technology power that combination, helping brands drive measurable, full-funnel results while simplifying execution. Founded in 2003, Kargo is a global company headquartered in New York, with offices across the US, APAC, and Europe.

kargo@ssmandl.com

releases.title: New ADL Research Reveals Systemic Exclusion of Jewish and Israeli Artists Across Museums, Entertainment and Publishing
releases.body:
Assessment of 40 Museums found that 30 percent are Failing, receiving the Lowest Grading Category of "Critically Deficient."

NEW YORK, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ADL (the Anti-Defamation League) today launched State of the Arts: Advancing Jewish Inclusion in Arts, Entertainment and Culture, a first-of-its-kind body of research and digital platform documenting the systemic exclusion and marginalization of Jewish and Israeli artists across American cultural life. The initiative from the ADL Ratings and Assessments Institute brings together a comprehensive look at three major cultural sectors –museums, live entertainment, and publishing– alongside a companion investigation from the ADL Center on Extremism into the activist networks driving this exclusion.

"Jewish artists are being canceled, blacklisted and pushed out of American cultural life. We knew the situation was bad, we just didn't know how bad, and no one had documented it this way before," said Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL CEO. "Forty leading museums, not one includes Jewish identity in its DEI commitments. Authors are being told to strip Hebrew words and change Jewish character names just to get published. Jewish and Israeli performers are being harassed off stages and dropped from lineups. This is antisemitism and anti-Israeli discrimination, plain and simple, and the arts and culture sector needs to wake up before Jewish voices are silenced entirely."

Key Findings from the Reports

"Behind the Frame": A Quiet, Systemic Erasure in America's Museums

ADL conducted the first-ever systematic evaluation of antisemitism and Jewish representation across 40 leading U.S. art museums, developed in consultation with a 15-member external expert panel of artists, curators, collectors and museum leaders, and grading institutions across three categories: policies and internal standards, art and artist representation, and partnerships and programming. Of the 40 museums invited to review and corroborate their assessments before publication, 23 (58 percent) participated, while the remaining half did not engage in the process. The findings reveal a pattern of erasure by omission:

  • Highest standard remains the exception: Only one of the 40 museums assessed – the Berkeley Art Museum & Pacific Film Archive – achieved the Gold Standard. Other strong performers, earning a place in the Good Showing category, included The Cleveland Museum of Art and the Detroit Institute of Arts.
  • Around one-third were critically deficient: Twelve of 40 museums (30 percent), including major institutions such as the Philadelphia Museum of Art and The Broad, received the lowest possible rating of Critically Deficient.
  • Jewish American Heritage Month received minimal recognition: Only one of 40 museums demonstrated recognition of Jewish American Heritage Month in 2026, even as 24 of 40 museums (60 percent) continued actively recognizing other heritage months during the same period. Moreover, only six of the assessed museums (15 percent) recognized JAHM prior to October 7, five completely ceased doing so by 2026 while the remaining one has not done dedicated programming.
  • Many museums hold substantial, even world-class, Jewish and Israeli collections, yet these works are often absorbed into broader narratives that obscure their Jewish or Israeli significance or are difficult to discover online.

"Missing Chapter": Suppression of Jewish Voices in Publishing

This report, based on secondary research and more than 30 interviews with authors and publishing professionals, identifies seven anti-Jewish trends reshaping the publishing industry since October 7, 2023:

  • Suppression of books with Jewish, Israeli or Zionist characters and themes at the acquisition stage, with authors describing pressure to remove Hebrew words, Israeli settings, and even Jewish-sounding character names.
  • Blacklisting and boycotts of Jewish, Israeli and Zionist authors, including a viral spreadsheet that sorted authors by perceived political affiliation and urged readers not to buy their work.
  • Boycotts of Israeli publishing and institutions, including a 2024 letter signed by more than 1,000 writers calling for a boycott of Israeli publishers.
  • Author-level exclusion from festivals and events.
  • Review-bombing and online harassment, including books receiving negative Goodreads ratings before anyone could have read them.
  • Struggles to get and keep literary agents: Jewish, Israeli and Zionist authors described being told directly that their Jewish or Zionist identity, not the quality of their work, made them "too risky" to represent.
  • Institutional silence and failure to name antisemitism directly, including at organizations like the Authors Guild and PEN America. When statements are issued, they frequently frame the issue as a broad matter of censorship, civility, free expression or generalized anti-bigotry, rather than directly naming the targeting of Jewish and Zionist authors.

Author and photographer Alyssa Rosenheck described the shift in her own career: "This is what literary antisemitism looks like. It doesn't announce itself with swastikas. It hides behind excuses, shifting standards, institutional silence, community exclusion, and decisions that become impossible to separate from the climate surrounding Jewish voices after October 7."

"Dark Stage": Jewish and Israeli Performers Are Being Canceled, Harassed and Silenced

This report and interactive case archive document 65 cases across 41 U.S. locations, the most recent from August 2026, showing how Jewish, Israeli and openly Zionist artists face growing scrutiny, protest, disruption and cancellation across live music, comedy, dance, film and campus programming.

Key trends identified include:

  • Protest activity expanding from political advocacy into cultural exclusion, with campaigns increasingly aimed at preventing Jewish or Israeli artists from performing at all, as seen in repeated demonstrations against dozens of artists, like Matisyahu, the Batsheva Dance Company, and the Israel Philharmonic.
  • Security concerns functioning as a "security veto," where the mere prospect of protest activity, rather than a concrete threat, is enough to cancel events, as occurred with musicians Mikey Pauker and Raviv Kaner.
  • Informal cultural boycotts and institutional distancing that unfold privately, including lost bookings and withdrawn invitations, such as Israeli singer Noga Erez's account of losing international bookings because she is Israeli.
  • Normalized audience disruption and harassment, including comedian Judy Gold being told "You're a Jew" during two shows in one weekend in April 2026, and singer-songwriter Regina Spektor being heckled mid-performance.
  • Social media escalation that compresses institutional decision-making and turns local disputes into national controversies within hours.
  • Institutional inconsistency, with venues and organizations responding unpredictably to controversies, leaving artists unable to anticipate how their appearances will be treated.

Companion Investigation: The Activist Networks Organizing to Exclude Jewish and Israeli Artists 

Alongside the three sector reports, the ADL Center on Extremism released an investigation on the activist networks organizing to infiltrate and pressure cultural institutions, including major museums, in order to exclude Jewish and Zionist artists and disrupt their operations. ADL has tracked a prominent and escalating trend of anti-Zionist protests targeting cultural institutions, including Jewish and Holocaust museums and Jewish entertainers. These trends have involved violence and physical intimidation, harassment, Holocaust trivialization, expressions of support for terror and antisemitic tropes, vandalism, extreme forms of disruption, organized blacklisting and coercive exclusion.

Companion Survey: What the U.S. Public Actually Thinks

A non-nationally representative survey of 951 U.S. adults, conducted by ADL in July 2026, further underscores that this exclusion is not being driven by audience demand: strong majorities of Americans said they would support Jewish and Israeli inclusion across galleries, performances and books, even as many respondents simultaneously said it was "understandable" that others would avoid such work, a disconnect that may explain how exclusion takes root and persists.

"This research shows a clear and consistent gap between perceived market risk, what Jewish and Israeli authors are being told, and actual audience demand," said Shira Goodman, ADL's Vice President of Public Affairs and Special Initiatives. "The interviews ADL carried out with literary professionals for this research, surfaced a recurring pattern of authors being told by agents and publishers to strip Jewish and/or Israeli themes and characters from their work over fears it won't sell or is too much of a risk. The survey findings suggest this risk aversion is a misperception, not a market reality, and something that urgently needs to be addressed by the industry."

The Bottom Line

These findings reflect a combination of organized pressure campaigns, institutional risk-aversion, and structural blind spots in how museums, entertainment venues and publishers recognize and respond to antisemitism.

ADL is calling on museums, publishers, agents, venues and cultural institutions across the country to close these gaps: to name antisemitism explicitly in policies and DEI commitments, to recognize Jewish American Heritage Month alongside other heritage observances, to resist pressure campaigns rooted in identity-based exclusion, and to trust the data showing that American audiences want, and will support, Jewish and Israeli inclusion in the arts.

ADL is the leading anti-hate organization in the world. Founded in 1913 to protect the Jewish people, ADL works to stop the defamation of the Jewish people and secure justice and fair treatment to all. In the face of rising antisemitism and extremism, we protect, advocate, and educate, through a mix of programs and services using the latest innovations and technology, and seek to create a world without hate. More at www.adl.org.

releases.title: Financial Executives International Launches Media Finance Section
releases.body:
Financial leaders in media and entertainment join FEI's cross-industry community

as MFM members become FEI Members today

MORRISTOWN, N.J., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Financial Executives International (FEI) today opened its Media Finance Section, the association's first industry-specific section and the new home for the members, programming and peer networks of the Media Financial Management Association (MFM). The Section gives financial leaders in media and entertainment a permanent place inside one of the longest-standing communities of senior-level corporate financial executives, and it gives that community a direct line into an industry that is rewriting how subscription, advertising, and content revenue is earned, valued and reported.

MFM members voted to approve the merger on July 15, 2026, following due diligence and board endorsement by both organizations. MFM, founded in 1961 and serving approximately 1,200 business and financial executives across broadcast, cable, publishing, streaming and digital media, now operates as FEI's Media Finance Section.

"Media and entertainment financial leaders are working through questions that much of corporate finance is only beginning to confront: bundled revenue, content valuation, structural separations and the use of AI in the close," said Andrej Suskavcevic, CAE, President and CEO of FEI. "Giving that work a named seat inside FEI does two things at once: it connects media finance professionals with peers across every industry, and it brings their hard-won experience to the broader finance community. Both were overdue."

What is live today

  • A dedicated Media Finance Section serving as the hub for media-specific programming, content, research and networking.
  • Full FEI membership for every former MFM member, including access to FEI's professional development, career services, publications and research through the Financial Education & Research Foundation (FERF).
  • Access to FEI's local Chapter network, a benefit not previously available to MFM members. Chapters add a second, geographic layer of peer connection alongside the industry one.
  • Continuity of the media finance programming members have relied on, including the Financial Leaders Forum, the Executive Summit, and the Section's webinar and education calendar.

"Our members were clear about what they wanted: their community intact and their programming stronger, not smaller," said Joseph Annotti, Executive Director of FEI's Media Finance Section and former President and CEO of MFM. "That is what today delivers. The Financial Leaders Forum, the peer networks and the media-specific education all continue, now with the research, Chapter network and professional voice of a larger organization behind them."

Why it matters

Finance teams across media and entertainment have absorbed a sustained run of structural change: revenue arriving through bundles and platform intermediaries rather than direct customer relationships, content assets whose carrying values move with shifting distribution strategy, mid-year separations of linear and streaming businesses, and advertising sold against inventory that did not exist in the prior reporting period. Those are no longer media-only problems. They are appearing across consumer products, software, sports and healthcare as more businesses shift from selling units to sustaining subscriptions.

Placing media finance inside a broader financial-executive community is intended to move expertise in both directions: cross-industry peer exchange, research capacity and policy voice for media finance professionals, and early visibility into emerging reporting and control questions for the wider membership.

Availability

Media Finance Section membership information and the Section's program calendar are available at www.financialexecutives.org.

About Financial Executives International (FEI)

Founded in 1931, FEI is a leading association for senior corporate financial management. Members hold policy-making positions as chief financial officers, chief accounting officers, controllers, treasurers and tax executives at companies across major industries. FEI supports member professional development through peer networking, career services, conferences, research and publications, and members participate in local Chapters across the United States. FEI is headquartered in Morristown, N.J. Learn more at www.financialexecutives.org.

About the Media Finance Section

The Media Finance Section is FEI's first industry-specific section, formed on October 1, 2026, through the merger of the Media Financial Management Association (MFM) into FEI. Founded in 1961, MFM served business and financial executives in media and entertainment with networking, education and media-specific information services. The Section continues that work inside FEI.

Mackenzie Global Equity & Gold Overlay ETF (TSX: MGEG)

MGEG is an alternative mutual fund that combines an actively managed global equity allocation with a strategic 50% notional gold futures overlay in a single ETF. As global equity markets have become increasingly concentrated in U.S. equities, portfolios may also carry greater exposure to common U.S. market and currency drivers. Gold has historically exhibited different return drivers than global equities, while also demonstrating a negative historical relationship with the U.S. dollar, providing diversification.

"By implementing the gold allocation through futures, MGEG maintains full global equity exposure while adding strategic gold exposure in a capital-efficient structure," said Kristi Ashcroft, Executive Vice President, Products and Solutions, Mackenzie Investments. "Investors gain access to the diversification benefits of gold without having to reduce their allocation to global equities."

Mackenzie Modus Global Equity ETF (TSX: MMGL), Mackenzie Modus International Equity ETF (TSX: MMEA) and Mackenzie Modus Global Small-Mid Cap Equity ETF (TSX: MMSD)

Mackenzie Modus is the firm's new brand for a suite of rule-based factor investing strategies. Each Modus ETF systematically targets four established sources of return, value, momentum, quality and low volatility, using a defined and repeatable investment process, rather than relying on manager judgment. Each ETF holds a diversified portfolio built on those four factors while seeking to minimize exposure to uncompensated factors such as size, liquidity, country and sector biases.

MMGL invests primarily in mid and large cap companies globally, while MMSD invests in small and mid-cap companies globally. MMEA focuses on mid and large cap companies across developed markets outside the U.S. and Canada.

The initial offerings of the ETFs have closed, and they will begin trading today on the Toronto Stock Exchange under their respective ticker symbols.

releases.title: USANA CEO Kevin Guest Shares Three Ways to Celebrate International Music Day
releases.body:
SALT LAKE CITY, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In recognition of International Music Day on Oct. 1, USANA Health Sciences (NYSE: USNA) Chairman and CEO Kevin Guest is urging people to experience music as a force that can reduce stress, lift spirits and connect people across cultures.

International Music Day celebrates the world's diverse musical traditions and music's ability to advance peace, friendship, and mutual appreciation. Guest, a lifelong musician who plays guitar and sings, says the day offers a simple invitation: slow down, listen and share music with a friend.

"Music is medicine for the soul," Guest said. "It can meet us where we are emotionally, help us reset, and bring people together even when they're from different backgrounds or languages."

That conviction is deeply personal. In his bestseller, All the Right Reasons: 12 Timeless Principles for Living a Life in Harmony, Guest writes that music filled his childhood home and became his passion. With a love for music, his parents bought a piano before they could afford a car, and Guest grew up singing, playing instruments and dreaming of performing on stage.

"When music comes from the heart, the connection between the musician and the audience is honest and powerful," Guest said. "Music speaks to the soul like nothing else can. It has transformed my life."

Research points to two clear benefits of making music part of daily life:

  1. Music can help regulate stress and emotion. A review of 47 studies involving 2,747 people found that music therapy can significantly reduce physical and emotional stress. Research also suggests that listening to music can calm the body and help people manage difficult emotions.



  2. Music can strengthen human connection. Research on music and social bonding indicates that listening, singing and making music together can encourage shared emotion, coordination and a stronger sense of belonging.

Guest offers three ways to celebrate International Music Day:

  1. Listen beyond your usual playlist. Choose a genre, artist or musical tradition from another culture. Give it your full attention and learn something about the people and history behind it.



  2. Experience music with other people. Attend a local concert, school performance, community event or open-mic night. Live music creates a shared experience that a solo playlist cannot fully duplicate.



  3. Share a song that matters to you. Send a favorite tune to a friend or family member and share why it matters. Then ask them to send one back. A simple exchange can start a meaningful conversation and introduce both of you to something new.

"You don't need to be a professional musician to feel music's power," Guest said. "Sing, play, listen or share a song. On Oct. 1, let music help you find a little more peace within yourself and a little more harmony with the people around you."

About Kevin Guest

Kevin Guest is Chairman and CEO of USANA Health Sciences, a global health and wellness company based in Salt Lake City. He is also a musician, author, speaker and humanitarian. His book, All the Right Reasons, shares lessons on leadership, integrity, relationships and purpose. All proceeds from book sales go to feed hungry children. Visit kevinguest.com for more information.

About USANA Health Sciences

USANA (NYSE: USNA) has provided nutrition and lifestyle products for more than 30 years. Its portfolio includes award-winning supplements, Celavive® skincare and healthy living products. USANA products are used by athletes, Olympians and health-conscious consumers in more than 25 markets worldwide.

releases.title: American University Taps DC College Access Program to Expand Pathways to Opportunity for Local Students
releases.body:
Pioneering D.C. nonprofit welcomes its newest university partner, unlocking financial aid and wraparound services for college-ready students in the District

WASHINGTON, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The DC College Access Program (DC CAP), a nonprofit dedicated to eliminating the higher education achievement gap for Washington, D.C. students, announced American University as its newest university partner today. The collaboration will expand access to higher education pathways that change lives and strengthen communities in the nation's capital.

"Together with DC CAP, we're taking a critical next step toward closing the college opportunity gap for D.C. students. Washington, D.C. isn't just where American University is located, it's our home, and we have a responsibility to ensure that talented students across the District can see a path to an AU education," said Jeremy Lowe, interim vice president of Undergraduate Enrollment Management at American University. "Our partnership with DC CAP strengthens that commitment by helping more D.C. students obtain access, afford, and ultimately thrive in college."

American University joins DC CAP's broader network of University Partners, which provide eligible D.C. students with the support and structure they need to thrive in college, from application to degree completion. Students who participate in the University Partnerships program are more likely to persist through college than their peers: 85% of freshmen continue on to their sophomore year, and 57-100% graduate from college within five years, 3-5 times the national average, reducing the likelihood of accruing unnecessary educational debt and opening the door to greater economic and career opportunities.

As a DC CAP University Partner, American University certifies its commitment to ensuring every college-ready D.C. student has the financial resources, coaching, and community they need to succeed. American University will collaborate closely with DC CAP to maximize financial aid availability, stacking DC CAP scholarships, Pell Grants, D.C. Tuition Assistance Grants (DCTAG), and institutional aid with the goal of helping D.C. students finish college with little to no debt. The partnership will also provide tailored academic and socio-emotional support to D.C. students, from enrollment to graduation.

"For so many of our scholars, staying close to the community they grew up in matters, and having one of the nation's top universities just a short Metro ride away means they don't have to choose between a great education and home," said Eric Waldo, executive director of DC CAP. "We couldn't be more thrilled to be joining forces with American University. This partnership will help turn proximity into opportunity, and ensure that more students in the District can access the support they need to learn and thrive."

By leveraging dollars, connecting students to better match universities, and providing wraparound support, DC CAP Scholars works to ensure students graduate ready to compete in today's economy.

About American University

American University leverages the power and purpose of scholarship, learning, and community to impact our changing world. What began as a partnership rooted in mentorship and empowering women in the industry has grown into something far bigger: Legacy Distribution's acquisition of global distribution powerhouse Vision Films.

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This extraordinary combination brings together the unique strengths of both companies, uniting their content portfolios and operations into a single distribution entity. Dana Webber, CEO and Managing Partner of Legacy Distribution, will be the CEO of the expanded company operating under "Vision Films." Lise Romanoff, Founder and Managing Director of Vision Films, will transition into a consultant role; she will represent Vision Films at AFM in November. Vision will continue to offer acclaimed new releases alongside the robust merged libraries of features, TV series, documentaries, specials, and music programming.

Vision's deep library spans decades and includes award-winning and critically acclaimed independent films from all genres, television series, documentaries, narrative features, and specialty programming that has been distributed across theatrical, digital, and broadcast platforms to audiences in more than 190 countries. It is a prestigious VOD aggregator and direct supplier to all major global TVOD, SVOD, and AVOD platforms.

"I've spent years building Vision Films into a company I'm proud of. This is a dream opportunity to pass the baton to a colleague and friend who shares my commitment and dedication. Dana is the right leader for this next chapter of Vision's library, to seamlessly take care of my producers, company, and everyone who helped me build it. I could not find a better partner to carry on and grow my legacy (pun intended)," shares Lise Romanoff.

"Vision Films' global reach and powerful operations position us to advance our mission of delivering diverse and compelling content to audiences worldwide," says Dana Webber. "Lise is widely respected across the media industry for building a leading global content distribution business through sheer grit and vision."

Vision Films' extensive library consists of Murder Between Friends, Time Hoppers, Christmas With A Crown, The Healer, My Secret Billionaire, Tango Shalom (a.k.a. Forbidden Tango), Walt Before Mickey, If I Could Ride, and Off The Menu, as well as acclaimed documentary features including Hired Gun, Living in the Future's Past, In the Company of Wolves, Gandhi, Fantasy Rising, American Clowns, and You Belong To Me, among many others. New releases include Pinball: Beyond The Bumpers, Love on Tap, Line of Control, and UFOs and God.

Legacy's vast library includes popular true-crime series such as Crime Stories, Blood, Lies & Alibis, Crime Stoppers: Case Files, Bounty Hunters, and Murder At My Door; fan-favorites including Funniest Pets and People, Positively Paula, A+E After Dark, Pets In Paradise, Ex-Wives of Rock, and Restaurant Takeover; feature films such as Authors Anonymous, Wake, Moving Mountains, The Luau, and Crazylove, alongside the iconic The Other Side of Hell and Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders, and documentary features 9/11: The Day The World Stood Still, Michael Jackson: Ungloved, Tina Turner: Simply the Best, Dolly Parton: Big Hair, Bigger Heart, and Disasters of the Decades.

California Bank & Trust served as senior lender to Legacy Distribution. The Mager Law Firm served as exclusive legal advisor, and Errol Antzis served as exclusive investment consultant to Legacy Distribution. Harris Tulchin & Associates served as exclusive legal advisor to Vision Films.

releases.body:
FREDERICK, Md., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Frederick Arts Council (FAC) is proud to announce the launch of its new FAC record label, Good People, expanding its commitment to supporting, promoting, and creating opportunities for artists across Frederick County. The label will officially launch on October 30, 2026, with the release of two songs by local Frederick artist Libby Knight, available on vinyl and across major streaming platforms.

Libby Knight is a 14-year-old singer-songwriter born and raised in Frederick, Maryland, whose music is soulful, honest, and unafraid to explore life's challenges. A self-taught piano player, Libby writes songs about the complicated reality of human relationships.

The debut will feature Knight's songs "Someone So Bad" and "Bows," marking an exciting new chapter in FAC's ongoing work to support the creative community and provide artists with opportunities to share their work with broader audiences. The songs will be available digitally on October 30, with a vinyl release also contributing to the launch of the new label.

The release will coincide with a special performance by Libby Knight at Sky Stage, 59 South Carroll St., on October 30th. Local Hip-Hop artist Retro/Ricole will MC the event. Audiences will be able to experience the exciting FAC record label artist live as the debut officially begins. FAC's Sky Stage continues to serve as a platform for original music and emerging and established artists throughout the creative community.

"The launch of the FAC record label builds upon the Council's longstanding commitment to investing in artists and strengthening Frederick's creative economy," said Louise Kennelly, executive director of the Frederick Arts Council. Through grants, artist opportunities, public art initiatives, performances, exhibitions, and community partnerships, FAC works to ensure that artists have the resources and platforms they need to create and share their work.

The label is just one of the many projects FAC has undertaken for local artists during its 50th Anniversary year. For five decades, the Frederick Arts Council has advocated for the arts and helped cultivate the vibrant creative community.

More information about the FAC record label, Libby Knight's release, vinyl availability, and the October 30th performance at Sky Stage will be available on the Frederick Arts Council website as the launch date approaches.

Tickets for the event at Sky Stage can be purchased at

https://www.eventbrite.com/e/sky-stage-presents-libby-knight-with-special-guests-tickets-2002227466250?aff=oddtdtcreator&keep_tld=true 

About the Frederick Arts Council

The Frederick Arts Council invests in a vibrant and cohesive arts community for the people of Frederick County. The organization fosters an environment where the arts flourish in the community through grants and scholarships, arts advocacy, and links to essential resources. FAC is responsible for large-scale programming such as Sky Stage, Frederick Festival of the Arts, Art in the Park, the Public Art Initiative, and Frederick County's Arts in Education grants.

For more information about the Frederick Arts Council, visit www.frederickartscouncil.org.

releases.title: Corgi Insurance Launches Sports and Entertainment Coverage Through Its Surplus Lines Carrier
releases.body:
SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Corgi Insurance today announced the launch of Golden by Corgi, a dedicated sports and entertainment insurance platform providing coverage for the organizations, events, facilities, and businesses that power the sports industry.

Golden provides insurance solutions for teams, leagues, federations, National Governing Bodies, tournaments, athletic facilities, sporting events, and other organizations operating across the sports ecosystem. The platform offers more than 20 lines of coverage designed around the specialized risks these organizations face.

Golden is led by Peter Akman and Mike T. Brown, former founders and professional athletes who bring experience building businesses and competing professionally. Their backgrounds have shaped Golden's approach to insurance, with a focus on the operational realities of sports organizations.

Through Corgi's surplus lines carrier, Golden can build customized insurance programs for organizations with specialized or complex coverage needs. The platform combines underwriting, claims, and risk management capabilities under one system, with certificates of insurance available in minutes and in-house claims handling.

"Sports is an incredibly diverse industry, and the insurance needs of a national governing body can look very different from those of a tournament, facility, or professional organization," said Peter Akman, Co-Founder of Golden. "We built Golden to give each organization the flexibility to build coverage around how it actually operates."

Golden is already working with National Governing Bodies and Olympic programs, including USA Fencing, as well as organizations across the broader sports ecosystem.

The platform is designed to support organizations throughout the lifecycle of their operations, from day-to-day activities and facilities to tournaments, events, athletes, and other specialized exposures.

"Insurance should not be another operational hurdle for sports organizations," said Mike T. Brown, Co-Founder of Golden. "Golden brings sports expertise together with Corgi's insurance infrastructure to make the process faster, simpler, and more tailored to the organizations we serve."

About Golden

Golden is Corgi's dedicated sports and entertainment insurance platform, providing commercial insurance solutions for sports organizations across the United States. The platform offers more than 20 lines of coverage designed for the unique risks faced by teams, leagues, tournaments, facilities, events, and sports organizations of all sizes.

Learn more at getgolden.insure.

About Corgi

Corgi is an AI-native insurance carrier built for high-growth companies. The company combines proprietary underwriting technology, in-house claims handling, and modern insurance infrastructure to deliver coverage built for the way businesses operate today.

In the news release, Reel Wheels Entertainment™ Unveils Hundreds of Film and Television Icons, Backed by Award-Winning Hollywood Talent, issued 30-Sep-2026 by Reel Wheels Entertainment LLC. over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that the original version did not include public-facing contact details as incorrectly formatted by PR Newswire.

Reel Wheels Entertainment™ Unveils Hundreds of Film and Television Icons, Backed by Award-Winning Hollywood Talent

The extraordinary private collection spans vehicles, aircraft, props, wardrobe and memorabilia, forming the foundation of a new global experiential entertainment platform.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Maybe it was the Lamborghini Countach poster on your bedroom wall. Maybe it was Jake Ryan's Porsche 944 in Sixteen Candles. Maybe it was the Thunderbird from Thelma & Louise.

"The cars are the gateway. They open the door into an entire world of film and television."

Somewhere along the way, a car stopped being transportation and became part of a memory.

For the past three years, Reel Wheels Entertainment™ ("Reel Wheels") has been assembling those memories in physical form.

Now, the company is stepping into the public spotlight with a private collection spanning hundreds of vehicles, aircraft, props, wardrobe, memorabilia and entertainment assets connected to some of the most recognizable movies, television shows and moments in popular culture.

At a time when almost anything can be generated, streamed or digitally recreated, Reel Wheels is building around something increasingly powerful: real community formed around physical objects people can see up close and experience together.

But Reel Wheels is not being developed as a traditional museum, and the cars themselves are only the beginning.

"The cars are the gateway," said Aaron Phillips, CEO of Reel Wheels. "They open the door into an entire world of film and television. The characters, scenes, props, music and memories people already carry with them."

Phillips describes the vision as a cultural time tunnel, reconnecting audiences with what they loved growing up, surrounding them with what they love today, and creating anticipation for what comes next.

FROM COLLECTION TO EXPERIENCE

The collection includes original screen-used pieces, production-related artifacts and recreations, with provenance identified individually.

Among its holdings is the original screen-used cockpit from Airplane! Co-writer and co-director Jerry Zucker recently sat down with Reel Wheels for an interview about the film, the cockpit and why physical pieces of filmmaking still matter decades later. Reel Wheels plans to release that conversation soon.

"These objects also carry memories that belong to the audience as much as to us. People tell me they watched Airplane! with their dad, or on a first date, or at a sleepover where they laughed until they couldn't breathe. Seeing something real from the film brings that moment back. It connects people to a time in their own lives, not just to the movie," Zucker said.

Other highlights include an aircraft used in M*A*S*H, a screen-used mid-engine Dodge Charger from F9: The Fast Saga, a production aircraft fuselage associated with Sully, an original production stunt proton pack from Ghostbusters, The Cannonball Run ambulance, and vehicles, props and wardrobe connected to Men in Black and other celebrated film and television properties.

The assets currently visible publicly represent only a portion of Reel Wheels' holdings. Additional vehicles, aircraft and significant entertainment memorabilia continue to be documented and introduced.

A WORLD-CLASS TEAM OF INDUSTRY VETERANS

Reel Wheels has assembled a world-class design and production team capable of helping brands, studios, resorts, hospitality groups and destination developers integrate Reel Wheels assets into their own creative vision, from a single high-impact activation to a fully developed immersive environment.

Rick Carter, advisor to Reel Wheels, is a two-time Academy Award-winning production designer whose credits include Avatar, Lincoln, Jurassic Park, Forrest Gump and The Fabelmans.

"What could be more real than Reel Wheels?" Carter said. "These are the cars we all dreamed of driving and owning, the cars that made us want to be those characters and ignited our sense of speed, adventure and imagination in the 'reel worlds' of classic movies."

Doug Meerdink, Chief Creative Officer of Reel Wheels, has spent more than two decades working in feature-film art direction and production design.

"Reel Wheels gives us the opportunity to extend cinematic storytelling beyond the screen," Meerdink said. "By placing extraordinary physical assets at the center of immersive environments, we can transport audiences directly into the stories they love."

Veteran picture-car specialist Dennis McCarthy, founder of Vehicle Effects and advisor to Reel Wheels, brings decades of experience across more than 100 motion pictures, including extensive work throughout the Fast & Furious franchise, Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice and Avengers: Endgame.

"Cars in movies and television are more than transportation, they're characters," McCarthy said. "The right car can tell you who someone is before they ever say a word."

BUILT AROUND A PARTNER'S VISION

"We don't expect a partner to build their vision around our collection," Phillips said. "Our job is to understand their vision and use our assets, designers and production capabilities to help make it extraordinary."

Potential applications range from brand activations and resort programming to touring entertainment, studio collaborations and permanent destination-scale attractions.

Reel Wheels is also exploring opportunities internationally, including in Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as investment in tourism, hospitality and location-based entertainment creates opportunities for ambitious physical experiences at scale.

"A recognizable car may be what gets someone through the door," Phillips said. "But the destination is the world it came from."

AN INVITATION TO CREATE

Reel Wheels is inviting filmmakers, production designers, technologists, global brands, hospitality leaders, studios, destination developers and storytellers to imagine what can be built around the collection.

"After three years of collecting, preserving, building and imagining what Reel Wheels could become, we're ready to open the door," Phillips said.

The cars are the gateway. The stories are the destination.

ABOUT REEL WHEELS

Reel Wheels is an experiential entertainment company built around a private collection spanning hundreds of vehicles, aircraft, props, wardrobe, memorabilia and entertainment assets connected to film, television and popular culture. The company is backed by a world-class team of industry veterans spanning production design, art direction, picture cars and experiential entertainment, bringing decades of experience from major motion pictures and global entertainment projects.

The collection includes assets with differing provenance, including original screen-used pieces, production-related assets and recreations. Reel Wheels identifies provenance individually and does not represent every asset as an original screen-used piece.

The publicly displayed collection represents only a portion of Reel Wheels' holdings, with additional vehicles, aircraft and entertainment memorabilia continuing to be documented and introduced.

For media inquiries, partnership opportunities, collection-related questions, or to learn more about Reel Wheels Entertainment™, please contact Aaron Phillips directly at aaron@reelwheels.com or by phone 310 879 5289

reelwheels.com

BOSTON, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Boston Globe Media and Tufts Health Plan, a Point32Health company, have partnered once more to launch season six of Turning Points: Navigating Mental Health, an original podcast series focused on important conversations around mental health.

The five-episode series, created in collaboration with Boston Globe Media's branded content experts at Studio/B will feature stories from those who have reclaimed their emotional well-being by finding their "Turning Points." For its sixth season, Turning

Points: Navigating Mental Health will tackle topics such as parenting in the age of social media, starting over after loss, and navigating mental health in a constant news cycle, among other topics. New episodes will be launched every Wednesday, beginning October 7, 2026.

"We're privileged to continue our impactful partnership with Point32Health and Tufts Health Plan to help bring these meaningful stories to life," said Angus Macaulay, chief commercial officer of Boston Globe Media. "Past seasons of Turning Points peaked at #1 on Apple's mental health podcast charts and we were nominated for Webby and Shorty Awards alongside industry giants like Sanjay Gupta and Esther Perel. Both honors are an incredible testament to how conversations around mental health are important for a much broader audience than we ever imagined."

Renowned clinical social worker and accomplished writer and public speaker Frantzes Lys will return to host season six of Turning Points. Lys has dedicated her life's work to helping people heal by removing emotional blocks in their lives. In each episode, Lys digs into mental health journeys through conversations with various personalities who share unique perspectives of mental well-being.

"Mental health is just as important as physical health, but it can often feel harder to talk about," said Edward Walker, president of government markets for Tufts Health Plan, a Point32Health company. "The stories shared through Turning Points help normalize those conversations while offering listeners insight, hope and connection. We're excited to partner again with Boston Globe Media to continue elevating perspectives that encourage people to prioritize their emotional well-being."

Visit Globe.com/TurningPoints to learn more about Turning Points, and find episodes on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other podcasting platforms.

Its flagship publication, The Boston Globe, is a 27-time Pulitzer Prize-winning news organization with the largest digital subscriber base of any metro news organization in the United States and the largest newsroom in New England. Together, this media platform reaches, serves, and convenes smart audiences with world-class journalism, curated events, creative marketing services, data services, and original video storytelling.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

WHAT: A new photography and listening installation at Wrensilva | Los Angeles pairs Linda McCartney's music photography with the album covers that featured her work, alongside Wrensilva record consoles where vinyl copies can be played. Artists featured include The Beatles, The Cimarons, Denny Laine, Paul McCartney, The Pretenders, Professor Longhair, and Neil Young.

WHEN: Open through February 2027. Gallery hours: Monday - Saturday, 11 a.m.-6 p.m.

WHERE: Wrensilva | Los Angeles, 8625 Melrose Ave., West Hollywood, CA 90069

BACKGROUND: Linda McCartney (née Eastman, 1941 – 1998) didn't direct her subjects. She was already in the room, camera in hand, while some of the most magnetic artists of her generation lived their lives around her. Her professional photography career began with shooting musicians, and music photography continued as a steady thread throughout her life.

McCartney had a particular skill for putting musicians at ease and producing uniquely unguarded portraits. For the most part, she rejected the stiff studio setups in favour of informal settings and nature. She preferred prolonged shooting sessions where exchanging knowledge and enthusiasm for the music shared space with the photography itself. She photographed people as she found them, never encouraging contrived performance for her lens.

Photography connected with all of the facets of her career and life - musician, activist, food entrepreneur, family documentarian. Her photographs on display here were used on album covers. Some were the result of official commissions from record labels; some were personal photographs lifted out of their intimate context. Shown here beside the records that enshrined them, to be enjoyed alongside the albums themselves, which are available to play on a Wrensilva record console.

Presented by Wrensilva, The Linda McCartney Archive LLP, and MPL Communications.

About Wrensilva

Handmade in San Diego since 2016, Wrensilva® crafts the ultimate record consoles—timeless centerpieces that invite you to slow down and reconnect with the music that defines you. Seamlessly blending generational-quality craftsmanship with modern audio performance, each console is built with beautifully grained hardwoods and enduring material selections. Created for design-minded music lovers, Wrensilva consoles offer effortless transitions between vinyl and streaming. With every detail thoughtfully considered, Wrensilva transforms listening to music into a ritual—one that brings warmth, beauty, and connection into your home. Learn more at wrensilva.com.

About MPL Communications

MPL Communications is Paul McCartney's company, founded in 1969. It manages his catalog, his post-Beatles work, and his archive, including the Linda McCartney Archive.

releases.title: Study Finds Majority of Advertisers Would Pay a Premium for More Audience Choices and Faster Campaign Delivery
releases.body:
Although most advertisers are bullish on commerce media spending, 86% say slow audience fulfillment could cause them to cut spending or leave a network partner

NEW YORK, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GrowthLoop, a pioneer in agentic AI-powered marketing solutions, today released its 2026 Commerce Media Investment Index, revealing that activation speed and audience options have become decisive factors in where advertisers place retail and commerce media budgets. Conducted in partnership with Ascend2, the study surveyed nearly 300 U.S. and Canadian marketing professionals involved in retail media network (RMN) or commerce media network (CMN) advertising decisions.

The findings reveal what motivates advertisers to spend more with network partners and shed light on how execution friction could put that spend at risk:

  • 86% say slow audience fulfillment could cause them to reduce spend or leave a network partner, while 85% say they would pay a premium for same-day fulfillment.  
  • Nearly all respondents indicate that access to more segments would make them more likely to increase spend.
  • 32% of advertisers have reduced, paused, or reconsidered investment because of difficulty proving ROI to leadership.

"Advertisers are telling media networks how to win more budget: Provide better audiences, activate them faster, and deliver meaningful results quickly enough to inform the next campaign," said Anthony Rotio, co-founder and co-CEO of GrowthLoop. "As we've seen with customers like Gopuff, a warehouse-native audience building solution is the way to fulfill these requirements and ultimately build stronger advertiser relationships."

Key report findings

The Index shows that advertisers spread significant budget across a crowded commerce media market. The majority of advertisers allocate at least 15% of their digital advertising budgets to these networks and 90% work with two or more RMN or CMN partners. No respondents plan to decrease commerce media spend in the next year, and a full 85% plan to increase their spend.

Additional findings include:

Speed shapes spending decisions

  • 92% would be more likely to increase spend with faster audience fulfillment.
  • 94% would likely spend more with partners offering self-service audience-building tools.
  • Advertisers reporting the strongest ROI are five times more likely than others to receive custom audiences the same day.

Advertisers want more audience choice

  • Only 38% are extremely satisfied with the number of audiences available through their partners.
  • 95% say they would be more likely to increase spend with access to more segments.

Confidence in incrementality measurement drives investment and ROI

  • Only 40% are very confident in their partners' incrementality measurement.
  • Advertisers with high confidence in their partners' measurement spend a larger share of their digital budget on RMN/CMN and are more than twice as likely to significantly exceed ROI targets.

Campaign results often arrive too late to guide the next decision

  • Nearly half of advertisers wait at least one week for post-campaign performance data, while only 8% receive it the same day.
  • Just 32% say they can consistently use campaign results to optimize future audience targeting.

Putting audience scale and speed into practice

As audience speed and scale remain top of mind for advertisers, Gopuff — the leading instant commerce platform that delivers thousands of everyday products to customers in minutes — has shown how media networks can successfully address these priorities. Leveraging a composable commerce media solution, Gopuff can provide brand advertisers with a larger pool of audiences, activate campaigns quickly, and provide faster, more comprehensive visibility into campaign metrics.

"Advertisers increasingly expect both greater audience customization and faster activation, and we no longer have to trade one for the other," said JR Crosby, director of data partnerships at Gopuff. "After implementing a warehouse-native stack, we increased our audience segments from 100 to more than 600, and expanded audiences for our subsidiary, BevMo!, from 75 to 400. These expanded audience catalogs give our internal teams and brand partners a broader range of ready-to-use targeting options and create the groundwork for more customized segment offerings."

To download the full 2026 Commerce Media Investment Index, visit go.growthloop.com/cmn-index. To learn more about GrowthLoop's Composable Commerce Media solution, visit https://www.growthloop.com/teams/commerce-media.

About GrowthLoop

GrowthLoop is a pioneer in composable, AI-powered marketing on the data cloud, featured on G2 by its customers as a momentum leader with the best ROI for enterprise. The GrowthLoop agentic, composable CDP drives compound growth by accelerating the marketing cycle using agentic AI powered by your enterprise cloud data. Working alongside AI agents, teams use GrowthLoop to translate customer data into precise audiences and activate those audiences across real-time customer journeys, measuring and improving performance through always-on analysis — all with zero data movement. Thousands of marketers at enterprises like Costco, Albertsons, Fanatics, and Ford rely on GrowthLoop to bring their AI strategy to life, grow faster with every experiment, personalize every customer touchpoint, and drive rapidly compounding results.

releases.title: Ringmaster Launches "Cited Conversations," the First Podcast Made by Humans for an AI Audience
releases.body:
RINGMASTER (ringmaster.com)

New show debuts on International Podcast Day, structuring expert conversation so answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and Gemini can retrieve and cite it

NASHUA, N.H., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ringmaster, the B2B content capture engine, today launched Cited Conversations, the first podcast built from the ground up for an AI audience.

The subtitle says it plainly: "Human expertise structured for AI agents." Each episode is an on-the-record conversation between two named, verifiable human experts. Not a script read by a voice clone. Not content generated by a model. Ringmaster designs each conversation so that answer engines can find the expertise inside it, pull it apart, and cite it back to the people asking questions.

AI-generated podcasts already exist. They recycle what machines already know. Cited Conversations captures what they don't: original expert perspective from a conversation that hasn't happened yet.

Each episode is built using Ringmaster's Plan, Capture, Transform (PCT) Framework™. The PCT Framework™ designs questions around AI visibility gaps before the recording begins, captures structured expert dialogue, and transforms each conversation into a library of content assets that answer engines can index and cite. Today, a single 45-minute expert conversation already produces as many as 40 content assets for human audiences. Cited Conversations is the start of building AI-specific assets on top of that same conversation.

"We've spent eight years helping companies connect with their customers through expert conversations. Now we're helping them connect with the machines that talk to their customers," said Casey Cheshire, Founder of Ringmaster. "A great podcast used to mean somebody listened all the way through. Now it also means an AI agent can find the ninety seconds that matter and hand it to someone who never pressed play."

The launch is timed to International Podcast Day, September 30. More than 4.7 million podcasts have been created worldwide (Podcast Index, 2026). The number built for an AI audience: one.

"This is just the beginning. The number of shows designed for AI consumption will surpass the ones that aren't," Cheshire said. "And the 4.7 million podcasts that already exist will rethink how they serve both audiences. The content is already there. It's just trapped in audio."

The podcast is available for AI agents at citedconversations.com. (The audio is there for curious humans.)

Ringmaster will unveil the show live at the Connect to Market community event, a private roundtable for B2B marketing leaders, on September 30 at 3:00 p.m. ET. The session is themed "Creating Content for Humans and AI," where Cheshire delivers a lightning talk introducing Cited Conversations.

Casey Cheshire is a Marine Corps veteran, author, and the founder of Ringmaster. He has personally hosted over 600 podcast episodes and spent more than 500 hours conducting expert conversations.

About Ringmaster

Ringmaster is a B2B content capture engine that designs expert podcast conversations and transforms each episode into structured content assets that AI answer engines can retrieve and cite. Founded by Casey Cheshire, Ringmaster has launched over 100 B2B podcasts across cybersecurity, fintech, HR tech, healthcare, and professional services. The company's Plan, Capture, Transform (PCT) Framework™ turns a single expert conversation into a full library of AI-ready content. Learn more at ringmaster.com.

releases.title: Telit Cinterion and Commstar Radio Partner to Bring Multi-Network Connectivity to Municipal and Critical Infrastructure Operations
releases.body:
Telit Cinterion's NExT™ connectivity solutions provide reliable coverage and secure communications for Commstar Radio's customers across urban, rural and hard-to-reach environments

  • Commstar Radio selected Telit Cinterion to deliver secure, resilient and scalable connectivity for critical communications environments, including push-to-talk, utility workforce communications, fleet coordination, dispatch operations and remote infrastructure connectivity.
  • Built-in network redundancy keeps customers connected where single-carrier coverage falls short.

BOCA RATON, Fla., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Telit Cinterion, a global enabler of the Internet of Things (IoT), today announced a partnership with Commstar Radio, a Wisconsin-based technology and communications company. Through the partnership, Commstar Radio will offer Telit Cinterion's NExT™ SIM connectivity solution, giving customers access to multiple carrier networks on a single SIM for secure communications in urban, rural and hard-to-reach areas.

For more information about Telit Cinterion's IoT connectivity solutions, visit: https://www.telit.com/telit-next-network/

The NExT SIM connectivity solution provides secure access through a single SIM to more than 600 mobile carrier networks globally, including the three major U.S. networks.  Built on Telit Cinterion's georedundant NExT global network, it supports cellular technologies from 2G to 5G and serves both low-power wide-area (LPWA) devices and high-bandwidth applications.

With NExT SIM, Commstar Radio can now offer customers resilient multi-network connectivity, extensive Cat M and narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) coverage and greater operational reliability across urban, rural and hard-to-reach environments.

Commstar Radio specializes in wireless communications and connectivity for organizations that depend on reliable service in demanding environments, including municipalities, utilities, transportation providers, field service teams and public infrastructure operators. Its services span land mobile communications, push-to-talk over cellular, wireless infrastructure connectivity, secure wireless services, mobile device management, cloud communications and cybersecurity.

The company serves customers across sectors such as:

  • Utilities
  • Field services
  • Local government
  • Energy
  • Transportation
  • Public infrastructure

An initial deployment with the Village of Reeseville, Wisconsin, demonstrates how Commstar Radio and Telit Cinterion are delivering resilient multi-network connectivity for municipal communications and public service operations.

"Commstar Radio has been a trusted and reliable partner for the Village of Reeseville since the company's inception," said Jake Pacala, village president, Reeseville, Wisconsin. "Municipalities require an abundance of services in this domain, making reliability and service a must. When asked by neighboring municipalities for recommendations in this field, Commstar Radio is the first we mention."

"Our customers depend on communications systems that work wherever their teams operate," said Kevin Hankes, president of Commstar Radio.  "By partnering with Telit Cinterion, we can provide resilient multi-network connectivity across urban and rural environments while giving customers greater reliability, security and flexibility than traditional single-carrier solutions."

"Organizations responsible for public services, utilities, transportation and field operations need connectivity that goes beyond a single carrier, leveraging multiple networks to protect critical operations," said Martin Krona, president of services and solutions at Telit Cinterion. "Together with Commstar Radio, we're enabling secure, resilient communications that can intelligently leverage multiple carrier networks to keep people, devices and operations connected."

About Telit Cinterion

Telit Cinterion is a global IoT leader with over 30 years of innovation experience. It provides modules, connectivity plans and services, platforms, and secure, scalable custom solutions.

Telit Cinterion's product portfolio supports mission-critical applications across industries. In addition, it simplifies lifecycle management and device-to-cloud security. The company helps enterprises connect, manage and grow their IoT systems with confidence.

OEMs, system integrators and service providers worldwide trust Telit Cinterion. The company drives digital transformation and unlocks the power of connected technology.

INDIANAPOLIS, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NHRA officials announced it has reached new, landmark multi-year media rights agreements for the Mission Foods Drag Racing Series with three standout distributors – FOX Sports, The CW Network and FloSports – positioning NHRA to enjoy the largest household reach in its 75-year history.
