releases.body:
Annually updated guide provides strategies for completing the 2027–2028 FAFSA and CSS Profile to one's best advantage as well as planning for college costs

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Princeton Review®, a provider of education services and college admission resources since 1981, today released the 35th edition of its annual guide to getting funding to pay for college.

Paying for College: Everything You Need to Maximize Financial Aid and Afford College (2027 Edition, Penguin Random House, September 22, 2026, $25.99) is authored by Kalman A. Chany, a nationally recognized expert on college funding, with Geoff Martz. Chany is founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent college financial aid advisory firm based in New York City.

When Paying for College debuted in 1992, it was a one-of-a-kind resource in the category of personal finance guides. It provided detailed line-by-line guidance on strategically completing the two most important financial aid application forms for the upcoming aid application year, and it was the only book to do so.

Paying for College remains the only resource offering such targeted guidance for submitting those two crucial forms. They are the U.S. Department of Education's FAFSA® (Free Application for Federal Student Aid), which all financial aid applicants must submit, and the College Board's CSS Profile®, an application that hundreds of selective colleges require (and which has as many as 200 questions).

"You might think that families who receive the most financial aid would be the families with the most need," Chany says in the introduction of the book. "In fact, this is not necessarily true. The people who receive the most aid are the people who best understand the aid process." 

Chany well understands the process. Since 1981, he has annually analyzed the major aid application forms as well as the formulas by which federal and institutional financial aid administrators assess an applicant's need for aid based on answers on the forms. He guides his clients (and readers of this book) on how to maximize their eligibility for financial aid much in the same way an accountant advises clients on submitting their IRS returns to their best advantage. (All the strategies Chany recommends follow the law to the letter.)

In Paying for College, Chany also covers other subjects important to aid applicants and parents, including how to:

  • explore long- and short-term strategies for reducing college costs
  • research colleges with financial aid in mind
  • compare financial aid offers and, if necessary, appeal for more aid
  • obtain education loans, understand payment plans, and manage loan debt

A Special Topics chapter in the book gives particular advice on aid applications for parents who are single, separated, divorced or in blended families as well as advice for students who are independent, international or older than the traditional applicant.

The 2027 edition of Paying for College also reports on tectonic changes that have impacted the college funding landscape as a result of various provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) signed into law in July 2025. Chany discusses what parents and students need to know about these changes. Icons in the margins flag topics that were pending as the book went to press that readers are advised to check.

Some provisions of the OBBBA that impact federal student aid are still unresolved. "Unfortunately," Chany notes, "some guidance involving federal education loans issued by the U.S. Department of Education is being misinterpreted—even by college aid professionals."

Over the years, Paying for College has been praised by reviewers and finance professionals alike. Forbes contributor John Wasik noted it "can save thousands in college bills." Washington Post syndicated columnist Michelle Singletary chose it for her Color of Money book club. Newsday Family Finance columnist Lynn Brenner recommended it as "a first-rate guide through the financial aid maze."

Said Rob Franek, Editor-in-Chief of The Princeton Review, "Our company has a deep appreciation for the concerns of students and parents about paying for college. Among nearly 10,000 college applicants and parents of applicants who completed our 2026 College Hopes & Worries Survey in February, 93% reported they would need financial aid to pay for college, and 81% of that cohort characterized their level of need as "very" or "extremely" necessary. We hope the advice in this new edition of Paying for College will help parents and students apply strategies to get all the financial aid they are entitled to and enable them to pay less for college."

Paying for College is one of more than 150 books developed by The Princeton Review and published by Penguin Random House in a line that includes The Best 392 Colleges  and guides to the SAT®, ACT®, and AP® exams. The Princeton Review is also known for its annual college rankings in dozens of categories including its popular "Great Financial Aid" college ranking list and its "Best Value Colleges" lists.

About Kalman A. Chany 

Kalman A. Chany is the founder and president of Campus Consultants Inc., an independent New York City-based financial aid advisory firm. For more than four decades, his firm has helped thousands of families maximize their financial aid eligibility and save tens of thousands of dollars off the cost of their children's college education. Kal has been sourced in The Wall Street Journal, on CNBC, and in Money magazine, and he has appeared on CBS Evening News, NBC Nightly News, and other broadcast media.

About The Princeton Review

The Princeton Review is a leading tutoring, test prep, and college admissions services company. Every year, it helps millions of college- and graduate school–bound students as well as working professionals achieve their education and career goals through its many education services and products. These include online and in-person courses delivered by a network of more than 4,000 teachers and tutors; online resources; a line of more than 150 print and digital books published by Penguin Random House; and dozens of categories of school rankings. Founded in 1981, the company is now in its 45th year. The company's Tutor.com brand, now in its 25th year, is one of the largest online tutoring services in the U.S. It comprises a community of thousands of tutors who have delivered more than 29 million tutoring sessions. The Princeton Review, headquartered in New York, NY, is not affiliated with Princeton University. For more information, visit PrincetonReview.com. Follow the company on Facebook (@ThePrincetonReviewSAT), Instagram (@theprincetonreview), LinkedIn (the-princeton-review), YouTube (@ThePrincetonReview), and TikTok (@princeton.review). releases.body:
Multi-year partnership opens a new advertiser category for Expedia Group and gives travelers earlier details about travel protection across its brands

SEATTLE, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Expedia Group today announced a marketing collaboration with Redion, a world leader in assistance, travel insurance and employee benefits, marking the first time a travel insurance and assistance brand has joined Expedia Group Advertising as a dedicated partner. The agreement opens an entirely new advertiser category for the company and reshapes how travelers encounter protection options during planning and booking.

The addition reflects the accelerating expansion of Expedia Group Advertising beyond its traditional base of hotels, airlines, and destinations. Over the past year, the business has increasingly powered campaigns for non-travel brands, from retail to entertainment to financial services, connecting them with high-intent traveler audiences across Expedia Group's sites and apps, offsite channels, and partner publishers. Redion's arrival extends that trajectory into travel insurance and assistance, a category that sits at the intersection of both worlds.

The two companies are not new to each other. For more than 15 years, Redion, formerly known as Europ Assistance worldwide and Generali Global Assistance (GGA) in the U.S., has provided travel protection to Expedia Group customers. This collaboration moves that relationship beyond product distribution into a strategic advertising alliance, with co-branded editorial, on-platform experiences, and targeted activations rolling out across Expedia Group brands beginning in Q3 2026.

For travelers, the shift means that Redion can now cohesively appear throughout the traveler's journey to maximize brand awareness and peace of mind.

Expedia Group's research points to the opportunity: 62% of travelers made a non-travel purchase tied to their most recent major leisure trip, spending an average of $500 beyond the trip itself, and 38% of Gen Z travelers bought financial products or services before departure. For Redion, that creates a timely opportunity to reach travelers as they consider trip-related protection and financial decisions.

"Opening a category is not something we do often," said Jennifer Andre, Vice President, Business Development at Expedia Group. "Redion earned this as our first insurance advertising partner because of a 15-year track record of protecting our travelers. Together we can bring travel protection into the journey earlier and more easily than either of us could alone."

"This partnership marks a defining moment for Redion," said Virginie Babinet, CEO, Travel Insurance & Assistance – Redion Group. "As we introduce the Redion brand to the world, we're doing it from the center of the traveler's journey, alongside a longstanding partner. We intend to make it a partnership that others are measured against."

releases.title: MUSIC DAY IN CANADA BRINGS 60+ CANADIAN ARTISTS TO STAGES ACROSS THE COUNTRY ON SEPTEMBER 26
releases.body:
20 cities and 20+ live events come together for one national day celebrating Canadian music, local venues and the communities that sustain them.

VANCOUVER, BC, Sept. 22, 2026 /CNW/ -- On Saturday, September 26, Music Day in Canada will connect stages across the country for one shared national celebration of Canadian music.

More than 60 artists across 20+ live events in 20 cities will perform as venues, music organizations, local producers and communities come together under one national banner.

From St. John's to Vancouver, Music Day in Canada is built around a simple idea: Canadian music is shaped locally, and those local scenes become stronger when the country pays attention together.

"Canada doesn't have one music scene. It has hundreds of them," says Michael Sriven,  Founder of Music Day In Canada.   "Music Day in Canada gives those communities a shared date and a national platform while keeping the artists, venues and people who build music locally at the centre of it."

The September 26 program stretches across genres, generations and types of stages.

In Saskatoon, six Saskatchewan acts will take over Gather Local Market for five hours of free live music. Edmonton will see multiple independent venues participating across the city. Oshawa will enjoy a free show at the Biltmore theatre featuring Wine Lips, The Anti-Queens, Shiv & the Carvers and Sigh Die . In Barrie, Brian John Harwood, Andy Colonico, Beasley and Graham Scott Fleming will come together for an all-country night at The Queens Hotel.

On the East Coast, events extend through St. John's, Antigonish, New Glasgow, Sydney, Charlottetown, Fredericton, Truro  and Moncton, while additional programming takes place in Winnipeg, Regina, Calgary, Mississauga, Abbotsford, Kelowna, Whitehorse and Vancouver.

Some events are free and all ages. Others take place in established independent music venues. Each city determines what Music Day looks and sounds like in its own community.

LOCAL SCENES. ONE NATIONAL MOMENT.

Music Day in Canada is led by The Lemmon Foundation, with Lemmon Entertainment curating and producing the national platform alongside local venues, producers, artists and music organizations.

Rather than building the same event in every market, Music Day connects existing local infrastructure and new community-led programming through coordinated national promotion, partnerships and visibility.

The model is designed to strengthen the people and places already doing the work: putting artists on stages, bringing audiences into local rooms and creating opportunities for Canadian music to be discovered live.

The day also connects to the Foundation's year-round work supporting artists and aspiring industry professionals through education, mentorship and professional development.

SEPTEMBER 26, 2026

Music Day in Canada takes place Saturday, September 26, with events currently announced in:

Abbotsford • Antigonish • Barrie • Calgary • Charlottetown • Edmonton • Fredericton • Kelowna • Mississauga • Moncton • New Glasgow • Oshawa • Regina • Saskatoon • St. John's • Sydney • Vancouver • Winnipeg • Whitehorse • Truro

Programming and ticketing vary by city.

The complete and continuously updated national schedule is available at musicdayincanada.com.

ABOUT MUSIC DAY IN CANADA

Music Day in Canada connects local stages into one national moment, strengthening visibility, participation and long-term sustainability for live music across the country. Led by The Lemmon Foundation, the initiative brings together artists, venues, producers, music organizations, partners and audiences while allowing each participating community to build programming that reflects its own local music scene.

releases.body:
Endorsed by the Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding and accepted by Worldpay, ScriptSafe certifies pharmacies in 7 to 10 business days based on the licenses they already hold

WASHINGTON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ScriptSafe launched last Tuesday, September 15, at Compounders on Capitol Hill, the Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding's annual conference. ScriptSafe certifies pharmacies for payment processing and, coming next, for online advertising.

What ScriptSafe does

ScriptSafe verifies what a pharmacy is licensed to do, against the state boards and federal databases that actually license it. The ScriptSafe system and team run a 152-point verification against all 50 state boards, the DEA, and federal databases, then issue a written decision within 7 to 10 business days. Certification covers a full year, with the pharmacy's licenses and website monitored every night.

For payment processors and online advertising platforms

ScriptSafe does not take the pharmacy's word for it, and it does not stop checking after approval. Every night, ScriptSafe checks the pharmacy's website to confirm the prescription requirement is still in place, what the pharmacy sells has not changed, and licenses and board standing are current. If a pharmacy drops its prescription gate or loses a license, the processor or platform is flagged within hours. Approval is where most certification programs stop. It is where ScriptSafe starts. Worldpay has accepted ScriptSafe certification, and ScriptSafe worked directly with Visa on the requirements for pharmacy merchants. ScriptSafe is actively pursuing recognition as a certification option for online pharmacy advertising, built on that same nightly monitoring.

For pharmacies

Pharmacies have had two certification options, both costly, often $3,000 or more, with decisions that can take six months or longer. ScriptSafe certifies pharmacies on the licenses they already hold, with no separate application fee and a written decision in 7 to 10 business days. Certification is $1,685 for a full year. APC members pay $1,348. The same documents go to the processor's underwriting team, so the pharmacy fills out one application instead of two.

"ScriptSafe's platform made it very easy to upload documents, answer questions, and finish our application. ScriptSafe is the best platform we have used for pharmacy online payment certification," said David Martinez, Senior Vice President of Specialty Veterinary Pharmacy.

"State boards of pharmacy decide whether a pharmacy can legally operate. That is how this industry is regulated," said Aaron Van Stone, founder and CEO of ScriptSafe. "ScriptSafe verifies what a pharmacy is licensed to do, against the boards and databases that actually license it. Fast, affordable, and built by people who understand pharmacy and payments."

BUFFALO, N.Y., Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BetterMynd, a leading online therapy platform centered on the mental health needs of university and college students, has announced a partnership with Lavender Psychiatry, the largest nurse-led online psychiatry and therapy practice in the United States. Together, the organizations will expand access to flexible, high-quality care by integrating Lavender's medication management services into the BetterMynd therapeutic ecosystem.

With one in three students reporting symptoms of moderate anxiety or depression (Healthy Minds, 2025), the demand for accessible care is at an all-time high. This partnership reflects a shared belief that students are best served by adaptable care models built around the individual. By combining their expertise, BetterMynd and Lavender can better respond to the full spectrum of mental health needs seen across the student population.

For educational institutions navigating growing demand and increasing complexity in student mental health, the partnership offers a high-quality, scalable solution that is easy to implement.

"Our mission is to make getting help easier for every college student, and we believe every student deserves an exceptional experience," said Cody Semrau, Founder and CEO of BetterMynd. "We're excited to partner with Lavender, an organization that shares our mission-driven focus and also puts the students first in all that they do. This ensures students have the most comprehensive resources available while providing institutions with a trusted, scalable model."

Accessing psychiatric care can often mean navigating long wait times, referrals between multiple providers, and limited prescribing options; barriers that can be especially challenging for student populations. Lavender removes this friction by providing integrated psychiatric services within BetterMynd's established care pathway, from assessment and prescribing to ongoing medication management, including ADHD treatment and controlled substances when clinically appropriate. With virtual appointments typically available within one week, students can get the support they need without lengthy delays. A network of 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across more than 40 states, supported by customized referral pathways and dedicated administrative support, helps make that access seamless and scalable for BetterMynd's university partners.

"We believe in creating a world where feelings are respected and cared for. BetterMynd shares our passion for making kind, effective, high-quality care more accessible," said Pritma Dhillon-Chattha, DNP, MHA, RN, Co-Founder of Lavender. "Mental health journeys are unique and we're reflecting that in our joint adaptable approach to therapy and medication management. By embedding Lavender's online psychiatry services naturally into the BetterMynd community, we're making the student journey more seamless and serving as a true extension of the campus counseling center."

The partnership is currently live at select institutions. Both organizations will continue to build and expand access across multiple states and campuses throughout 2026 and beyond.

About BetterMynd

BetterMynd is a leading online therapy platform designed specifically to meet the mental health needs of college students. BetterMynd supplements and expands on-campus resources by providing personalized care and scheduling flexibility. Serving more than 100 colleges and universities, BetterMynd reaches over 500,000 students through a network of 400+ licensed clinicians. Learn more at www.bettermynd.com.

Lavender Psychiatry is the largest nurse-owned and operated online psychiatry and therapy office in the U.S. Founded on the principle that care should be kind, collaborative and effective, Lavender provides timely access to high-quality therapy and medication management through 150+ board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioners across 40+ states. The practice also works with partners by integrating select services into existing mental health care ecosystems. Learn more at www.joinlavender.com.

releases.title: IAB Releases Measurement Services Addendum v1.0 for Public Comment
releases.body:
New Draft Framework Introduces Standardized Contractual Terms for Advertising Measurement, Verification, Attribution, and Analytics Services

Public Comment Open Until October 22, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade association for the digital advertising industry, today released the Measurement Services Addendum v1.0 for public comment, introducing a standardized contractual framework for companies that provide, purchase, or use advertising measurement, verification, attribution, and analytics services. Developed through IAB's Terms & Conditions Task Force, the addendum expands IAB's modular legal framework to support more consistent, efficient, and interoperable agreements across the digital advertising ecosystem. The public comment period will be open for 30 days until October 22, 2026.

"Reliable measurement is fundamental to a healthy digital advertising marketplace, but the legal frameworks supporting those relationships have often been shaped one agreement at a time," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "By developing a common contractual foundation for measurement services, we're giving the industry a practical starting point that can reduce friction, improve efficiency, and help organizations spend less time negotiating custom agreements and more time delivering value for all."

The Measurement Services Addendum is the latest component of IAB's modular legal framework, building on the General Terms v1.1 and Direct Buy Addendum v1.0 released earlier this year. Designed for use by advertisers, agencies, publishers, media owners, platforms, and measurement providers, the framework establishes standardized terms for advertising measurement relationships, helping reduce contractual fragmentation, streamline negotiations, improve operational efficiency, and create greater consistency across the digital advertising ecosystem while remaining flexible enough to accommodate different technologies, methodologies, and business models.

"Measurement has become increasingly sophisticated, but the contracts governing those services haven't kept pace," said Cintia Gabilan, SVP, Centers of Excellence & Industry Initiatives, IAB. "The Measurement Services Addendum gives organizations a practical legal framework they can adopt as written or incorporate into existing agreements, making it easier to create greater consistency across measurement relationships while accommodating different business models and technologies."

The public comment package includes the Measurement Services Addendum v1.0, General Terms v1.1 and Appendix 1 – Definitions v1.1, which together establish a shared legal baseline for advertising measurement relationships. The General Terms are incorporated by reference into the addendum and are intended for use with an applicable addendum rather than as a standalone agreement.

IAB invites advertisers, agencies, publishers, platforms, measurement providers, ad technology companies, and legal, procurement, finance, privacy and ad operations professionals to review the draft and provide feedback. Comments received during the public comment period will be considered in the finalization process.

Public comments will be accepted through October 22, 2026. Feedback, including suggested edits, implementation questions, and general usability comments, may be submitted to terms-comments@iab.com. Draft documents are available here.

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. The trade group fields critical research on interactive advertising, while also educating brands, agencies, and the wider business community on the importance of digital marketing. In affiliation with the IAB Tech Lab, IAB develops technical standards and solutions. IAB is committed to professional development and elevating the knowledge, skills, expertise, and collaboration of the workforce across the industry. Through the work of its public policy office in Washington, D.C., the trade association advocates for its members and promotes the value of the interactive advertising industry to legislators and policymakers. Founded in 1996, IAB is headquartered in New York City.

releases.title: Simpli.fi Scales Localized Advertising for Multi-Location Brands with New Simpli.Hub Portal
releases.body:
On-demand advertising portal empowers local operators to launch pre-approved, high-performing campaigns while preserving corporate brand integrity

FORT WORTH, Texas, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Simpli.fi, the real-world media platform built for the age of immediacy, has launched Simpli.Hub, an on-demand self-serve advertising portal that balances corporate brand control with local execution, allowing multi-location brands, franchise networks, co-ops, and distributed agencies to create consistent yet localized ads across various markets and channels, from programmatic to walled gardens.

Today, 76% of nearby smartphone users who search for a business will visit that result within a day, which means local relevance is critical to driving foot traffic and store sales. However, scaling localized campaigns for even as few as three locations, let alone hundreds, creates operational bottlenecks, brand drift, and fragmented reporting. Adding to the challenge, many local operators or store managers have limited advertising experience, leading to unnecessary time spent trying to localize an ad or funneling precious ad dollars to the wrong channels. In most cases, corporate either struggles to micromanage ad spend or is left to trust operators with limited experience to know how to best use that spend. It's a lose-lose situation that wastes time and money for all involved.

"Multi-location advertisers have historically had to choose between strict brand control and local flexibility," said Michael Schoen, Chief Product and Technology Officer of Simpli.fi. "Simpli.Hub delivers both. By bridging corporate strategy and local execution, teams can unlock unused local ad budgets and convert them into store foot traffic, helping to direct every location to reach the target customer at the right moment while avoiding wasted spend."

Built on top of the Simpli.fi unified media platform as an easy-to-use storefront for multi-location execution, Simpli.Hub empowers local operators and franchise owners with on-demand, self-serve campaign execution without sacrificing top-level brand control or consolidated reporting. Simpli.Hub allows customers to place orders that flow into the Simpli.fi platform for activation across channels from search and display to premium CTV and DOOH, allowing teams to launch fast while maintaining strong corporate alignment. By directly linking digital campaigns to real-world impact, Simpli.fi provides a uniquely scalable solution for distributed teams.

Simpli.Hub turns localized advertising into an efficient, turnkey process:

  • Corporate Control: Corporate teams set the campaign strategy, creative assets, geographic parameters and brand guardrails centrally within the platform.
  • Local Activation: Local franchise operators and store managers select from pre-approved campaign options, set their local budget and launch targeted campaigns across channels without requiring media buying expertise.
  • Unified Intelligence: Corporate leadership gains comprehensive, aggregated visibility into performance across every location, designed to help maximize ad spend effectiveness and drive real-world outcomes.

"Simpli.Hub solved a franchise marketing problem we've been working around for years," said Roxane Harris, Vice President, Franchise Operations & International, H&R Block. "Our operators launch their own campaigns, corporate stays in the loop across every location, and our brand stays consistent—locally relevant, nationally on-brand."

Simpli.Hub connects localized campaigns directly into Simpli.fi's core media capabilities, leveraging place-based, purchase and identity signals to link digital engagement with real-world store visits.

Simpli.Hub is available starting today, following successful rollouts with multi-location brands and enterprise franchise networks managing campaign activations across thousands of locations nationwide.

To learn more about Simpli.Hub, visit simpli.fi/solutions/simpli-hub.

About Simpli.fi

Simpli.fi is the real-world media platform built for the age of immediacy. By unifying digital behavior and real-world movement into a single actionable signal, Simpli.fi enables over 2,000 agencies, advertisers, and media groups to target, optimize, and measure campaigns precisely where consumer decisions happen. Built on the truth that people use digital to navigate the physical world, Simpli.fi is engineered to connect these signals in real time—allowing brands to act on consumer intent the moment it occurs and measure the impact all the way to the door. We thrive on innovation, data-driven results, and a culture of continuous improvement to make marketing more immediate, intelligent, and connected. LEHI, Utah, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In roofing, the contractor who reaches the homeowner first and quotes fastest wins the job. Sales Rabbit, the field-sales platform used by more than 225,000 sales representatives, today announced Roof Rabbit, the only connected machine that takes a roofing job from first lead to final payment. Roof Rabbit opens today in limited release, and roofing contractors can apply for early access at roofrabbit.ai.

Own the lead, own the quote, own the payment. Roof Rabbit runs the whole roofing job in one machine, one place, one login. It covers canvassing and lead generation at the door, instant roof quoting on the contractor's own website, and production, CRM, and payment. Most roofing companies run that same job across a stack of tools that don't talk to each other, and every handoff leaks revenue: the lead nobody called back, the quote that took days, the signed job re-typed into the office system, the check that shows up late. Roof Rabbit closes those leaks.

A homeowner who used to wait days for a callback can now get a full estimate from the contractor's website at any hour. A rep who used to leave the door with a maybe can now build the quote in under 30 seconds and close on the spot. Once the proposal is signed, the job goes straight to production. Nobody types it in twice. The same system handles materials, crew scheduling, and getting paid.

"In roofing, the contractor who gets to the homeowner first and closes fastest wins," said Ben Alves, CEO of Sales Rabbit. "That's the reality every operator in this business knows. The time between the knock and the collected check is where deals are made or lost, and every hour of delay is an opportunity for a competitor to get there first. We built Roof Rabbit to compress that cycle at every step."

Roof Rabbit is new. What it is built from is proven. Sales Rabbit acquired RoofLink in November 2024 for its roofing CRM and production software, and Roofle in January 2026 for its instant quoting engine, which has delivered more than 2.4 million estimates from aerial measurement data. The company took the strongest parts of all three, canvassing from Sales Rabbit, quoting from Roofle, production and payments from RoofLink, and engineered them into a single solution for the whole roofing job.

"Roofle was built to solve one specific problem: getting a real, accurate quote in front of a homeowner before anyone else could," said Travis Harvego, VP of Strategic Partnerships and Growth and Co-founder of Roofle. "More than 3,000 contractor sites are quoting online today because of it. That front-of-funnel capability is now part of a system that follows the job all the way through to payment: Roof Rabbit."

Jesse Mahan, VP, Business Owner, and a Founding Collaborator on RoofLink, points to the back-office problem in roofing companies where most margin gets lost. "After the contract is signed, you still have to manage materials, coordinate crews, track the job, and collect the money. That's where a lot of revenue disappears. RoofLink was built to make that process run without the office chasing every step, and that's what Roof Rabbit carries forward."

Roof Rabbit is live today for a limited group of roofing contractors, with access expanding in the weeks ahead. Early access includes the full product, done-for-you setup, and a direct line to the team building it. Contractors can apply at roofrabbit.ai.

The company's software powers field teams through canvassing, lead management, and revenue operations. Roof Rabbit is Sales Rabbit's AI-native roofing machine, taking a job from first lead to final payment: canvassing, online quoting, proposals, production, and payments in one place.

releases.title: ASU London opens, welcomes students to a new model of global higher education
releases.body:
Students begin new academic journeys in London, combining project-based learning, industry engagement and the opportunity to earn bachelor's and master's degrees in four years

LONDON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ASU London has officially opened its academic year, welcoming students to a new international higher education experience built around project-based learning, real-world challenges and global opportunities.

"We have designed ASU London to provide students with a compelling new way they can both gain an international experience and prepare for their careers, in the U.K. and the U.S.," Arizona State University President Michael Crow said. "We're in the business of changing people's lives and futures. We will continue to expand our efforts and our impact to engage with learners all over the world."

ASU London — an independent U.K. degree-awarding higher education provider — will offer three-year bachelor's degrees in areas including business, computer science, engineering and design. Its programs are built around project-based learning and real-world experience, with students working on challenges shaped by industry and community needs, leading to opportunities for Arizona State University master's degrees.

"I don't think this has happened before, and that is what is so extraordinary," said Sir Malcolm Grant, grant chair of ASU London's board of trustee directors, a senior advisor to Crow and part of London's university system since 1972. "We can take students internationally, give them three years' education here in London, and then they may go onto a master's program (at ASU).

"Being able to offer students this extraordinary opportunity...I am totally committed to this."

The institution's approach places particular emphasis on future-focused skills, including artificial intelligence, technology and sustainable innovation. Students from different disciplines can work together on complex problems that require practical solutions and collaboration.

Those who pursue master's degrees at Arizona State University will gain exposure to one of the fastest-growing U.S. research universities, known for innovation, sustainability, the largest engineering school and its location within a region rapidly expanding in microelectronics and the knowledge economy.

"ASU is an exceptional partner in elevating Phoenix on the global stage, and I know ASU London will help our city and region take another important step forward," said Phoenix Mayor Kate Gallego. "I look forward to continuing to work with Michael Crow and ASU to connect the world with the dynamic opportunities Phoenix and Arizona offer for innovation, investment and collaboration."

Tackling global challenges

ASU London is designed to prepare students for a changing world of work and the challenges facing communities around the world.

"The world's biggest challenges require collaboration across disciplines and borders," said ASU London Managing Director Michael Goodwin. "ASU London gives students the opportunity to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to contribute to those challenges while building careers in a changing global economy."

The opening of the academic year also begins a new phase in ASU London's relationship with the U.K. The institution is developing relationships with local communities, universities, employers, alumni and other organizations as it contributes to London's educational and innovation ecosystem.

Learn with industry

ASU London's hands-on approach reflects one of its central principles: to learn by doing. Students are encouraged to build, test and experience ideas through practical projects. They can work on issues including sustainability, artificial intelligence and smart cities while developing technical, professional and collaborative skills.

James Woods, who is studying business management after graduating from high school in Phoenix this May, said everything about ASU London — from its learning approach to its global focus — convinced him to cross the pond to begin his college education.

"I feel as I come to London, it's going to open up more opportunities for me to be a leader," Woods said. "You're surrounded by leaders. And what I particularly like is that they're not just handing you a paper to work on. You're actually working on a project. You're given a purpose."

Industry engagement is a core part of the ASU London learning experience. Students work on projects shaped by employers and build professional skills from day one. Through project-based learning, real-world challenges and industry engagement, students develop portfolios of work that demonstrate what they can do as well as what they know.

The institution's location in the heart of the city, at the Clerkenwell campus of City St. George's, University of London, also places students within a diverse environment of businesses, creative organizations, technology companies and cultural institutions.

"Effectively, we're giving them this very small, friendly and supportive community as part of ASU London," Goodwin said. "But they have access to a much wider, bigger university experience should they choose to take it up."

Connecting continents

ASU London also provides qualified graduates with opportunities to select one-year master's degrees at Arizona State University in the U.S., subject to program requirements and applicable U.S. immigration and visa requirements.

These include master's degrees in areas such as computer science, cybersecurity, electrical engineering, business analytics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing, artificial intelligence in business, economics, information systems management, supply chain management and user experience.

Beyond these one-year programs, qualified graduates from ASU London bachelor's degree programs will have additional pathways to the wider portfolio of Arizona State University graduate degrees.

This gives students the opportunity to begin with a U.K. bachelor's degree in London and continue their academic journey in the United States.

"What we're doing with ASU London is we're launching an experiment in academic innovation," Crow said. "We're launching an initiative where we can partner with more people in the U.K., an English-speaking country that's deeply connected with people all over the world.

"We're also trying to build in more agility for ourselves. You can't come to the United States? Well, maybe you can go to England."

For the 320 students beginning their studies this September, the new academic year represents the start of their own journey.

Among them are Gustavo Alves, a first-year student from Brazil who will major in business management. For him, the decision to enroll at ASU London was easy. It has everything he could want, both personally and professionally.

"The teenager life and the university life are great," said Alves. "And the professional side, with the job market, with the connections you can make with companies in London, I think it's a great city to be in."

Although ASU London is in its infancy, Crow already is thinking about the future. He said ASU London could have as many as 4,000 students and be a global model for other universities.

"We hope that it's a pilot for a global model because we're working with Cintana Education to not only help start universities around the world but to help enhance universities around the world," Crow said. "The education sector has under-innovated for the challenges that are ahead, and are very much focused on status and selectivity as their method of competition.

"So welcome, in a sense, to an innovative project."

releases.title: Disasterville Returns: Army National Guard Brings Mixed-Reality Disaster Response Missions Back to Schools
releases.body:
At a Glance

  • This fall, the U.S. Army National Guard's mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, is returning to high schools nationwide to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies. 
  • Disasterville guides students through high-tech, virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes in the same way as the Guard.
  • The Disasterville tour continues to introduce students to the possibilities available in the Army National Guard—a unique component within the U.S. Army where Soldiers have the flexibility to serve their country part-time while also pursuing a civilian career or higher education. 

WASHINGTON, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This fall, the Army National Guard's immersive mixed-reality experience, Disasterville, will begin its second nationwide tour of high schools, giving students a first-hand look at how to prepare for and respond to natural disasters—without leaving their schools. Disasterville is activating in high school gyms where it will take students through virtual missions to tackle wildfires, floods, and earthquakes, just like Soldiers responding to similar emergencies in communities across the country. This follows Disasterville's successful inaugural tour in spring 2026, which reached more than 2,000 students.

"Natural disasters are not slowing down, and Army National Guard Soldiers are playing a critical role in response efforts across the country," says Lt. Col. Sabrina Zowada, Chief of the National Guard Bureau's Marketing and Advertising Branch. "Disasterville is a one-of-a-kind perspective for students to see how and when the Guard is showing up in their communities, and experience the real skills and impact of these important missions." 

Disasterville is transforming high school gyms from September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga.

Students Work Together to Respond to Common Missions

Disasterville uses advanced mixed-reality technology to create three 10-minute missions most common to Army National Guard response efforts. Working together in teams of five, students are called to service at the following sites:

  • Wildfire: Amid a raging wildfire, teams work together to push back fires encroaching on a home in Disaster Canyon. Students will put out small wildfires, combine forces to push back larger flare-ups, save animals, and dodge falling trees. 
  • Flood Zone: After a major hurricane, civilians are fighting to stay above water on the streets they call home. Students will board their Zodiac and use headlamps to find and safely evacuate survivors while avoiding dangerous wildlife and other lurking hazards.
  • Earthquake: After a devastating earthquake, a train carrying hazardous chemicals and passengers derails, pinning civilians and spilling dangerous material, poisoning the air. Time ticks down as students arm themselves with the jaws of life to rescue survivors and clean up debris, all before the train gives way under its own weight.

"We saw firsthand how students connected with the Disasterville experience. They didn't just learn about disaster response—they felt the responsibility," says Lt. Col. Zawada. "Today's young people want purpose; they want action, and they want to know how they can contribute to something meaningful. We're excited to show even more students how the Guard meets that need."

Mixed-Reality Technology Brings Immersion and Impact

Disasterville utilizes advanced mixed-reality technology with augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) graphics mapped to large plywood structures, creating a free-roam virtual neighborhood experience in high school gyms. Students wear virtual reality headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, and hazards, rescuing people in need. The technology also features advanced hand tracking, eliminating the need for game controllers and allowing students to interact with others and physically use in-game props and Army National Guard rescue tools like oars, hoses, chainsaws, and the jaws of life.  

Extended reality (XR) industry expert Dale Carman helped the Army bring the Disasterville experience to life. Carman is the co-founder and executive creative director at Groove Jones, which has over 25 years of experience in feature films, immersive tech, and branded productions.

A specialized tour crew will be present at each tour stop to guide participants safely through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about service.   

For more information on the Army National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

Supplementary Information

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is Disasterville, and how does the experience work?

A: Disasterville is a mixed-reality experience from the U.S. Army National Guard touring the nation, transforming gymnasiums into full-scale, mission-oriented disaster zones to show students how National Guard Soldiers respond to natural disasters and emergencies through hands-on simulations. Students wear Meta Quest 3 headsets with multiplayer, local-network tracking to engage with classmates in-game as the structures around them become devastated buildings, debris, rough terrain, hazards, and people in need. Students are guided firsthand through high-tech, virtual missions, working together in teams to tackle three disaster zones -- wildfire, flood zone, and earthquake -- the same way as the Guard, by combining communication, physical endurance, and ingenuity to save lives, landscape, and their communities.

Q: Where will Disasterville be traveling?

A: Following a successful 2026 spring tour, Disasterville will head to even more high schools September through November in the following cities: Memphis, Tenn.; Chicago, Ill.; Hagerstown, Md.; Philadelphia, Pa.; Long Island, N.Y.; Richmond, Va.; and Atlanta, Ga. At each tour stop, a specialized tour crew will ensure the safety of and guide participants through each mission. Army National Guard recruiters will also be available to connect with students and answer questions about Guard service.   

Q: What do Army National Guard Soldiers do? Where and how do they serve?

A: With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers serve part-time to support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Serving at least one weekend a month and two weeks a year, National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to pursue their civilian personal and professional passions.

Q: Where can I learn more about opportunities in the Army National Guard?

A: For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

About the Army National Guard (ARNG):

With a presence in 54 states and territories, the Army National Guard is a unique component of the U.S. Army where Soldiers support communities in their home state by responding to domestic emergencies and at the federal level as standby support for Active Duty Soldiers. Army National Guard Soldiers have the flexibility to serve part-time across medical, aviation, law enforcement, transportation, and engineering fields and beyond, while also pursuing their personal and professional goals through a civilian career or higher education. For more information on the opportunities in the National Guard, visit NationalGuard.com.

OpenProposal Brings a Common Standard to a Historically Manual Stage of Media Buying, Connecting RFPs to Buy Commitments and will be in Public Comment until October 22, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, IAB Tech Lab, the global digital advertising technical standards-setting body, announced AAMP 3.0, the next major release of its Agentic Advertising Management Protocols framework, introducing a standardized way for buyers and sellers to move from an RFP through proposal evaluation and toward a buy commitment in agentic advertising.
releases.title: IAB Tech Lab Introduces AAMP 3.0 to Standardize the RFP-to-Buy Process for Agentic Advertising
releases.body:
OpenProposal Brings a Common Standard to a Historically Manual Stage of Media Buying, Connecting RFPs to Buy Commitments and will be in Public Comment until October 22, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, IAB Tech Lab, the global digital advertising technical standards-setting body, announced AAMP 3.0, the next major release of its Agentic Advertising Management Protocols framework, introducing a standardized way for buyers and sellers to move from an RFP through proposal evaluation and toward a buy commitment in agentic advertising.

While standards exist for many stages of digital media buying and execution, the process between an RFP and a buy commitment has historically been handled largely through human and manual workflows. As AI agents take on more responsibility for discovering, evaluating and planning media, that gap creates the need for a common way for buyer and seller agents to exchange and evaluate proposals before a transaction moves toward execution.

AAMP 3.0 addresses that gap through OpenProposal, a new specification that defines how sellers can represent advertising products and respond to buyer briefs in a standardized, agent-readable format. OpenProposal enables buying agents to discover and compare opportunities against a brief while giving sellers control over how their inventory and ad products are represented. The new specification will be in Public Comment until October 22, 2026, during which time it will be built into the Buyer and Seller Agent SDK reference implementations.

OpenProposal extends AAMP into the RFP and proposal stage while connecting to the IAB Tech Lab standards already used across media execution, including AdCOM, OpenDirect, and the Deals API. Together, these standards provide a common foundation for agentic workflows to move from discovery and planning through negotiation, buying, execution and reporting.

"As agents take on more of the work in media planning and buying,the industry needs a common framework for the RFP and proposal process," said Anthony Katsur, CEO, IAB Tech Lab. "OpenProposal fills a major gap between a buyer's brief and a buy commitment, giving buyer and seller agents a standardized way to exchange and evaluate opportunities. By connecting that process to the standards the industry already uses for execution, AAMP 3.0 creates a foundation for agentic workflows across the media buying lifecycle."

From Discovery to Execution

OpenProposal creates a standard way for publishers to define advertising products and packages and to represent them in RFP responses. Buying agents can evaluate those proposals against a buyer's brief, compare opportunities and assess suitability before moving toward a buy commitment. Once an opportunity moves forward, AAMP connects that proposal to the standards and infrastructure used for all types of transaction and execution.

AAMP 3.0 supports a media lifecycle that includes:

  • Publish: Sellers publish a catalog of public packages that can be browsed, while retaining some products for custom proposals.
  • Discover: Buyer agents retrieve available public packages, enabling inventory discovery before a negotiation begins, or submit a full brief to get a custom proposal.
  • Compare: Buyer agents evaluate and rank opportunities against a declared brief, creating the ability to process information from a broader set of publishers than would be practical through manual evaluation alone.
  • Qualify: Agents evaluate availability and fit for the specific audience, flight and requirements of a media plan.
  • Negotiate: When needed, buyer and seller agents can negotiate custom terms while maintaining a reference to the original published offer.
  • Bind & Execute: Transactions can be executed using the existing standards and infrastructure of the digital advertising ecosystem.
  • Report: Performance can flow back through existing reporting standards, allowing results to be evaluated against the original objectives and commitments of the plan.

AdCOM provides a common vocabulary throughout these stages, allowing the information represented at discovery to remain consistent as an opportunity moves through planning, negotiation, execution and reporting.

OpenProposal Makes Publisher Ad Products Agent-Readable

OpenProposal gives publishers a standardized way to make a broader range of ad products understandable to buying agents and to create proposals in response to buyer briefs. In the proposal, sellers can include information necessary for buyers to understand how the products can be bought, executed, measured and evaluated.

For buyers, this creates the ability to evaluate a much broader universe of potential media opportunities. Agentic technology can process and compare more information across more publishers than a human planner could reasonably evaluate alone, helping buying organizations build plans informed by a larger and more diverse consideration set.

OpenProposal maintains continuity with the digital advertising infrastructure already in the market. It complements OpenDirect, AdCOM, and the Deals API, using those established standards as opportunities move from planning into transaction and execution. Existing programmatic implementations of those standards can continue operating as they do today, without requiring DSPs, SSPs or other technologies to change their existing use cases.

In addition, the AAMP agent software development kits (SDKs) continue to further harden deterministic guardrails governing pricing, ad packages, orders and media buy details, increase trust in agent identities, and strengthen idempotency across transactions to help ensure consistent responses and data integrity as agents operate at greater speed and scale. In practical terms, idempotency means an instruction can be sent twice without happening twice; so when an agent retries a request it didn't get an answer to, the result is confirmation of the original order rather than a duplicate.

Industry Support for an Agentic Media Ecosystem

As agencies, brands and publishers begin building agents into their planning and transaction workflows, industry participants are rallying around the need for common standards that allow those agents to communicate across companies and platforms. AAMP agents with OpenProposal are designed to create that shared foundation while allowing every participant to maintain control over its own technology, inventory, business rules and data.

"By providing full agentic coverage for all existing IAB Tech Lab standards, while at the same time standardizing agent authentication and authorization protocols, AAMP 3.0 delivers a transaction-ready framework that will aid our industry's movement from proof-of-concept tests towards the wide-spread use of AI Agents in media transactions." added Michael Palmer, Global Vice President, Emerging Technologies at WPP Media.

"Agentic planning gives us the opportunity to evaluate a much broader range of media opportunities and information when we build a plan," added Mike Treon, Head of CTV Strategy at PMG. "What's new in AAMP 3.0 is that the reasoning travels with the proposal. A seller can tell us not just what a package costs, but why they believe it fits the brief — the audience rationale, the formats, the terms behind the price. That context is what our planning models need, and now it arrives in a form they can actually read."

The global IAB Network is also getting involved. "IAB Australia has opened expressions of interest for a seller-side pilot using the AAMP reference implementations available today," said Jonas Jaanimagi, Technology Lead, IAB Australia. "We've been running those implementations in a lab for months and contributing feedback upstream. Our role now is to help Australian publishers test discovery, proposal and approval workflows in a sandbox before any live spend is involved, and to turn that practical experience into useful evidence for the industry."

AAMP 3.0 represents the next stage in IAB Tech Lab's work to apply agentic capabilities to the proven standards that underpin digital advertising. By standardizing the RFP-to-buy commitment process and connecting it with established standards for transaction, execution and reporting, AAMP 3.0 helps create a common foundation for agentic media buying without requiring the industry to rebuild the infrastructure it relies on today.

To review the OpenProposal specification, supporting technical resources, and to provide feedback, via Public Comment until October 22, 2026. please visit: iabtechlab.com/AAMPv3.

About IAB Technology Laboratory

Established in 2014, the IAB Technology Laboratory (Tech Lab) is a non-profit consortium that engages a member community globally to develop foundational technology and standards that enable growth and trust in the digital media ecosystem. Comprised of digital publishers, ad technology firms, agencies, brands, and other member companies, IAB Tech Lab focuses on solutions for brand safety and ad fraud; identity, data, and consumer privacy; cross-channel programmatic effectiveness and ad measurement; and the impact of LLMs and AI agents on advertising. Its work includes the OpenRTB real-time bidding protocol, ads.txt anti-fraud specification, Open Measurement SDK for viewability and verification, VAST video specification, Trusted Server, and the Agentic Roadmap initiative for agentic advertising. Board members and companies are listed at https://iabtechlab.com/about-the-iab-tech-lab/tech-lab-leadership/. For more information, please visit https://iabtechlab.com.

releases.body:
• Minivela's Manny Ruiz will serve as creative and content strategy partner for Great American Media's new streaming destination for Latino families

     
  • Actor-producer Carlos Ponce will support creative development, talent relationships and audience engagement

NEW YORK, Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Great American Media today announced it has tapped Minivela, the Latino media entertainment and production company co-founded by media entrepreneur Manny Ruiz and actor-producer Carlos Ponce, to support the creation and production of Pure Flix Familia, Great American Media's new streaming destination created for Latino families.

Great American Media expands its Minivela partnership to help build Pure Flix Familia for Latino families.

Minivela will serve as Pure Flix Familia's programming, content and creative partner, working closely with Great American Media and Pure Flix leadership on original programming, content development, creator relationships, licensing, cultural strategy and audience engagement.

Ruiz and Ponce bring decades of experience working within the Latino community at the grassroots level, with deep track records across Hispanic media, entertainment, cultural marketing and storytelling that have connected them directly with Latino audiences, creators and communities.

"Pure Flix Familia represents an important expansion of Great American Media's mission to serve families with trusted entertainment grounded in faith and shared values," said Bill Abbott, President and CEO of Great American Media. "Manny, Carlos and the Minivela team bring a strong creative instinct and a deep understanding of Latino audiences and a commitment to faith and family entertainment. They know this community because they are part of it. Their perspective will be invaluable as we build a distinctive programming strategy and develop authentic stories that resonate across generations."

Manny Ruiz, CEO and co-founder of Minivela, will lead Minivela's work as programming, creative and content strategy partner. In this role, he will collaborate with Great American Media and Pure Flix executives to help identify original programming opportunities, cultivate relationships with Latino creators and producers, and advise on the platform's cultural and audience strategy.

"This is an opportunity to work alongside Great American Media to build a streaming destination that understands Latino families and reflects their faith, values, experiences and aspirations," Ruiz said. "Our focus will be on helping Pure Flix Familia develop authentic programming, meaningful creator relationships and a consistent content pipeline that can earn a lasting place in people's homes."

Carlos Ponce, who co-founded Minivela with Ruiz, will play a key creative and audience-facing role in the partnership. Ponce will support the development of Pure Flix Familia's creative identity, help establish relationships with actors, writers, filmmakers and other creators, and contribute to audience-engagement initiatives. He is also expected to participate as on-screen talent in future Pure Flix Familia projects.

"Authenticity begins by ensuring that the people and communities we hope to serve have a meaningful voice in the creative process," Ponce said. "We will work directly with writers, actors, filmmakers and producers who know these families because they come from these families. That is how we can help create stories audiences recognize, trust and want to share."

Minivela will help develop original movies, series and mobile-first microdramas; identify potential content and acquisition opportunities; cultivate emerging and established Latino talent; and advise on programming, social media, community partnerships and audience-growth initiatives. The expanded relationship gives Minivela a broader leadership role in the development and operation of Pure Flix Familia.

Great American Media will retain responsibility for Pure Flix Familia's business operations and final approval over its brand, budget, programming, acquisitions and distribution.

The expanded partnership builds upon Great American Media and Minivela's previously announced development, distribution and marketing relationship that was initially only focused on producing mobile-first microdramas for U.S. Hispanic and Latin American audiences.

Pure Flix Familia is scheduled to launch in early October with Spanish-language entertainment and will expand over time to include bilingual and English-language programming created and curated for Latino audiences. The service is part of Great American Media's broader strategy to grow its faith-and-family entertainment ecosystem and reach new audiences with programming families can confidently enjoy together.

Additional details about Pure Flix Familia's launch programming, subscription options, supported devices and availability will be announced separately.

ABOUT GREAT AMERICAN MEDIA

Great American Media is a leader in faith-and-family entertainment and one of the fastest-growing entertainment networks on television. Great American Media is home to a portfolio of brands that celebrate faith, family and country, including Great American Family, the flagship linear network featuring original Christmas movies, romantic comedies and beloved series; Great American Pure Flix, a leading faith-and-family streaming service; Great American Faith & Living, the company's unscripted companion network; and GFam+, an app that allows viewers to watch Great American Media programming anytime and anywhere.

Established in June 2021 by Bill Abbott and a group of U.S.-based family offices, Great American Media programming is available through cable and satellite providers, Great American Pure Flix, YouTube TV and the GFam+ app.

ABOUT PURE FLIX FAMILIA

Pure Flix Familia is an operating entity within Great American Pure Flix and Great American Media dedicated to culturally relevant entertainment centered on faith and family. The streaming destination is being developed to serve Spanish-dominant, bilingual and English-dominant Latino audiences through original movies, series, mobile-first microdramas and thoughtfully curated programming that families can confidently enjoy together.

ABOUT MINIVELA

Minivela is a Latino-focused entertainment and production company co-founded by media entrepreneur Manny Ruiz and actor-producer Carlos Ponce. The company develops culturally relevant programming for U.S. Hispanic and Latin American audiences, with an emphasis on mobile-first storytelling, emerging creative formats and authentic relationships with Latino creators and communities.

releases.title: "Detroit Remembers Richard Smallwood" A Concert Tribute to Honor the Gospel Music Icon This October
releases.body:
BMJ Productions and Empowerment Church present a two-night tribute, 50-member choir, legendary Detroit artists and musicians led by Bill Moss Jr. in a celebration of Smallwood's five-decade legacy.

SOUTHFIELD, Mich., Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hundreds of metro Detroiters will pay tribute to one of gospel music's most influential composers this fall, as BMJ Productions LLC and Empowerment Church present Detroit Remembers: Richard Smallwood, a two-night musical tribute concert Friday, October 9 and Saturday, October 10, 2026, at Empowerment Church in Southfield, Michigan sponsored by Salathiel Records. Tickets are available for $30 in advance, $40 at the door and $75 VIP through bmjproductionsll.com or empowermentmi.org.

The event honors Richard Smallwood, the Grammy-nominated composer, pianist and choir director who died in December 2025 at age 77. Over four decades, Smallwood blended classical training earned at Howard University with the fervor of traditional Black gospel, creating songs including "Total Praise," "Center of My Joy" and "I Love the Lord" that reached mainstream audiences through artists such as Whitney Houston and Destiny's Child.

The tribute will bring 15 of his most iconic songs to life through a 50-member choir and celebrated Detroit talent, led by:

  • Bill Moss Jr., Visionary Music Director
  • Pam English, Vocal Director and Master Clinician
  • Alvin Waddles, Principal and Featured Artist
  • Rev. Kimberly Whitsett, Artistic Director
  • Ernest Tolbert, Band Director

Moss, son of gospel great Bill Moss Sr. of Bill Moss and the Celestials and part of the extended Clark Sisters family, brings his own deep Detroit gospel roots to the production, making the concert both a tribute to Smallwood's national legacy and a homecoming for the city's gospel community.

"Richard Smallwood didn't just write songs, he gave the church a new language for worship," said Bill Moss Jr., renowned gospel artist and Art and Music Director for Empowerment Church. "This isn't just a concert, it's a love letter to a man who changed how the world worships. Detroit is going to feel every note."

Sponsorship opportunities are available for organizations that want to connect with a highly engaged audience of faith leaders, music lovers and community members across Southeast Michigan, including logo placement, event visibility and complimentary VIP tickets. Ticket and sponsorship inquiries can be directed to shantl.olovson@gmail.com.

releases.body:
Acquisition strengthens Media One's home décor and apparel offering with expanded fabrics, pigment printing technology and technical expertise

GARDEN GROVE, Calif., Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Media One ("M1"), a leading full-service integrator and value-added distributor of wide-format printing solutions, announced today that it has acquired the U.S. business and assets of Premex Solutions, a leading supplier of high-quality, print-ready fabrics for the digital textile printing industry. Premex Solutions builds on the more than 40-year textile heritage of its parent company, Premier Textiles UK, an independent family-run business founded in 1981, with a modern focus on digitally printable fabrics for the U.S. market.

The acquisition builds on Media One's growing portfolio, alongside Fisher Textiles and Hyperflex Vinyls, and expands the range of applications and solutions Media One and Fisher Textiles can bring to its customers in the home décor, interior décor and fashion markets. Premex Solutions brings an extensive range of high-quality, print-ready fabrics, deep textile knowledge and technical expertise, and established customer relationships that round out Media One and Fisher Textiles' existing product and service offerings.

"We're excited to welcome Premex Solutions to the Media One family," said Jake Feldman, Chief Executive Officer of Media One. "Premex has developed best-in-class print-ready and pre-treated fabrics, along with real technical depth in natural and specialty textiles that complements our own printing technology and service expertise. Paired with our differentiated printing solutions, distribution scale and nationwide technical support, we can now bring an end-to-end, industry-leading solution to the home décor and apparel markets."

Premex Solutions will join Media One's growing portfolio alongside Fisher Textiles and Hyperflex Vinyls. The combination extends Media One's integrated model into home décor and apparel, bringing together print-ready fabrics, printing equipment, inks, finishing solutions and nationwide technical service under one organization. Premex Solutions customers will continue to work with the people and products they know today while gaining access to Media One's broader capabilities and support.

"Premier Textiles has been my family's business for more than four decades, and we are extremely proud of the reputation, relationships and textile expertise we have built over that time," said Ashok Kallumpram, Managing Director of Premier Textiles. "Premex Solutions represents an important extension of that legacy into the U.S. digital printing market, so finding the right long-term home for the business was very important to us. We believe Media One shares our commitment to customers, people and the textile industry and has the capabilities and vision to build on that legacy for many years to come."

"This is an exciting next chapter for Premex Solutions," said Nick Smith, Managing Director of Premier Digital Textiles. "Combining our textile expertise and product portfolio with Media One's broader digital print capabilities creates meaningful opportunities for our customers and our team. We look forward to supporting a smooth transition and helping build on the momentum Premex Solutions has created in the U.S. market."

Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

About Media One

Media One Digital Imaging, LLC is the only full-service integrator and value-added distributor of large format printing solutions in the United States. The company provides best-in-class printers, inks, fabrics, paper, vinyl, laminates, equipment, finishing solutions, color management, software, and training and maintenance services to print providers nationwide. Through its portfolio, including Fisher Textiles and Hyperflex Vinyls, Media One is a true one-stop solution for the large-format and textile printing industry.

About Premex Solutions

Premex Solutions is a leader in high-quality, print-ready fabrics for the digital textile market, serving customers across home furnishings, interior décor, fashion and related applications. Based in Marietta, Georgia, Premex Solutions combines deep textile knowledge, technical expertise and innovation to deliver a broad range of fabrics designed for digital printing. Premex Solutions is currently a subsidiary of Premier Textiles, an independent, family-run textile business founded in 1981 with more than 40 years of textile industry experience.

releases.title: Austin Business Journal Ranks Status Labs Among Top 10 Advertising & Marketing Agencies
releases.body:
The Austin-founded global reputation-management firm strengthens its position at the intersection of AI, search, and public trust with fast-growing GEO division

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Status Labs, the premier digital reputation management firm in The Millbrook Companies agency collective, is pleased to announce its No. 10 ranking on the 2026 Advertising & Marketing Agencies list by the Austin Business Journal.

Status Labs was founded in Austin in 2012, at a time when online reputation management had yet to become an established industry. Fourteen years later, the firm remains headquartered in Austin while serving enterprise organizations, growth-stage businesses, family offices, and high-profile public figures in over a dozen countries through satellite offices in New York, Los Angeles, Miami, and London.

Its gradual expansion to new markets – and continued growth in the Austin market where the company and the Millbrook holdco originated –  can be attributed to a commitment to cutting-edge innovation, which most recently has been exemplified by Status Labs early entry and expertise in the burgeoning generative engine optimization vertical. 

The firm has built its business around a question that has become central to modern corporate reputation: What do people find – and now, what are they told – when they seek information about an organization or individual?

That question has taken on new urgency with generative AI. AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity increasingly provide direct answers rather than a page of links, shaping how customers, investors, partners, journalists, and the public encounter a company for the first time.

Status Labs formally launched its Generative Engine Optimization, or GEO, offering in October 2025. The work itself began earlier, as the firm studied how emerging generative AI systems were interpreting, synthesizing, and recommending information about companies and public figures in 2023, before GEO was widely recognized as a service category.

Today, GEO is Status Labs' fastest-growing workstream, accounting for almost a quarter of new client engagements in the first half of 2026.

"Status Labs was built on the understanding that reputations are increasingly formed online, often before a client has the opportunity to tell its own story," said Darius Fisher, CEO of Millbrook Companies and co-founder of Status Labs. "As AI becomes a primary interface for information, that work has become more consequential. The question is no longer only where a company ranks in search. It is whether the answer someone receives accurately reflects who that company is."

Status Labs' 2026 AI Reputation Report found that roughly 60% of searches now end without a click to a website. When AI systems assemble an answer, the report found, they draw heavily on earned media and other third-party sources—not simply the material a company publishes about itself. Visitors who arrive through an AI-generated answer convert at 4.4 times the rate of visitors from organic search.

For clients operating across markets, sectors, and public audiences, the consequence is practical: a company can have a strong website and a well-defined brand, yet still be inaccurately represented—or absent entirely—when an AI platform is asked who leads its category.

Status Labs' GEO practice combines AI-driven language-model diagnostics, semantic content mapping, and credibility-signal engineering. The firm audits how large language models interpret and summarize a client's business; structures priority messages so they remain intact through AI summarization; and strengthens the high-quality, corroborating sources that influence whether a model cites a company, represents it accurately, or overlooks it altogether.

"A decade ago, a reputation challenge often appeared as a page of search results," Fisher said. "Today, it may appear as a paragraph response assembled from sources a company did not create. We began preparing for that shift before there was a standard name for the work because the direction of the internet was already clear."

Status Labs is part of Millbrook Companies, which brings together earned media, owned content, search, and reputation strategy through Status Labs, Sensei Advisory, and BLP.

The 2026 Advertising Agencies list is available via ABJ. To request a GEO consultation, visit StatusLabs.com/Contact.

About Status Labs

Status Labs is the world's leading digital reputation management, SEO, and generative engine optimization (GEO) firm for Fortune 500 companies, growth-stage businesses, family offices, and public figures. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Status Labs is now part of Millbrook Companies alongside agencies Sensei Advisory and BLP. To learn more about Status Labs, visit StatusLabs.com.
