releases.title: United Teams Up with DISH to Broadcast Professional and College Football Games Live on Starlink-Enabled Seatback Screens
releases.body:
United flyers won't miss a play this football season, with live broadcasts from ABC, CBS, NBC, FOX, FS1, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network and TNF on Prime Video on Starlink-enabled seatback screens starting this week through the big game in February

Starlink is the fastest, most reliable WiFi in the sky and live TV streaming on seatback screens is now on board more than 220 mainline aircraft for customers in every class of service – up to 700 flights per day – with plans to reach 700 mainline planes early next year

United sponsors nine NFL teams and expects to operate 200+ team charter flights this season for 11 teams.

CHICAGO, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- United Airlines customers won't miss a play this football season, thanks to a new agreement between the airline and DISH. Starting this week, travelers can catch live professional and college football games right on their Starlink-enabled seatback screen.

Starlink is the fastest, most reliable Wi-Fi in the sky and United is installing Starlink at a rapid rate - and, fans can now watch live broadcasts from ABC, CBS, NBC, FOX, FS1, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network and TNF on Prime Video on more than 200 Starlink-equipped airplanes – about 700 of flights per day. The service will be available on domestic flights through the big game in February, and United expects to have Starlink on nearly 700 airplanes by then.

Starlink is free for MileagePlus members in every class of service, and the airline expects to complete installations before the end of 2027.

This new entertainment offering builds on the airline's long history of supporting professional football, sponsoring nine professional football teams in New York, Chicago, San Francisco, Houston, Washington D.C., Denver, Kansas City, Cleveland and Nashville and operating more than 200 team charter flights for 11 teams this season.

"Starlink opens a whole new world of features and benefits for our customers, regardless of where they sit on the plane – now football fans don't have to schedule their flights around game day," said Andrew Nocella, United's Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer. "Instead, they can watch their favorite team on seatback and also make changes to their fantasy roster, text or live chat with friends, or even stream different games on their phone, laptop or tablet, just like they would do at home."

United's new agreement represents a collaborative effort with DISH, utilizing its OnStream platform, to deliver content to next-generation aviation environments.

"With United, we are helping to rewrite the inflight playbook," said Amir Ahmed, Executive Vice President, Video Services, DISH. "Whether you're sitting on your couch or cruising at 35,000 feet, you should be able to watch your favorite teams play. By pairing DISH's OnStream platform with United's Starlink connectivity, we're keeping fans connected to the moments that matter most."

Starlink Sets a New Standard for Live Entertainment in Flight

This new service is just the latest example of how United is using Starlink to redefine the inflight entertainment experience. Last month, United partnered with ESPN to host a first-of-its kind live Fantasy Football Draft from 30,000 feet where ESPN analyst Tyler Fulghum made his picks live from the sky during the two-hour broadcast. And earlier this summer, United customers could stream the biggest soccer tournament in the world onboard Starlink-powered domestic flights.

Starlink is now active on more than 560 United mainline and United Express® aircraft and the airline has already flown more than 31 million passengers on Starlink-powered aircraft across more than 464,000 flights, powering 14.2 million devices.

Starlink is just one way United is investing nose to tail in its customer experience. The airline continues to install seatback screens across its fleet – up to 1,000 aircraft before the end of 2027 – and is rolling out new airplanes with 27-inch, 4K OLED seatback screens, the largest among U.S. carriers. Passengers can now access more than 2,500 hours of premium entertainment content including Apple TV, HBO Max, A24 and Spotify.

Football Flies United

Separately, for the second year in a row, United is celebrating the intersection of football, fashion and travel for its Football Flies United advertising campaign. Featuring New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh, Giants players Abdul Carter and Arvell Reese, and Chicago Bears players Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland, the campaign is built around a simple idea: how you arrive matters. Whether stepping off a plane for game day or arriving for an important business meeting, traveling well can help people feel refreshed, confident and ready to work – no matter what comes next.

"When our players step off the plane, we want them to feel rested, confident and ready to compete. Football Flies United celebrates the idea that when you travel well and feel your best, you're going to perform at your best," said Coach Harbaugh. "And for football fans traveling this season, they can bring that same game-day energy with them knowing they won't have to miss a play – they can watch their favorite teams live on United flights all season long."

The campaign is featured across prominent out-of-home locations in Chicago and New York, including Wrigleyville and Penn Station, with additional content rolling out across social media throughout the NFL season. The teams and locations were chosen to highlight United's roots as Chicago's hometown airline, and its global reach with Newark as a gateway to more than 90 international destinations.

The airline will also charter flights for the Washington Commanders, New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers for their international games in London, Paris and Mexico City.

About United

At United, Good Leads The Way. With U.S. hubs in Chicago, Denver, Houston, Los Angeles, New York/Newark, San Francisco and Washington, D.C., United operates the most comprehensive global route network among North American carriers and is now the largest airline in the world as measured by available seat miles. For more about how to join the United team, please visit www.united.com/careers and more information about the company is at www.united.com. United Airlines Holdings, Inc., the parent company of United Airlines, Inc., is traded on the Nasdaq under the symbol "UAL".

releases.title: Regal Delivers Its Biggest Domestic Summer at the Box Office Since 2018
releases.body:
Revenues up 35.3% thanks to strong performance with the biggest movies of the summer

KNOXVILLE, Tenn., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Regal's gross domestic box office revenues grew more than 35% year-over-year this summer, marking the company's biggest summer in eight years.

Performance in the period (May 1-Sept. 7) was driven by outstanding delivery across all movies with particular strength on the biggest films of the summer, Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey. The company took 18.2% of share on Spider-Man and 19.5% of The Odyssey, both well ahead of its 16.5% share of the market as a whole.

"A summer like this starts with filmmakers and studios making films that people really want to see on a big screen, and there have been a lot of them already this year," said Eduardo Acuña, Chief Executive Officer of Regal Global Entertainment. "The slate had real depth and range to it, and audiences kept coming back to share it with family and friends. I'm grateful to Regal's theatre teams who worked so hard to look after moviegoers, and to the staff in our offices who set the summer up so well. Our partners are putting money into films worth seeing, and we're putting money into the experience of watching them—moviegoers get the benefit of both."

The depth of the movie slate this summer played a key part in the success of the season. Alongside the summer's two biggest releases, Toy Story 5, Michael, The Mandalorian and Grogu, Obsession, The Devil Wears Prada 2, Backrooms, and Minions & Monsters each brought a different audience into theatres. The strength of the schedule was consistent from the first weekend in May through Labor Day rather than being concentrated in a handful of dates.

Premium large formats continue to contribute to ongoing growth through company investment in renovating theatres with expanded premium offerings including the recently opened Regal Sherman Oaks Galleria in Los Angeles. Regal's premium format box office rose 63% year over year and represented 22% of the circuit's summer revenue in the period, up from 18% a year ago, and contributing a third of the company's total increase. IMAX revenue at Regal more than doubled, RPX grew 80%, ScreenX grew 45%, and 4DX grew 13%. Premium formats made up more than 60% of Regal's gross on The Odyssey, a third on The Mandalorian and Grogu, and a quarter on Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Standard format revenue grew 29% over the same period, showing that the increase came from across the circuit rather than from premium alone.

About Regal Global Entertainment

Regal Global Entertainment operates the second-largest theatrical exhibition business in the world with 7,648 screens across 629 locations. Through its Cinema City, Cineworld, Picturehouse, Planet, and Regal brands, the company is committed to delivering exceptional moviegoing experiences through premium large formats, innovative loyalty and subscription programs, enhanced food and beverage offerings, and outstanding guest service.

The 2026 summer season runs from Friday, May 1 to Labor Day, Monday, September 7. The 2025 summer season ran from Friday, May 2 to Labor Day, Monday, September 1.

releases.title: New Retirement in America Podcast: Rising Healthcare Costs Put Retirement Security Under Pressure
releases.body:
Segal Board Chair David Blumenstein Examines the Changing Benefits Landscape, the Enduring Value of Pensions and the Future of Retirement

WASHINGTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Institute on Retirement Security (NIRS) today released Episode 5 of its Retirement in America podcast, "The New Reality of Retirement and Workplace Benefits."

The new episode features David Blumenstein, board chair and immediate past president and CEO of Segal, and podcast host Dan Doonan in a wide-ranging conversation about the forces reshaping employee benefits and retirement security. They examine rising healthcare costs, the shift of retirement responsibility to individuals, the continuing value of pensions, changing expectations for workplace benefits, and how technology and artificial intelligence could transform the field.

Retirement in America is available on the NIRS website, YouTube, and all major podcast platforms.

"Healthcare and retirement benefits do not exist in separate silos," Doonan said. "When healthcare costs consume a larger share of compensation, there is less room for wages and retirement contributions. David brings decades of experience working with employers and plan sponsors, and this conversation helps explain why strengthening retirement security requires looking at the entire benefits landscape."

Blumenstein says the pace of change confronting employers and plan sponsors has accelerated significantly. On the retirement side, advances in computing have enabled more sophisticated risk modeling. On the healthcare side, employers are navigating rapidly evolving treatments, telehealth and other new approaches to care. At the same time, workers increasingly expect benefits information and tools to be as immediate and easy to use as other digital services.

The conversation also explores the broader shift toward placing more responsibility for saving for retirement on individual workers. Blumenstein says that while defined contribution plans are an important part of the retirement system, many workers cannot simply save more when their income is already consumed by basic necessities. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss the role defined benefit pensions can play by providing lifetime income workers can count on, as well as the need for personal savings to supplement retirement income.

Blumenstein also offers an optimistic view of technology and artificial intelligence. He expects new tools to make benefits analysis faster and more responsive while allowing employers and workers to model decisions more easily. But he emphasizes that critical thinking, problem solving and judgment will remain essential as the benefits field continues to evolve.

Among the topics discussed in the episode:

  • Rising healthcare costs and retirement security. Healthcare inflation puts pressure on employer compensation budgets, potentially leaving less available for wages and retirement benefits while workers and retirees face higher medical expenses.
  • The changing employee benefits landscape. Employers and plan sponsors are adapting to faster technological change, new healthcare treatments and rising expectations for easy, real-time access to benefits information.
  • The growing burden on individuals. Workers are increasingly responsible for saving for their own retirement, even as affordability pressures can make it difficult to maximize 401(k) or IRA contributions.
  • The enduring value of pensions. Doonan and Blumenstein discuss how defined benefit plans provide lifetime income and reduce some of the complex financial decisions and risks individuals otherwise must manage on their own.
  • Technology and AI. Blumenstein sees technology as a force that can improve modeling, communication and decision-making, while increasing the importance of critical thinking and problem solving.
  • A collective approach to retirement security. The episode closes with a discussion of the need for employers, policymakers and other stakeholders to work together on challenges that cannot be solved by individuals alone.

Retirement in America is a podcast from NIRS examining the economic, workforce and policy trends influencing retirement security. Combining expert insight with real-world experiences, the podcast helps listeners better understand one of the most important financial issues facing American workers and families today.

The National Institute on Retirement Security is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization established to contribute to informed policymaking by fostering a deep understanding of the value of retirement security to employees, employers, and the economy as a whole. Located in Washington, D.C., NIRS membership includes financial services firms, employee benefit plans, trade associations, and other retirement service providers.

releases.title: Notes.fm Raises $5 Million to Unify Royalties, Publishing, and Distribution for Independent Artists
releases.body:
New funding from leading artists and music industry executives—including Zach Bryan, Benny Blanco, Tainy, Ari Emanuel, Julie Greenwald, Sam Hendel, and others—supports the next phase of growth as Notes.fm builds a new financial layer for the music economy

Download Image Assets Here

NEW YORK, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Notes.fm, the music royalty collection platform helping musicians and music companies identify and collect 100% of their royalties, announces it has raised $5 million from leading artists, managers, executives and strategic partners across the music industry. Notes is the latest venture from Stem co-founder Tim Luckow, on a mission to support independent artists with the best-in-class technology for distribution and publishing under one roof so they can have full control over their earnings and stop missing out on money that is rightfully theirs.

The round includes participation from a range of influential artists and music industry leaders from Benny Blanco, Zach Bryan and his managers Stefan Max and Danny Kang, Tainy, Blake Slatkin, and Mt. Joy frontman Matt Quinn, WME Group Executive Chairman Ari Emanuel, Chord Music founder Sam Hendel, longtime Atlantic Records chief and 26.2 founder Julie Greenwald, as well as many of the industry's leading companies including Foundations, Mick Management, Twenty Ten Management, Triple 8, KMGMT, Good Boy, Mexican Summer, and Breakaway. The funding will support continued platform development and scaled marketing efforts as Notes expands its offering to artists globally.

Notes recently debuted a new feature "Releases" and unveiled its new partnership with Stripe, to streamline distribution, publishing admin and money management into one simplified release flow for musicians. This allows artists to use Notes.fm as the home for both distribution and royalty collection, making it easy for artists and their teams to take simultaneous ownership of their creative output and the income it generates. Notes is founded on the principle that every artist should receive all of their royalties. That's why they take 0% participation in distribution and publishing royalties, charging a flat monthly subscription fee instead. It's the same ethos behind their catalog royalty review technology, which helps rights owners identify missing royalties across their catalog and fix the issues so they can claim all of the royalties they've earned while they can.

This isn't new for Notes. Since launch, they've rolled out capabilities that allow artists and rights holders to more seamlessly manage their earnings, including integrated financial accounts designed to give users more flexibility in how they collect, store, and transfer, and earn on income. These updates are part of a broader effort to build a more complete financial layer for the modern music ecosystem.

Prior to Releases, Notes also announced  Credits.fm, a free and open music credits database indexing more than 150 million song codes and credits to help the music industry organize, verify, and connect the data powering royalties and artist compensation in the age of AI.

"Music is evolving quickly, and the finance systems around it need to evolve at a faster rate," said Tim Luckow, CEO and co-founder of Notes.fm. "Between all of the actions required to properly release, credit and collect on music, there are a lot of places where money falls through the cracks. We built Notes to bring all of that into one platform — so artists can release music and collect every royalty from day one, and recover what's historically been missed."

"Having spent our careers working with artists at every level, we've seen firsthand how much value gets lost to fragmented, unnecessarily complex systems," adds co-founder Derek Davies. "The response to Notes from the music community has been incredibly meaningful, and we're proud to announce a raise funded almost exclusively by artists, managers and music industry strategics who have a native understanding of these issues firsthand. This raise gives us the resources to keep building the infrastructure and applications that we believe the next generation of artists deserves."

Notes has created an artist-friendly, automated process to simplify a notoriously complex and outdated system that has historically led to hundreds of millions of dollars in royalties going unclaimed by artists every year. Notes brings clarity to the complexity, requiring only a musician name and list of songs to start reviewing streaming services, collection societies, and registries like the MLC and SoundExchange. The platform not only identifies missing royalties, but it also helps an artist fix issues and directly claim the royalties that result from those corrections while ensuring future income flows correctly.

Following its public launch last year, Notes has already demonstrated strong early traction, identifying more than $10 million in previously unclaimed royalties across a broad range of artists and catalogs including James Blake, Zach Bryan, Mt. Joy, Girl In Red and more. The platform continues to grow across both emerging and established artists, reflecting a shared demand for greater clarity and access in how music earnings are tracked and distributed.

By bringing together royalty discovery, payments infrastructure, and music-centric financial management into a single experience, Notes.fm is helping to create a new system that better supports artists as their careers and audiences grow.

About Notes.fm

Notes.fm is a music royalty collection platform built to help independent musicians, artists and music companies collect all of their royalties in one easy-to-use place. Founded by Stem co-founder Tim Luckow, Notes brings distribution, publishing, and financial tools under one roof, giving musicians and companies the technology to release music, verify song credits, manage their catalogs, and collect every royalty they're owed. Music Royalties, Simplified.

Learn more at www.notes.fm.

The Untold: Chelsey Northern (cn@wearetheuntold.com), Chloé Snyder (cs@wearetheuntold.com), Cory Councill (cc@wearetheuntold.com)

releases.title: SOUNDEXCHANGE & MUSICNATION EXPAND GLOBAL RIGHTS MANAGEMENT ACCESS FOR US AND UAE RIGHTS HOLDERS
releases.body:
Agreement establishes new cross-border pathway for artists, labels, and rights holders

WASHINGTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SoundExchange, the largest neighboring rights organization in the world, and Music Nation Copyrights Management (MusicNation), a pioneer in music rights management in the United Arab Emirates, today announced the signing of a groundbreaking reciprocal agreement to strengthen cross-border neighboring rights administration and create new revenue streams for rights holders in the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

The agreement builds on SoundExchange's previously announced partnership with MusicNation to provide technology, data, and industry expertise supporting neighboring rights administration in the UAE. Together with MusicNation's partnership with BMI, the agreement reflects MusicNation's pivotal role in building the UAE's premier music licensing and royalty distribution infrastructure across neighboring rights, public performance rights, and mechanical rights. MusicNation was established as a collective management organization (CMO) to ensure that local and international performing artists, record labels, songwriters, publishers, and other rights holders are fully and fairly compensated for the use of their works in the UAE and, through reciprocal arrangements, in other markets where their works are used commercially. 

Michael Huppe, President and CEO of SoundExchange, said, "This groundbreaking reciprocal agreement with Music Nation will open a new revenue stream for SoundExchange artists and rights owners whose music is played in the UAE while ensuring Emirati creators are compensated when their music is played in the United States. It also enables SoundExchange to seamlessly provide these services for some of its partner CMOs around the world, who have the option of collecting UAE royalties through their existing agreements with SoundExchange."

For MusicNation, the agreement represents another step in developing a globally connected rights management framework for the UAE. As the country's music, entertainment, hospitality, and cultural sectors continue to expand, MusicNation is building the infrastructure needed to support trusted licensing, transparent royalty collection, and accurate distribution for creators and rights holders in the UAE and around the world.

Rasha Khalifa Al Mubarak, Chairwoman of MusicNation, said, "Music is one of the most powerful expressions of identity, culture, and human artistry. As the UAE continues to develop and attract foreign investment into its creative economy, we have a responsibility to build the systems that ensure artists and rights holders are respected, and that musical IP is protected and fairly compensated to global standards. This agreement with SoundExchange represents a national and industry milestone, advancing MusicNation's mission to create a transparent, globally connected music rights ecosystem in the UAE and strengthens the foundation for a more sustainable creative future for our region."

Amer M. Samhoun, CEO of MusicNation, said, "This agreement marks a pivotal step in MusicNation's international role as the UAE's music rights infrastructure continues to expand. It gives international CMOs and rights partners confidence that they can work with MusicNation in the UAE through a transparent and efficient system, and participate in the opportunities created by one of the region's fastest-growing creative markets."

SoundExchange manages a worldwide network of more than 100 agreements with CMOs, covering 93% of the available global neighboring rights market. Nearly 600,000 artists and rights owners entrust SoundExchange to collect worldwide royalties on their behalf. Its agreement with MusicNation adds the UAE to that network and supports greater connection between the nation's rights holders and the global neighboring rights ecosystem.

About MusicNation

MusicNation, a pioneer in music rights management in the UAE, licenses the rights of authors, publishers, sound recording owners and performers throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These rights are referred to as neighboring rights (for sound recordings), public performance rights (for musical compositions) and mechanical reproduction rights (also for musical compositions). With world-class partnerships and technology, MusicNation is helping implement the UAE's vision for the protection and enforcement of musical copyrights by developing a world-class music licensing and royalty distribution infrastructure. MusicNation, with its partners BMI and SoundExchange, will help ensure that music creators and rights holders are fully and fairly compensated for the use of their work. For more information, visit https://www.wearemusicnation.ae.

About SoundExchange

SoundExchange is the largest global neighboring rights organization in the world, redefining how creators in the music industry get paid. By turning data into fast, accurate revenue for artists and rights owners, we have collected and distributed more than $13 billion in digital performance royalties to date on behalf of more than 800,000 music creators. As the sole organization designated by the U.S. government to administer the Section 114 sound recording license, SoundExchange seamlessly collects and distributes digital performance royalties from platforms like Pandora, SiriusXM, iHeartRadio, and thousands more, as well as all available international performance royalties through a strong global partnership network. For more information, visit soundexchange.com.

The competition celebrates eight years in partnership with the CCMA at Country Music Week, delivering a $25,000 grand prize and $10,000 awarded to each runner-up

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- Following last night's live finale in Saskatoon, SiriusXM Canada, in partnership with the Canadian Country Music Association® (CCMA®), announced Blue Ridge Band as the winner of the 2026 SiriusXM Top of the Country competition. Fellow finalists Shawnee Kish and Morgan Griffiths were named runners-up, closing out an exciting year of mentorship opportunities and live performances.

The finale was broadcast live on SiriusXM's Top of the Country Radio (Ch. 155), giving country music fans across Canada the chance to tune in, vote live and share in the excitement as the 2026 competition came to a close.

Taking the stage one final time, all three finalists delivered standout performances in front of a live audience and a panel of industry experts and judges. After months of competition, Shawnee Kish, Morgan Griffiths and Blue Ridge Band showcased their unique sounds and styles, with Blue Ridge Band ultimately securing the 2026 title and $25,000 grand prize. Runners-up Shawnee Kish and Morgan Griffiths each received $10,000. The celebration was followed by a headline performance from Jade Eagleson with special guest SACHA.

"This competition has definitely been one for the books," said the Blue Ridge Band. "Being part of this program and competing alongside such talented Canadian artists has been a highlight of my career so far. I'm incredibly grateful to SiriusXM and the CCMA for their support throughout this experience, and I'm so excited for what comes next."

The road to the 2026 SiriusXM Top of the Country finale began earlier this year, when country artists from across Canada put their names forward for a chance to take the national stage. Eight semi-finalists were selected to record original songs and videos before fans voted to determine the final three. Along the way, the top three finalists gained valuable experience through mentorship from leading voices in country music and live performances at major events, including CMA Fest in Nashville and LASSO Montréal.

"This year's finalists are a testament to the depth of country talent across Canada," said Michelle Mearns, Senior Vice President of Programming and Operations at SiriusXM Canada. "It's been rewarding to watch them grow throughout the competition, and we're incredibly proud to continue amplifying Canadian talent. Congratulations to the Blue Ridge Band on a well-deserved win."

"The CCMA's partnership with SiriusXM Canada has helped educate, elevate and celebrate emerging artists across the Canadian country music community," said Amy Jeninga, President, CCMA. "Seeing these artists bring their passion and creativity to every stage of the competition, and knowing the program is creating meaningful opportunities for the next steps in their careers, is what makes Top of the Country so special. We're incredibly proud to celebrate another great year."

SiriusXM Top of the Country, in partnership with the CCMA, is part of SiriusXM's ongoing tradition of promoting and elevating the best emerging Canadian music talent. SiriusXM continues to offer a leading platform for Canadian artists through its significant financial contributions and North American-wide reach.

releases.title: Semperis Secures IMDA Accreditation to Strengthen Identity Resilience in the AI Era
releases.body:
As Semperis achieves triple-digit APAC growth, it is expanding its senior leadership team to accelerate regional momentum.

HOBOKEN, N.J. and SINGAPORE, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Semperis, the identity-driven cyber resilience and crisis response company, today announced accreditation from Singapore's Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), which recognizes Semperis for its innovative Identity Resilience Platform. This is a strong validation of the company's product capabilities, operational maturity and readiness to serve enterprise and public sector customers. The recognition comes on the back of the company's triple-digit revenue growth across the Asia-Pacific region, including Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, and Japan.

The company also announced several new hires amid this growth phase, with Shekhar Thakurdesai joining Semperis as AVP of India and SAARC business and Ridwan Basri as Channel Director in Asia. Nick Lowther and Daniel O'Mara have joined Semperis in key sales roles to bolster growth across the region.

Organizations across Asia-Pacific look to bolster cyber resilience amid the rapid adoption of AI agents, with threat actors increasingly targeting identity systems such as Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta and Ping Identity. According to Semperis' newest study, State of Identity Security in the AI Era, only 21% of the organizations in Singapore and Australia are confident they could fully regain control of their identity infrastructure if an AI agent exposes admin credentials to an attacker. At the same time, 93% already use or plan to use AI agents for sensitive security tasks such as password resets and VPN access.

"Asia-Pacific is one of the fastest-growing global digital economies, and organizations in the region are embracing AI agents and integrating them into their identity systems. However, Semperis' study highlights that to date, many haven't adopted safeguards to manage them," said Gerry Sillars, Vice President, Asia-Pacific and Japan, Semperis.

"Unfortunately, cybercriminals are moving just as quickly. Businesses are recognizing that cyber resilience starts with protecting the identity systems that every user, application and AI agent depends upon. Our exceptional growth across APJ reflects this shift in mindset. We're investing aggressively in local talent, expanding our regional presence and strengthening our partner ecosystem so we can help more organizations prevent, respond to, and recover from identity-based cyberattacks with confidence."

"Identity systems are a key target for cyberattacks, with AI adding new complexity to an evolving threat landscape," said Edwin Low, Director, Enterprise & Ecosystem Development, IMDA. "With IMDA's accreditation, we look forward to Semperis bringing its resilience and recovery capabilities to help organizations better safeguard their critical identity infrastructure."

With continued investment in regional talent, strategic partnerships and innovation, Semperis is well positioned to support organizations across Asia-Pacific and Japan as they strengthen identity resilience against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats in the AI era.

About Semperis

Semperis is the identity-driven cyber resilience and crisis management company trusted by the world's largest enterprises and government agencies to protect critical identity systems. Purpose-built for multi-cloud and hybrid identity environments — including Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta, and Ping Identity — Semperis helps organizations prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from identity-based cyberattacks.

Modern cyberattacks are won or lost at the identity layer, where failures now escalate into full-scale business crises. Semperis' AI-powered platform unifies identity lifecycle defense and crisis management — hardening identity infrastructure, detecting and containing active threats, enabling rapid, trusted recovery, and supporting secure, out-of-band coordination when core systems are disrupted — all reinforced by a world-class identity forensics and incident response team.

As part of its mission to help organizations achieve true cyber resilience, Semperis supports the broader cyber community through the award-winning Hybrid Identity Protection (HIP) Conference and Podcast and free identity security tools including Purple Knight and Forest Druid. More than 1,200 organizations — including over 25% of the 100 largest U.S. companies — rely on Semperis. The company is privately held, headquartered in Hoboken, New Jersey, and serves customers in more than 40 countries.

releases.title: New UC Irvine Study Links Podium's Global Career Accelerator to Higher Undergraduate Retention
releases.body:
Researchers see a 10-percentage-point increase in retention rates for Arizona State University students participating in Podium's work-integrated program.

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Podium Education released findings from independent research showing that undergraduate college students who participate in its flagship experience, the Global Career Accelerator (The Accelerator), have significantly higher college retention rates than peers who did not participate.

The Accelerator is a for-credit academic initiative that offers students work-integrated learning within their college curriculum. The Accelerator aims to boost career readiness for students by rotating participants through immersive projects and live experiences co-designed with Podium's 50-plus industry partners, including Crocs, L'Oreal, and Wells Fargo.

Through an innovative student success research partnership between Podium, the University of California, Irvine, and Arizona State University (ASU), UC Irvine researchers tracked over 350,000 ASU students across three academic cohorts from 2021-2022 through 2023-2024. The findings show that students who completed Podium's Accelerator remained enrolled in subsequent semesters at rates 6 to 10 percentage points higher than non-participants year over year.

In a matched-sample analysis, which paired nearly 3,000 participants with demographically and academically similar peers, participants were retained at 90%, compared to 86% for matched non-participants. Additionally, researchers found statistically significant improvements in retention after controlling for factors like first-generation status, Pell eligibility, online versus on-campus enrollment, race, and GPA.

"The consistency of this finding across three years and two distinct analytic methods points to the exciting results of this experiential programming," said Richard Arum, Professor of Sociology and Education at UC Irvine.

"The results of this study are promising," said Anne Jones, ASU vice provost for undergraduate education. "The ASU Global Career Accelerator helps students see how their academic experience connects to the world of work. That kind of relevance can be powerful in keeping students engaged and on track to complete their degree."

Podium's innovative platform is available to more than 1.7 million students, including over 550,000 who are Pell-eligible, across more than 100 university partners. The program is backed by leading industry partners ranging from large technology organizations like Intel to consumer brands like Procter & Gamble, to non-profits like charity: water.

Increasing demand for work-integrated college experiences is driving Podium's growth. Recent data from the Business-Higher Education Forum reports that the gap between internship interest among college students and availability is a growing concern. While 8.2M learners in the U.S. reported wanting one annually, only an estimated 2.5M high-quality internships are available.

The Accelerator was designed to close that gap by embedding real, credit-bearing work experience directly into the degree, with no prerequisites, so access doesn't depend on a student's major, financial means, or ability to relocate.

"This research is the first large-scale, independent confirmation of what we've seen anecdotally since day one — that when students get real, embedded work experience, they see a brighter future for themselves and stay in college," said Chris Parrish, Co-Founder and President at Podium Education. "We're committed to expanding our partnerships with institutions to offer more industry-integrated academic experiences to both drive stronger retention for schools and better return on investment for students."

About the Research

UC Irvine researchers Richard Arum and Jeffrey M. DeVries independently conducted and reported the study, in collaboration with Jennifer Malerich of Arizona State University, and the UC Irvine Institutional Review Board reviewed and approved it. The UC Irvine research team maintained full analytic independence throughout.

A full accounting of methodology, including cohort-specific and propensity-score-matched models, is available to download: HERE.

About Podium Education

Podium Education is the leading experiential education company partnering with universities and industry to embed scalable, real-world, high-impact practices directly into the undergraduate degree for credit. Podium works with more than 100 universities, including ASU, Penn State, and Rice, and 50+ leading industry partners like L'Oréal, OpenAI, and Wells Fargo. Podium's experiences deliver fully digital, for-credit learning that strengthens student retention, confidence, and career readiness. Students from all backgrounds gain early career experience, explore potential pathways, and build the skills and competencies employers expect through hands-on, work-based learning experiences aligned with workforce needs. For more information, visit Podium Education at www.podiumeducation.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

releases.title: JobGet Announces Free Access to RippleMatch Platform for Universities
releases.body:
Career services teams nationwide can now use RippleMatch's career guidance, opportunities marketplace and job search analytics tools at no cost.

BOSTON, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RippleMatch, a leading early career recruiting platform, today announced that its university product is now available free of charge to all higher education institutions. The news follows RippleMatch's acquisition by JobGet, the fastest-growing job platform connecting workers to employers at scale, and provides universities a valuable tool to support students through an entry-level hiring market that's challenged by AI disruption.

"Career services teams are being asked to do more for students at exactly the moment when the job market has become most unpredictable for them," said Audrey Patenaude, General Manager of RippleMatch. "AI is reshaping the entry-level roles where graduates have traditionally gotten their start. The job search process has become more opaque, and universities are doing this with fewer resources than ever. With our acquisition by JobGet, we've gained access to a dramatically larger job inventory and employer network, and that growth allows us to expand access to universities at no cost, and we believe that's what this moment calls for."

The announcement comes as recent graduates face one of the toughest labor markets in years. Unemployment among recent college graduates has climbed to 5.7% — a three-year high — while underemployment sits at 41.5%. Junior-level job postings fell 7% last year even as senior-level openings grew, and AI is reshaping the career ladder.

Universities are absorbing this pressure directly. Higher education institutions shed over 9,000 positions in 2025, and budget constraints have left many career services teams trying to support more students with fewer resources.

RippleMatch's Free Platform for University Career Centers

Through RippleMatch, students gain access to a personalized job feed matched to their skills and goals, verified skill badges recognized by employers, and an application process that surfaces them directly to recruiters, resulting in interview rates 20x higher than traditional job boards.

For career services teams, the platform provides real-time analytics on student engagement, verified skills, application volume, interview conversion rates, and placement outcomes, as well as tools to communicate directly with student cohorts and track activity across communities.

The acquisition of RippleMatch by JobGet further expands the diversity and volume of job opportunities available to students on the platform, adding JobGet's broad employer network to RippleMatch's existing early career recruiting relationships.

RippleMatch's university platform is available immediately to all higher education institutions at no cost. Universities can get started at ripplematch.com/universities.

About RippleMatch

RippleMatch is an early career recruiting platform that connects students with employers through intelligent matching, verified skills assessments, and personalized job feeds. Trusted by universities and employers across the country, RippleMatch is now part of the JobGet family of products.

About JobGet

JobGet is the leading hourly hiring platform helping employers and workers connect faster across the U.S. With a reach of over 100 million job seekers, JobGet combines large-scale candidate supply, AI-powered screening, interview scheduling, and hiring manager workflows to help employers hire more efficiently. JobGet partners with leading brands including Whole Foods, Avis, Hobby Lobby, Sprouts, Taco Bell, Uber, Aldi, UPS, and more to fill everyday roles across food service, retail, customer service, hospitality, manufacturing, construction, healthcare, warehouse, transportation, and other high-volume hiring categories. Through its acquisition of RippleMatch, JobGet is expanding its reach into early career and university recruiting.

Notes to Editors

On graduate unemployment and underemployment: 5.7% unemployment rate among recent college graduates (Q4 2025, three-year high) and 41.5% underemployment rate. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Labor Market for Recent College Graduates, newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market; Economic Policy Institute, Class of 2026, epi.org.

On junior-level job postings: 7% year-over-year decline in junior-level postings. Source: CNBC, New College Graduates Face a Tough Job Market (April 2026), cnbc.com.

On higher education job losses: Over 9,000 positions eliminated across higher education institutions in 2025. Source: Inside Higher Ed, December Cuts Close Out Brutal Year for Sector (January 2026), insidehighered.com.

The story opens with the brutal murders of a bus driver and a high school basketball star, beaten to death on a bus, an act that ignites community outrage and pulls authorities into a hunt for the culprits caught on video. As the investigation widens, it collides with a string of missing Black women cases and a killer who has operated undetected for years. The series stars Christopher Livingston, Elijah Collins, Tonia Jackson, Lawrence Robinson, Rico Ball, and Cuyle Carvin, alongside Moore.

"Clark brought a steadiness to this set that you notice immediately. He shows up prepared, he listens, and he makes the scene better for everyone standing in it. I'm glad audiences are finally going to see this work."

Cuyle Carvin, actor, Route 187 (Paramount+)

Moore plays Lt. Jeff Gibson, a police lieutenant working the South Winslow case as it grows from a single bus stop into something far larger than the community first understood.

"South Winslow is fiction, but the pattern underneath it is not. Cases like these get worked hard when the cameras are on and quietly shelved when they aren't. Mark Swinton wrote a show that refuses to let that go, and playing a man carrying the weight of that investigation was the kind of work you don't get offered every year."

Clark Moore, actor (Lt. Jeff Gibson, Route 187)

Route 187 arrives with a festival run already behind it. The series was an official selection of the 7th Annual LightReel Film Festival in Washington, D.C., where it opened the festival in June 2026, and was officially accepted into the RSF Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival, one of the summer's most closely watched showcases for Black storytelling.

The role also lands squarely in the territory Moore is best known for. Much of his career has been built on blue-collar authority in detective, lawman, and military parts, from SEAL Team and NCIS to S.W.A.T. and Yellowstone, and Lt. Gibson extends that line into one of the most talked-about independent productions of the year.

Route 187 closes out a three-production year for the SAG-AFTRA actor. Moore appeared as Detective Moreno in Lifetime's Murder in Music City, which premiered in February, and as guest star Caleb Easton in Hulu's Furious, the Elizabeth Meriwether crime thriller that ran through August.

Moore's career highlights include a recurring role as D.A. Stanny Sanders in the ABC limited series Women of the Movement, executive produced by Will Smith and Jay-Z, and a leading performance in Aaron Mahnke's Amazon Prime series Lore. Born and raised on his father's ranch in Laredo, Texas, Moore studied film at The University of Texas at Austin before relocating to Los Angeles. His special skills include Krav Maga, weapons handling, and horseback riding, capabilities that inform his approach to tactical, military, and western roles.

All four episodes of Route 187 are now streaming exclusively on Paramount+. The official trailer is available on YouTube, and the series can be followed on Instagram at @route.187.

For more information about Clark Moore and his complete filmography, visit officialclarkmoore.com/credits or his profile on IMDb.

releases.body:
Appalachian Soul Power and Companion Novel Mountain Alchemy Arrive September 22, 2026

Campaign Launch Celebrates the Artists, Music and Cultural Traditions That Have Helped Shape Appalachia's Place in Music History

OSAGE, W.Va., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Award-winning West Virginia singer, songwriter, storyteller, and author Aristotle Jones, known as "The Appalachian Soul Man," will mark the September 22 release of his new album, Appalachian Soul Power, and companion book, Mountain Alchemy, by launching a campaign to establish July as Appalachian Soul Month, celebrating the artists, music, and cultural traditions that have helped give Appalachia its soul.

The Appalachian Soul Month campaign seeks to establish an annual celebration spotlighting the many sounds of Appalachia and their place in the larger story of American music. The initiative will honor the artists who came before, celebrate those carrying those traditions forward, and encourage new audiences to discover and share Appalachian music and culture.

"For me, Appalachian Soul has never been about creating another genre or putting a new label on the music," Jones said. "It is about recognizing what has always been here. Soul, Gospel, Blues, Folk, Country, R&B, and Rock & Roll have crossed paths in Appalachia for generations. Artists from these mountains, towns, churches, clubs, front porches, and communities have helped shape American music, even when Appalachia hasn't always been included in that story."

As part of the campaign launch, Jones is asking people to share an Appalachian artist who has moved them, inspired them, or deserves to be discovered. Participants can honor an artist from the past, introduce someone making music today, or share a favorite song, performance, photograph, memory, or story using #AppalachianSoulMonth.

The campaign coincides with the release of Appalachian Soul Power, a 10-track album drawing from the region's vast musical traditions. Percussive guitar, piano, horns, layered vocals, and a tightly connected rhythm section move throughout the record, shifting between intimate moments and high-energy arrangements.

The album serves as a musical companion to Mountain Alchemy, a fictional work Jones drew from family and community stories that peppered his childhood. Together, the projects explore Black Appalachian culture, resilience, community, and cultural memory, with the songs providing a musical landscape for themes at the heart of the book.

"I can't think of a better way to release this record than by using the moment to celebrate something much bigger than me," Jones said. "I want us to remember the artists who came before us, celebrate the people making music here today, and introduce each other to voices we may not know yet."

Jones was named a 2026 United States Artists Fellow, selected for the 2026–2027 Central Appalachia Living Traditions Emerging Artists Cohort, funded by Mid Atlantic Arts, and featured on the Summer 2026 cover of Morgantown Magazine. In July, Jones and his band won the International Blues Competition Affiliate Challenge and will represent West Virginia at the 43rd International Blues Challenge, January 19–23, 2027, in Memphis.

Appalachian Soul Power and Mountain Alchemy are available beginning September 22, 2026, via Jonesin' Records.

PHILADELPHIA, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This Kids Music Day, Keep Music Alive is inviting people across the country to grab anything they can find and start drumming. The nonprofit's "Drum on Anything" Challenge is a fun, social media-driven campaign encouraging musicians, students, families and music fans of all ages to post a short video of themselves "drumming ON anything WITH anything" while helping raise awareness and support for music education. Inspired by the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge, participants are asked to use #DrumOnAnything, tag three friends to take part, and either share their own video or make a donation to a music education nonprofit of their choice. Music education organizations nationwide are also encouraged to use the challenge to engage supporters and raise funds for their own programs.

More than 1,200 locations across all 50 U.S. states, Canada and 15 additional countries are expected to participate in the 11th Annual Kids Music Day, with special events and promotions designed to celebrate and support children making music. Kids Music Day activities will take place from Friday, September 18 through Sunday, October 11. Families in the United States and Canada can find participating events in their area by entering their ZIP or postal code on the locator page at KidsMusicDay.org. International participants can find events by scrolling below the map and selecting their country's flag.

Kids Music Day events will feature a wide variety of hands-on and family-friendly activities, including musical instrument petting zoos, student performances, free trial music lessons, kids open mics, ukulele, drum and guitar circles, instrument donation drives, special Kids Music Day promotions and more. These activities are designed to give children more opportunities to experience the joy of making music while highlighting the importance of music education in communities around the world.

Kids Music Day is supported by a number of popular family-friendly brands including CASIO, Kala Brand Music, Independence Blue Cross, Les Paul Foundation, Music Nomad Equipment Care, Panyard, Remo Percussion and Taylor Guitars.  Keep Music Alive is honored to welcome these valued partners, helping to support more kids to start their own musical journey.

13-year-old violinist Sabrina Patel returns as Kids Music Day Spokesperson this year as she continues her quest to perform the National Anthem at major events in all 50 states.  Currently young Sabrina is 90% complete on her quest having performed in 45 States at major sporting and other events. Major league sports teams welcoming Sabrina so far include MLB's Texas Rangers (ALCS Playoffs), Colorado Rockies, Cleveland Guardians, Detroit Tigers, Boston Red Sox, NBA's Dallas Mavericks, Detroit Pistons, Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks and WNBA's Connecticut Sun

Over a dozen celebrity artists are also showing their support for Music Education by lending their name as Kids Music Day Ambassadors including:   Julie Andrews, Jack Black, Ann & Nancy Wilson of Heart, Pat Benatar & Neil Giraldo, Michael Feinstein, Kenny Loggins, Richie Sambora, Sarah McLachlan, Vanessa Williams, Victor Wooten, Todd Rundgren, Neil Nayyar, Philip Lawrence, Bernie Williams, Damien Escobar and Mandy Harvey.

releases.title: This Is Wild, WWF-Canada's hit podcast, returns with a look at the fragile future of southern resident killer whales and other species at risk
releases.body:
Hosted by award-winning filmmaker and environmental journalist Aliya Jasmine, the second season premieres Sept. 17.

TORONTO, Sept. 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- WWF-Canada's top science podcast This Is Wild returns for a second season, opening with a powerful episode about the urgent threats facing southern resident killer whales, one of Canada's most iconic species.

The season premiere revisits the story of Tahlequah, the southern resident killer whale who captured international attention in 2018 when she carried her dead calf through the Salish Sea for 17 days (a behaviour we saw again in 2025 after the tragic loss of another calf). Her journey became a symbol of this orca population in crisis and raised awareness about the immense pressures they're facing.

Declining chinook salmon populations, underwater noise from vessels and industry, and pollution are just some of the growing threats to southern resident killer whales. Today, only around 75 remain, with their future hanging in a precarious balance.

Episode 1 features WWF-Canada conservation experts Hussein Alidina and Emily Giles alongside Ecojustice lawyer Margot Venton with narration by award-winning environmental journalist Aliya Jasmine. Together they explore the science behind these threats, the conservation efforts aimed at supporting their recovery, and the legal and policy hurdles that are slowing down action and ramping up risks.

"We know better. We have to do better. It's our responsibility to do better. And we need to do that better because in many ways, we're part of the same circle of life that the whales are," said Hussein Alidina, WWF-Canada's lead specialist for marine conservation.

"Southern resident killer whales are one of the most beloved species in Canada, and one of the most endangered. At a time when Canada is accelerating approvals for major projects like ports and pipelines that risk their survival, the first episode of This is Wild asks the important question of what we're willing to lose for economic gain," said Megan Leslie, WWF-Canada's president and CEO. "Each episode takes listeners to different parts of the country, exploring the species that are shaping our world and what it will take to protect theirs."

Co-produced with Antica Productions, the second season of This Is Wild continues WWF-Canada's commitment to making conservation stories engaging and accessible.

Aliya Jasmine previously appeared on an episode of WWF-Canada's Good Nature podcast, talking about her new short documentary Bird Names.

Listen to season two of This is Wild wherever you get your podcasts. New episodes about a different incredible species that call Canada home, and the people working to protect them, will be released every two weeks. 

  • YouTube
  • Apple Podcasts
  • Spotify
  • Podlink for more streaming platforms
  • https://wwf.ca/this-is-wild/ 

For a copy of the episode transcript or to arrange an interview with our experts, email media@wwfcanada.org 

About the host, Aliya Jasmine

Aliya Jasmine ("AJ") is an award-winning filmmaker, environmental journalist and climate storyteller whose work sits at the intersection of climate solutions, wildlife and belonging. Her stories have appeared on CBC, NBC News, MTV News, Discovery Channel, and Smithsonian Channel, and she has built a large trusted online community through years of broadcast journalism, digital-first reporting and environmental storytelling.

AJ is co-Founder of Earth Tones, a purpose-driven media company amplifying underrepresented voices in environmental storytelling. AJ directed, wrote and produced Bird Names, a CBC Short Docs documentary with an impact campaign spanning private, public, academic, and conservation-facing screenings. She is also directing Lion Bridge, an independent feature documentary from Executive Producer Leonardo DiCaprio, about LA's mountain lion population, currently in production. 

She is a recipient of the King Charles III Coronation Medal for journalism in service of Canada, a Fellow of the Royal Canadian Geographical Society, and serves on the board of Nature United.

About WWF-Canada

WWF-Canada is committed to equitable and effective conservation actions that restore nature, reverse wildlife loss and fight climate change. We draw on scientific analysis and Indigenous guidance to ensure all our efforts connect to a single goal: a future where wildlife, nature and people thrive. For more information, visit wwf.ca.

releases.title: Kapwork Launches Free $42.45 Billion BEAD Tracker and Invoice Certification for Contractors
releases.body:
Free data from 80 plus federal agencies shows where the work is; free invoice certification helps the businesses doing it get funded faster. Data center fit-out and federal contract award trackers come next.

LOS ALTOS, Calif., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kapwork today introduced Kapwork Growth Suite, a free platform that helps small businesses find relevant infrastructure work and access capital to grow. The suite brings together data from 80 plus federal departments and agencies. It sits alongside Kapwork's free invoice certification, which verifies money a business is owed so it can be matched with credit providers and funded faster. Any US business can join today at kapwork.com/grow.

The AI buildout needs more than GPUs, it needs the businesses that build America's network: fiber connections, electrical systems, cooling and the contractors who install them. Alongside private investment in AI infrastructure, federal funding is expanding broadband networks. For telecom providers, fiber crews and specialist contractors, the challenge is knowing which projects to pursue, and how to pay for growth.

See where infrastructure money is going

The suite is built around the questions a business owner needs answered. It launches with the BEAD tracker; two more trackers follow:

  • BEAD Awards — Who received funding to build broadband? The Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment program is a $42.45 billion federal initiative to expand high-speed internet access. Kapwork's live tracker helps businesses research award recipients. A fiber contractor can use that information to decide which operators to approach before committing a crew.
  • Data Center Fit-Outs — Which projects are moving beyond an announcement? Coming next: a tracker that organizes fit-outs by location, operator, and reported stage: proposed, under construction, operating, cancelled, or suspended.
  • Federal Contract Awards — Which prime contractors are winning work? Also coming: a tool that will organize more than 50 million federal award actions to help small businesses find federal work.

Kapwork's BEAD tracker covers $11.46 billion in announced awards as of September 16 and adds new awards as states announce them.

"The businesses that build America's network have a cashflow problem. Unless we solve it, we can't build at the speed the country needs to stay competitive," said Mauricio Vergara, co-founder and CEO at Kapwork. "Our goal is to help small businesses grow by providing free tools to understand where the market is going, see who's getting the work, and access working capital."

Turn unpaid invoices into growth capital

A new job can create costs before it generates cash. Contractors need to pay crews and buy materials while invoices for earlier work remain unpaid. Kapwork certifies those receivables and helps the business get funded faster, at better rates.

Once a business sends out an invoice, by email or through a vendor portal, Kapwork proves the invoice exists with the customer who owes it. Kapwork's AI agents verify invoice amounts, approval status and payment terms at the debtor's source turning self pledged paper into certified receivables that a credit provider can evaluate.

""Fabricating invoices is the fraud risk everyone in this space is watching for right now. Pulling from the debtor's own portal cuts that off at the source. Kapwork's certified data gives us the confidence to deploy capital faster and price deals without carrying that doubt in the rate." said Saul Gewer, Chief Strategy Officer, TowerCap. 

Kapwork then matches the business with participating capital providers, including banks, factoring companies and private credit funds that prefer issuing credit against certified invoices. The business reviews available offers and decides whether to accept. The Growth Suite, Invoice Certification and credit matching are free for businesses.

"In Brazil we processed more than US$1 trillion in receivables. As a result, credit supply to SME's more than tripled, with an average cost of credit 75 percent lower than the cost observed before we began operations. Once an invoice is verified, it can't be pledged twice, so funders trust what they're financing, and credit reaches companies that never had it before," said Marcelo Maziero, co-founder of CERC, the Brazilian financial market infrastructure and an investor in Kapwork.

Businesses can join and explore Kapwork Growth Suite today at kapwork.com/grow.

About Kapwork

Kapwork is an AI-native platform helping small businesses find growth opportunities, certify receivables and get matched with capital providers. The company has certified over half a billion dollars in receivables, most of that coming from telecom and datacenter providers. Backed by SaaSholic, Kapwork is also a member of NVIDIA's Inception, a program supporting innovative AI startups.

Kapwork was founded by Pete Thomas and Mauricio Vergara. Thomas helped build C2FO, the working capital platform with half a trillion dollars in receivables flowing through it. Vergara, CEO, saw how "third party" developers at Google struggled with cashflow. Learn more at kapwork.com.

releases.body:
First installment of a two-part educational series provides hospitality owners, buyers, and developers with an in-depth framework for navigating state ABC regulations, municipal population caps, Class C license privileges, and asset valuation.

ALLENHURST, N.J. , Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Commercial real estate brokerage firm Bielat Santore & Company has officially released Episode 6 (Part I) of its Owner's Edge Podcast Series, titled "New Jersey Liquor Licenses: Regulatory Structure and Market Value". The episode delivers a comprehensive analysis of how New Jersey's unique statutory framework governs retail alcoholic beverage licenses and creates private-market economic value.

Although New Jersey law classifies a liquor license as a regulated government privilege rather than ordinary property, eligible licenses command substantial market value across the state.

Key Topics Covered in Episode 6 (Part I):

  • The Statutory Framework & Municipal Population Caps: Established under Title 33 following the repeal of Prohibition in 1933, New Jersey's Alcoholic Beverage Control system ties retail licenses to local population limits.
  • Essential Class C Retail Licenses: An overview of key retail license types, including Type 33 (Plenary Retail Consumption for standard bar/restaurant service), Type 32 (Plenary Retail Consumption with Broad Package Privilege, no longer newly issued), Type 44 (Plenary Retail Distribution for package stores).
  • Person-to-Person & Place-to-Place Transfers: Clarifying the legal separation between purchasing a business asset and transferring a license.
  • The Six-Step Valuation Framework: Addressing why there is no standardized statewide price database and presenting a six-step valuation methodology.
  • Impact on Operating Economics & Real Estate: How beverage service enhances average guest checks, gross profit margins, and late-day sales.

Coming Next Month - Part II: "Recent Changes in New Jersey Liquor License Law"

About Bielat Santore & Company

Bielat Santore & Company is a New Jersey commercial real estate brokerage specializing in restaurants, hospitality properties, business enterprises, and liquor licenses. For more than 45 years, the firm has advised owners, operators, developers, buyers, and lenders on the sale, acquisition, financing, and valuation of hospitality assets throughout New Jersey.

releases.title: HIGH LINE AND CHANEL CULTURE FUND CO-COMMISSION ALISON NGUYEN FOR FIFTH HIGH LINE ORIGINALS FILM
releases.body:
Nguyenʼs Prior Occupants Unearths the Industrial and Cultural Histories of the High Line and Westbethʼs Past

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The High Line and CHANEL Culture Fund today announced that Prior Occupants, a new film by Alison Nguyen commissioned by the High Line as the fifth High Line Originals film, and the second High Line Originals co-commissioned with CHANEL Culture Fund, is now on view. The High Line Channel, located in the High Lineʼs covered passage at 14th Street, screens Prior Occupants daily from 10am to 10pm on a loop, through November 16, 2026.

Prior Occupants explores the obscure nuclear history of Westbeth Artist Housing's building—the former headquarters for Bell Laboratories, a research facility tied to the development of communication technologies and, later, the atomic bomb. Inspired by a severed fragment of the original High Line freight rail left embedded in Westbeth's facade, and the High Line's own history of transformation, Nguyen reflects on the historical narratives that persist—and those quietly erased—within sites of adaptive reuse.

"Through extensive research, ongoing conversations and relationship-building with Westbeth residents past and present, and highly crafted visual choreography, Alison Nguyenʼs Prior Occupants sheds vital light on the industrial and scientific legacies built into our surroundings,ˮ said Taylor Zakarin, associate curator of High Line Art. "Iʼm thrilled the High Line and CHANEL Culture Fund could collaborate with Alison to bring this compelling work to life, and to present it outdoors by the very spaces she investigates.ˮ

"Great artists enter into a dialogue with history, revealing new ways to understand the present. Through her new commission, Alison Nguyen excavates the layered histories surrounding the High Line, uncovering a legacy of innovation and human experimentation—and raising questions about technology, memory, and our shared future that feel more urgent than ever,ˮ said Yana Peel, President of Arts, Culture & Heritage, CHANEL. "CHANEL Culture Fund is proud to continue our partnership with the High Line in support of artists whose original ideas celebrate the singular power of human imagination. By bringing ambitious moving-image commissions into public space, we hope to spark curiosity and reflection for the millions of people who encounter them amid the extraordinary urban landscape of the High Line.ˮ

"I'm grateful for the support of the High Line and CHANEL Culture Fund which gave me the resources to create a work that examines the invisible structures of power embedded in a site,ˮ said artist Alison Nguyen. "As the filmmaking process unfolded, relationships I formed with past and present Westbeth artists along with architectural archives opened up directions for the film which I had not anticipated, and was thrilled by.ˮ

Long before Westbeth's conversion into a historic public housing community for artists in 1970, the site was occupied by Western Electric and later Bell Labs—a crucible of innovation where critical cinema, telecommunications, and military technologies were researched, including components later used in the development of the atomic bomb.

Both Bell Labs and Westbeth Artist Housing are places created to pursue large, even utopian ideals. In the case of the former, technological innovation; in the case of the latter government-funded artist housing. Prior Occupants explores what remains of the pursuit of these ideals, how the surrounding architecture has shaped its inhabitants, and the contradictions of present-day Westbeth in the context of the High Lineʼs surrounding neighborhood.

Prior Occupants is an assemblage of audiovisual material including sculpturally re-filmed archival documents, choreographed performance sequences, and layered fragments of audio interviews with the very residents and architects who have shaped Westbeth and the High Line. Through this collage of voices and textures, the artist explores individual and collective relationships to place, technological acceleration, and mortality, and foregrounds the ways in which the structures of the past quietly haunt our future-present. Questioning the relationship between ruination and cultural production, the work asks: What does it mean to stage the decay of an industrial past within public environments and within public artist housing? What role does nature play in these acts of preservation?

Nguyenʼs film weaves together infrastructure, memory, and technology to consider how the legacy of the nuclear age continues to shape our collective experiences, and positions the High Line not just as a space for leisure, but as an active conduit of our historical consciousness.

Alison Nguyen is a visual artist working across video, installation, performance and painting. Using approaches of speculative fiction, documentary research and embodied performance, Nguyen creates works that reconsider how narratives operate within the individual, the institution, the archive, and within the politics of cultural memory.

In addition to Prior Occupants, CHANEL Culture Fund and High Line Art presented a special two-day screening, on September 6 and 7, of two prior commissions from The Window, CHANEL Culture Fund's site-specific public art program in Central London for cutting-edge works exploring the breadth of todayʼs digital technologies. The screening featured Our Bodies (2024-2025), by Cecilia Bengolea, and Inhale/Exhale (2021) by Noémie Goudal.

Another work from The Window, The Last Post (2010) by Shahzia Sikander, will be included in a forthcoming High Line Channel exhibition alongside The Hedge ofi Halomancy (2025) by the artist duo Hylozoic/Desires (artist Himali Singh Soin and musician David Soin Tappeser) in November 2026. Following its exhibition on the High Line, Prior Occupants will screen at The Window in London.

Part of High Line Channel, High Line Originals is High Line Artʼs commissioning program for artists working in time-based media. This initiative invites emerging or underrecognized US-based artists, nominated by a trusted group of contemporary curators, to submit a proposal for a new video work that considers the context of the park in a meaningful way and will resonate with our diverse audience.

High Line Originals launched in 2019 with Tourmalineʼs Salacia, which is now held in the Museum of Modern Artʼs permanent collection. Other past commissions include Onyeka Igweʼs The Miracle on George Green (2021) and Alicia Mersyʼs NYC Wisdom (2024). In 2025, High Line Art partnered with CHANEL Culture Fund, and together co-commissioned Frank WANG Yefengʼs Groundless Flower – ཨ (2025).

ABOUT THE ARTIST

Alison Nguyen (b. 1986, Wilmington, Delaware) lives and works in New York, New York. Solo screenings and exhibitions of Nguyen's work have been presented at Storefront for Art and Architecture, New York, New York (2026); Art Basel Hong Kong Encounters, Hong Kong (2025); Murmurs, Los Angeles (2024); Museum of Modern Art, New York, New York (2023); MIT List Center for Visual Arts, Cambridge, Massachusetts (2023); and e-flux, Brooklyn, New York (2023). Nguyen has participated in group exhibitions and screenings at the Busan Biennial, Busan, South Korea (2026); Kunsthalle Mechelen, Mechelen, Belgium (2026); Vienna Secession, Vienna, Austria (2024); EMAP x Frieze Seoul Film, Seoul, South Korea (2024); National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Korea, Seoul, South Korea (2023); The Everson Museum, Syracuse, New York (2022); The Dowse Art Museum, Lower Hutt, New Zealand (2021); The International Studio & Curatorial Program, Brooklyn, New York (2019 & 2020); KAJE, Brooklyn, New York (2020); and Microscope Gallery, Brooklyn, New York (2017).

She has participated in film festivals around the world, including Oberhausen International Film Festival, International Shorts Online (2021); CPH:DOX, Copenhagen, Denmark (2021); Edinburgh International Film Festival, Edinburgh, United Kingdom (2021); Ann Arbor Film Festival, Ann Arbor, Michigan (2020); Open City Documentary Festival, London, United Kingdom (2019); Channels Festival International Biennial of Video Art, Melbourne, Australia (2019), and True/False Film Festival, Columbia, Missouri (2018); among others.

Nguyen has received residencies and fellowships from Pioneer Works, New York Foundation for the Arts Artist Fellowship in Film/Video, International Studio & Curatorial Program, The Institute of Electronic Arts, BRIC, and Squeaky Wheel Film and Media Art Center. She was a 2023-2024 Studio Fellow at the Whitney Independent Study Program.

ABOUT HIGH LINE ART

Founded in 2009, High Line Art commissions and produces a wide array of artworks on the High Line, including site-specific commissions, exhibitions, performances, video programs, and a series of billboard interventions. Led by Cecilia Alemani, the Donald R. Mullen, Jr. Director & Chief Curator of High Line Art, and presented by the High Line, the art program invites artists to think of creative ways to engage with the unique architecture, history, and design of the park, and to foster a productive dialogue with the surrounding neighborhood and urban landscape.

For more information on High Line Art, please visit thehighline.org/art.

ABOUT THE HIGH LINE

The High Line is a public park on the West Side of Manhattan operated, maintained, and funded by the nonprofit conservancy Friends of the High Line. Through our work with communities on and off the High Line, Friends of the High Line is devoted to reimagining public spaces to create connected, healthy neighborhoods and cities.

Built on a historic, elevated rail line, the High Line was always intended to be more than a park. You can walk through the gardens, view art, experience a performance, enjoy food or beverage, or connect with friends and neighbors—all while enjoying a unique perspective of New York City.

Nearly 100% of our annual budget comes through donations. The High Line is owned by the City of New York, and we operate the park under a license agreement with NYC Parks.

For more information, visit thehighline.org and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, and Tiktok.

ABOUT CHANEL CULTURE FUND

CHANEL Culture Fund fosters a vibrant network of creators and innovators to advance the ideas that shape culture worldwide. Core programs include CHANELʼs Art Partners, nearly fifty international institutions whose leaders are supported in the development of ground-breaking, long-term initiatives that bring innovation to the cultural landscape. The CHANEL Next Prize celebrates artists and accelerates their future successes through access to resources and mentorship. And the podcast CHANEL Connects amplifies the voices of thought-leaders across disciplines, generations, and geographies—tackling the defining issues of our time.

From driving artistic innovation with technology at CalArts in Southern California to catalyzing creative freedom at scale at Hamburger Bahnhof in Berlin, from championing game-changing artists at the Venice Biennale to celebrating the brightest directors at the British Film Institute and opening Chinaʼs first public contemporary art library at the Power Station of Art in Shanghai, CHANEL Culture Fund extends a century of commitment to the arts and champions creative audacity for a better future.

SUPPORT

Lead support for High Line Art comes from Amanda and Don Mullen. Major support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Inc. of Houston, Charina Endowment Fund, and Shelley Fox Aarons and Philip E. Aarons.

Major support of High Line Artʼs digital infrastructure is provided by Bloomberg Philanthropies.

Program support for High Line Art is provided by Sarah Arison, Suzanne Deal Booth, Charlotte Ford, Molly Gochman, and Joyce F. Menschel.

Additional support is provided by Agnes Gund and Shane Akeroyd.

High Line Art is supported, in part, with public funds from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, and the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the New York City Council, under the leadership of Speaker Julie Menin.

Major support for High Line Originals is provided by CHANEL Culture Fund.
