releases.body:
CHICAGO, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Cook County Treasurer will commemorate Mexico's Independence on Wednesday with a noontime reception honoring the cultural contributions of Mexican Americans to Cook County.

The reception will take place in the Treasurer's Office at 118 N. Clark Street, Room 112, on the first floor of the County Building. The public is invited. The event will feature Morton High School's Mariachi Band and will celebrate the vibrant culture and enduring traditions of Cook County's Mexican diaspora through music and song.

"Mexican Independence Day is an opportunity to celebrate the history, culture and achievements of Mexican Americans who've enriched Cook County through their hard work, entrepreneurship, civic engagement and commitment to family and community," said the Treasurer. "Our county is strengthened by the diversity of its residents, and we're proud to recognize the more than one million people of Mexican heritage who call Chicagoland home by celebrating their contributions to the social, cultural and economic life of Cook County."

Observed annually on September 16, Mexico's Independence Day commemorates the beginning of country's struggle to free itself from Spanish colonial rule in 1810. The event known as the Grito de Dolores or the Cry of Dolores is named for the town where that first revolutionary spark ignited 116 years ago. That first "Cry" resulted in 11 more years of struggle before the Spanish were ultimately defeated in September of 1821. The observance honors Mexico's enduring commitment to freedom, democracy and national pride while celebrating the traditions and accomplishments of Mexicans both at home and abroad.

The reception will provide an opportunity to honor local community leaders by presenting them with Certificates of Excellence. 

Honorees: Andres Cervantes, Morton High School music director; Kevin Vesper, Morton High School fine arts and social director; Nazario Perez, La Cremeria la Ordena president; Mario Contreras, Medieval Times horse director and trainer; Adriana Rodriguez, vice president Necalli Cultural Movement; Gabriela Flores, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement; Amelia Gradilla, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement; Adriana Rangel, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement; Jacqueline Villanueva, co-founder, Necalli Cultural Movement

releases.title: Schmear We Go Again, as New York BagelFest Rolls Out Its 2026 Judges, Industry Talks and Entertainment
releases.body:
Acclaimed judges, bagel industry icons, world-class magic and live art join an international lineup of leading bagel makers at Citi Field on November 15th

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The dough is rising, and so is demand for New York BagelFest, Presented by King Arthur Baking Company. The ultimate celebration of bagel culture returns to Citi Field on Sunday, November 15, 2026, bringing together more than 25 acclaimed bagel makers, culinary personalities, industry leaders and thousands of hungry fans for a day of unlimited tastings, friendly-but-fierce competition, conversation and entertainment.

"The global bagel industry is growing at a rapidly accelerating rate. The 7th Annual New York BagelFest will be the most magical one yet - quite literally, with a magician and mentalist joining this year's entertainment lineup - for our foodies, industry professionals, and competitors," says BagelFest founder Sam Silverman.

Bagel lovers don't want to miss a bite. Early Bird tickets sold out in just three hours, and one-third of all available tickets were sold within the first 24 hours. Tickets are now on sale, as anticipation builds for one of the festival's most ambitious editions yet. This fall, New York BagelFest will welcome bagel shops representing ten states and five countries, with bakers traveling from Ireland, Spain, Canada and India to compete alongside legendary New York institutions and leading bagel makers from across the United States. Getting a spot at BagelFest is no schmear feat. Fewer than 9% of applicants were selected to compete in 2026, following a highly curated selection process evaluating bakeries on quality, originality, reputation and the passionate communities they've built.

Now, BagelFest is rolling out the next batch of news: the experts who will determine which bagels rise above the rest, an Industry Talks series bringing together influential voices in the business, and world-class entertainment spanning magic, mentalism, live fine art, and family programming.

But first, a hole lot of responsibility comes with judging. Choosing among some of the world's best bagels is a tough job, but somebody has to do it. The judging lineup brings together acclaimed voices from food journalism, restaurants, culinary culture and digital media, including Joan Nathan, the James Beard Award-winning author of twelve cookbooks known as the "matriarch of Jewish cooking." Jake Cohen the New York Times bestselling author of Jew-ish and I Could Nosh the host of "Jake Makes it Easy" on A+E and Hulu. Ethan Zohn, a former professional soccer player, author, TV host, and champion of CBS's Survivor: Africa. Chef Einat Admony, the three-time James Beard Award-nominated chef, restaurateur and cookbook author behind New York City's Balaboosta and Moondog HiFi. Darra Goldstein, the founding editor of Gastronomica and editor in chief of the Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Food Studies, who has won numerous prizes for her work in food, including James Beard and IACP awards.

Gabriella Gershenson, a James Beard Award-winning food journalist, author and editor at the New York Times Wirecutter. Joining her is Leah Koenig, the IACP Award-winning author of eight cookbooks, including new title The Dessert Table: 100 Joyful Jewish Sweets. Jeremy Jacobowitz brings the perspective of a food and travel creator whose audience of more than 950,000 follows his culinary adventures around the world. Before building his digital presence, Jacobowitz worked in food television as an assistant to Bobby Flay and as a producer.

Jewish Food thought leaders such as Liz Alpern and Jeffrey Yoskowitz, co-founders of The Gefilteria, co-authors of The Gefilte Manifesto, and co-hosts of the Meet Me at the Deli podcast, and Shannon Sarna, the Founding Editor of The Nosher and author of Modern Jewish Baker and Modern Jewish Comfort Food.

Judges with deep production experience include Tim Von Hollweg, Director of Operations at Russ & Daughters, native New Yorker, and hospitality veteran; and Reva Castillenti, an award-winning baker turned bakery consultant and educator.

Joining are prolific bagel eaters and reviewers, like Mike Varley, the creator of EverythingIsEverything.NYC, a catalogue of over 200 New York City bagel reviews from across all five boroughs. The project has been featured in The New York Times, NPR, The Washington Post, and The Today Show. Justin Shukat, co-founder of Bagel Tawk, with over 100 bagel reviews under his belt. Sean Keeley, the creator and writer of It's a Shanda, a newsletter dedicated to bagels in Seattle and beyond. Joanna O'Leary, culinary consultant, food historian, and scientific writer, with bagel reviews from all around the world. And Morgan Carter, the Food and Drink Editor at Time Out New York.

Chairing the "Best Sandwich" Judge committee is Ben Gollan, founder of A Man and His Sandwich Tours, New York's sandwich-dedicated walking tour. Gollan has made a career out of debating what does, and doesn't, count as a sandwich, including in Forbes and on national television.

Rounding out the Expert Judge lineup are returning judges who demonstrate a deep passion and expertise: Dara Pollack, writer, food photographer, comedian, and bagel enthusiast; Tara Cox, Editor & Writer; Chrissy Traore, CEO of See and Be Kitchen, and Ryan Garson, NYC real estate agent and content creator with a focus on bagels.

"The BagelFest judges hold a critical responsibility. Winning a top BagelFest award has elevated neighborhood shops into the national culinary spotlight. PopUp Bagels went on to a $300 million valuation, and Starship Bagel became a James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Bakery. It's permanently altered the trajectories of countless businesses, and the lives of the employees and families behind them," says Sam Silverman.

The coveted Best Bagel title will be determined through a blind taste test by the judges. Each unsliced plain bagel will receive a score from 1–10 across flavor, texture, appearance and aroma. The highest average score takes the crown, with flavor serving as the tiebreaker. The same judging criteria will determine honors for Best Bagel – New York Style, Best Bagel – Sourdough and Best Bagel – Montreal Style.

Expert judges will also select Schmear of the Year, based on flavor, texture and consistency, and originality; Most Creative, evaluating original concept, execution, presentation and story; Best Showmanship, honoring booth presentation, team energy and brand representation; and Best Bialy, judged on flavor, texture, appearance and creativity while honoring tradition. But the experts don't get all the fun. Festivalgoers will have their say through public voting for People's Choice, Best of the Boroughs, Best Beyond the Boroughs, Best International and Rising Star. For competitors who prefer speed to schmear, the Bagel Rolling Championship returns to the main stage, challenging participants to see who can roll the most bagels in just one minute.

BagelFest isn't just about who makes the best bagel; it's also about the people, ideas and businesses shaping where bagel culture rolls next. The festival's Industry Talks will bring bakers, operators and industry leaders together throughout the day for conversations about craft, growth, tradition and the future of the business.

"No matter your level of experience or knowledge, the industry panels at BagelFest offer a valuable opportunity to learn from professionals across the business. Panelists bring expertise in areas ranging from bagel making and business operations to brand marketing and beyond. There is no better place to connect with and learn from the industry's leading experts, all in one location," says Jeff Yankellow, Director of Bakery and Food Services Sales at King Arthur Baking Company.

The program kicks off at 10:15 a.m. with "The Key to the Perfect Bagel," featuring Jeff Yankellow (King Arthur Baking Company), Joe Savelli (Malt Products Corporation) and Chris Sarkesian (All Bake Technologies) moderated by journalist Annie Hollon. At 11:30 a.m., "From Toasted to Thriving" will feature Chris Pugliese (Tompkins Square Bagels), and Emily Winston (Boichik Bagels), moderated by Karen Bornarth (Bread Bakers Guild of America). At 1:15 p.m., "Icons of Jewish New York" brings together Jake Dell (Katz's Delicatessen), Josh Russ Tupper (Russ & Daughters), and David Zabar (Zabar's) for a conversation featuring names closely connected to New York food culture, moderated by Sean Keeley (It's a Shanda). The Industry Talks continue at 2:30 p.m. with a conversation between Christian Petroni and Scott Spellman of Utopia Bagels. Together, the conversations give guests a chance to go behind the counter and hear directly from the people helping turn a centuries-old food tradition into a thriving, evolving industry.

The bagels may be the stars, but they won't be the only thing making jaws drop. Leading this year's entertainment lineup is New York-based magician and mentalist Daniel Nicholas, who has performed at more than 1,000 events over 15 years, nationwide and around the globe. His performances blend sleight of hand with sleight of mind: magic that happens in guests' own hands and mind reading that unfolds inside their heads. At New York BagelFest, Nicholas will bring both up close and to the stage, moving from encounters just inches away to moments designed to hold an entire audience. His magic happens to guests rather than simply in front of them: a signed card can disappear and turn up somewhere impossible; a borrowed object takes an unexpected journey; an unspoken thought is revealed. No boxes. No doves. No assistants. Just plenty of "How did he do that?" to chew on between bagels.

BagelFest is also turning the art of the bagel into actual art. New York City-based fine artist Melissa Mae Kors will set up her easel directly inside the festival and construct a fully realized, gallery-ready masterpiece from scratch…transforming the iconic culinary staple into a centerpiece of high-detail, whimsical art. The immersive performance bridges the gap between culinary celebration and fine art, leaving attendees with an unforgettable window into the creation of contemporary surrealism. After all, when more than two dozen of the world's leading bagel makers are treating dough as their canvas, it only seems fitting to have an artist return the favor.

The entertainment doesn't stop with magic and live art. Families can also explore a dedicated Kids' Zone, featuring chef hat and apron decorating and interactive entertainment designed for the next generation of carb connoisseurs. The Kids' Zone will also welcome Allyson Fisher, author of Bagel Finds His Center, for readings and book signing, with copies available for purchase at the festival. The charming picture book follows Bagel, a nervous newcomer searching for what makes him special, using playful rhymes and food-themed humor to explore self-worth, individuality, friendship and belonging.

The day culminates with the BagelFest Awards Ceremony, where the day's winners will be crowned and the competitors who rise to the occasion will take home BagelFest bragging rights. BagelFest will also present its Lifetime Achievement Award, recognizing lasting impact on bagel culture. The honor recognizes notable contributions to the craft, culture and community of bagels, including innovation, mentorship, influence and sustained excellence.

New York BagelFest is grateful for the support of its sponsors and partners. King Arthur Baking Company serves as the event's Presenting Sponsor and Official Flour Partner, while All Bake Technologies joins as a Gold Sponsor and Official Equipment Sponsor. Manischewitz is a Silver Sponsor and the Official Kosher Food Partner. Bronze Sponsors include Philadelphia Cream Cheese, the Official Cream Cheese Partner; Malt Products, the Official Malt Partner; Bettani Farms the Official Plant-Based Partner; noissue, the Official Packaging Partner; Echelon Payment Solutions Group (EPSG), the Official Merchant Services Partner; and thinkDesign Architecture, the Official Architecture Partner. Moonrise Bagels, the original stuffed bagel, will also return to New York BagelFest with its VIP All-Access Bites, available exclusively in the BagelFest press room. Magician and Mentalist Daniel Nicholas is the Official Entertainment Sponsor. New York BagelFest also thanks its supporting sponsors: the Bread Bakers Guild of America, Arnel Associates, Goldfine & Company CPA PC, Morgan Business Council, Polaris Risk Management, The Copy Specialist, Zimner Law, and Hudson Peak Wealth Advisors. Learn more about New York BagelFest's official partners here.

If the first 24 hours are any indication, New York BagelFest is shaping up to be one hot ticket. New York BagelFest takes place Sunday, November 15th at Citi Field in New York City. Tickets are now on sale at bagelfest.com, with general admission starting at $69. Across two sessions (10am-1pm or 1pm-4pm), guests will be able to enjoy unlimited tastings from more than two dozen premier bagel shops and discover an extraordinary variety of bagels, schmears, sandwiches and festival-exclusive creations. All Access ticket holders will also receive an exclusive behind-the-scenes stadium tour and access to the Infield Suite, where they can enjoy special bites from Moonrise Bagels. For press inquiries, contact Pietra Communications by email at info@pietrapr.com or by phone at 212-913-9761.

About New York BagelFest

Sample unlimited bagels and schmears from the best bakeries in the world, meet the makers, and experience bagel culture like never before with hands-on programming, one-of-a-kind competitions, and family-friendly activities for all ages. releases.title: Planet Classroom and VoiceAmerica Launch New "Net Zero Speaks" Podcast: "We Have Everything We Need": Solar Pioneer Andrew Blakers Says the World Already Has the Technology for a 100% Clean Energy Future
releases.body:
Australian National University professor and co-inventor of PERC solar cell technology joins youth host Ivan Ransom to explain why the clean-energy transition is no longer a technological challenge—it is a matter of action.

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The transition to clean energy is no longer constrained by technology—it is purely a matter of execution.

The Planet Classroom Network, in partnership with VoiceAmerica, today announces the podcast release of Net Zero Speaks to Andrew Blakers. Hosted by youth climate advocate Ivan Ransom, this briefing features Professor Andrew Blakers AO FAA FTSE FRSN of the Australian National University, one of the world's leading renewable energy researchers and co-developer of the PERC solar cell technology used in much of today's global solar industry.

At the heart of the discussion is an unequivocal message: the world already possesses the technology required to run on 100 percent renewable energy.

"We have everything we need," Blakers explains. "We don't need to invent anything. It's just a matter of getting out and doing it."

A VISION FOR CHEAP, CLEAN ENERGY FOREVER

Throughout the conversation, Blakers outlines a global future powered by what he calls "clean, cheap energy forever," noting that "most countries are their own Saudi Arabia of solar and wind."

Drawing on decades of research, he demonstrates how solar power, wind energy, pumped hydro storage, batteries, and electrification technologies can seamlessly integrate to create reliable, affordable, zero-carbon energy systems at scale worldwide.

A GLOBAL VOICE ON RENEWABLE INNOVATION

Professor Blakers is internationally recognized for helping develop the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell (PERC) solar cell—a breakthrough that dramatically increased solar panel efficiency, transformed the modern solar industry, and accelerated the dramatic decline in solar energy costs globally.

Today, Blakers leads research on large-scale renewable energy systems and the Global Pumped Hydro Atlas, which identifies hundreds of thousands of potential energy storage sites capable of supporting fully renewable electricity grids.

Key insights highlighted in the episode include:

  • The Scale of Solar & Wind: Why most nations possess more than enough renewable resources to achieve total energy independence.
  • Overcoming Misconceptions: Tackling persistent myths regarding land use, raw materials, grid stability, and waste management.
  • Deep Decarbonization: How governments, utilities, and communities can achieve deep decarbonization while maintaining lower energy costs and grid reliability.

FROM SOLAR PANELS TO "GRAVITY BATTERIES"

A central focus of the episode is solving the energy storage puzzle. Blakers explains how pumped hydro systems—often described as giant "gravity batteries"—store renewable energy by moving water between two reservoirs at different elevations.

His team's research identified approximately 820,000 potential pumped hydro sites globally, offering vastly more storage capacity than needed for a fully renewable energy future. The discussion explores how these systems balance solar and wind generation while maintaining grid reliability and affordability.

"Professor Blakers reminds us that many of the critical solutions we need already exist," said C. M. (Cathy) Rubin, Co-Founder and CEO of Planet Classroom. "Understanding that we already have the tools to solve these challenges is empowering for young people. The challenge now is accelerating action and building the political and social will to implement them globally."

releases.title: L.A. Film School Alumni Make Their Mark Across the 2026 Emmy Awards
releases.body:
Alumni contributed to 41 Emmy-nominated productions, including 32 that took home wins across television's biggest categories.

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As the 2026 Emmy Awards celebrated another year of outstanding television, alumni of The Los Angeles Film School were among the entertainment professionals contributing to many of this year's recognized productions.

L.A. Film School alumni were credited across 41 nominated productions, with 44 individual alumni credits spanning 218 Emmy nominations. Of those productions, 13 received at least one Emmy win and combined for 32 total wins, highlighting the range of roles alumni hold throughout the entertainment industry.

Among the year's biggest winners were The Pitt and Pluribus, each earning six Emmy wins. Alumnus Alexander Jongbloed was nominated as part of The Pitt's sound mixing team, while Mitchell Gebhard worked as first assistant sound and boom operator on Pluribus' winning sound mixing team.

Other Emmy-winning productions featuring L.A. Film School alumni included The Muppet Show, where Raul Perez worked as a loader; Margo's Got Money Troubles, where Márk Faragó worked as a finishing artist; and Fallout, where Brice Bradley worked as a gaffer on the show's volume stage.

On Hacks, alumni Jamiel VanOver and Yermin "Randy" Garcia worked in the camera and electrical departments, while Stephanie Goldstein worked as an assistant editor. Ira Parker serves as showrunner and executive producer of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms and was individually nominated for Outstanding Drama Series.

Alumni contributions also extended to a variety of other Emmy-recognized productions. Damian Drago contributed as a digital artist on Stranger Things, while Neiko Nagy worked as a compositor on The Diplomat's visual effects team.

Beyond the winning productions, L.A. Film School alumni contributed to a number of Emmy-nominated productions, including Nobody Wants This, Only Murders in the Building, Euphoria, and more.

This year's alumni credits reflect the many paths available to entertainment professionals and the range of disciplines that come together to bring stories to audiences. The Los Angeles Film School celebrates the continued work of its alumni as they build careers and contribute to the next generation of film, television, and entertainment.

Discover where an L.A. Film School education can take you. Read our accompanying blog article to explore the full list of alumni contributing to this year's Emmy-nominated and award-winning productions.

About The Los Angeles Film School

The Los Angeles Film School is an accredited higher education institution located in the heart of Hollywood. The school has served the community and its students since 1999. Offering both in-person or online-based learning programs, students can earn Bachelor of Science degrees in Animation, Audio Production, Digital Filmmaking, Entertainment Business, Film production, Graphic Design, Media Communications, Music production and Writing for Film & TV; and Associate of Science degrees in Audio Production, Music production, and Film. The campus facilities include the historic RCA Building at 6363 Sunset Blvd. and the studios at 6690 Sunset Blvd., where students have access to industry-standard equipment, editing labs, dub stages and recording studios.

The school's faculty of industry professionals have earned credits on major motion pictures, video games and music recordings. Numerous alumni have received awards at film festivals worldwide, engineered multi-platinum selling albums, and some credits include GRAMMY, Emmy and Oscar nominations and wins. releases.title: Palmetto Publishing Releases George Kerpi's Debut Crime Novel About a Cold Case That Refuses to Stay Buried
releases.body:
Treacherous Path, a newly published police procedural set in a small mountain town, explores the moral cost of silence through a dual timeline investigation spanning more than a decade.

CHARLESTON, S.C., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Palmetto Publishing has released Treacherous Path, the debut novel from author George Kerpi. The police procedural follows a detective in the mountain town of Oak Ridge as a gruesome discovery unravels the accepted story of a woman's disappearance and exposes layers of complicity that stretch far beyond a single crime.

The novel opens when a hunting party walks into the Oak Ridge sheriff's office carrying a severed finger bearing a gold ring. Detective Aaron Chase identifies it as belonging to Dr. Natalie Brooks, a physician who had said her goodbyes three days earlier and driven away from the mountain resort where she had worked for four years. Everyone believed she had simply moved on. Chase and his partner begin pulling at the threads of her disappearance, encountering an unsent letter, an ex-husband who surfaced the day she vanished, and a geologist carrying a debt he could neither repay nor acknowledge.

What initially appears to be a crime of passion reveals ties to something far more organized, patient, and dangerous. The investigation builds toward an arrest, a confession, and a verdict the community accepts. But the ground beneath that resolution is unstable. Eleven years later, a woman arrives in Oak Ridge with a cold case file, determined to find out how much was left buried. The dual timeline structure forces questions about institutional failure, personal complicity, and whether the people closest to the truth chose not to see it.

Treacherous Path enters a crime fiction landscape shaped by the atmospheric, character-driven work of authors such as Tana French and Jane Harper. The novel is positioned for readers aged thirty to sixty who gravitate toward procedurals set in insular communities where moral ambiguity matters more than plot twists. Its focus on silence, complicity, and the cost of looking away speaks directly to a cultural moment in which questions about institutional accountability remain urgent and unresolved.

Treacherous Path is available for purchase online at Amazon.com and BarnesandNoble.com. For more information about the author, please visit any of their social media platforms.

Facebook: George Kerpi - Author

Instagram: georgekerpiauthor

About the Author: George Kerpi brings firsthand insight into the world of law and justice to his crime fiction. Raised in a household of government lawyers who held institutions accountable for their actions, he was immersed in questions of right and wrong, legality and lawlessness, long before he could fully understand them. That foundation gives his writing an authenticity that readers can feel on every page.

Kerpi's debut novel, Treacherous Path, was born from a desire to explore crime fiction that resists easy moral categories. Drawn to stories where characters cannot be defined simply as good or bad, he set out to write a mystery that is equal parts dark suspense and human drama. The result is a novel about a violent crime that unravels into something far more complex: a crime of passion entangled with betrayal, organized crime, and the slow erosion of humanity. For Kerpi, the story is not merely imagined; it is a genuine, immersive, reflective experience meant to challenge readers and stay with them long after the final page.

When he is not writing, Kerpi draws inspiration from the tension between the ordinary and the extraordinary in everyday life. He believes that childhood and environment leave a tremendous mark on character, and that belief fuels his commitment to crafting layered, psychologically rich fiction. Follow George for updates on new releases.

releases.title: Sonilo Takes AI Music to the World Stage at the Venice Film Festival
releases.body:
The Silicon Valley company showcases its music and sound-effects models in a completed cinematic soundtrack, marking a milestone in its expansion into professional filmmaking.

SILICON VALLEY, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sonilo, a U.S. company developing multimodal audio AI, brought its AI music and sound effects to the 2026 Venice International Film Festival. The company's technology contributed to the soundtrack of the PRIMORDIA trailer, which premiered during the opening program of an industry forum organized by TapNow at Venice Production Bridge. The presentation placed Sonilo's audio technology in front of an international film-industry audience through a finished cinematic work.

For Sonilo, the showcase represents a significant step into professional cinema. Its technology contributed to the musical identities, emotional progression and physical world of a production presented at Venice, demonstrating how AI-powered music and sound effects can move beyond standalone generation into the demands of cinematic storytelling.

The significance extends beyond visibility. A completed soundtrack gives filmmakers and production partners a tangible basis for evaluating the technology: how it works with the picture, supports the narrative and contributes to the experience audiences ultimately see and hear.

"Bringing Sonilo's AI-powered music to Venice is a milestone in our push into professional filmmaking," said Trista Hong, Chief Marketing Officer of Sonilo. "Cinema demands more than an impressive track or a realistic sound. It demands emotion, timing and a world the audience can believe in. We are building audio technology powerful enough to support ambitious productions and intelligent enough to serve the story."

Technology That Understands What the Story Needs

Sonilo is developing its Sound World Model, a multimodal AI system designed to connect video understanding, audio generation and temporal alignment. Rather than treating music and sound effects as isolated assets, the company is building technology that understands visual stories and generates audio in relation to the action, environment and narrative.

The production presented at Venice illustrated that approach across both music and sound effects.

For the score, Sonilo helped the production team explore contrasting instrumental textures within a character-driven musical framework. The finished soundtrack progressed from restrained elements beneath dialogue to deeper bass and additional layers as conflict approached. Rhythm and intensity increased with the action, culminating in a combination of synthesizers, orchestral elements and percussion. The result demonstrated how generated material can be developed into music with narrative structure, rather than simply placed beneath a sequence of images.

For sound effects, Sonilo analyzed scene content, movement, materials and narrative context before generating audio. Sound creators then reviewed and refined the results, corrected mismatches and added further creative direction. This scene-aware approach connects generation to a central requirement of filmmaking: sounds must belong to the world on screen, not merely sound convincing on their own.

"Film music is not everywhere in the film," said Shawn Song, CEO of Sonilo. "The model has to know when to start, when to stop, and when to leave room for the dialogue."

That is the technical ambition behind Sonilo's approach: audio generation that responds to what a scene means, not only what it contains.

Turning Generation Speed Into Creative Capability

The production also demonstrated how Sonilo's performance can expand creative exploration. According to the workflow presented at Venice, Sonilo reduced one initial music-exploration stage from approximately 10 hours to around 20 seconds. The comparison applies to that specific exploration stage, not to completion of the entire soundtrack.

The team used Sonilo to generate multiple musical and sound-effect directions, evaluate their emotional and narrative fit, and develop the strongest material through selection, combination, editing and professional post-production. This gave the project's composer and creative team a broader range of material to work with while preserving the decisions that shaped the final soundtrack.

For Sonilo, the opportunity is larger than making an existing task faster. The company aims to put more creative possibilities within reach: more musical directions to test, more sound palettes to explore and more opportunities to discover an approach that strengthens the film. Generation speed becomes valuable when it expands what a production can attempt and accomplish.

Building a Lasting Place for AI-Powered Music in Cinema

Sonilo's approach pairs technical ambition with respect for intellectual property and creative labor. "We respect knowledge, we respect IP, we respect effort. It should be common sense," Song said during the forum.

The company sees responsible development and professional collaboration as essential to building a lasting place in the film industry. Its goal is to advance audio technology that fits the realities of production, supports demanding creative work and develops alongside the filmmakers, composers and sound professionals who use it.

The Venice presentation offers a concrete example of that direction: Sonilo's generation capabilities working within a production process that combined composition, sound design and post-production to deliver a finished soundtrack.

For Sonilo, this is a foundation for a broader ambition: to make AI music and sound effects a meaningful part of professional filmmaking, with the capability to support increasingly ambitious stories. Its presence at Venice marks a step toward that future, demonstrated through the work itself.

About Sonilo

Sonilo is a Silicon Valley-based U.S. company developing multimodal audio AI for visual storytelling. The company is building the Sound World Model, designed to connect video understanding, music and sound-effects generation, and temporal alignment. Its technology supports filmmakers, creators and creative platforms across film, video, gaming and generative media.

About 10000 Parallel Universes

10000 Parallel Universes is TapNow's long-term international AI-native IP incubation initiative, designed to connect emerging creators with creative development, production support, international collaboration and distribution opportunities.

The initiative aims to explore how technology can amplify culturally diverse voices, expand access to filmmaking and help meaningful stories reach international audiences.

releases.title: 5 Creator Economy Trends That Will Change How Creators Make Money in 2027
releases.body:
RM11 identifies the rise of owned audiences, diversified monetization, paid traffic, AI automation and creator wellness as forces reshaping the creator business model.

DALLAS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The creator economy is growing up. Building a large following is no longer enough to build a sustainable creator business as creators increasingly seek greater control over their audiences, revenue, workload and long-term careers.

RM11, a creator-first platform built around direct audience relationships and multiple monetization tools, has identified five trends it believes will reshape how creators build businesses and generate revenue in 2027.

Recent industry research supports that shift. CreatorIQ's 2026 State of Creators study, based on 5,095 creators, found that 67% earned less than $10,000 from content creation over the prior year and that content creation was not the primary source of income for 62% of respondents. Meanwhile, Epidemic Sound's Future of the Creator Economy Report 2026 found that 72% of creators are actively developing owned audiences, while 41% want to build a sustainable independent business or grow into a media brand or creator studio.

"The next evolution of the creator economy isn't about producing more content or accumulating more followers," said Olivier David, Chief Growth Officer of RM11. "It's about giving creators the infrastructure to operate like businesses — own their audience relationships, diversify revenue, acquire customers and protect their most valuable resource: their time."

RM11 identifies five shifts that will define the next era of creator monetization:

1. Owned audiences will become more valuable than follower counts.

Creators are increasingly looking beyond algorithm-dependent reach toward direct relationships with their audiences. Memberships, private communities, messaging and direct-to-fan experiences can give creators greater control over how they engage and monetize their most loyal followers. Epidemic Sound's 2026 research found 72% of creators are already developing audiences away from core platforms through channels such as newsletters and Discord.

2. Creator platforms will evolve beyond the paywall.

The next generation of creator platforms will function more like business operating systems. Rather than relying on subscriptions alone, creators will increasingly combine memberships, pay-per-view content, livestreams, messaging, video calls and other revenue streams while using integrated tools to manage customer relationships, content and day-to-day operations.

3. Creators will start thinking about customer acquisition — not just followers.

As the industry matures, creators will increasingly apply traditional business metrics such as customer acquisition cost, conversion and return on advertising spend to audience growth. RM11 is developing promotion tools designed to make paid traffic and measurable customer acquisition more accessible to eligible creators, moving growth beyond the traditional "post and hope" model.

4. AI will shift from content generation to workload reduction.

AI adoption is becoming mainstream, but creator control remains critical. Adobe's 2026 Creators' Toolkit Report found that 93% of surveyed creators say creative AI helps them produce content faster, while 85% say the final creative decision should always remain with the creator. RM11 believes the next opportunity lies in using AI to reduce repetitive work and expand creator capacity without sacrificing authenticity, ownership or human oversight.

5. Creator wellness will become business infrastructure.

Creator-first economics cannot stop at revenue share. As creators operate increasingly complex businesses, platforms will be expected to help address the workload, stress and burnout that can accompany always-on digital careers. RM11 is investing in this area through integrated human account-management support and relationships with creator wellness and mental health organizations, including Creators for Mental Health, Revive Health Therapy and Pineapple Support.

"At RM11, 'creator-first' has to mean more than a revenue split," David added. "It means asking what creators actually need to build sustainable businesses — and then building the technology, services and partnerships around them."

RM11's growing ecosystem combines direct monetization, creator CRM capabilities, human account-management support, audience-growth initiatives and creator wellness resources as the company works toward a broader vision: giving creators the infrastructure to build businesses, not simply profiles.

For more information, visit RM11.com.

For media inquiries, please email media@rm11.com

About RM11

RM11 is a creator-first platform designed to give creators greater control over their audience, earnings and digital businesses. Through memberships, exclusive content, messaging, livestreaming, native video calls, integrated creator tools, account-management support, and a free CRM for agencies, RM11 provides multiple ways for creators to monetize direct relationships with their audiences. Female-founded and led, RM11 is building a more sustainable, creator-first model for the next generation of the creator economy.

releases.title: Clear Channel Outdoor Selected to Lead Advertising Program at Pensacola International Airport
releases.body:
New Concession Will Modernize Airport Media Network and Support Long-Term Growth Strategy

PENSACOLA, Fla., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division, the leading U.S. airport sponsorship and advertising partner, today announced it has been selected to manage the advertising concession at Pensacola International Airport (PNS). The agreement gives Clear Channel Outdoor (CCO) responsibility for delivering a refreshed airport media program that connects brands with more than 3.1 million annual passengers and strengthens the airport's position as a key commercial gateway for the Gulf Coast region.

Following a competitive selection process, PNS selected CCO to lead its advertising program, which has been managed in-house since 2018. Having previously served as the airport advertising concessionaire until 2012, CCO will return with a major investment in upgraded infrastructure and new sponsorship inventory. The program is designed to modernize the terminal environment, enhance revenue opportunities, and introduce more dynamic, technology-enabled advertising formats across high-traffic passenger areas.

"Pensacola International Airport is experiencing remarkable growth, and we're proud to partner with the airport at such a pivotal moment in its development," said Morten Gotterup, President, Clear Channel Outdoor Airports Division. "This agreement enables us to bring a new level of innovation to the airport environment, creating high-impact opportunities for brands to engage travelers through modern, technology-driven media while enhancing the overall experience for the millions of passengers who move through PNS each year."

PNS is the busiest airport along the Interstate 10 corridor between Jacksonville and New Orleans, serving a broad mix of business, leisure, and military travelers. The airport offers 28 nonstop destinations and is served by major carriers including American, Delta, United, Southwest, Breeze, Frontier, and Contour.

Modernizing the Passenger Environment

The new advertising program aligns with PNS's broader capital investment strategy, including a $165 million terminal expansion and new concourse scheduled for completion in the first half of 2028, which will add five gates to the existing 12-gate facility.

"Pensacola International Airport is in the midst of one of the most transformative periods in our history, and every investment we make should reflect the future we're building," said Matt Coughlin, Executive Director of Pensacola International Airport. "Clear Channel Outdoor shares that vision by bringing innovative, technology-driven advertising solutions that will elevate the passenger experience while creating meaningful opportunities for businesses to connect with millions of travelers each year. We're excited to partner with them as we continue shaping the next chapter for PNS."

CCO's Airports Division will introduce a modernized advertising program across key passenger touchpoints, including:

  • Branded LED video walls across entryways, security checkpoints, and baggage claim – Large-format digital displays placed at key passenger touchpoints, delivering high-impact brand storytelling throughout the airport journey.
  • Digital concourse advertising network – A connected network of screens throughout the concourse, reaching travelers as they move between gates, dining, and retail areas.
  • Reimagined branded environments – Immersive media opportunities that transform high-visibility terminal spaces into memorable brand experiences while reinforcing the airport's identity.
  • Corner tension fabric displays – Architecturally integrated, large-format displays designed to maximize visibility while complementing the terminal environment.
  • New charging station sponsorship opportunities – A premium sponsorship platform that aligns brands with a high-demand passenger amenity, creating sustained engagement throughout dwell times.

The partnership reinforces CCO's commitment to helping airports modernize passenger environments through innovative, technology-driven advertising solutions while supporting long-term growth and investment across the aviation network.

To learn more about Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division, visit https://clearchanneloutdoor.com/airport-advertising/.

releases.title: SiriusXM's SXM-11 Satellite Successfully Completes In-Orbit Testing and Enters Operational Service
releases.body:
Most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's fleet is designed to improve signal reception, expand Alaska coverage and support reliable service across North America

NEW YORK, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SiriusXM today announced that the Company's SXM-11 satellite is now operational, following successful in-orbit testing and handover by Intuitive Machines. SXM-11 is the most powerful satellite in SiriusXM's high-powered fleet and is designed to improve signal reception, expand Alaska coverage and support reliable service across North America.

"Bringing SXM-11 into service strengthens our next-generation satellite fleet and reinforces the long-term resilience of our network," said Sean Gibbons, Chief Product and Technology Officer at SiriusXM. "For listeners, that means a premium in-car experience with broad, reliable coverage, including where cellular service may be limited. Through SiriusXM with 360L, we combine that reach with the choice, personalization and interactivity of streaming, to bring the best of both technologies together in millions of vehicles."

210 million SiriusXM-equipped vehicles across North America are on the road today and rely on the proprietary satellite infrastructure supporting SiriusXM's in-vehicle listening experience. Built on the Intuitive Machines IM 1300™ satellite platform, SXM-11 weighed more than 15,000 pounds, or nearly 6,950 kilograms at launch. The satellite stands 28 feet tall and spans more than 106 feet with its solar panels deployed. Orbiting 22,000 miles above Earth, SXM-11 features a large, unfurlable 30-foot (9 meter) main beam antenna that broadcasts audio and data to users on the ground, with an estimated eight million square miles of broadcast coverage.

"SXM-11 marks another milestone in our longstanding partnership with SiriusXM. Over the course of our relationship, we have built 13 spacecraft together," said Chris Johnson, President, Intuitive Machines. "This handover reflects our shared commitment to mission success and the confidence SiriusXM continues to place in our team to deliver high-performance, reliable space systems. We continue to demonstrate our ability to design, build, and deliver satellite systems that meet the demanding requirements of today's commercial space market with robust, scalable high-power platforms."

SiriusXM also offers satellite-delivered Marine and Aviation services that provide pilots and boaters with weather data and other important information directly in their cockpits. SXM-11 carries an additional communications payload that will be used to deliver expanded WCS-band coverage.

SXM-11 launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 10:25 p.m. ET on June 28. SiriusXM and Intuitive Machines subsequently completed the commissioning and testing required to verify that the spacecraft and its communications systems were ready for operational service.

SXM-11 is the 15th satellite launched for SiriusXM and will replace XM-5. It is part of SiriusXM's ongoing satellite fleet-refresh program. SXM-9 and SXM-10 commenced service in 2025, and SXM-12 is currently scheduled for launch in 2027.

SXM-11 by the numbers

  • More than 15,000 pounds: SXM-11's launch weight, approximately the weight of a school bus.
  • Nearly 60%: The portion of the satellite's launch weight made up of fuel supporting its journey and in-orbit operations.
  • 28 feet: The height of the satellite.
  • 22,000 miles: The satellite's orbiting distance above Earth.
  • 8 million square miles: The satellite's approximate broadcast coverage footprint.
  • More than 106 feet: The satellite's span with its solar panels deployed - approximately the height of a 10-story building laid on its side.
  • 30 feet: The diameter of SXM-11's large, unfurlable S-band reflector (9 meters).
  • 210 million: The estimated number of SiriusXM-equipped vehicles across North America supported by SiriusXM's proprietary satellite network.
  • 15th satellite: SXM-11 is the 15th spacecraft launched for Sirius, XM and SiriusXM.

About Sirius XM Holdings Inc.

SiriusXM is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, with a portfolio of audio businesses including its flagship subscription entertainment service SiriusXM; the ad-supported and premium music streaming services of Pandora; an expansive podcast network; and a complete ecosystem of advertising solutions through SiriusXM Media and AdsWizz. SiriusXM offers live, on-demand, and human-curated programming across music, talk, news, sports, and podcasts, and the company reaches approximately 255 million monthly listeners across its platforms. With deep automotive manufacturer relationships and unique spectrum assets, SiriusXM is built to reach listeners wherever they are. The company connects fans to the voices, creators, and moments they love - creating communities where listeners engage, participate, and belong. For more about SiriusXM, please go to: https://www.siriusxm.com/

About Intuitive Machines

Intuitive Machines is a leading space infrastructure company that builds spacecraft, connects networks and operates infrastructure-as-a-service for commercial, civil and national-security customers. With a proven track record across the space domain, the company, through organic growth and portfolio expansion, has built more than 300 spacecraft, delivered more than 260 kilograms of payload to the lunar surface and provided precision-navigation expertise that has guided spacecraft across the solar system. These capabilities form an integrated Build-Connect-Operate infrastructure service company, enabling customers to achieve mission and campaign outcomes through a single prime solution. Intuitive Machines' technology has been demonstrated across the space domain and is engineered to support the next century of opportunity in space.

releases.body:
BROOMALL, Pa., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shopley Inc. (the "Company" or "Shopley"), a consolidated commerce provider of operational and engagement solutions for merchants and merchant services providers, is pleased to announce they have signed an exclusive reseller agreement with Factor4 LLC ("Factor4"), a leading provider of omnichannel gift card and loyalty solutions.

With this new partnership Shopley will become an exclusive reseller of Factor4's gift card and loyalty solution in Canada, integrating their platform and enhancing it with Shopley's operational and engagement solutions. Factor4 gains a localized partner with deep expertise and relationships in the Canadian market plus a plan to better support the French and English market as part of the combined operational and technology plan. Shopley gains a stable and proven gift card solution to integrate with their advanced loyalty engine to take advantage of the constantly changing industry and growing needs of merchants and merchant services providers.

"We are excited to join forces with Factor4 to scale our business further," said Steve Levely, CEO of Shopley. "I joined Factor4 as an advisor in the fall of 2025 after selling my previous company Ackroo. Shortly after joining, I invested in and became CEO of Shopley where Dan and I began exploring how the two companies could work together to scale our respective businesses. We first explored working as complimentary solutions but with the many changes that have happened in the Canadian gift card and loyalty market, we decided Shopley becoming a formal reseller and us building a combined operational and technology solution was best. I am truly excited for how this partnership will transform our business and expect big success for both of our companies."

"Our team is thrilled to partner with Steve and the Shopley team," said Dan Battista, CEO of Factor4. "A lot of Factor4's success has come through the many great partnerships we have formed so to be able to work with someone like Steve who has already been assisting us in various ways is great. Steve and his team have great relationships and understanding of the Canadian market so in an effort to support him and to better expand our business we see this partnership model as the perfect fit."

From digital signage to niche point-of-sale software solutions and more, Shopley provides a shopping cart of operational and engagement solutions for merchants of all sizes. releases.title: Produced by a World-Class International Team! Adam Fan's Official New Album SKYFALL Makes Exclusive Debut on NetEase Cloud Music
releases.body:
HANGZHOU, China, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On September 15, Adam Fan's new album SKYFALL makes exclusive debut on NetEase Cloud Music. Meticulously crafted by top international production teams and Grammy-nominated producers, SKYFALL features 10 tracks spanning melodic rap, rage rap, trap, rock-infused rage rap, and other styles. With every track refined to meet world-class production standards, the album showcases Fan's musical versatility and creative edge, marking a dramatic transformation in his global music career.

The album's title track, SKYFALL, has been released as an advance single on September 8 and reached No.1 on NetEase Cloud Music's Rising Chart (飙升榜), Popular Recommendations Chart (全民热推榜), and Heartbeat Chart (心动榜) that same day. To date, the song has received more than 300,000 comments from listeners. This song was produced jointly by Fan and Lawson, a leading American hitmaker who has produced for superstars such as The Weeknd and Playboi Carti. The song seamlessly blends ethereal, hazy, atmospheric melodies with deep self-examination. Through its lyrics and composition, Fan delves into his inner world—confronting the high-pressure pace behind his success, his inner struggles, and the loneliness at the very top. SKYFALL demonstrates Fan's evolution from a C-POP idol into an avant-garde, internationally oriented musician.

Fan has successfully crossed over from C-POP and acting, making a striking impression with SKYFALL, an internationally oriented urban rap album. The album boasts a stellar songwriting and production lineup: it was crafted entirely by leading hitmaking teams who have worked with global icons such as Drake, The Weeknd, Playboi Carti, Beyoncé, Yeat, and Trippie Redd. The album moves from late-night uncertainty, loneliness and intense introspection (SKYFALL and CHANCES) into the dark aesthetic of raw, industrial rage rap (TTTM, ERROR, and MAKE IT ROCK), ultimately arriving at a celebration party with cinematic trap and lush-flowing (GO GIRL, HEARD OF US, MAKE IT MAKE SENSE, and PINK).

NetEase Cloud Music has more than 200 million monthly active users, with over 90% of its active users born in the 1990s or 2000s. The platform's large community of young music fans is precisely the target audience for a new generation of singers, including Fan. In 2020, EMERGING, Fan's concept EP marking his 20th birthday, sold more than 250,000 copies within six minutes of its release on NetEase Cloud Music and surpassed 400,000 copies within 24 hours. In 2021, Yi? (咦？), his concept EP celebrating his 21st birthday, sold more than 150,000 copies within five minutes of its release on the platform, topping both NetEase Cloud Music's daily and weekly digital album sales charts. Its lead track, Born to Lose, reached No.1 on the platform's Rising Chart and New Songs Chart. The newly released SKYFALL surprises and delights music fans with its musicality, sincerity, and innovation. The album shows that Fan is continually pushing his own boundaries and gradually evolving into an all-around musician.

NetEase Cloud Music and Fan have collaborated on multiple EPs and albums, all of which have earned both widespread attention and positive word of mouth. As of this new release, Fan describes SKYFALL as the color of black, because the album represents his journey from late-night introspection to a fresh start. "I hope we all stay clear-headed and confident, and I'd like to thank NetEase Cloud Music for helping this album reach more listeners."

Wei Yuan, Vice President of Copyright at NetEase Cloud Music, said, "We are delighted to partner with Adam Fan once again. NetEase Cloud Music offers a wealth of high-quality rap music and brings together a large community of young rap fans. We hope the platform will help Adam Fan's new album build a more direct and deeper connection with music fans."

NetEase Cloud Music is the leading music community in China, where users can listen for free to hundreds of millions of music tracks and other audio titles. Since the start of 2026, NetEase Cloud Music has continued to significantly expand its licensed music catalog, adding a large collection of classic film and television soundtracks from TVB, as well as officially licensed music from the Chinese-style martial arts game JX3, and exclusively premiering new works by renowned artists such as Ren Jialun (Allen Ren) and Mariah Carey.

At the same time, NetEase Cloud Music has continued to deepen its commitment to HIP-POP, launching the Chinese HIP-POP Music Awards (中文说唱音乐奖), along with semiannual charts, monthly and weekly charts, to identify outstanding work from multiple perspectives and highlight trends in Chinese HIP-POP. The platform also provides systematic support for the development of HIP-POP in China through initiatives including BeatSoul, its one-stop beat marketplace, income support programs, and rap projects. Going forward, NetEase Cloud Music will partner with more musicians to continue bringing users high-quality, officially licensed music.

All The Way Up Media is integrating AI search visibility into its existing SEO strategies, helping GTA businesses strengthen how their brands, services and expertise are understood across both traditional search engines and emerging AI-powered search experiences.

"SEO is not disappearing. It is evolving," said All The Way Up Media. "Businesses still need strong Google rankings, local search visibility and well-optimized websites, but they also need to prepare for the way people are beginning to search and make decisions using AI."

The agency's expanded approach includes technical SEO, content optimization, local SEO, Google Business Profile optimization, structured data, website authority development and strategies designed to strengthen brand visibility across emerging search platforms.

For businesses in competitive GTA markets, including legal services, healthcare, home improvement, professional services and technology, the changing search landscape creates both new challenges and new opportunities.

All The Way Up Media says its goal is to help local businesses build long-term digital visibility rather than rely on a single marketing channel.

Based in Toronto, All The Way Up Media works with businesses throughout the Greater Toronto Area and across Canada and the US, providing SEO, Google Ads, paid social advertising, website design and digital marketing strategy.

Businesses interested in improving their visibility across Google, local search and emerging AI search platforms can visit AllTheWayUpMedia.com or contact the All The Way Up Media team to discuss their digital marketing goals.

KNOXVILLE, Tenn., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Regal is giving moviegoers more reasons to come to the theatre with Regal Rewards+, a new subscription designed for people who love the movies but want more flexibility in how often they go.

releases.body:
The family-owned company marks the fall semester with national honor celebrating its culture of growth and development for early-career professionals.

PLYMOUTH, Wis., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As college students head back to campus for the fall semester, Sargento is proud to announce it has been named by Forbes as one of America's Best Employers for New Grads 2026. This prestigious accolade highlights the family-owned company's dedication to fostering a workplace where recent graduates can thrive, grow, and make a meaningful impact from day one.

The Forbes ranking was determined through an independent survey of over 100,000 U.S. young professionals (under 10 years of experience) working at companies employing at least 1,000 people. Out of 2 million evaluations, scores were based on direct employee nominations and public recommendations from industry peers.

The recognition marks the second major Forbes honor for Sargento in 2026. Earlier this year, Sargento was named to the Forbes list of America's Best Midsize Employers, solidifying its reputation as an employer of choice across all career stages.

"Our success has always been driven by our employees: the Sargento Family. We are committed to welcoming new graduates and students into our workforce, where they contribute at a high level and bring new ideas and ways of working to Sargento," said Louie Gentine, third-generation Chairman and CEO of Sargento. "Being recognized by Forbes as a top employer for both new graduates and midsize companies in America is an incredible honor. It shows that the culture we have built over generations continues to drive our success and makes Sargento a place where you can start and grow your career."

2026 Survey Highlights Strong Talent Pipeline   

Sargento's recognition is reinforced by the standout results of its 2026 Intern-Co-Op Survey*, which evaluated program performance, environment, and development:

  • 100% Program Advocacy: 100% of respondents stated they would recommend the Sargento internship or co-op experience to others.
  • 100% Fair Compensation Perception: 100% of participants agreed they are paid fairly for their work and contributions.
  • High Career Intent: 95% of interns and co-ops expressed a desire to accept a full-time, entry-level opportunity with Sargento upon graduation.
  • Exceptional Overall Quality: 95% rated their overall internship experience positively, supported by high marks for program leadership (100%), onboarding (91%), and skill-building projects (91%).

*The 2026 Intern-Co-Op Survey included 21 interns and co-ops, with a 100% participation rate.

"We don't view our interns and co-ops as temporary team members. We view them as the future of our business," said Anne Troka, Senior Manager of Community and Workforce Development at Sargento. "Seeing 95% of our 2026 cohort express a desire to stay with us full-time, alongside a 100% recommendation rating, proves that our focus on structured mentorship and high-impact work is creating a meaningful launchpad for early careers."

Sargento's Workforce Development program, which spans 21 distinct internship tracks across the organization, launched in 2016. Over the past decade, Sargento has established itself as an industry leader in connecting students to careers and transforming new graduates into long-term employees.

In 2026, the company welcomed its 50th student employee into a full-time role since 2016. The longevity of this program is reflected in its people. One of Sargento's earliest student hires from 2017 remains with the company today, with many of these employees choosing to grow their careers at Sargento for five years or more.

That focus on mentorship and real-world responsibility resonates with program participants.

"The most meaningful part of my internship was being surrounded by incredible mentors who encouraged my growth while trusting me with projects that allowed me to make real impact," said Carter Parker, Consumer Insights Intern, University of Michigan.

releases.title: College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free
releases.body:
Early College students can earn an associate degree while still in high school, potentially saving families tens of thousands of dollars.

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "I couldn't imagine how much money worth of free education my kids have received through this program."

For Ciara Selden-Ruffin, the mother of Grand River Preparatory High School Early College student Aamir Hollowell, the financial impact of the Early College program has been substantial. It has given Aamir the opportunity to earn an associate degree without the family taking on the tuition bill.

That kind of financial head start is critical for families worrying about how they will pay for college.

The nation's federal student loan portfolio stands at nearly $1.7 trillion, with about 44.6 million borrowers carrying federal education debt. The issue is back in the national spotlight as changes to the Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, Plan ended, requiring millions of borrowers to find a new way to repay their federal student loans.

For families with children approaching college, the uncertainty underscores a different question: What if students could reduce or even avoid some college debt before graduating from high school?

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) Early College program is helping their students do exactly that.

A $67,000 Head Start

At Grand River Prep, an NHA partner-school in Grand Rapids, Mich., students can earn college credits, career credentials, and even an associate degree through the school's Early College partnership with Davenport University.

Tuition, fees, and books are covered through the program. Based on Davenport's current published undergraduate tuition rate, the value of a two-year associate degree can total approximately $67,000.

Felicia Pope, who works with Davenport University's Early College partnerships, said the program can put students in a very different financial position when they enter adulthood.

"You can be 18, 19 years old, you have an associate degree, you have the entry-level position in the field, without any student loans," Pope said.

Students can use that degree to begin working in their chosen field or continue toward a bachelor's degree with a significant amount of college coursework already completed. "You're halfway through your degree, saved a ton of time, a ton of money," Pope said.

Nine of NHA's high schools have an Early College program. During the 2024-25 school year, 565 students earned 5,186 college credits, saving an estimated $1.12 million in college tuition.

For NHA, the opportunity is about making college more accessible while preparing students for what comes next.

Koree Woodward, NHA Director of High Schools, says Early College is a natural extension of NHA's mission to prepare students for life after graduation.

"The program makes college feel more attainable for families who may not have otherwise seen it as an accessible option," Woodward said. "It helps students develop the knowledge, habits, character, and sense of responsibility needed for lifelong learning, college success, and meaningful careers."

College With a Support System

The financial savings are only part of the Early College model.

Students gradually transition into college-level work, beginning with one college course per semester during 10th grade before increasing their coursework in their junior and senior years.

Pope calls it a "soft launch into college."

Davenport advisors work directly with students on applications, degree pathways, scheduling, and course selection. Grand River Prep advisors provide another layer of support, helping students monitor grades, manage college expectations, and stay on track.

Aamir Hollowell sees that support firsthand.

"Every week, you have a meeting with your advisor to help you stay on track," she said. "They just keep checking up on you."

Grand River Prep Early College Advisor Jayme McWain said students get the independence of college without having to navigate the experience alone.

"For them to have kind of a safety net and a support system built in is a really great feature of that program," McWain said. "It creates so much more access and skill building."

From College Credit to Career

In addition to the tuition savings, students can leave high school with college experience, career opportunities, and potentially two years of college already completed.

For some students, that head start can translate directly into a career.

Grand River Prep graduate Kennah Kalele earned an associate degree in medical assisting through Early College and is now pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Nursing at Grand Valley State University.

"I don't have to take any gen eds in the college that I'm going to, and I'm even ahead in some aspects of my nursing degree," Kalele said.

Her associate degree also helped her begin gaining professional experience. Kalele works part time as a medical transport technician while continuing her education.

For McWain, the value is clear.

"Anytime you can help someone get free college when the price is off the charts, that's a great thing," she said.

And for families like Ciara Selden-Ruffin's, it offers the opportunity for her children to start their futures with a college education rather than a tuition bill.

About National Heritage Academies:

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) was founded in 1995 with families in mind and the belief that every child deserves an education that builds knowledge and character. Today, NHA supports 105 tuition-free, partner-schools across nine states, serving more than 65,000 K-12 students through rigorous academics and Moral Focus™ programming. NHA

ST. LOUIS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nearly 40 years after Illinois alternative rock trio Lucky Mary Blonde disbanded, the band's long-lost 1988 live recording is being released worldwide today on major streaming services as the album Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! — completing one of the most unlikely journeys in the history of the group's music.
releases.title: Two Forgotten Cassettes, One Musical Miracle: Lucky Mary Blonde Releases Lost 1988 Live Album Today
releases.body:
Nearly 40 years after the band disbanded, an extraordinary discovery, a second forgotten cassette and advances in AI-assisted audio technology brought one of the group's last performances back to life

ST. LOUIS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nearly 40 years after Illinois alternative rock trio Lucky Mary Blonde disbanded, the band's long-lost 1988 live recording is being released worldwide today on major streaming services as the album Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! — completing one of the most unlikely journeys in the history of the group's music.

Lucky Mary Blonde emerged from the fertile Midwest alternative and college rock scene of the late 1980s. The trio's album Let the Moonlight Burn was released in December 1987 and climbed Midwest college radio charts the following year. The band performed at venues from Chicago to Memphis and opened for national acts before unexpectedly breaking up in late 1988.

The recordings that would eventually become the new live album began as private cassette tapes made directly from the sound board and stage microphones during one of the band's final performances in Carbondale, Illinois in 1988. They were never released publicly, never intended to become an album and, after the show, were immediately forgotten.

Nearly four decades later, one cassette was discovered by a friend of the band and ultimately sent to drummer John Baldus, based in St. Louis, Missouri. Baldus began experimenting with modern AI-assisted audio technology to clean up the recordings. AI technology made it possible to break down the aging two-track recording into multiple, individual vocal and instrumental stems. Separating the stems was only the beginning, some instruments and vocals were still stubbornly intertwined, and Baldus spent months repairing and working through the recordings piece by piece.

Baldus eventually moved the restoration into professional recording studios with engineers in St. Louis and Richmond, Virginia. The project ultimately became a year-long effort.

As the first cassette was processed in St. Louis, however, a serious problem emerged. Elements of the performance were missing, including portions of the guitar, backing vocals and the audience microphones that originally captured the energy of the concert.

"It was frustrating," Baldus recalled. "We knew there was something special in the performance, but important pieces were simply gone. I remember lamenting to the guys how difficult the audio was to work with and wished there was somehow another better copy of the tape."

That prompted bassist Jerry Tilk, based in Virginia, to scour hundreds of old cassettes sitting in storage for decades. After a painstaking search, he hit the jackpot: another missing cassette from the same 1988 show.

Tilk immediately sent it to the Richmond studio to be digitized. What happened next bordered on miraculous. The Richmond engineer reported that the second cassette was in good condition, but it seemed to contain only backing vocals, audience microphones and portions of the guitar.

For the band, it was a jaw-dropping revelation. The missing elements from the first cassette were not missing at all, they had been recorded on the second cassette. The two recordings contained complementary channels from the same performance. By digitally combining them, the restoration team could reconstruct the complete recorded show.

"At that moment, we realized this coincidence and chain of events were far too great to ignore.  We were on a mission now to complete this project.  After four decades, it really was amazing to put lost pieces of a puzzle back together," said Baldus.

Tilk long remembered that some of Lucky Mary Blonde's best songwriting came after the release of its first album. "I regretted that our post-album writing was never recorded. When we found and heard the tapes, we realized those songs actually had been recorded, they were just lost. It simply became a matter of restoring the recording to original concert quality. This is one positive aspect of AI. We had an opportunity to resurrect these great songs."

The result is a 16-song live album featuring 11 previously unreleased songs alongside five songs originally recorded for Let the Moonlight Burn .

For guitarist and songwriter Todd Baxter, hearing the performances again was about more than recovering old recordings. Now based in Florida, Baxter commented, "I hadn't heard these songs in 40 years. They capture a period of life of youth, tremendous energy and zeal, and listening to how well we performed them live, I just want to go back and pat these young guys on the back and tell them 'well done boys.'" Baxter wrote all of the songs on the live album and remains a prolific songwriter today.

Sometimes a lost recording is found. Sometimes it is found twice. And nearly 40 years later, the technology finally exists to hear what was there all along.

The complete Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! album is being released worldwide today on Apple Music, Spotify, Amazon Music and other major digital music services.

www.luckymaryblonde.com

Lucky Mary Blonde

Email: luckymaryblonde@gmail.com

Website: www.luckymaryblonde.com

About Lucky Mary Blonde

Lucky Mary Blonde was an Illinois-based alternative rock trio that gained a loyal following throughout the Midwest college music circuit during the late 1980s. Following the release of Let the Moonlight Burn in 1987, the band toured extensively before disbanding in late 1988. The Lucky Mary Blonde LIVE! album documents one of the group's final performances and preserves a chapter in independent college rock history.
