releases.title: Storyteller Overland Announces STO Fest: Where Overlanding Meets Live Music
releases.body:
Four days of live music, vehicles, and desert adventure in the high desert of Johnson Valley, October 15–18, 2026.

BIRMINGHAM, Ala., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- There's a reason a campfire and a concert feel like the same instinct. Gather. Listen. Connect. Stay longer than you planned. Storyteller Overland has built an entire festival around that overlap.

STO Fest is a four-day gathering in Johnson Valley, California, built around overlanding, live music, and the outdoors. It grew out of the brand's community of vehicle owners, but the gate swings both ways — STO Fest welcomes anyone ready to say yes to their next grand adventure, whether they show up in a fully kitted rig or have never set foot off-pavement.

Overlanding and live music pull from the same crowd: people who go find it instead of waiting for it to come to them. STO Fest puts them in the same place, at the same time, for the first time.

Presented by Gibson Guitars and Mercedes-Benz, the festival features two bands each night on the Gibson Stage, Thursday through Saturday, with headline sets from Ozomatli, Blackberry Smoke, and The Struts, plus a special appearance from The Dusty Bunch, a musical collective made up of Storyteller Overland's own team members — including CEO, Neil Grimmer.

Thursday, October 15

Headliner Ozomatli brings three decades of Grammy-winning genre fusion blending Latin, hip-hop, funk, and reggae, rooted in Los Angeles. Opening the night is The Western States, a rising force in the LA country scene built for high-energy sets that span classic country, honky-tonk, and alt-country.

Friday, October 16

Southern rock mainstays Blackberry Smoke headline, fresh off their latest album Be Right Here and a #1 Billboard Americana/Folk chart debut. Blues-rock guitarist Jared James Nichols opens, pick-less playing style and all.

Saturday, October 17

Glam-rock powerhouse The Struts close out the weekend known for arena-sized hits like "Could Have Been Me" and "Body Talks." All-female Black Sabbath tribute act Black Sabbitch opens, fresh off their live album Unrest in the West.

"Our community has always known how to gather around a campfire, a trailhead, a hot meal after a long adventure," said Josh Ehren, Chief Marketing Officer of Storyteller Overland. "STO Fest just gives those connections a stage and a lineup. It's the same incredible people, the same reason we all got into this in the first place, we just added the live music."

Beyond the music, STO Fest runs full days of programming. Learning Labs give guests hands-on skills sessions all weekend. Vendor Village showcases gear, mods, and makers. Attendees can get behind the wheel with demo drives in Storyteller vehicles and LiveWire electric motorcycles, or meet the Mojave mini donkeys who call the high desert home. Food, water, showers, and restroom facilities are on-site all weekend. Campfires and conversations round out each night, the space where the community connections really happen.

STO Fest 2026 runs October 15–18 at Lasertown in Johnson Valley, California. Tickets and full event details are available at stofest.com.

About Storyteller:

Storyteller Overland is widely regarded as the world's most all-encompassing and highest quality overland vehicle manufacturer. Launched in 2018 by a dedicated group of automotive and outdoor enthusiasts, Storyteller has always believed that capability is only half the story — what matters most is how that capability lets its community live and experience life exactly the way they want to. That belief drives the mission: to inspire and equip a growing community of adventurers with the proper gear, resources, and mindset to "live free, explore endlessly and tell better stories." Storyteller is honored to serve its STORYTELLERS owners group, a diverse, kind, helpful, and inclusive gathering of rugged individualists drawn together by a shared belief that life's greatest luxury is saying "yes" to the next grand adventure. Based in Birmingham, Alabama, the Soul of Storyteller is the unique connection that exists between the stellar group of people who design, engineer, and build our vehicles and gear, and the incredible people who experience them.

releases.title: Amuze Acquires Sweet Attractions, Strengthening California Operations and Family Entertainment Capabilities
releases.body:
Acquisition brings together local customer relationships, regional service expertise and national equipment and merchandise resources

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Amuze, a national amusement equipment and route-services platform, today announced the acquisition of the operations of Sweet Attractions, a California-based amusement operator serving family entertainment centers, restaurants, bars and other entertainment venues. The transaction also brings affiliated Paramount Amusement Group operations into Amuze. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Sweet Attractions provides equipment installation, operation and ongoing service across arcade games, cranes, redemption attractions and photo booths. The business is growing throughout California and expanding into markets outside the state.

Amuze plans to build its coordinated California operations around a Fresno-based hub while maintaining local field-service coverage. Integration will prioritize customer and employee continuity, shared resources and support for Sweet Attractions' expansion.

Amuze's vertically integrated platform includes Pipeline Games, which designs and manufactures redemption, crane and merchandiser games, and Quality Plush, a supplier of licensed and generic plush merchandise. These businesses will provide Sweet Attractions with equipment, plush and merchandising support, helping venues deliver engaging entertainment experiences.

"Sweet Attractions has always been about taking care of our customers and finding the right entertainment mix for each location," said Mark Knepper, President of Sweet Attractions. "Joining Amuze gives us more equipment choices and deeper service support while preserving the relationships and personal attention our customers value."

"Sweet Attractions is a strong fit with our broader California growth plans," said Stephen Lahti, co-CEO, Finance + M&A. "Mark and his team bring valuable customer relationships, hands-on operating knowledge and a commitment to service. Bringing those strengths together with Amuze's equipment, sourcing and regional support capabilities will help us serve customers more effectively and grow with them."

Knepper will continue working with the business, supporting customer relationships, the team's transition and continued growth.

About Amuze

Amuze combines venue-based entertainment operations with equipment development, sourcing and distribution.

About Sweet Attractions

Sweet Attractions installs, operates and services amusement equipment for family entertainment centers, restaurants, bars and other venues.

releases.title: Hisense Unveils New C3 Projector Family for Immersive Home Entertainment
releases.body:
QINGDAO, China, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hisense, a leading brand in global consumer electronics and home appliances, is expanding its home entertainment portfolio with the new C3 projector family, designed to bring cinema-sized entertainment into everyday life. Showcased at IFA 2026, the C3 Ultra and C3 Ultra Max are launching across global markets this September, with the C3 Pro set to follow.

From movie nights and live sports to gaming with friends, the C3 family is designed around the moments people want to make bigger. With projection sizes of up to 300 inches, powerful brightness and immersive sound, it transforms living rooms, bedrooms and other spaces into flexible entertainment destinations, giving users more freedom to enjoy the big-screen experience at home.

The C3 Ultra delivers 4,000 ANSI lumens and a 5,000:1 contrast ratio with an IRIS Lens, combining vivid visuals with gaming-enhanced performance. Its Devialet-tuned audio system, featuring co-engineered hardware and a built-in subwoofer, delivers deep bass and immersive surround sound for a more engaging entertainment experience.

For users seeking greater visual power and responsiveness, the C3 Ultra Max delivers 5,000 ANSI lumens, 5,000:1 contrast with an IRIS Lens and 1ms ultra-low latency, supporting dynamic entertainment across movies, sports and gaming. Enhanced by Devialet audio, it completes the experience with rich, immersive sound that matches its high-performance visuals.

The C3 Pro brings the C3 experience to more users with 3,000 ANSI lumens, 5,000:1 contrast with an IRIS Lens and Devialet-tuned audio with a built-in subwoofer, offering a compelling balance of performance and value.

Together, the C3 Ultra, C3 Ultra Max and C3 Pro further enrich the C3 family, offering consumers a broader range of choices to suit different entertainment needs and spaces. Earlier this year, the C3 has undergone Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and product carbon footprint (PCF) verification by SGS, supporting transparent evaluation of environmental impact across the product lifecycle and reflecting Hisense's commitment to transparent product-level environmental assessment.

With the C3 family, Hisense continues to bring more immersive entertainment into everyday spaces, making it easier for people to turn ordinary moments at home into experiences worth sharing.

releases.body:
BEIJING, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Orange Lion Sports, founded by Alibaba Group, has unveiled Smartshot 2.0, the upgraded version of its AI sports solution, at the Sports Services exhibition during the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS), held September 9-13 in Beijing.

From six-camera Hawk-Eye electronic line calling and AI-powered auto-directing to the debut of a voice-interactive smart ball machine, the company is advancing a cost-effective approach to inclusive sports technology, bridging the gap between professional competition and mass participation to "make sports simple."

At CIFTIS 2026, Orange Lion Sports' replica tennis court became a focal point. Smartshot 2.0 introduced an upgraded electronic line calling system designed to address long-standing disputes over line calls at amateur tennis events. As soon as the ball lands, a large screen provides instant in/out calls and can announce "IN/OUT" at adjustable volumes. The system supports smoother, fairer amateur competitions at a low marginal cost without requiring additional labor.

AI commentary and auto-directing cut broadcasting costs of up to hundreds of thousands of yuan, making high-quality broadcasts more accessible. AI-powered robots are becoming a valuable complement to traditional sports coaching.

In Orange Lion Sports' roadmap, Smartshot will work with the smart ball machine to interact with trainees through natural language, instantly adjusting ball settings, placement and speed to create personalized training programs and help beginners improve more efficiently.

Leveraging Alibaba's technology capabilities, Smartshot has integrated the Tongyi Qwen large language model to launch what it describes as the industry's first "AI Tournament Assistant" in the first half of 2026. The assistant understands natural-language instructions and parses PDF regulations, enabling scheduling and registration to be completed in minutes. Smartshot now offers pricing at one-tenth that of comparable offerings.

"Our goal is to find the optimal balance between precision and cost control, consistent with our long-standing technical philosophy. We reject expensive professional premiums and pursue cost-effective, inclusive technology," said Peng Wei, CTO of Orange Lion Sports.

Since its launch, Smartshot has been deployed across more than 500 courts and expanded into overseas markets, with installations in Europe, Australia, Hong Kong SAR, and Taiwan region. Looking ahead, as AI advances in sports, Orange Lion Sports' approach to balancing commercial value with accessibility aims to make professional-grade smart equipment more affordable and accessible worldwide.

releases.title: Gold House Honors the 2026 Multicultural Emmy® Nominees at the One House Toast to the Emmys®
releases.body:
Red Carpet Photos (Credit: Andrew Ge)

Party Photos (Credit: Duke Winn)

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Gold House, the cultural platform shaping global opportunity, honored the multicultural nominees of the 78th Emmy® Awards at its annual One House Toast to the Emmys® on Thursday, September 10, at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills. The One House Toast is a celebration of multicultural excellence in television and media, convening over 200 creatives and artists, including Emmy-nominees from BEEF, Bridgerton, The Pitt, Abbott Elementary, and others, as well as industry leaders and creators. This year's event was made possible by presenting sponsor Chase Sapphire Reserve for BusinessSM, exclusive automotive partner Genesis Motor America, lead media partner Variety, Asian entertainment streamer Viki, and WME.

Netflix's BEEF had another historic awards season with 16 nominations, including nods for executive producer, writer, and director Lee Sung Jin, Charles Melton, and Youn Yuh-jung. Their nominations are joined by Sepideh Moafi (The Pitt), who became the first Iranian woman nominated for an Emmy, and members of The Pitt's cast, including Kristin Villanueva and Amielynn Abellera.

Notable guests included Lee Sung Jin, The Pitt's executive producer Simran Baidwan, Street Fighter director Kitao Sakurai, Creative Arts Emmy winner Sang Kim, Seoyeon Jang, Dante Basco, Dolly de Leon, Will Yun Lee, Leah Lewis, Monica Padman, Tal Anderson, Gurinder Chadha, Albert Cheng, Justin Chien, Hanelle M. Culpepper, Percy Daggs IV, Fiona Dourif, Edwin Lee Gibson, Chin Han, Ryan Alexander Holmes, Scott and Mark Hoying, Madison Hu, Gia Kim, Ken Kirby, Hiro Koda, Raymond Lee, Michelle Mao, Dana Ledoux Miller, Minnie Mills, Daniella Monet, Yoko Okumura, Monica Padman, Brandon Perea, Huma Qureshi, Salli Richardson-Whitfield, Saagar Shaikh, Joanna Sotomora, Regan To, Kristin Villanueva, Cole Walliser, Janet Yang, Hanbit Yi, Phinehas Yoon, and many others.

Throughout the evening, guests enjoyed a custom portrait studio presented by Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business, an exclusive photo experience featuring the all-new Genesis GV90 from Genesis Motor America, and a custom BEEF-themed food-and-beverage experience presented by WME. Variety returns as the Toast's lead media partner for the third year.

"Gold House has meant a lot to my journey and BEEF's journey. These events are fun, but it's also a place of true community. Having people here to support makes a difference; you never know who you'll run into or what conversation turns into what. I'm really grateful that we get to do this and do it together," said Lee.

"In a week when several whistleblowers are warning that new technologies can decimate our species by the end of the decade, it is hybridized, undefinable-by-a-single-genre art like BEEF that reminds us of what most makes us human, of our fallacies, and our right to exist. On platforms and spaces, when people try to flatten us into one thing, it is polymathical, multi-skilled creators who don't just write, who don't just produce, who don't just direct, but do it all to create historic pieces of art that remind us what it takes to get this far. And it is in our own lives that we're reminded that when things get toughest, we take our broken hearts and turn them into art. That reminds us why we are still here—and why we must stay." said Bing Chen, Executive Chairman and CEO of Gold House.

Jazz Tangcay, Senior Artisans Editor at Variety, ended the remarks by urging the crowd to "[p]lease keep telling your stories because… it means so much to see our faces on [television]."

The One House Toast continues Gold House's commitment to advancing Asian Pacific representation in entertainment. This year's celebration builds on the organization's Gold List for Film and Gold List for TV honoring Asian Pacific excellence, and its ongoing industry-leading consultation, investment, and marketing partnerships across film and television to ensure opening weekend success. Its platform now includes the recently launched Gold House Studios, which provides development and financing for Asian Pacific-led films, series, and IP. Through these initiatives, Gold House continues to empower and enable affirming and authentic portrayals of Asian Pacific and multicultural voices in front of and behind the camera.

For further inquiries, please contact goldhouse@havasformula.com.

Gold House is the cultural platform shaping global opportunity. We foster spaces where established and emerging makers gather to amplify their impact. We shape public perceptions by consulting on, investing in, and marketing society-defining media properties. We create new economies by backing the boldest entrepreneurs and scaling them internationally.

By fueling unity, visibility, and economic mobility, success becomes our shared world. With roots in Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, and Singapore, Gold House operates with the heart of a nonprofit and the reach of a world-class enterprise.

We don't just change culture—we make it.

To learn more, visit goldhouse.org or follow @GoldHouseCo on Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, Threads, and LinkedIn.

releases.body:
APJ raises over $700,000 to support education and community-led initiatives in Haiti

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /CNW/ -- Board Chair Natasha Koifman and powerhouse board members George Stroumboulopoulos, Kardinal Offishall, Amanda Brugel and more, hosted the 18th annual Artists for Peace and Justice (APJ) Gala this evening at the Windsor Arms Hotel, the landmark venue that hosted the organization's first Toronto gala. Recognized as one of the city's most anticipated philanthropic events, the gala raised over $700,000 to support education and community-led initiatives in Haiti.

Since its founding, APJ has raised over $37 million and supported more than 32,000 students through access to quality education, healthcare, and opportunity.

The evening honoured three remarkable women whose careers and philanthropy embody the spirit of Artists for Peace and Justice: Andrea Martin, Emily Hampshire and Jann Arden.

Natasha Koifman, Chair of the Board, opened the evening with remarks on APJ's evolving mission, from rebuilding after the 2010 earthquake to using education as a lifeline for children caught in Haiti's escalating gang crisis today. "Believing in a better future is no longer enough. We have to be the lifeline that helps pull these children out of danger. The situation in Haiti has changed dramatically since APJ was founded, and while we haven't been able to return to the country because of the ongoing crisis, our commitment to the children we serve has never wavered. Today, education is not just about preparing young Haitians to rebuild their country in the future - it is a lifeline in the present, giving children a safe place to learn, hope, and build a path beyond the violence. The humanitarian crisis and the daily struggle to survive are unimaginable, and that makes our work more urgent than ever."

Evening Highlights

  • Setting the tone for the night, a buzzy red carpet welcomed a special group of guests: adoptable puppies from Project Paws, who posed for photos with talent and guests to help spotlight pets in need of a home.
  • APJ Board Members George Stroumboulopoulos and Kardinal Offishall returned as emcees for the evening, welcoming guests and expressing gratitude for the continued generosity that fuels APJ's mission.
  • Rick Mercer, a past APJ Award recipient, presented Emily Hampshire with the Canadian Artists for Peace and Justice Changemaker Award, celebrating her work using her platform to raise awareness around mental health and queer experiences. Hampshire's Schitt's Creek co-star Noah Reid took the stage after to perform a special song in her honour.
  • Amanda Brugel, last year's Changemaker Award recipient and a new APJ board member, presented Jann Arden with the Artists for Peace and Justice Impact Award, in recognition of her decades-long commitment to philanthropy, humanitarian causes and giving back to communities in need.
  • George Stroumboulopoulos presented Andrea Martin with the Global Artists for Peace and Justice Award, honouring her longstanding commitment to humanitarian causes and her dedication to creating positive change. Martin surprised the room with an impromptu rap after accepting the honour.
  • Norman Gaudet, former head of the Toronto French School, took the stage to announce an extraordinary milestone: inspired by Wes Hall, he created a full international scholarship after discovering APJ's mission last year. He proudly shared that Schnaider, the Academy's scholarship recipient, has officially arrived in Canada and is settling in with his host family, a testament to the importance of giving these children new opportunities outside of Haiti.
  • The live auction, led by The Auctionista, was one of the night's most electric moments, as guests bid fast and furiously on an extraordinary collection of art. Celebrated artists Russell Young, Tyler Shields and Mr. Brainwash, courtesy of Taglialatella Gallery, along with Anthony Ricciardi, saw their work draw serious heat in the room. Young, in attendance for the evening, unveiled a truly one-of-a-kind charitable commission: a family portrait shot by CAFA winner Renata Kaveh and rendered in his signature diamond dust technique, destined to become a cherished heirloom for its new owner.
  • The energy hit a fever pitch over a rare Birkin, courtesy of Carly Jordan, sparking a spirited bidding war between guests determined not to leave empty-handed. Also up for grabs: travel packages from Air Canada, a culinary evening at Michelin-starred Enigma Yorkville, and two once-in-a-lifetime experiences, the Bautista Impact Summit in the Bahamas and a getaway to Hightail Ranch in Montana.
  • Mandy Rennehan and Lauren Ferraro led a lively final Fund the Need moment, courtesy of Dean Davidson, with guests raising their hands to purchase 20 special bracelets to support some of the highest-need areas of APJ's Academy for Peace and Justice.
  • Haitian music icon and long-time APJ supporter Paul Beaubrun closed the night with an emotional performance.

Generous sponsors for this year's event include: Air Canada, 2Fifteen by DBS Developments, Audi, and Forest Hill Group.

ABOUT ARTISTS FOR PEACE AND JUSTICE

Artists for Peace and Justice (APJ) is a non-profit organization that encourages peace and social justice and addresses issues of poverty around the world. APJ's immediate goal is to serve the poorest communities in Haiti with programs in education, healthcare, and dignity through the arts. The organization is committed to long-term, sustainable development in direct partnership with the Haitian people. APJ partners with St. Luke's Foundation in Haiti. To learn more, visit www.apjnow.org or follow @artistsforpeace on Instagram and Twitter.

ABOUT NKPR

NKPR was started in 2002 by Natasha Koifman to combine two passions: shining a spotlight on stories of substance and supporting causes that are making a difference around the world. Over the past 24 years, NKPR has established itself as a highly regarded full-service public relations, artist management and digital agency with offices in Toronto, New York and Los Angeles, representing over 40 national and international brands and supporting charitable organizations like Artists for Peace and Justice. For more information, visit NKPR on social media @natashankpr or at www.nkpr.net.

releases.body:
Debuting during the 2026 football season on a streaming service, the new campaign marks 120 years of Coldwell Banker affiliated agents handing families the keys to the places where their lives unfold.

MADISON, N.J., September 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coldwell Banker Real Estate LLC today announced The Letter, a new national advertising campaign premiering on select Thursday evenings this fall during football season on a streaming service. The campaign follows one family across three generations in the same home, celebrating the central role the home played in a family's life in a letter drafted to wish the new owner well. 

As the Coldwell Banker® brand celebrates its 120th anniversary this year, the campaign honors all of the little moments that add up to make a house into a home: the dinner parties, holiday celebrations, graduations, visitors, and new additions. The 60-second spot tells one family's story across more than 30 years, while a series of original 15-second spots highlight individual moments in the family's life – and the home that served as the setting. It's a vantage point Coldwell Banker has held since 1906, across generations of families and the agents who walked them through the door.

"The Letter isn't about the value of a house in dollars, cents or square footage. It's about the value of life that happens inside," said Brandon Newman, Vice President of Marketing, Coldwell Banker Real Estate LLC. "Homes are an ecosystem for your life, so we built our campaign the same way. There is no single hero spot with cut downs. Instead, there's a whole life that takes place in this world we have created, which celebrates the real lives people live in their homes every day." 

Capturing three decades of one family in the same home shaped every production choice, from casting to cameras. The Coldwell Banker team cast the family at multiple ages, spent up to six hours a day on makeup to age or de-age actors, and evolved wardrobe and production design through the decades. Three cameras marked the passage of time, including a 16mm film camera for the earliest era.

"Much of the conversation around real estate today is about technology, listings, transactions and market conditions, but buying or selling a home has always been about more than that," said Mary Lee Blaylock, President of Coldwell Banker Affiliates. "Homes are incredibly emotional, and after 120 years in the business, Coldwell Banker has seen all of it. Coldwell Banker affiliated agents don't just close transactions. They hand people the keys to the places where their lives unfold. The physical letter is a beautiful way to conceptualize the ending of one family's chapter in a home by welcoming another, reminding us what a home really is."

The campaign was created with Siltanen & Partners, directed by Alice Gu. You can view all the spots in The Letter here and find behind the scenes content here to discover the story, inspiration and creative thinking behind The Letter and "120 Years of Home," the full year campaign celebrating the role home plays in shaping our lives.

But another asset can have an enormous influence on how those retirement years are lived: muscle. The good news is that it is never too late to start investing in physical strength.
releases.title: Your Muscles May Be One of Your Most Valuable Retirement Assets
releases.body:
Fitness & Finance co-founders explain why preserving muscle should be part of the retirement-planning conversation

FREDERICKSBURG, Va., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- When it comes to retirement planning, most people focus on how much to save and where to invest it. But another asset can have an enormous influence on how those retirement years are lived: muscle. Maintaining strength and muscle mass as we age can help support mobility, balance and independence—factors that can influence both quality of life and healthcare needs later in life. The good news is that it is never too late to start investing in physical strength.

"We spend decades building a financial portfolio for retirement, but we should be building our physical portfolio at the same time," said Jennifer Scherer, co-founder of the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, registered dietitian, medical exercise specialist, certified personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of Fredericksburg Fitness Studio. "Muscle is one of the assets that helps protect our ability to move, remain independent and enjoy the life we worked so hard to build. Financial longevity means much less if our physical health doesn't allow us to enjoy it."

While people are focused on building their financial portfolio, they may be overlooking their physical one. Age-related losses in muscle and strength can affect mobility, balance and independence and are associated with greater risk of falls and hospitalization. Those health consequences can also create significant expenses during retirement.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), starting at around 30, our bodies naturally begin losing muscle mass. We lose 3-5% of muscle mass every decade, and while that change may happen slowly, it adds up, leaving people with weakened strength. Sarcopenia, the gradual loss of muscle mass, increases the risks of falls, broken bones, and hospitalization. These are all things that are going to dip into the financial savings that someone has accumulated for retirement.

A study published in the Journal of Frailty & Aging reports that the hospitalization costs associated with sarcopenia are around $40 billion. They report that those with the condition are more likely to be hospitalized, with it costing each person an average of over $2,300 per year. Add to that the costs that people incur outside of the hospital due to broken bones, falls, and any hired help they need due to the lack of independence. It adds up to a financial burden that people may have been able to avoid if they had worked on maintaining muscle mass over the years.

The key is to start working on building and maintaining muscle mass, regardless of what age someone is at. It's never too late to take this issue on. According to the NIH, 30% of adults over the age of 70 have trouble walking, getting up from a chair, or climbing stairs. They report that such mobility issues not only lead to a loss of independence, but are also linked to higher rates of falls, chronic diseases, nursing home admissions, and mortality. They report that the big culprit is a loss of muscle mass, and that it can be slowed down by maintaining an active lifestyle.

Here are some tips to keep in mind to help slow the muscle-mass loss problem:

  • Get active no matter what age you are. Know that you can always start slow and build it up as you get stronger. Being physically active is crucial to healthier aging.
  • Ensure that your workout routine has you lifting weights and challenging yourself. It's important to get things in there like resistance exercises. Include progressive resistance training. Muscles need an appropriate challenge to adapt and remain strong. Resistance can come from weights, machines, bands or body weight, and the program should be appropriate for the individual's health, abilities and experience.
  • Be sure to get the right foods in your diet in order to build and maintain muscle. Getting enough protein is a must in order to build and maintain muscle mass over the years. Know how much you need per day and pay attention to ensure you get it. Prioritize adequate nutrition, particularly protein. Protein provides the amino acids needed to support muscle maintenance and repair, but individual needs vary based on age, health status and activity level.
  • If you have one day that you slip or one week where you falter on your new fitness plans, don't give up. Just start again. Too often, people throw in the towel and give up, rather than simply getting back at it. Working with someone, such as a coach or trainer, can help keep you on track.
  • Build a professional team. A qualified fitness or healthcare professional can assess physical function and help create an appropriate plan for maintaining strength and mobility, while a qualified financial professional can help prepare for the financial realities of retirement. Both plans should support the same goal: maintaining independence and quality of life for as long as possible.

"One of the biggest expenses in retirement can be needing help with the things you once did independently," said Jeff Smith, co-founder of Fitness & Finance Radio, financial planning expert, personal trainer, master-level Pilates instructor and founder of The Retirement Smith. "We can build a strong financial plan, but preserving the physical ability to enjoy those years is equally important. Financial planning and fitness planning have more in common than people realize: both benefit from starting early, being consistent and thinking long-term."

Smith and Scherer co-founded Fitness & Finance Radio to explore an often-overlooked connection: the relationship between physical health and financial health throughout the lifespan. Drawing on Scherer's expertise in nutrition, medical exercise and fitness and Smith and Scherer are a married couple who co-founded the Fitness & Finance Radio podcast, where they come together to share their fields of expertise. The information focuses on offering a mix of nutrition, healthy lifestyle, and financial retirement planning strategies. Listeners can tune in to hear the duo discuss the issues and gain advice and insight that may help them now and in their retirement years. The Fitness & Finance Radio podcast is available for free on YouTube. Recent episode topics cover credibility, stress, funding adult children, saving money and losing weight on vacation, obesity and preventative care, and more. To get more information and listen, visit the site at: https://www.youtube.com/@fitnessfinanceradio?app=desktop 

About Fitness & Finance Radio

Fitness & Finance Radio is a podcast produced by the married couple Jeff Smith and Jennifer Scherer. Smith is a financial planning expert and founder of The Retirement Smith, located in Fredericksburg, Va. Scherer is a registered dietitian, fitness expert, and founder of Fredericksburg Fitness Studio. To get more information and listen to the podcast, visit the site at: https://www.youtube.com/@fitnessfinanceradio?app=desktop or https://fitnessfinancepro.com/index.html

VANCOUVER, BC, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- After five years of work, six singles, and a rollout that has steadily built him into one of the most electrifying new voices on the West Coast, ALPHA CENTAURI is here with his full debut album, 'The Future Right Now,' out now via Rogue Planet. "Never Be," "Grow," "Get Your Money Up," "I'll Fly," "Higher Up" and "We Rise" each landed with their own moment in the spotlight. The ten-track album is a genre blending, funk soaked, Afrobeat charged, jazz-tinged hip-hop statement recorded entirely live off the floor with his eight-piece band.

ALPHA's own story is exactly the kind that makes a debut like this hit harder. Trained and licensed as a lawyer in Zimbabwe, he walked away from a secure, respected career to chase the thing he could never actually let go of, music. It started long before law school, back when he was 13 years old breakdancing with his crew, Blade Squad, at pageants and basketball halftime shows. "I took what I understood from dancing, rhythm and movement, and turned it into rap," he says. "I tapped into my background in English literature and realized, I know how to write poems. I understand rhythm. Maybe I can do this."

'The Future Right Now' is built entirely around that idea: self belief as fuel, motivation as philosophy, the present moment as the only place the future actually gets built. "Everything I do today, everything I did all these years, has brought me here, because my future was always in the present," ALPHA says. "We Rise," was originally written back in 2014 while he was finishing his law degree. "Expect Us" channels real testimony, drawn directly from ALPHA's own experience as a practicing lawyer in Zimbabwe supporting the movement built by activist Evan Mawarire against corruption and injustice. And "Never Be" is a full display of technical firepower, stacking wordplay, literary references and mythology into bars built to be replayed just to catch everything packed inside them.

That live reputation has already put ALPHA on some seriously big stages. He has shared bills with Method Man & Redman, Ja Rule, Chali 2na and Cut Chemist of Jurassic 5, The OBGMs, Moka Only and Tanika Charles, and lit up major festival stages across Western Canada.

releases.body:
Spotify I YouTube I Instagram I TikTok

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Toronto-based producer, DJ, and beatmaker Ladji Mouflet unveils "Hatuey," a warrior of a single that pulls its title and its spirit from one of Caribbean history's most defiant figures. Built on the hypnotic percussion and rolling low end that have become his signature, the track finds Ladji at his most physical, a record made for the dance floor that carries something much older underneath it.

The name is not incidental. Hatuey was a Taino Indigenous chief who led resistance against the Spanish conquistadors in the sixteenth century and was burned at the stake for it, choosing defiance rather than surrender. Through his mother's lineage, Ladji carries Taino heritage himself, and the parallel is intentional: a song about refusing to bend. The connection runs through the visuals too, with cover art weaving together Taino imagery and the tribal tattoos Ladji and his brother wear in tribute to that history.

Ladji built "Hatuey" the way he builds everything: alone in the studio at first, composing, producing, and arranging every layer himself before bringing in his family, team and label. The result sits at the intersection of baile and the wider electronic sounds he has spent years refining, hypnotic Afro percussion set against sleek, modern production.

That sound was shaped long before Ladji touched a fader. Raised between Harlem, the South Bronx and the Lower East Side of New York, he grew up inside a household built around rhythm. His mother, from the Dominican Republic, danced salsa on stages alongside Tito Puente and Celia Cruz. His father, Senegalese and Martinican, founded a dance and music school blending West African tradition with ballet and jazz.

That sound has already found a massive audience without a major. Ladji's breakout single "Baiana 2022" has passed 35 million streams and became an unofficial anthem of the last World Cup, shared by Tom Brady, Lamine Yamal and Wayne Rooney. "French Bossa Nova" followed with more than 44 million streams. Today Ladji reaches 1.5-2.2 million monthly listeners on Spotify and more than 350,000 followers across social platforms, all built independently through his own label, Alkebulan Records.

"Hatuey" arrives as the first single from Ladji's upcoming album, 'The Pilgrimage,' a journey back to himself, tracing his roots one track at a time and letting that heritage lead the record.

releases.title: As Live Nation Enters Its Busiest Week of the Year, New Global Report Reveals a Return to Real
releases.body:
New research spanning tens of thousands of fans worldwide explores why real-world experiences are gaining value as more of life moves online.

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This week, millions of fans will compare set-list predictions as merch lines wrap around venues and restaurants and bars fill before the show. Once the lights go down, they will share an experience that can only happen live.

In the U.S., it is expected to be the busiest week for Live Nation's fan attendance this year. The milestone reflects a much larger cultural shift playing out around the world. As more of life moves online, people are placing greater value on experiences that feel unmistakably real.

The Return to Real, a new global report from Live Nation for Brands, examines what is driving that shift and what it means for culture, commerce and brands. Drawing on multiple surveys of tens of thousands of fans worldwide, the research found that 93% of fans crave real experiences over digital ones, while 80% would rather spend on experiences than on things. Live music emerged as the world's favorite form of entertainment.

As technology becomes more deeply woven into everyday life, it is getting harder to tell what was made by a person, what was generated and what actually happened. At a concert, there is no question. The artist is on stage. You are in the room. Thousands of other people are experiencing the same thing alongside you.

"People can do almost everything from their phones now," says Russell Wallach, Global President, Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. "That's exactly why the things worth leaving home for matter more than ever. The brands building lasting loyalty are becoming part of those experiences."

For brands, that opportunity comes at an interesting moment for loyalty. While 66% of fans say they engaged with loyalty programs more than a year ago, 64% say they feel less loyal to brands, and 71% say loyalty programs feel the same. More than 9 in 10 say live music benefits would make them sign up for or switch loyalty programs.

Brands across industries are already responding.

Reserved by Spotify is using its digital platform to connect fans with live experiences. "There's just no replacement for the live music experience," says Jon Ostrow, Spotify's Head of Business Development, Live Music. "Obviously, we're a digital platform, and we've got thousands who are thinking deeply daily about how to create a more robust digital environment, but we're starting to see how digital and live can go hand in hand, creating a better experience both offline and online."

Mastercard sees exclusive access becoming a new form of loyalty. "As people place greater value on real-world experiences, access has become one of the most powerful forms of loyalty," says Monica Biagiotti, EVP, Global Consumer Marketing and Sponsorships. "Whether it's traveling to experience a bucket-list concert, discovering a new destination through music, or sharing an unforgettable night with friends and family, these experiences create lasting memories. Through the Priceless Platform and our partnership with Live Nation, we're making those moments more accessible for millions of cardholders around the world."

Lowe's is extending loyalty beyond the store. "Products may bring someone through the door, but experiences are often what make them want to come back," says Amanda Bailey, VP of Customer Marketing and Loyalty. "Music connects people through emotion. Almost everyone has a song, an artist or a concert that means something to them. Live music gives us a chance to surprise and delight our loyalty members with experiences and benefits that make those moments even better."

Across industries, brands are finding new ways to make live experiences part of how they build customer relationships. The Return to Real explores what fans value about experiences they can see, feel and share for themselves, and what that shift means for brands.

Download The Return to Real here.

Live Nation Entertainment (NYSE: LYV) is the world's leading live entertainment company comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.

WINDSOR, Conn., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Many Americans approaching retirement spend more time scrolling social media in a single week than they spend planning for retirement in an entire year. releases.title: LIMRA: Many Americans Spend More Time on Social Media in a Week Than on Retirement Planning All Year
releases.body:
Nearly 6 in 10 pre-retirees say they feel highly prepared for retirement. But new LIMRA research finds that confidence often outpaces action — 76% either have no written plan or have spent fewer than five hours on one in the past year. 

WINDSOR, Conn., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Many Americans approaching retirement spend more time scrolling social media in a single week than they spend planning for retirement in an entire year. That is one of the more striking takeaways from new research from LIMRA's 2026 Retirement Income Readiness Report, which finds a wide gap between how prepared Americans feel for retirement and how much they are actually doing to prepare.

Nearly six in ten pre-retirees (59%) — workers age 45 and older who plan to retire within 10 years — rate themselves highly prepared for retirement, and 88% say they have thought about how they'll generate income once they stop working. Yet that confidence and those good intentions are not always reflected in recent planning activity. Half of pre-retirees (50%) either have no written retirement plan or have one they haven't recently updated, and 76% have either no plan or spent fewer than five hours developing, reviewing, or updating one in the past year.

"Most Americans approaching retirement genuinely feel prepared, and that confidence matters," said Tina Beckwith, Chief Marketing Officer, LIMRA. "But confidence and planning activity do not always align. Many people who feel prepared have not put a written plan in place or have not revisited one recently. Thinking about retirement is a good start, but having a plan and actively engaging in the planning process can strengthen people's sense of preparedness for retirement."

A Week of Scrolling vs. a Year of Planning

The scale of the gap comes into focus with a simple comparison. More than a quarter of pre-retirees (26%) spent fewer than five hours in the past year planning for retirement. Meanwhile, Americans age 45 and older spend an estimated 1.5 to 2 hours a day on social media — roughly 10 to 14 hours in a single week, according to DataReportal's Digital 2026 Global Overview. For many people nearing retirement, one week of scrolling outpaces an entire year of retirement planning.

It's not that Americans aren't worried about retirement. Cost-of-living increases, healthcare expenses, inflation, and the fear of outliving their savings weigh heavily on pre-retirees and even those who feel fully prepared report anxiety about whether their money will last. The issue is that concern isn't consistently translating into preparation.

"When people spend more time on social media in a week than they spend planning for retirement in a year, the barrier clearly isn't awareness — it's action," Beckwith said. "The encouraging part is that planning is one of the few retirement variables people can actually control. You can't control the markets or inflation, but you can decide to make a plan — and that single decision changes how prepared people feel and how prepared they actually are."

Planning — Not Just Wealth — Drives Confidence

LIMRA's research shows that retirement preparedness isn't determined by savings alone. Planning behaviors and professional guidance each contribute meaningfully to how prepared consumers feel. Pre-retirees who work with a financial advisor or planner are far more likely to feel highly prepared — 77% versus 47% of those who don't — yet only 40% currently work with one. Consumers with a written retirement plan likewise report significantly higher preparedness than those without.

A Simple Way to Check Your Readiness: The Three "R's"

LIMRA's research highlights several factors that contribute meaningfully to how prepared consumers feel, including their financial resources, having a written plan, actively engaging in the planning process, working with a financial advisor or planner, and understanding how savings will generate income in retirement. Based on these findings, consumers approaching retirement can begin by considering three questions:

Readiness — Do I have the financial resources and a current written plan to support the retirement I envision?

Resilience — Does my plan account for risks such as inflation, market swings, healthcare expenses, and other unexpected costs?

Retirement Income — Do I know how I'll turn my savings into income that lasts?

Consumers who regularly revisit all three areas are more likely to feel confident about their retirement future. The takeaway from the research is ultimately an encouraging one: retirement confidence isn't reserved for the wealthy or the lucky. It's built — through planning, guidance, and a clear picture of where the income will come from. And it can start with an hour that might otherwise be spent scrolling.

About the Research

The Retirement Income Readiness Report is based on a LIMRA survey of 486 pre-retirees (workers age 45 and older who plan to retire within 10 years) and 804 retirees age 45 and older, fielded in April, 2026. Social media usage figures are drawn from DataReportal's Digital 2026 Global Overview Report, which estimates average daily social media use at roughly 1.5 to 2 hours for adults age 45–54 and under 90 minutes for adults age 55 and older.

About LIMRA

Serving the industry since 1916, LIMRA offers industry knowledge, insights, connections, and solutions to help more than 600 financial services member organizations navigate change with confidence. Visit LIMRA at www.limra.com.

New product connects business worth with incentives that help retain the people driving growth

LAS VEGAS, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Reins, which gives contractors the tools to grow what their business is worth and their key people a real stake, announced today the launch of Valuation, a new standalone AI-powered product that gives owner-operators in the trades a clear view of what their company is worth and what they can do to increase that value.

Reins has raised $5.5 million to date from Album, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Torch Capital and Animo Ventures to level the playing field for independent business owners by giving them access to tools traditionally available to larger companies and private equity-backed businesses.

Valuation joins Reins' existing Incentives product, which helps owners create long-term incentives, including phantom stock and stock appreciation rights (SARs), as well as short-term profit-sharing plans that give key employees a real stake in the value they help create.

Reins initially developed this technology to support Incentives but saw a broader need among contractors for greater visibility into their companies' value. Valuation uses carefully developed AI agents to analyze financial and operating data, deliver a current valuation, identify the factors driving it and pinpoint opportunities for improvement.

Valuation gives owners:

  • A clear number for what the business is worth today, built from the owner's own financial and operating data, including QuickBooks and ServiceTitan data.
  • Visibility into what is holding that number back and how the business compares with peers.
  • Guidance on what to do next, including the incentive plans, KPIs and targets that can help move the business forward.

"Independent business owners spend years building companies that support their families, their employees and their communities, but they haven't always had access to the same sophisticated tools larger companies use to understand and grow their value," said Chris Buttenham, co-founder and CEO of Reins. "We want to change that. Valuation gives owners a clear picture of what they have built, shows them where they can create more value and connects that insight to Incentives so they can give key people a real stake in helping the business grow."

Valuation begins with the owner's own books and operating data to establish what the company is worth today. Its agentic analysis then identifies the factors driving that value, benchmarks the business against peers and highlights the levers with the greatest potential impact. Owners can then use Incentives to align key employees with the KPIs and targets that matter most through long- or short-term plans tied to the value they help create.

"Big companies have a CFO, an appraiser and a compensation consultant a phone call away," Buttenham said. "The owner of a 30-person HVAC shop has none of that: no real number on the business, no plan for what comes next. Valuation is how we level that. It gives independent owners the leverage private equity and big corporations have had for decades."

Valuation and Incentives run on the same data and are designed to work in the background of the business an owner already operates, without adding administrative burden or requiring a consultant. Together, they help contractors understand what their business is worth, act on the factors that can increase that value and build a stronger company with more options when the time comes to sell, hand off or step back on their terms.

For more information about Reins, visit myreins.com.

About Reins

Reins is the ownership operating system for independent businesses, giving owners the tools to understand and grow their business value while giving key employees a real stake in the value they help create. Through Valuation and Incentives, Reins helps owners understand what their business is worth, identify opportunities to increase its value and create long- and short-term incentive plans without giving up ownership or control. Reins works with hundreds of owner-operators in the trades, including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, restoration and landscaping, who have granted more than $50 million in incentives to key employees through Reins. Headquartered in Las Vegas, Reins is backed by Album, Better Tomorrow Ventures, Torch Capital and Animo Ventures.. Learn more at myreins.com.

releases.title: Legal Bay Announces Pre Settlement Funding for Social Media Addiction, Suicide and Youth Harm Lawsuits Following Historic Meta Settlement
releases.body:
Landmark $16.68 billion states settlement prompts Legal Bay to expand lawsuit funding for qualified victims and families pursuing individual claims involving alleged social media-related injuries and deaths.

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Legal Bay LLC, a national leader in pre settlement funding, lawsuit funding, legal funding, and settlement funding, announced today that it is actively considering funding applications from qualified plaintiffs pursuing social media addiction, personal injury, and wrongful death lawsuits following Meta's landmark settlement with 29 U.S. states.

Meta recently agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion to resolve state allegations that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to addict children, misrepresented platform safety, and improperly collected children's personal data. The agreement also requires significant changes intended to protect younger users, including usage restrictions, stronger age-verification measures, and additional safeguards surrounding potentially harmful content. Meta has denied wrongdoing.

The historic settlement represents an important development in the rapidly expanding litigation surrounding social media platforms and alleged harm to children and teenagers.

Thousands of individual personal injury cases remain separate from the states' settlement. These lawsuits allege that addictive platform features contributed to serious injuries among young users, including depression, anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm, suicidal ideation, attempted suicide, and, tragically, suicide deaths. More than 3,300 personal injury claims have already been consolidated in California litigation involving allegations of social media addiction and related harm.

Legal Bay is now providing pre settlement funding for qualified individual plaintiffs and families pursuing these claims, including parents who have filed wrongful death lawsuits following the suicide of a child allegedly associated with social media addiction or harmful online content.

Chris Janish, CEO of Legal Bay, commented, "The size of this settlement demonstrates that allegations surrounding social media addiction and youth safety have become a major area of litigation. Behind these cases are real children and families who have suffered devastating consequences, including self-harm and suicide. Legal Bay is now prepared to evaluate qualified cases for funding and provide financial assistance to victims and families while their attorneys pursue accountability."

If you or your child suffered serious psychological injury, self-harm, attempted suicide, or other damages allegedly related to social media addiction—or if you lost a loved one to suicide and are pursuing a wrongful death claim—Legal Bay is now accepting qualified cases for pre settlement funding. Please visit Legal-Bay HERE or call toll-free at 877.571.0405.

Individual lawsuits may involve allegations that social media companies knowingly incorporated features designed to maximize engagement among young users despite potential risks. Claims have focused on compulsive use and exposure to harmful content, as well as psychological and behavioral injuries. The social media companies have disputed allegations that their platforms caused plaintiffs' injuries and continue to defend individual cases.

Legal Bay believes the latest settlement could become an important benchmark as attorneys evaluate the continuing individual litigation against Meta and other social media companies. While no settlement or verdict guarantees the outcome or value of another case, major resolutions and bellwether verdicts can provide valuable information as mass litigation develops.

However, for families who have already endured severe psychological injury or the unimaginable loss of a child, the prospect of lengthy litigation can add another layer of stress. Drawn-out litigation can create substantial financial pressure if they are facing medical bills, therapy expenses, lost income, and other costs long before their cases reach settlement. Legal Bay's pre settlement funding can provide qualified plaintiffs with immediate cash while their attorneys continue pursuing their claims.

If you are involved in an active social media addiction lawsuit and need an immediate cash advance against an anticipated settlement—or if you need assistance finding an attorney—please visit Legal-Bay HERE or call toll-free at 877.571.0405.

Legal Bay offers pre settlement funding, lawsuit funding, legal funding, settlement funding, loans on lawsuits, loans on lawsuit, and loan on lawsuit programs for qualified plaintiffs involved in complex litigation. These non-recourse funding programs provide immediate cash against an anticipated recovery, allowing plaintiffs to address financial needs while giving their attorneys additional time to pursue fair compensation. Legal Bay can also assist potential claimants who have not yet retained counsel by connecting them with attorneys experienced in this developing litigation.

Legal Bay's funding is non-recourse, meaning repayment is required only when a plaintiff successfully obtains compensation through a settlement or verdict. If there is no recovery, there is no obligation to repay the advance.

To apply right now for a loan settlement program, please visit the company's website HERE or call toll-free at: 877.571.0405 where agents are standing by to answer any questions.

A live Zoom event, Thursday, October 1, 2026, 2-3 PM ET

NEW YORK, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The American Council of Learned Societies presents "Hashtag Humanities: Scholars, Social Media, and Knowledge for the Public Good," a virtual discussion panel, on Thursday, October 1, 2026, 2-3 PM ET.

As social media continues to play a critical role in how many people receive news and information—in some cases being their primary source—it has become increasingly important for scholars to have a significant voice on popular platforms.

Rigorous training in research and analysis gives today's PhDs in humanistic fields an advantage in the ongoing battle for revealing truth and fact in a crowded multimedia landscape.

This live Zoom panel discussion will feature three popular scholarly influencers on why and how they've built their social media followings and how they hope to change how people access knowledge beyond the academy.

Meet the Panelists:

Dr. Xavier Buck | @historyIn3

Executive Director of the Dr. Huey P. Newton Foundation, founding director of the Black Panther Party Museum in Oakland, CA, and a 2021 ACLS Leading Edge Fellow

Heather Colley | @heathercolleyauthor

PhD student in English Literature at Oxford University, author of The Gilded Butterfly Effect: A Novel (Three Rooms Press)

Dr. Dan McClellan | @maklelan

Public scholar of the Bible and religion

The discussion will be moderated by Dr. Keyanah Nurse, ACLS Senior Program Officer for Intentional Design for an Equitable Academy (IDEA) programs.

This live Zoom event is free to join and registration is required. Learn more at bit.ly/4AciCCo.

Formed over a century ago, the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) is a nonprofit federation of 85 scholarly organizations. As the leading representative of American scholarship in the humanities and interpretive social sciences, ACLS upholds the core principle that knowledge is a public good. In supporting its member organizations, ACLS expands the forms, content, and flow of scholarly knowledge, reflecting our commitment to diversity of identity and experience. ACLS collaborates with institutions, associations, and individuals to strengthen the evolving infrastructure for scholarship.

releases.body:
LAS VEGAS, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SIRUI, an imaging brand specializing in innovative lens design and technology, showcased its latest lens innovations at IBC 2026. A major highlight of the show was the Aurora 15mm F1.6 full-frame autofocus lens receiving a Best of Show Award on September 13. At Booth 12.D31, SIRUI also featured the newly launched Saturn V2, two upcoming new focal lengths in the Aurora series, and the Swift series, alongside its established Vision Prime, Iron-Star and Astra lineups.

Aurora 15mm F1.6 Receives "Best of Show" Award

SIRUI's upcoming Aurora 15mm F1.6 full-frame autofocus lens received a "Best of Show" Award during IBC 2026 on September 13.

Combining an ultra-wide 15mm focal length with a large F1.6 aperture, the lens features a 0.3m minimum focusing distance, low distortion and a compact, lightweight design. The combination of ultra-wide coverage, large aperture and portability makes it a versatile option for full-frame creators.

The lens also reflects SIRUI's focus on optical design and manufacturing, including the in-house development and production of aspherical lens elements.

New Lens Innovations at IBC 2026

SIRUI's IBC lineup featured several recent additions across anamorphic, autofocus and lightweight imaging solutions.

The Saturn V2 drew attention with its 1.6x anamorphic design, full-frame coverage and horizontal-and-vertical shooting capability, offering greater flexibility across different production formats.

The Aurora series introduced new focal lengths while maintaining a focus on compact design and image quality. The Aurora 24mm, for example, was designed for video creators with low focus breathing and a compact form factor suited to applications including vlogging, handheld video, weddings, events and documentary production.

SIRUI also showcased its upcoming Swift autofocus lens series, developed around the "Daily Carry" concept for users seeking a compact and lightweight solution for everyday shooting. Together with the Vision Prime, Iron-Star and Astra series, the lineup demonstrated SIRUI's expanding portfolio of imaging solutions.

The two new focal lengths in the Aurora series and the Swift series are set to launch progressively over the coming months. For further details, please stay tuned to SIRUI's official store.

Connecting with Creators and the Imaging Industry

Beyond product demonstrations, SIRUI engaged with filmmakers, creators, media and industry professionals throughout the show.

At the show, SIRUI was also joined by creators Sightseeing Stan, Vi-Dan, and INDIE Filmmakers, who took part in on-site talks sharing their experiences working with SIRUI lenses and their perspectives on visual storytelling. International imaging media outlet CineD also conducted an on-site interview with the SIRUI team.

SIRUI also partnered with EVOTO and HOLLYLAND on a joint on-site check-in campaign during the show.

SIRUI's participation at IBC 2026 highlighted its latest lens developments and continued engagement with the global imaging community.

About SIRUI

Founded in 2006, SIRUI is a global brand specializing in optical imaging products and dedicated to providing professional, high-quality optical and imaging solutions for photographers, filmmakers, and imaging enthusiasts. Through continuous innovation in optical technology and product design, SIRUI strives to empower creators with greater freedom to explore, create, and bring their vision to life.

releases.title: Red Bank Catholic High School and Conscientia Health Open New Wellness Room, Marking Expanded Commitment to Student Mental and Physical Health
releases.body:
Ribbon-cutting held on World Suicide Prevention Day

RED BANK, N.J., Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Red Bank Catholic High School officially opened a new Wellness Room on its Broad Street campus today, with a ribbon-cutting and blessing ceremony marking the next chapter of the school's student wellness initiative, developed in partnership with Conscientia Health. 

The event fell on World Suicide Prevention Day, within National Suicide Prevention Awareness Month, timing both organizations say reflects their shared commitment to student mental health. 

The Wellness Room is part of a broader initiative between RBC and Conscientia Health that includes a wellness curriculum focused on mental health awareness, resilience, and coping strategies; educational programming workshops; and expanded support pathways for students and families. 

"This is about creating a culture where wellness is foundational to student success," said Nicole Wall, RBC Student Assistance Counselor. "As RBC continues to expand opportunities and strengthen student support systems, we remain committed to exceeding the needs of the whole child academically, spiritually, and emotionally." 

"We didn't choose today's date, the timing found us," said Dr. Simbiat Adighije (Dr. Sim), Founder of Conscientia Health, who has led the partnership. "But it's a reminder of why this work matters. Too many young people carry real struggles quietly, and too many adults around them don't know until it's a crisis. This room is one answer to that: a place where a student can be seen and supported before things reach that point. We're proud to build that alongside Red Bank Catholic." 

The Wellness Room includes a private consultation space, a group and workshop area for peer support sessions, and a self-guided check-in tool connecting students directly with a clinician when needed. The initiative is part of RISE by Conscientia, a program extending Conscientia's integrated care model into school communities. 

About Red Bank Catholic High School 

Red Bank Catholic is a vibrant, beloved, Catholic co-educational institution with a storied history, an extraordinary spirit, and a record of achievement in the classroom and beyond. Our programs pursue excellence in faith, academics, cultural awareness, athletics, and personal wellness in a mission to fully engage the minds, hearts, and souls of students in our Roman Catholic community so that they can succeed in every aspect of their lives. 

About Conscientia Health 

Conscientia Health is a telehealth provider offering integrated psychiatry, therapy, and primary care, with a mission to make whole-person care accessible and coordinated. Conscientia operates over 20 physical locations across New Jersey, providing hybrid in-person and virtual care. 

Conscientia Health's R.I.S.E. Teen Mental Health Program supports adolescents ages 12 to 19 through personalized teen mental health services for emotional, behavioral, and mental health challenges. We help teenagers reclaim their inner strength, develop practical life skills, and build resilience through integrated behavioral health and primary care support.

releases.title: Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival
releases.body:
Out of the Ashes receives the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize and Empire at Sea receives the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize; the two projects offer distinct approaches to climate storytelling

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Two projects supported by Agog: The Immersive Media Institute won two of the three prizes awarded today in the Venice Immersive competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. Out of the Ashes, co-directed by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña, received the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize. Empire at Sea, created and directed by Peter Flaherty, earned the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize.

The awards celebrate two distinct approaches to climate storytelling. Out of the Ashes is a virtual-reality documentary about loss, memory, resilience, and rebuilding after the January 2025 Los Angeles fires. Empire at Sea is an interactive solarpunk augmented-reality drama that asks audiences to confront questions of sustainability, migration, inclusion, and collective survival.

Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

"Wendy Schmidt and I founded Agog on the belief that immersive media can bring people closer to urgent issues and help them imagine what change could look like," said Chip Giller, co-founder and executive director of Agog. "At Venice, we saw creators expand what these emerging technologies can do—and audiences responded in deeply personal ways. Out of the Ashes brought people from around the world close to the human toll of the Los Angeles fires, and many saw echoes of what their own communities have experienced. Empire at Sea shows new possibilities for filmmaking by pairing cinematic performance and an accomplished cast with the power of immersive media. Seeing both works recognized on a global stage makes us more excited than ever about immersive media's potential to advance storytelling, contribute to social change, and serve the public good."

"Out of the Ashes and Empire at Sea are ambitious, deeply human works that demonstrate the creative range of immersive storytelling," said Liz Rosenthal and Michel Reilhac, curators of Venice Immersive. "Agog made a meaningful contribution to Venice Immersive this year, not only through its support of three projects selected for competition, but also by creating spaces where artists, producers, technologists, and changemakers could experiment, exchange ideas, and form new connections. That combination of supporting individual projects and investing in the wider ecosystem is exactly what an emerging field needs to grow."

About Out of the Ashes

Narrated by award-winning actor Courtney B. Vance, Out of the Ashes places audiences within the events and aftermath of the Los Angeles wildfires. The 26-minute documentary combines first-person storytelling with volumetric reconstructions of participants' homes, created in part from their own family photos and videos. It closes by highlighting community organizations leading recovery efforts, including My Tribe Rise, Evolve Altadena, and the Palisades Recovery Coalition.

The work was created by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña and co-produced by The Mercantile Agency, Emblematic Group, and Arizona State University's MA in Narrative and Emerging Media program, with support from Agog and the MacArthur Foundation.

Out of the Ashes assets: project page | press kit

About Empire at Sea

Empire at Sea is a 22-minute interactive augmented-reality drama about climate scientists building a sustainable community on a remote oil rig after a catastrophe cuts them off from the mainland. Up to 10 audience members experience cinematic holograms around a custom interactive LED table and navigate together a story about science, sustainability, immigration, and community.

The work was created, directed, and produced by Peter Flaherty; commissioned by Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts and ASU Gammage; developed with Flaherty Pictures, 4DV.ai, and NightLight Labs; and supported by Agog, the Schwarzman Center at Yale University, and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. It is scheduled to be presented at Lincoln Center in January 2027.

Empire at Sea assets: project page | website | press kit

Agog at Venice Immersive

Agog supported three projects selected for this year's Venice Immersive competition. The third, Solwata, is a mixed-reality documentary that brings audiences into the lives of communities in Solomon Islands confronting rising seas, displacement, and planned relocation. Created by NowHere Media and co-produced by Human Rights Watch and Agog, the experience is narrated and executive produced by Mark Ruffalo. Following its Venice premiere, Solwata is now being presented at the Toronto International Film Festival's Innovation Hub through Sept. 16. It will next appear at the BFI London Film Festival and COP31, the annual United Nations climate change conference.

Beyond its involvement with the three projects, Agog partnered with Venice Immersive on the occasion of the festival's 10th anniversary to shape discussions about what the next decade could hold, with a focus on impact. Throughout the festival, Agog convened creators, nonprofit leaders, funders, technologists, and cultural leaders for programming including a Smart Glasses Petting Zoo offering hands-on access to the latest emerging technology to consider ways it could be harnessed for storytelling and social good, an imagination workshop focused on expanding what is possible in immersive storytelling, and hands-on- conversations about new creative possibilities and the opportunities for immersive media to spur social change.

These activities are part of Agog's broader efforts to champion ambitious work, connect people across the immersive ecosystem, and help immersive media develop with public purpose at its center. Learn more

About Agog: The Immersive Media Institute

Agog: The Immersive Media Institute is a philanthropic organization founded by Chip Giller and Wendy Schmidt that is dedicated to helping creators and nonprofit leaders use immersive media—including virtual, augmented, and mixed reality—to imagine and build a more connected, just, and compassionate world. Agog operates as a field builder and creative partner, supporting immersive storytellers whose work addresses urgent social and environmental challenges. Learn more at agog.org

DENVER, Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evergreen Digital Media Corp. (EDM), a premier operator of digital signage and retail media networks, and Adwave Digital Inc. (Adwave), a technology company that operates an AI-powered advertising platform, have finalized a strategic partnership in which EDM will provide capital to facilitate the continued development of Adwave's AI platform. EDM will also receive a preferred licensing agreement to the platform as part of the agreement.

Adwave's WaveRunner platform buys and runs ad campaigns across streaming TV, Google, Meta, Reddit, and the web from a single daily budget, optimizing placement using a business's own site data, without requiring an agency or separate accounts for each channel.

This is EDM's third strategic investment in the past year, but a different type of deal. The earlier investments brought new screen networks into EDM's fold. In this partnership, EDM obtains rights to run Adwave's AI ad-buying technology directly, without taking on another network to operate.

"Adwave brings a level of talent and technical knowledge in the advertising AI space that's rare to find," said Don Winfrey, CEO of Evergreen Digital Media Corp. "We're excited to learn from this team as we bring that expertise into our networks."

"EDM has built something real in the DOOH space, and we're glad to be working alongside a team with that kind of reach," said David Naffis, CEO of Adwave. "We're looking forward to what this partnership produces."

About Evergreen Digital Media Corp. Evergreen Digital Media Corp. (EDM) is the parent company of NTV360, N-Compass TV and OnPremise Networks. Collectively, these entities operate uniquely through a network of exclusive local dealers calling on local advertisers in the Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) sector, delivering digital signage, content and local marketing opportunities to communities throughout the United States and Canada. 

About Adwave Digital Inc. Adwave is an AI-powered advertising platform. Its WaveRunner product buys and runs cross-channel ad campaigns, spanning streaming TV, social, video, and display, from a single daily budget. More information is available at waverunner.adwave.com.

releases.title: Frank Russo Calls for Florida Crackdown on Addictive Social Media Features Targeting Children
releases.body:
Independent candidate for Governor says protecting children, parents and classrooms must come before Big Tech profits

NEW SMYRNA BEACH, Fla., Sept. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Non-party affiliated candidate for Florida Governor Frank Russo today announced that, if elected, he will support and sign legislation restricting addictive social media design features aimed at children under the age of 16.

The proposal comes as California moves forward with new protections limiting addictive features for young users - but Russo said Florida should not wait for another state or Washington to decide how to protect its children.

As a father, Russo said he understands the concerns parents have about what their children are exposed to online – from addictive algorithms designed to keep them scrolling to predatory content and pornography that can be only a few clicks away.

"This isn't about Republicans or Democrats. It's about our kids," Russo said. "Parents are doing everything they can to protect their children, but they are up against some of the largest technology companies in the world designing products to keep kids hooked. At some point, someone has to stand up for Florida families."

Russo also connected online safety directly to his experience listening to Florida educators. Teachers across the state have repeatedly raised concerns about the impact social media and constant phone use are having on student attention, behavior and learning.

"I've been listening to teachers, parents and families across Florida, and they are telling us the same thing – social media is affecting what happens inside our classrooms," Russo said. "If we are serious about improving education, we cannot ignore what is competing for our children's attention every minute of the day."

Russo said Florida should establish clear, enforceable standards for technology companies serving minors while giving parents stronger tools to protect their children.

"Big Tech has had plenty of time to police itself," Russo said. "Our children's safety, their mental well-being and their ability to learn have to come before another click, another view or another dollar in corporate profit. Florida can lead on this - and as Governor, I will."

The Russo campaign will release additional details of its proposed child online safety legislation
